entries.summary: 빈센트가 파리를 떠나 아를에 막 도착한 직후 테오에게 쓴 첫 편지로, 60센티미터가 넘게 쌓인 눈과 낯선 남프랑스 풍경에 대한 인상을 전한다. 노란 바위산과 붉은 흙의 포도밭, 눈 덮인 산봉우리가 어우러진 풍경을 일본 판화 속 겨울 풍경에 비유하며 감탄한다. 도착 첫날이라 아직 마을을 조금 둘러본 정도이며, 골동품상에게서 몽티첼리를 안다는 이야기를 들었다는 소식도 덧붙인다. 전반적으로 새로운 정착지에 대한 기대와 테오에 대한 애틋한 마음이 드러나는 편지다.
entries.why: Van Gogh arrived in Arles on Monday, 20 February (see n. 1). From ll. 40-45 we can deduce that that the letter was written the next day. We have therefore dated the letter Tuesday, 21 February 1888. Jo van Gogh-Bonger also gave this date in Brieven 1914 – she may have had a postmark to go on.

facts.said: My dear Theo, During the journey I thought at least as much about you as about the new country I was seeing.
facts.note: In a letter written to his sister Willemien on 24 and 26 February 1888, Theo reported that Vincent left for Arles in the south of France ‘last Sunday’; this was therefore Sunday, 19 February. Since Theo also wrote that the journey would take a ‘day and night’, Vincent must have reached Arles on Monday, 20 February (FR b914). In his letter Theo explained Vincent’s motives for going to Arles: he was looking for lighter colours than he could find in the north, and he wanted to recover his physical strength.

facts.said: Here’s my address Restaurant Carrel 30 rue Cavalerie Arles
facts.note: Between the end of February and early May Van Gogh rented a room from Albert Carrel and Cathérine Carrel-Garcin. Hotel-Restaurant Carrel was at 30 rue Amédée-Pichot, in the northern part of the town. This section of the street was known as rue de la Cavalerie until 1887; Van Gogh was therefore using the old address. The hotel was a ‘two-storey house, small terrace on top and balcony on the first floor’ (maison à deux étages, petite terrasse au-dessus et balcon au premier). See Coquiot 1923, p. 161. In the official deeds the name is spelled ‘Carel’ (ACA and L’indicateur marseillais 1888).

facts.said: Before reaching Tarascon
facts.note: Van Gogh took the express train from Paris to Marseille (the ‘Paris-Lyon-Méditerranée’) that left at 9.40 p.m. on Sunday 19 February and arrived in Arles at 4.49 p.m. the following day. The train passed through Tarascon, a small town about 20 km to the north of Arles. See Murphy 2016, pp. 25, 36, 263 (n. 33), 264 (n. 3).

facts.said: I’ll write to you soon — an antique dealer whose shop I went into yesterday in this very street was telling me he knew of a Monticelli.
facts.note: Van Gogh wrote that the antique dealer had his premises ‘in this very street’; however the address books do not record any in rue Amédée-Pichot or rue de la Cavalerie. The closest antique dealer was Berthet, 5 rue de la Sous-Préfecture, just off rue Amédée-Pichot.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 아를 정착 초기 생활비가 예상보다 많이 든다고 전하며, 습작 세 점을 완성했다고 알린다. 화상 레이드가 몽티첼리 그림 거래와 인상파 화가들을 영국에 소개하는 문제로 자신들과 이해관계가 얽혀 있음을 분석하고, 테오에게 신중하게 대응할 것을 조언한다. 코닝을 테오의 집에 머물게 해달라는 부탁과 함께, 마르세유에서 좋은 파란색 물감을 구하고 싶다는 바람도 덧붙인다.
entries.why: Theo wrote to his sister Willemien about Vincent in a letter of 24 and 26 February (FR b914). See Documentation, 24 and 26 February 1888. In the second part, written on the 26th, he quoted from the present letter from Vincent. This means that it must have been sent on 25 February at the latest. Since his letter of 21 February (577) Vincent had been to the museum and made three studies. Since all this would probably have taken a few days, we are dating the letter on or about Friday, 24 February 1888.

works.title: Landscape with Snow
works.said: Yours truly, Vincent The studies I have are an old woman of Arles, a landscape with snow, a view of a stretch of pavement with a butcher’s shop.

works.title: View of a Butcher's Shop
works.said: Yours truly, Vincent The studies I have are an old woman of Arles, a landscape with snow, a view of a stretch of pavement with a butcher’s shop.

works.title: An Old Woman of Arles
works.said: Yours truly, Vincent The studies I have are an old woman of Arles, a landscape with snow, a view of a stretch of pavement with a butcher’s shop.

works.title: Snowy Landscape with Arles in the Background
works.said: Yours truly, Vincent The studies I have are an old woman of Arles, a landscape with snow, a view of a stretch of pavement with a butcher’s shop.

facts.said: You would definitely be doing our friend Koning a favour if you let him stay with you
facts.note: The Dutch painter Arnold Koning was in Paris from September 1887 to the end of May 1888. After Vincent went to Arles, Koning stayed with Theo in the apartment in rue Lepic for a short time. See also the letter from Theo to Willemien van Gogh ( Documentation, 24 and 26 February 1888). Koning moved in with Theo soon after 14 March (FR b915); he returned to the Netherlands on 30 May 1888 (FR b1077).

facts.said: So far I’m not finding living here as profitable as I might have hoped,
facts.note: Van Gogh started out paying 5 francs and later 4 francs a day for board and lodging. From 1 May onwards, when he had his studio in the Yellow House and consequently took up less space, he only paid 3 francs. See letters 587 and 603.

facts.said: If you see Bernard tell him that so far I’m having to pay more than at Pont-Aven,
facts.note: Pont-Aven, a small village in Brittany, was discovered by painters around 1865, and grew to become a well-known artists’ colony. Bernard had been to Pont-Aven in August 1886 and had met Paul Gauguin there. The latter had been staying there again since late January 1888, as he had told Van Gogh (letter 581). The group of artists who worked there in Gauguin’s style is known as the School of Pont-Aven. See exhib. cat. Paris 2003. The cost of living in Brittany and the south of France had evidently been a subject of discussion between Bernard and Van Gogh.

facts.said: I have to buy my colours and canvases from either a grocer or a bookseller,
facts.note: We do not know which bookshops in Arles sold paint and canvas. Not long afterwards, Van Gogh says that he knows a grocer who sells artists’ supplies; this was probably Jules Armand. See letter 583, n. 8. It may well also have been possible to buy artists’ materials in Bompard fils’ wallpaper (papiers peints) shop at 14 place de la République; it is clear from the local newspapers that work by local artists was regularly displayed in the shop window.

facts.said: For us to say we’d never have benefited from knowing him would be relatively unfair since, 1, he made us a gift of a very fine painting (which painting, let it be said by the way, we intended to acquire), 2, Reid made Monticellis go up in value, and since we own 5 of them the result for us is that these paintings have increased in value — 3, he was good and pleasant company in the first months.
facts.note: Reid, who had been working for Boussod, Valadon & Cie since June or July 1886, presumably lived with Theo and Vincent in rue Lepic for some time. This was probably a period of some six months between the summer of 1886 and the spring of 1887. See Fowle 2000, p. 93.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 볼테르의 풍자와 인생의 진지함에 관해 논한다. 스승 안톤 마우베의 죽음을 애도하며 인간으로서 그를 사랑했다고 고백하고, 배추벌레의 비유를 들어 인간이 사후 세계를 함부로 판단할 수 없다는 사유를 전개한다. 화가는 그림을 그려야 한다는 소명을 채소벌레가 뿌리를 먹어야 하는 이치에 비유하며, 자신이 남쪽 아를로 내려온 이유를 설명한다.
entries.why: Theo wrote Vincent’s address for Willemien at the bottom of the letter (see Additional details), which means that it was sent to her by way of Theo. Theo most probably received the present letter enclosed with letter 578, and sent it on to Willemien, accompanied by his letter to her of 24 and 26 February (FR b914), since in that he remarks: ‘Since I had put my letter to one side ... I can now tell you a little more about him and also send you a letter from him’.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: My dear sister, For my part, I could just as well say that I’ll stop writing to you immediately at the moment you reply to me;
facts.note: Vincent is replying here to an unknown letter from Willemien, in which she must have expressed her disappointment that he did not write often (cf. letter 574). It is also clear from Theo’s letter to her that Vincent did not write much: ‘Vincent started writing to you ten times and I have read more letters to you than you have received from him, but sometimes one begins rattling away if one has finally got started, and then it is better to start afresh. But his letters are always interesting, which is why it’s a pity that he doesn’t write more’ (FR b914).

facts.said: But be this as it may, it’s very good that you’re starting by finding out what sort of harm that wretch Voltaire has done — and you’ll certainly find this in Candide, that Voltaire dared to laugh at the ‘highly serious life which we ought only to devote to or spend on the best ends’.
facts.note: See for Voltaire’s Candide : letter 568, n. 3. Van Gogh is not quoting literally here; it may be that he is paraphrasing the theme of the book in Panglossian terms, but it is more likely that he is quoting from Willemien’s last letter: she must have read the book because of what Vincent said about it in his previous letter to her (letter 574).

facts.said: It has affected me very badly
facts.note: Anton Mauve, Van Gogh’s first teacher, had suddenly died on 5 February 1888 (Laren, Civil registration). He was 49 years old.

facts.said: And that it would be rash of them to undertake overground studies to throw light on this question, since the gardener or others interested in salad and vegetables would immediately trample them underfoot as being harmful insects.
facts.note: This metaphor may derive from Frederik van Eeden’s De kleine Johannes (1887), which Van Gogh undoubtedly chose in order to appeal to Willemien’s frame of reference. (Van Gogh was to refer to the book again later; see letters 626 and 740). De kleine Johannes is a Bildungsroman disguised as a fairy tale, in which Johannes tries to find ‘wisdom’ with the help of various allegorical fairy-tale figures. The contrast between idealized nature and man is the connecting thread throughout the book.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오에게 자신이 대신 써준 테르스티흐 앞 편지를 검토해 전달할지 판단해달라고 부탁한다. 레이드, 반 비셀링, 테르스티흐 등 영국 화상들 사이의 미묘한 이해관계를 조율하며, 파리·런던·마르세유에 인상주의 상설 전시를 만들자는 구상과 화가들의 협동조합적 연대를 제안한다. 화상들의 경쟁 구도 속에서 신중하게 처신해야 한다는 사업적 고민이 중심이다.
entries.why: Van Gogh continues to discuss the plan he formulated in letter 578 of about 24 February, and he says he has made another study since then (l. 107). The letter precedes letter 582 of about 2 March 1888, because in it Vincent thanks his brother for the draft letter he wrote to Tersteeg; in the present letter he suggests that Theo should get in touch with Tersteeg. We have therefore dated this on or about Monday, 27 February 1888.

works.title: Still Life: Potatoes in a Yellow Dish
works.said: Vincent I have one more study.

people.name: David Croal Thomson
people.note: (1855-1930) director of Goupil & Cie in London

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

people.name: Boussod, Valadon & Cie
people.note: art dealers in Paris, successors of Goupil & Cie

facts.said: Vincent I have one more study.
facts.note: This new study may have been Bowl of potatoes (F 386 / JH 1365), which is dated to February-March 1888; see cat. Otterlo 2003, pp. 199-201.

facts.said: On the contrary, I ask no more than this, that what you’ve started in the shop on the boulevard should last and become more important.
facts.note: Since 1886 Theo had regularly exhibited and sold work by the Impressionists in Boussod, Valadon & Cie’s upstairs gallery in boulevard Montmartre.

facts.said: You see, for myself I thought we had to make an effort from this end, because we’ll have Reid through Van Wisselingh  and Van Wisselingh through Tersteeg.
facts.note: Van Wisselingh had done his training at Goupil’s branch in The Hague (1864-1866) and then worked at the firm’s headquarters in Paris (1866-1874). Between 1881 and 1890, as an independent art dealer, he was an important customer of Goupil’s in The Hague, where Tersteeg had been manager since 1867. See Stolwijk 1998, p. 218 (n. 104).

facts.said: has married the daughter of the Glasgow picture dealer who’s in competition with Reid.
facts.note: On 1 July 1887 Van Wisselingh, who had had his own art gallery in Amsterdam since 1884, married Isabella Murray Mowat Angus in Glasgow. She was the daughter of William Craibe Angus. See Heijbroek and Wouthuysen 1999, p. 27. Angus was Reid’s main competitor in the trade in Monticellis in Scotland.

facts.said: Really, this way Tersteeg and the London manager
facts.note: David Croal Thomson managed the London branch of Boussod, Valadon & Cie from 1884 to 1897. In April 1889 he staged an exhibition of twenty works by Monet. See Fowle 1993, pp. 53-54 (appendix 2).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오가 테르스티흐에게 보낸 편지 초안이 잘 되었다며, 인상주의 화가들을 영국에 소개하자는 아이디어가 자신의 편지에서 비롯되었음을 언급한다. 고갱이 몸이 아프고 빚에 시달려 그림 값을 더 낮추려 한다는 소식을 전하며 러셀에게 편지를 써보겠다고 하고, 테르스티흐가 고갱의 바다 그림을 사줄 수 있는지 묻는다. 테오가 코닝을 집에 들인 것을 반기며, 서리와 눈 속에서도 이미 꽃핀 아몬드 나무 가지를 그린 소품 이야기로 편지를 맺는다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he had sent; this must be the first instalment of the March allowance. We have therefore dated the letter on or about Friday, 2 March 1888. This is borne out by what he says about the weather: ‘There’s a hard frost here, and out in the country there’s still snow’. The weather reports for 2 March mention ‘hoarfrost’ (Météo-France).

works.title: Blossoming Almond Branch in a Glass with a Book
works.said: And then 2 little studies of a branch of an almond tree that’s already in flower despite everything.

works.title: Snowy Landscape with Arles in the Background
works.said: There’s a hard frost here, and out in the country there’s still snow — I have a study of a whitened landscape with the town in the background.

works.title: Blossoming Almond Branch in a Glass
works.said: And then 2 little studies of a branch of an almond tree that’s already in flower despite everything.

works.title: Montmartre: behind the Moulin de la Galette
works.said: It’s all much the same to me, I’m inclined to place slightly more hopes in this year’s work.

works.title: Kitchen Gardens on Montmartre
works.said: It’s all much the same to me, I’m inclined to place slightly more hopes in this year’s work.

works.title: Still Life with French novels and glass with a rose
works.said: It’s all much the same to me, I’m inclined to place slightly more hopes in this year’s work.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: About the Independents’ exhibition,
facts.note: The fourth exhibition of the Société des Artistes Indépendants was due to be staged in Paris from 22 March to 3 May 1888. This society, founded in 1884 by Odilon Redon, Albert Dubois-Pillet, Georges Seurat, Paul Signac, Charles Angrand and Henri Edmond Cross, invited artists to exhibit at its alternative Salon, where the works were not adjudicated.

facts.said: Would you risk buying the seascape from him for the firm?
facts.note: Paul Gauguin, The beach at Dieppe, 1885 (Copenhagen, Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek; W178/W166). Ill. 2143. This work had been on commission with Boussod, Valadon & Cie since December 1887; see letter 581, n. 2. Theo sent it to the Hague branch in March 1888. See letter 589, n. 4.

facts.said: I’m sending you a few lines for him in case you have something to tell him,
facts.note: It emerges from letter 583 that on second thoughts Van Gogh wrote to Gauguin direct rather than enclosing a letter for him.

facts.said: Enough for today, I’m writing a note to Koning.
facts.note: This enclosed letter to Koning is not known. Theo told Willemien about Koning in his letter of 14 March 1888: ‘It still seems strange to me that he [Vincent] has gone, he was so important to me in recent times. Now the studio will soon be occupied again, by a young Dutch painter, but he has by no means as much talent as Vincent, although he’s not bad’ (FR b915).

entries.summary: 혹독한 겨울이 끝나가는 아를에서, 반 고흐는 미스트랄 바람 속에서도 여덟 점의 습작을 완성했다고 전한다. 고갱과 러셀을 서로 연결해 주었고, 앙통 마우버를 추모하며 그의 부인에게 그림을 보내자고 제안한다. 테르스테흐가 냉담해도 개의치 않겠다는 다짐과 함께, 병약한 예술가들의 처지를 한탄하며 건강한 신체를 가진 화가 세대가 오기를 갈망한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes: ‘this morning the weather has changed and has turned milder’. Following a period of cold and the mistral, after a slight improvement on 8 March the weather became considerably milder on 9 March (Météo-France). We have therefore dated the letter Friday, 9 March 1888.

works.title: Still Life with Oranges Basket
works.said: Now I’ve just finished a study like the one of mine Lucien Pissarro has, but this time it’s of oranges.

works.title: The Gleize Bridge over the Vigueirat Canal
works.said: I’ve bought some coarse canvas here and I’ve had it prepared for matt effects,

works.title: Avenue of Plane Trees near Arles Station
works.said: I’ve bought some coarse canvas here and I’ve had it prepared for matt effects,

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: For example, we’ll send Mrs Mauve a painting in memory of Mauve

works.title: Still Life with Basket of Apples
works.said: Now I’ve just finished a study like the one of mine Lucien Pissarro has, but this time it’s of oranges.

works.title: Baby Marcelle Roulin
works.said: On Saturday evening I had a visit from two amateur painters, one of whom is a grocer — and also sells painting materials — and the other a justice of the peace who seems kind and intelligent.

works.title: Landscape with Snow
works.said: That makes eight studies I have up to now.

works.title: Still Life: Potatoes in a Yellow Dish
works.said: That makes eight studies I have up to now.

people.name: Lucien Pissarro
people.note: (1863-1944) French artist, son of Camille Pissarro

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: On Saturday evening I had a visit from two amateur painters, one of whom is a grocer — and also sells painting materials — and the other a justice of the peace who seems kind and intelligent.
facts.note: The grocer was Jules Armand, ‘épicier-droguiste’, 30 rue du Quatre-Septembre. Stokvis mentions a Madame J. Armand, the widow of a grocer who was an amateur artist, ‘where Vincent occasionally bought what he needed’. Coquiot calls her ‘the widow of a colourman, where Vincent bought supplies the first few days’. See Stokvis 1929, p. 4, and Coquiot 1923, p. 164. Jules Armand was the first known owner of Marcelle Roulin (F 440 / JH 1639). In the Museon Arlaten in Arles there is a portrait of an Arlésienne, signed ‘J. Armand 1889’.

facts.said: For example, we’ll send Mrs Mauve a painting in memory of Mauve
facts.note: Mauve died on 5 February. Around 30 March, in response to his death, Van Gogh painted Pink peach trees (‘Souvenir de Mauve’) (F 394 / JH 1379) and decided to give it to Mauve’s widow, Jet Mauve-Carbentus. See letter 590.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Now at long last, this morning the weather has changed and has turned milder — and I’ve already had an opportunity to find out what this mistral’s
facts.note: The mistral is a cold, dry katabatic wind from the north-west or north, which blows in the Rhône valley and the coastal regions of south-east France.

facts.said: I’ve just read Tartarin sur les Alpes, which I greatly enjoyed.
facts.note: Alphonse Daudet’s Tartarin sur les Alpes (1885), like Tartarin de Tarascon (1872), is a satirical novel that mocks the men of southern France, and particularly the inhabitants of Tarascon. The central character, Tartarin, a self-proclaimed lion-hunter and the president of the Tarascon mountain climbing association – whose members have never been further than the foothills of the Alpilles – goes to Switzerland to conquer the highest peaks in the Alps and strengthen his position as president before the elections.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오에게 화가들의 협동조합 결성이라는 야심찬 구상을 상세히 제안한다. 드가, 모네, 르누아르, 시슬레, 피사로 같은 그랑 불바르의 대가들이 그림을 공동재산으로 내놓고, 고갱·기요맹·쇠라 등 프티 불바르 화가들도 동참시켜 판매금을 나누는 협회를 만들자는 것이다. 테르스티흐의 협조가 관건임을 강조하며, 덴마크 화가 무리에-페테르센과의 만남과 풍경화 작업 근황도 함께 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh confirms the receipt of 100 francs; this must have been the second instalment for March, since he refers to the death of Kaiser Wilhelm (ll. 12-13) on 9 March and the ensuing unrest. Since Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave the date as 10 March in Brieven 1914 and she may have had a postmark to go on, we have dated the letter Saturday, 10 March 1888.

works.title: Still Life with French novels and glass with a rose
works.said: This study should be given the title: ‘Parisian novels’.

works.title: The Gleize Bridge over the Vigueirat Canal
works.said: I have two more studies of landscapes,

works.title: Avenue of Plane Trees near Arles Station
works.said: I have two more studies of landscapes,

works.title: Willows at Sunset
works.said: I have two more studies of landscapes,

facts.said: Then the great Impressionists of the Grand Boulevard,
facts.note: Van Gogh described Degas, Monet, Renoir, Sisley and Camille Pissarro as ‘Impressionists of the Grand Boulevard’ because their reputations were already established and their work was exhibited by renowned galleries like Boussod, Valadon & Cie, Durand-Ruel and Georges Petit, which were in or near the chic boulevards around place de l’Opéra. Van Gogh saw opportunities for an association of these artists with the younger generation of artists of the ‘Petit Boulevard’, among whom he counted Guillaumin, Seurat and Gauguin, as well as Bernard, Anquetin, Angrand, Toulouse-Lautrec, Signac, Lucien Pissarro and himself.

facts.said: He’ll probably come to Paris for the Salon, and wants to tour Holland to see the museums.
facts.note: Mourier-Petersen went to Paris around 22 May. The Salon in 1888 ran from 1 May to mid-July. He stayed in Paris for almost three months, and then spent November and December 1888 in the Netherlands. See Larsson 1993, p. 29.

facts.said: Congratulations on buying the Seurat
facts.note: At the Pillet sale in Paris (Hôtel Drouot, 2 and 3 March 1888; Lugt 1938-1987, no. 47127) Theo had bought a drawing by Georges Seurat for 16 francs; it was Woman singing in a café-chantant, 1887 (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 424. See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 1999, p. 179. It emerges from a letter from Lucien Pissarro to his father Camille of 12 March 1888 that Theo was not at the sale in person, but got Emile Bernard to buy the drawing for him: ‘he had young Bernard buy the drawing that Seurat had put in the sale, it fetched very little, because you know how stingy he is, he wasn’t there, otherwise I would…

facts.said: I’ve made the acquaintance of a Danish artist
facts.note: The Danish painter Christian Vilhelm Mourier-Petersen was in Arles from about 10 October 1887 to around 22 May 1888, apart from a brief stay in Martigues at the end of March 1888. On 16 March 1888 he wrote about meeting Van Gogh: ‘Initially I considered him to be mad, but by and by I note that there is method in it. He knows the friends of Jastrau: McKnight, Russell etc. – but at the moment I can’t remember his name: Van Prut or something of the kind.’ See Larsson 1993, pp. 14, 26.

facts.said: I find what you write about the Lançon sale and the painter’s mistress very interesting.
facts.note: The Lançon sale is the auction of the estate of the artist, who had died in 1885: Tableaux, dessins, aquarelles, sculptures et eaux-fortes. Oeuvres de Auguste Lançon, Paris (Hôtel Drouot), 5-6 March 1888 (Lugt 1938-1987, no. 47131). No information about Lançon’s mistress has been found.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 도개교와 빨래하는 여인들을 그린 작품 등 아를에 온 뒤 완성한 12점의 습작을 테오에게 알리며, 원근틀을 활용한 작업 방식에 자부심을 보인다. 몸이 아직 완전히 회복되지 않았지만 덴마크 화가 무리에 페테르센과의 교류를 즐기고 있으며, 아를이 마치 일본에 온 듯한 느낌을 준다고 감격한다. 브로델 인근에서 목격한 살인 사건 재판과 이탈리아인 추방 소동을 전하는 한편, 건강이 나빠진 고갱의 처지를 걱정하며 편지를 맺는다.
entries.why: The letter was written after 11 March, the date two Zouaves were murdered in Arles (see n. 8). As Van Gogh writes (ll. 91-95), many Italians were hounded out of town over the next few days because of this. The letter must therefore date from a few days after the crime. Van Gogh also refers to the fact that Koning has moved in with Theo (ll. 37-40). This must have been shortly after 14 March (FR b915).

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing, The
works.said: As far as work goes, I brought home a no.15 canvas today, it’s a drawbridge, with a little carriage going across it, outlined against a blue sky — the river blue as well, the banks orange with greenery, a group of washerwomen wearing blouses and multicoloured bonnets.

works.title: The Gleize Bridge over the Vigueirat Canal
works.said: And another landscape with a little rustic bridge and washerwomen as well.

works.title: Avenue of Plane Trees near Arles Station
works.said: Lastly an avenue of plane trees near the station.

works.title: Landscape with Snow
works.said: 12 studies altogether since I’ve been here.

works.title: Still Life: Potatoes in a Yellow Dish
works.said: 12 studies altogether since I’ve been here.

works.title: View of a Butcher's Shop
works.said: 12 studies altogether since I’ve been here.

works.title: An Old Woman of Arles
works.said: 12 studies altogether since I’ve been here.

works.title: Snowy Landscape with Arles in the Background
works.said: 12 studies altogether since I’ve been here.

facts.said: I attended the inquiry into a crime committed at the door of a brothel here; two Italians killed two Zouaves.
facts.note: At eleven o’clock in the evening of 11 March the Zouaves Louis-Edouard Dupont and Jean Destanque were stabbed to death when leaving a brothel in rue des Récollets after a row with three Italian labourers. This brothel, the ‘maison de tolérance’ no. 14 on the corner of the rue du Bout d’Arles and rue des Récollets, must have been the one that Van Gogh visited. See Murphy 2016, pp. 60-61, 270 (n. 8). The investigation of the crime (and hence also Van Gogh’s brothel visit) took place in the afternoon of Monday, 12 March. See further n. 11 below.

facts.said: The crowd almost (the southerner, following Tartarin’s example, being braver in good intentions than in action), the crowd, I’m telling you, almost lynched the murderers locked up in the town hall, but its revenge was that all the Italians, men and women, including the young chimney-sweeps, had to leave the town under duress.
facts.note: The local newspapers L’Homme de Bronze and Le Forum Républicain reported on the occurrence at length in their editions of Sunday, 18 March. L’Intransigeant of 19 March 1888 also covered it. The incident brought the whole town of Arles up in arms. When the offenders were rounded up, the buildings where they were locked up were besieged by a crowd of angry inhabitants. They also drove virtually all the Italians out of the town, prompted in part by anger that they took a lot of jobs while there was high unemployment among the local population.

facts.said: You’ll do well to go and see Signac at his place.
facts.note: In 1888 Signac lived at 130 boulevard de Clichy, where he also had his studio. Theo could have visited him there, or it might have been in his mother’s house in Asnières, where Signac often received his friends.

facts.said: I took advantage of the opportunity to go into one of the brothels in the little street called ‘des Récollets’.
facts.note: Rue des Récollets opened off rue de la Cavalerie, where Van Gogh’s boarding-house was.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 아를의 맑은 대기와 화사한 색채가 일본처럼 아름답다고 감탄하며, 인상파 예술이 프랑스에서 일본 미술의 정신을 이어가고 있다고 말한다. 퐁타벤보다 생활비가 비싸다고 아쉬워하면서도 여러 화가가 함께 지내면 비용을 절감할 수 있으리라 기대한다. 도개교와 빨래하는 여인들을 그린 습작을 언급하며 근황을 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent sent this letter off with one to Theo dating from Wednesday, 21 or Thursday, 22 March (letter 588). It emerges from letter 585 of about 16 March that Van Gogh planned to write the present letter the following Sunday, the day of the week that he often set aside for his correspondence. Since there is no reason to believe that he departed from that plan, and lacking any other clues, we have dated the letter Sunday, 18 March 1888.

works.title: Two Lovers (Fragment)
works.said: At the top of this letter I’m sending you a little croquis of a study that’s preoccupying me as to how to make something of it — sailors coming back with their sweethearts towards the town, which projects the strange silhouette of its drawbridge against a huge yellow sun.

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing, The
works.said: I have another study of the same drawbridge with a group of washerwomen.

facts.said: The stretches of water make patches of a beautiful emerald and a rich blue in the landscapes, as we see it in the Japanese prints.
facts.note: Although strictly speaking a ‘crépon’ is a woodcut printed on crepe paper or crepe fabric, Van Gogh uses the term for Japanese prints in general, which he also calls ‘Japonaiseries’. He and Theo had built up a collection in Paris, and later he repeatedly urged his brother to acquire new ones. See for their collection of Japanese prints: cat. Amsterdam 1991. In July 1888 Van Gogh wrote to Theo telling him that he had introduced Bernard and Anquetin to Japanese graphic art (letter 642). It was a major influence on the new style that Anquetin and Bernard developed, Cloisonnism. Cf. letter 575, n. 7.

facts.said: One would need to know the local patois, and know how to eat bouillabaisse and aïoli,
facts.note: Bouillabaisse is a regional fish soup served with garlic-flavoured mayonaise (aïoli).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오에게 베르나르와 로트레크에게 전할 편지를 동봉하며, 테르스테흐가 답장을 하지 않는 것에 대해 강경하게 대응할 것을 촉구한다. 고갱의 궁핍한 처지를 전하고, 모파상의 소설과 플로베르의 문장론을 언급하며 예술가의 과장할 자유에 대해 논한다. 생트로핌 성당의 고딕 문과 아를의 이국적 풍물들이 마치 다른 세계처럼 느껴진다고 묘사한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he has read about the snow in Paris in L’Intransigeant. These reports were in this newspaper on 20 and 21 March. We can tell from his comment about the rain and wind in the last few days (l. 32) that the letter cannot have been written before 21 March, because this was the only day when rain was reported during this period (Météo-France). We have therefore dated the letter Wednesday, 21 or Thursday, 22 March 1888.

works.title: Two Lovers (Fragment)
works.said: Rain and wind these past few days, I’ve worked at home on the study of which I’ve made a croquis in Bernard’s letter.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: However, it’s not a bad idea for a journalist to advise General Boulanger to put the secret police off the scent by henceforth wearing rose-tinted spectacles, which in his opinion would go better with the General’s beard.
facts.note: General Georges Boulanger was the leader of the ultra-nationalist party (Boulangists). In 1886 he was appointed War Minister in the Freycinet cabinet. In 1888, however, he was dismissed, partly because of his inflammatory language towards Germany. He was stripped of his powers and ordered not to leave Clermont-Ferrand. The background to Van Gogh’s remark about ‘rose-tinted spectacles’ is not clear; he is responding to something Theo had written.

facts.said: Must I tell the truth and add that the Zouaves, the brothels, the adorable little Arlésiennes going off to make their first communion,
facts.note: The first communion of Catholic children had taken place shortly before, on 18 March. See Merlhès 1989, p. 260.

facts.said: It’s beautiful — have you read the preface explaining the freedom the artist has to exaggerate, to create in a novel a more beautiful, simpler, more consoling nature,
facts.note: Guy de Maupassant’s novel Pierre et Jean (1888) had come out in January 1888. It is a Naturalist story about a family that falls apart because of the jealousy and rivalry between the two brothers Pierre and Jean. Maupassant prefaced his novel with an essay titled ‘The Novel’ (‘Le roman’), in which he argues that every literary work should be judged according to the extent that the author has succeeded in realizing his objectives.

facts.said: You’ve had plenty of snow in Paris, from what our friend L’Intransigeant tells us.
facts.note: The political daily L’Intransigeant, founded in 1880 by Henri Rochefort, had been the organ of General Boulanger’s radical-nationalist party since 1887. There were reports on 20 and 21 March (both times on p. 2) about the problems that the snow was causing in Paris: the traffic was disrupted and people were hurt because of the icy conditions; the city was said to look like St Petersburg.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테르스티흐가 보낸 우호적인 답장에 크게 기뻐하며, 몽티첼리의 꽃 그림과 자신들이 소장한 꽃다발 그림을 비교하며 그 가치를 설명한다. 살구나무 과수원을 그렸고 다리와 노을 습작은 어려움을 겪었다고 전하며, 앵데팡당전 출품과 관련해 캔버스 서명을 '반고흐'가 아닌 '빈센트'로 표기해달라고 요청한다. 레이드와의 관계가 틀어진 것에 대한 아쉬움도 언급된다.
entries.why: Van Gogh confirms the receipt of 50 francs. The letter must date from after 22 March 1888 because this was when the Indépendants exhibition opened (ll. 89-93; cf. also nn. 13 and 14). He received the next instalment on or about 1 April (see letter 591); we therefore date the present letter on or about Sunday, 25 March 1888.

works.title: Two Lovers (Fragment)
works.said: Had some trouble with the sunset with figures and a bridge that I was talking to Bernard about.

works.title: The Langlois bridge
works.said: However, I started the same subject again immediately afterwards on another canvas, but as the weather was quite different, in a grey palette and without figures.

works.title: The Seine with the Pont de Clichy
works.said: I hope you’ll send him Gauguin’s fine seascape.

works.title: Old Man with his Head in his Hands ("At Eternity's Gate")
works.said: When I write to Russell myself, I’ll talk about his paintings and I’ll ask him to do an exchange with me,

works.title: Grass and Butterflies
works.said: That one, or the butterflies

works.title: Green Ears of Wheat
works.said: That one, or the butterflies or the field of poppies

works.title: Orchard in Blossom
works.said: I’ve just done a clump of apricot trees in a little fresh green orchard.

works.title: The pink orchard
works.said: I’ve just done a clump of apricot trees in a little fresh green orchard.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: When I write to Russell myself, I’ll talk about his paintings and I’ll ask him to do an exchange with me,
facts.note: This exchange was discussed several times between March and July 1888, but does not seem to have gone ahead. Van Gogh had probably already exchanged work with Russell in Paris; see letter 569, n. 13. Russell’s Vincent van Gogh and the Seated female nude that has meanwhile been attributed to him (both Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum) may have been obtained by way of exchange. Russell owned two paintings by Van Gogh – only one of which, Shoes (F 332 / JH 1234), can now be identified – and one lithograph, ‘At eternity’s gate’ (F 1662 / JH 268). See cat. Amsterdam 2011.

facts.said: If we do the 3 permanent exhibitions, we’d need a large Seurat
facts.note: A few hours before he left for Arles, on 19 February 1888, Vincent went with Theo to Seurat’s studio (see letter 695) at 128bis boulevard de Clichy. Models and A Sunday afternoon on the island of La Grande Jatte were probably among the large canvases they saw there; Van Gogh mentions them both in letter 710.

facts.said: I hope you’ll send him Gauguin’s fine seascape.
facts.note: See for Gauguin’s The beach at Dieppe : letter 582, n. 5. Tersteeg had asked Theo to send him a number of ‘modern’ paintings (see letter 592). At the end of March 1888 Theo sent a consignment to the Hague branch. It contained one work each by Degas, Monet, Sisley, Camille Pissarro, Guillaumin, Gauguin, Van Gogh (The Seine with the Clichy bridge (F 303 / JH 1323), after which is the letter sketch of the same name F - / JH 1324; see n. 9 below) and Toulouse-Lautrec, and two by Monticelli. See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 1999, p. 81.

facts.said: If you happen to feel that way, you could tell Tersteeg that I myself think I have a better chance of sales in Holland with the studies of nature in the south, and that when Tersteeg comes to Paris in May he’ll find a consignment with some subjects from down here.
facts.note: Tersteeg’s trip to Paris took place a little later, in the first half of June: see letter 625.

facts.said: That — I’m referring to the painting at the Delarebeyrettes’
facts.note: In the 1880s François Joseph Delarebeyrette’s gallery was located at 43 rue de Provence in Paris. He was the leading dealer in Monticelli’s work. After his death in September 1886, his wife and his son Gabriel took over the running of the business. Theo and Reid regularly bought work by Monticelli there. See Fowle 2000, p. 94, and Nonne 2000, p. 42. We do not know which of Monticelli’s flower pieces Van Gogh had seen at Delarebeyrette’s; in 1886 the gallery had some forty works by Monticelli in stock. See Alauzen and Ripert 1969, p. 447.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 아를의 자연이 매우 아름답다고 전하며, 만발한 과수원 그림들과 무브에게 선물할 '무브를 추억하며'라는 작품을 소개한다. 졸라와 모파상의 문학, 로티의 소설을 언급하며 오늘날 회화는 북부의 무브식 회색 팔레트가 아니라 하늘색·분홍·주황 등 강렬한 색채를 요구한다고 설명한다. 일본 판화와 바그너 음악을 예로 들어 색채의 조화와 강렬함이 공존할 수 있음을 이야기하고, 여동생의 생일 선물로 꽃과 책이 있는 소품을 준비하겠다고 약속한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh thanks his sister for her letter with ‘good wishes’ from her and from their mother (ll. 3-4); these relate to his birthday, which was on 30 March. Since he replied ‘immediately upon receipt’ (ll. 2-3), we have dated the present letter on or about Friday, 30 March 1888.

works.title: Blossoming Almond Branch in a Glass with a Book
works.said: Vincent For my part I must also wish you a happy birthday — since I’d like to give you something of my work that you’ll like I’ll set aside a little study of a book and a flower

works.title: Still Life with French novels and glass with a rose
works.said: Vincent For my part I must also wish you a happy birthday — since I’d like to give you something of my work that you’ll like I’ll set aside a little study of a book and a flower for you — in a large format with a whole mass of books with pink, yellow, green covers and fiery red — my painting Parisian novels was the same subject.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: Now here, for instance, at this moment, I have 6 paintings of blossoming fruit trees.

works.title: Apricot Trees in Blossom
works.said: Now here, for instance, at this moment, I have 6 paintings of blossoming fruit trees.

works.title: Orchard in Blossom, Bordered by Cypresses

works.title: Orchard with Peach Trees in Blossom
works.said: Now here, for instance, at this moment, I have 6 paintings of blossoming fruit trees.

works.title: Orchard in Blossom

works.title: Flowering orchard, surrounded by cypress
works.said: Now here, for instance, at this moment, I have 6 paintings of blossoming fruit trees.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: My dear sister, So as not to let your letter go unanswered I’m writing immediately upon receipt of your letter and Ma’s and the good wishes from you both.
facts.note: Willemien and Mrs van Gogh wrote to Vincent on the occasion of his thirty-fifth birthday on 30 March.

facts.said: By next year — when the World Exhibition will be held
facts.note: The World Exhibition was staged in Paris from 5 May to 5 November 1889. Van Gogh, like his artist friends, wanted to take advantage of the enormous influx of visitors and show work during this period.

facts.said: And the one I brought home today would possibly appeal to you — it’s a dug-over patch of ground in an orchard, a wicker fence and two peach trees in full bloom, pink against a sparkling blue sky with white clouds and in sunshine.
facts.note: The work that Van Gogh earmarked for Mauve’s widow was Pink peach trees (‘Souvenir de Mauve’) (F 394/ JH 1379); he sent it to Theo in May 1888 with his first batch of paintings. See letters 583 and 608. It emerges from letter 719 that Jet Mauve did receive the painting.

facts.said: And something happens like with the Wagner music which, performed by a large orchestra, is no less intimate for that.
facts.note: Richard Wagner composed large-scale, ambitious operas for big orchestras. Van Gogh had been to performances of Wagner in Paris. Theo wrote to Willemien about it: ‘And before Vincent left I went to a couple of Wagner concerts with him and we both enjoyed them very much’ (FR b915, 14 March 1888).

facts.said: I’ve written on it Souvenir de Mauve Vincent & Theo
facts.note: Van Gogh added the sentence ‘You may ... Theo’ later, after he had written the postscript. The words ‘& Theo’ cannot now be seen on the painting. Vincent probably removed them at Theo’s insistence, because it was done before the canvas was completely dry. See cat. Otterlo 2003, pp. 212-213.

entries.summary: 반 고흐는 복숭아나무 과수원을 그린 대작을 완성한 뒤, 세상을 떠난 화가 안톤 마우버를 기리며 그림에 '마우버를 추억하며'라는 헌사를 적어 그의 부인에게 보내자고 제안한다. 죽은 이도 산 자의 기억 속에 살아 있다는 시구를 인용하며 애도의 감정을 전한다. 또한 화상 알렉산더 레이드의 처신에 불만을 표하며, 테르스테흐가 영국에서의 인상파 전시를 주도해야 한다고 강하게 주장한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for his letter and the enclosed money. This must have been the allowance of about Sunday, 1 April, since he tells Theo that he had recently received a letter from Willemien, to which he had replied immediately with letter 590 of about 30 March; the present letter must therefore have been written later. We have consequently dated it on or about Sunday, 1 April 1888.

works.title: The Seine with the Pont de Clichy
works.said: Am very pleased that your consignment goes off on Monday and after all, perhaps also because there’s a canvas of mine in it.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: 20 canvas in the open air in an orchard — ploughed lilac field, a reed fence — two pink peach trees against a glorious blue and white sky.

works.title: Orchard in Blossom
works.said: In addition to that I now have another 4 or 5 studies of orchards

works.title: Apricot Trees in Blossom
works.said: In addition to that I now have another 4 or 5 studies of orchards

works.title: Peach Tree in Blossom
works.said: In addition to that I now have another 4 or 5 studies of orchards

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

people.name: Boussod, Valadon & Cie
people.note: art dealers in Paris, successors of Goupil & Cie

facts.said: I don’t at all like Reid’s way of behaving towards us, it seems funny to me that you and Guillaumin haven’t already arranged to cancel the sale of the painting in question.
facts.note: Reid evidently wanted to buy a work from Guillaumin at a low price, and the latter had complained to Theo (cf. undated letter from Guillaumin to Theo, sale Piasa, Hôtel Drouot, Paris, 20 November 2008, lot 201).

facts.said: Am very pleased that your consignment goes off on Monday and after all, perhaps also because there’s a canvas of mine in it.
facts.note: The consignment to Tersteeg included The Seine with the Clichy bridge (F 303 / JH 1323); it arrived in The Hague on 6 April (see letter 589, n. 4).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 프로방스 과수원의 만개한 봄빛에 열정적으로 몰두하며 작업하는 한편, 네덜란드 지인들에게 헌정할 그림 계획을 구상한다. 안톤 모베를 추모하는 작품을 예트 모베에게, 테르스티흐에게는 도개교와 빨래하는 여인들을 그린 화사한 색채의 그림을 보내기로 한다. 화상 레이드에 대한 실망과 불신도 언급하며, 어머니와 여동생 빌에 대한 그리움이 짙게 묻어난다.
entries.why: In letter 591 of about 1 April, Van Gogh said he hoped to write ‘tomorrow’. Now he says that he wrote letters ‘yesterday’ but tore them up (l. 7). This letter therefore dates from Monday, 2 April at the earliest – and at any rate it follows 591, since Van Gogh goes on about his plan to give Jet Mauve Souvenir de Mauve and about the consignment to Tersteeg. We have therefore dated the present letter on or about Tuesday, 3 April 1888.

works.title: The Langlois Bridge at Arles
works.said: If necessary, the frame can be of blue plush, but it would be better to paint it.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: Let’s suppose, then, that first of all we gave Jet Mauve the Souvenir de Mauve.

works.title: Still Life with Basket of Apples
works.said: Pissarro

works.title: Still Life, Basket of Apples

people.name: Lucien Pissarro
people.note: (1863-1944) French artist, son of Camille Pissarro

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh

facts.said: But it would be a loud and clear reply to certain muffled insinuations treating us more or less as if we were already dead, and a revenge for your trip last year when the welcome they gave you was lacking in warmth &c.
facts.note: A reference to Theo’s stay in the Netherlands in the second half of July 1887. At the time Vincent wrote in a letter to Willemien that Theo’s family and friends in Amsterdam and The Hague had not received him very warmly. He attributed this attitude to ‘professional jealousy’, because Theo was still selling pictures despite the difficult times. See letter 574.

facts.said: Pissarro  and Reid’s one, oranges, foreground white, background blue).
facts.note: Basket of oranges (F 395 / JH 1363) of early March 1888 (see letter 583). Breitner never had this study in his possession, nor was it dedicated to him.

facts.said: If you see Reid again it would be a good idea to tell him we don’t have much confidence in the success of ambitious people and that we prefer to do good work, that we were surprised at his ways of behaving, which in the end were inexplicable, and that since then we no longer know what to think of him.
facts.note: By Reid’s inexplicable behaviour Van Gogh was probably referring to his view that Reid had paid Guillaumin too low a price for a painting. See letter 591.

facts.said: The painting of the garden with lovers is at the Théâtre Libre.
facts.note: The progressive Théâtre Libre in Paris, founded by André Antoine (96 rue Blanche), opened on 30 March 1887. Van Gogh’s Garden with courting couples: square Saint-Pierre (F 314 / JH 1258) hung in the rehearsal room. Seurat and Signac also exhibited there. See exhib. cat. Paris 1988, p. 34.

facts.said: Boyer, the framer, still has a lithograph, the old man with a bald head.
facts.note: The frame maker Jean-Marie Boyer had his shop at 38bis rue Fontaine in Paris (Almanach du commerce de Paris 1887, and AP, Liste électorale 1889, 9e arr.). The lithograph was ‘At eternity’s gate’ (F 1662 / JH 268).

entries.summary: 빈센트가 타세 & 로트 화방에 보낼 물감과 캔버스 주문을 테오에게 상세히 나열하며, 할인 협상과 배송 문제를 꼼꼼히 지시하는 실무적인 편지다. 아를 현지 물감상이 게을러 파리나 마르세유에서 재료를 받기로 했으며, 개화한 과수원을 그릴 시간이 촉박하니 서둘러 물감을 보내달라고 재촉한다. 돈이 거의 없는 상황에서도 최소 10점의 캔버스를 포함한 첫 소포를 준비 중이라며 작업에 대한 열의를 드러낸다.
entries.why: Vincent has meanwhile spent the 50 francs for which he thanked Theo on or about 1 April (letter 591) on paint and canvas (see letter 592); now he says he is broke. In the next letter (594, of 9 April) he thanks Theo for sending 100 francs. He has finished another orchard since he wrote the previous letter (592). The present letter must have been written some time between these two letters; we have therefore dated it on or about Thursday, 5 April 1888.

facts.said: As soon as I can pay for crates and postage (which is probably cheaper at the little station here than it would be at the Gare de Lyon)
facts.note: The station in Paris from which trains for the south depart.

facts.said: I’m quite curious to know what you’ll say about my first consignment, which will definitely contain at least 10 canvases.
facts.note: Van Gogh sent Theo the first batch of paintings from Arles on 7 May; see letter 606, n. 4.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Am obliged to write to you as I’m sending you an order for colours which, if you place it with Tasset & Lhote, rue Fontaine,
facts.note: The artists’ supplies shop run by Guillaume Charles Tasset and his (unidentified) partner Lhote, 31 rue Fontaine-Saint-Georges in Paris.

facts.said: 30 absorbent canvas I painted two on non-absorbent canvas.)
facts.note: See for this absorbent size 30 canvas: letter 594, n. 2. One of the two works on non-absorbent canvas was the ‘new orchard’ that Van Gogh mentions a little later in the letter (the sentence ‘while waiting ... non-absorbent canvas’ (en attendant ... non absorbante) (ll. 81-81a) was added later). We do not know which work this was; all the orchards that are now known have already been mentioned or are referred to later in the correspondence. The other work cannot be identified either.

facts.said: The colourman here
facts.note: Van Gogh probably bought his paint from the grocer and chemist Jules Armand; see letter 583, n. 8.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 남프랑스의 공기가 건강에 도움이 된다고 느끼며 개화기 과수원 연작을 활발히 그리고 있다고 전한다. 투우 구경, 피사로와 쇠라와의 교환 희망, 모브의 죽음에 대한 안타까움 등 다양한 소식을 전하며, 별이 빛나는 밤을 사이프러스나 밀밭과 함께 그리고 싶다는 구상을 밝힌다. 색채와 가치(명암)를 동시에 완벽히 표현할 수 없으며 자신은 색채를 택하겠다는 예술론도 서술한다.
entries.why: The bullfight that Van Gogh had been to ‘yesterday’ took place on Sunday, 8 April (see n. 6). This means that the letter was written on Monday, 9 April 1888.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: A toreador crushed one of his balls jumping over the barrier.
facts.note: The bullfight Van Gogh describes here took place on Sunday, 8 April. We learn from a letter to the editor in Le Forum Républicain that the fight had to be abandoned because the torero, Eugène Hélias, was injured. See Clébert and Richard 1989, p. 72.

facts.said: This is to tell you that you shouldn’t force yourself for no reason — there’s so much to do here, all sorts of studies, that it’s not the same as in Paris, where you can’t sit down wherever you please.
facts.note: Theo wrote to Jo Bonger on 14 February 1889 about the problems Vincent had encountered when painting out of doors in Paris: ‘In Paris he saw masses of things he wanted to paint, but time and again he was prevented from doing so. Models didn’t want to pose for him, he was forbidden to sit and work in the street and because of his volatile disposition this repeatedly led to scenes, which upset him so much that he became completely unapproachable and by the end of it all he’d had more than enough of Paris.’ See Brief happiness 2000, pp. 160-161.

facts.said: Mauve’s death was a rude shock for me.
facts.note: Van Gogh’s first teacher Anton Mauve had died on 5 February 1888.

facts.said: Bravo for Pissarro, he’s right, I think.
facts.note: This was most probably about the falling-out between Camille Pissarro and the collector, amateur artist and pastrycook Eugène Murer, who owned several of Pissarro’s early works. In a letter of 12 March 1888 Pissarro had refused Murer’s offer to dedicate his book Un quart d’heure d’amour to him because their artistic views had meanwhile diverged to such an extent that they could no longer understand each other. Pissarro’s refusal meant an irreversible breach. See Correspondance Pissarro 1980-1991, vol. 2, p. 219 (no. 473).

facts.said: I hope he’ll do an exchange with us one day.
facts.note: There was probably no exchange with Camille Pissarro during Van Gogh’s lifetime, since the only works in the estate are an etching, which the artist gave Theo, the fan he made for Jo (see letter 830) and a small watercolour. In August 1890 Theo exchanged Vincent’s Mulberry tree (F 637 / JH 1796) for a painting by Pissarro. Jo van Gogh-Bonger sold this unidentified work, ‘a no. 10 canvas’, to Ambroise Vollard in 1897. See FR b825, b936 and Account book 2002, pp. 24, 199.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오가 보내준 물감에 감사하며, 강풍 속에서도 자두나무 과수원을 그린 하루를 전한다. 랑글루아 다리 그림을 테르스테흐와 옛 스승의 부인을 위해 반복 제작할 계획을 밝히고, 인상주의가 유행시킨 크롬옐로우·프러시안블루 등 불안정한 색채를 대담하게 써야 한다는 색채론을 델라크루아를 예로 들어 설명한다.
entries.why: The order of letters 595, 596 and 597 can be established on the basis of the descriptions of the progress of the work. It emerges from letter 597 that Van Gogh painted the plum trees first and then turned his attention to the enclosed orchard (the third triptych, as yet at an early stage). In letters 594 and 595 he is still working on the plum trees, but in letter 596 to Bernard he describes the new subject of the enclosed orchard with pear and peach trees.

works.said: This morning I worked on an orchard of plum trees in blossom

facts.said: You were right to tell Tasset that the geranium lake should be included after all, he sent it, I’ve just checked — all the colours that Impressionism has made fashionable are unstable, all the more reason boldly to use them too raw, time will only soften them too much.
facts.note: On the discolouration of red pigments in Van Gogh, see Maarten van Bommel, Muriel Geldof and Ella Hendriks, ‘Examination of the use of organic red pigments in paintings by Vincent van Gogh (November 1885 to February 1888)’, Art matters. Netherlands technical studies in art 3 (2005), pp. 111-137.

facts.said: My dear Theo, It’s awfully good of you to have sent me the complete order of colours,
facts.note: See letter 593 for Van Gogh’s order from Tasset & Lhote in Paris; he had left it up to Theo to place either a limited or a large order.

facts.said: Don’t forget to say hello to him for me if you see him, and tell him that if he’d like any paintings for his shop window he can have some from here, and the best.
facts.note: At this time the paint merchant Julien Tanguy had works by Van Gogh in stock. It emerges from a letter of 29 May 1888 from Gustave Geffroy to Theo that the collector Paul Gallimard wanted to buy two works by Van Gogh from Tanguy (FR b1199).

facts.said: I would really like to have seen the embodiment of Marat you spoke about the other day.
facts.note: It is not clear what this remark relates to. There is possibly a link with the legal proceedings that one of Jacques Louis David’s heirs had instituted against someone who had presented a copy of his famous painting of Marat as the original. See Gazette des Beaux-Arts of 10 March 1888. It is not impossible that the reference is in some way an extension of this topical issue.

facts.said: Who nevertheless is still touching — but in the end it’s not as jolly as Guy de Maupassant’s La Maison Tellier.
facts.note: The novella La Maison Tellier (1881) by Guy de Maupassant describes a day in the life of Madame Tellier, the owner of the brothel Maison Tellier, and her five girls. The ladies set off to attend the first communion of Madame’s niece, they enjoy ordinary everyday life and the festivities, and they go to Mass.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 상상력으로 그림을 그리는 것에 대한 동경과 스스로에 대한 비판을 함께 이야기하며, 별이 빛나는 하늘 같은 것을 상상으로 그려보고 싶다는 바람을 밝힌다. 현재는 만개한 과수원(분홍 복숭아나무, 노란빛 배나무)을 그리고 있으며 자신의 자유분방한 붓질과 단순화된 색채 기법을 설명한다. 아를에서 본 투우 경기의 화려한 군중 풍경도 생생하게 묘사한다.
entries.why: See for our dating of on or about Thursday, 12 April 1888: letter 595, Date.

works.title: Orchard in Blossom, Bordered by Cypresses
works.said: At present I’m busy with the fruit trees in blossom: pink peach trees, yellow-white pear trees.

works.title: Orchard with Peach Trees in Blossom
works.said: At present I’m busy with the fruit trees in blossom: pink peach trees, yellow-white pear trees.

works.title: Flowering orchard, surrounded by cypress
works.said: Here’s a croquis, by the way, the entrance to a Provençal orchard with its yellow reed fences, with its shelter (against the mistral), black cypresses, with its typical vegetables of various greens, yellow lettuces, onions and garlic and emerald leeks.

facts.said: My dear old Bernard, Thanks for your kind letter and the croquis of your decoration included with it, which I find really amusing.
facts.note: No such sketches are known. They would have been for the decoration of the wooden studio that had been built for Bernard in his parents’ garden in Asnières. There may be a connection with the paintings of ‘flowers ... trees ... fields’ mentioned by Van Gogh in letter 696. With thanks to Fred Leeman.

facts.said: Wish you bon voyage
facts.note: Bernard had spent the summers of 1886 and 1887 in Brittany, mainly in Saint-Briac, and was now preparing to go there again. He left for Saint-Briac on 23 April 1888. See Harscoët-Maire 1997, p. 162.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오에게 물감 배송 상태를 점검해달라 부탁하며, 현재 만발한 과수원을 그린 여러 점의 캔버스 작업 진행 상황을 상세히 설명한다. 분홍 복숭아나무, 배나무, 랑글루아 다리 그림 등 9점 규모의 연작을 구상하며 이를 훗날 더 큰 장식화의 밑그림으로 삼겠다는 계획을 밝힌다. 기유맹의 파스텔화 구입과 베르나르가 보낸 소네트에 대한 짧은 언급도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: See for our dating of on or about Friday, 13 April 1888: letter 595, Date.

entries.summary: 러셀에게 보낸 편지로, 아를 인근에서 매크나이트와 덴마크 화가 무리에-피터슨을 만난 근황을 전한다. 화상 레이드의 처신에 실망감을 드러내며 그를 예술가라기보다 장사꾼에 가깝다고 평가한다. 몬티첼리의 색채가 지닌 정열적이고 영원한 가치를 델라크루아의 남프랑스관과 연결지어 옹호하며, 벨라스케스와 고야로 이어지는 색채의 역사를 논한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh remarks that he met Macknight and Mourier-Petersen ‘last Sunday’ (l. 6); that must have been Sunday, 15 April because on 19 April 1888 Macknight mentioned this meeting in a letter to Eugène Boch (see n. 2). Since Van Gogh also writes that it is raining (l. 5) – something he likewise mentioned in his letter to Bernard (see letter 599) – and the weather reports record heavy rain on 19 April 1888 (Météo-France), we have dated the letter that day.

facts.said: Last Sunday I have met Macknight and a Danish painter and I intend to go and see him at Fontvieille next Monday.
facts.note: In 1888 the American artist Dodge Macknight, who Van Gogh had met through Russell in Paris, spent some time in Fontvieille, a village 9 km to the north of Arles. On 19 April 1888 Macknight wrote to Eugène Boch and told him that he had seen Van Gogh in Arles. See exhib. cat. Pontoise 1994, pp. 80, 96 (n. 18). The Danish painter is Christian Mourier-Petersen.

facts.said: My dear Russell, I ought to have answered your letter ever so long ago
facts.note: Van Gogh had received a letter from Russell about a month before; he sent it on to Theo with letter 589.

facts.said: And unvoluntarily thought often of you because you did the same in Sicily.
facts.note: In the late autumn of 1886 Russell left Paris and set off on a six-month trip around Italy, during which he also went to Sicily. One of the studies of trees in blossom he made there is Almond trees and ruins on Sicily , c. 1887 (sale Christie, Manson & Woods, Australia, 6-7 June 1989, p. 71, no. 184).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르의 소네트 시편들을 세심하게 비평하며 언어와 회화 모두 어렵고 가치 있는 예술임을 역설한다. 아를의 흰 꽃, 벚나무 등 여러 과수원 습작을 동시에 진행 중이라 전하고, 일요일에 목격한 사창가의 강렬한 색채 인상도 생생히 묘사한다. 위장병으로 요양 중이지만 알제리로 떠나는 베르나르에게 건강 관리를 당부하며 마르세유에서의 재회를 기약한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes: ‘Unfortunately there’s rain today’ (l. 70). The weather reports record that it rained heavily on Thursday, 19 April (Météo-France), so we have dated the present letter, like letter 598, to that day.

facts.said: There’s the art of lines and colours, but there’s the art of words that will last just the same.
facts.note: In a letter to his parents of 26 April 1888 Bernard wrote that he had found Van Gogh’s letter on his arrival in Saint-Briac on Wednesday, 25 April. He used his reaction as an argument for pursuing his poetic ambitions. ‘On arriving I found a very interesting letter from Vincent which I read and re-read to divert myself, because with the wind that’s blowing, the rain and the cold, the countryside, although very wild, is still really dreary. Vincent congratulates me on my decision about Algeria, and tells me that he will perhaps also go to see me there himself.

facts.said: I now have a terrace for a studio.
facts.note: The covered roof terrace that Van Gogh used as a studio and where he dried his paintings (letter 600) was that of Hotel-Restaurant Carrel (see letter 577, n. 4).

facts.said: Here’s a new orchard, quite simple in composition; a white tree, a small green tree, a square corner of greenery — a lilac field, an orange roof, a big blue sky.
facts.note: The letter sketch – Vincent also sent one to Theo (letter 600) – is based on Orchard with pear trees in blossom (F 406 / JH 1399).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 갈대펜으로 그린 데생 작업과 코닝과의 작품 교환 이야기를 전하며, 테오가 브뤼셀과 네덜란드로 떠나는 소식에 부소&발라동 화랑 내부 갈등을 걱정한다. 개화한 과수원 연작 10점을 완성했다고 알리고, 몽티첼리가 압생트에 찌들어 있었다는 소문에 의문을 제기하며 그의 작품 수준을 옹호한다. 위장이 약해 고생 중이지만 파리에 있을 때보다 건강이 나아졌다고 안심시키며, 동생 코르의 건강 문제도 함께 언급한다.
entries.why: The letter follows letter 599, which was written on Thursday, 19 April. In that one Van Gogh has nine orchards on the go; in the present letter he mentions ten. Both letters include a sketch after Orchard and house with orange roof and a reference to the failed study of a cherry tree. Vincent also says he hopes that Theo will receive this letter before he leaves on Sunday (ll. 144-145), so he must have posted the letter by Saturday at the latest. We have therefore dated it on or about Friday, 20 April 1888.

works.title: Orchard with Arles in the Background
works.said: About the previous letter containing 50 francs, I received it as well, and I also wrote telling you that the day before or two days before I sent the two drawings.

works.said: So these orchards with the Langlois bridge

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing, The
works.said: So these orchards with the Langlois bridge

works.title: Marsh with Water Lilies
works.said: It’s a process I already tried in Holland in the past, but I didn’t have as good reeds there as here.

works.title: The Swamp / Marsh
works.said: It’s a process I already tried in Holland in the past, but I didn’t have as good reeds there as here.

works.title: Apricot Trees in Blossom
works.said: I have 10 orchards now, not counting three small studies and a large one of a cherry tree that I worked to death.

works.title: The white orchard
works.said: I have 10 orchards now, not counting three small studies and a large one of a cherry tree that I worked to death.

works.title: The pink peach tree
works.said: I have 10 orchards now, not counting three small studies and a large one of a cherry tree that I worked to death.

facts.said: Now that was an important piece of news about your trip to Brussels.
facts.note: Later in the letter it says that Theo was planning to go to Brussels ‘this coming Sunday’; this would have been 22 April. He cannot have returned to Paris before 12 May at the earliest, since Vincent had still not had any word from him on that date (letter 609) and thanked him in letter 610 of about 14 May for writing so soon after he got back. It emerges from letter 602 that Theo combined his business trip to Brussels with a visit to his mother and sister Willemien in Breda.

facts.said: What a pity about Cor, let’s hope it’s nothing serious.
facts.note: Apparently Cor, who was employed in an engineering works in Lincoln, was ill or had some other problem. On 18 March his mother had told Theo that she had received good reports about her youngest son (FR b2417). Vincent himself had little contact with him: Cor wrote to Theo from Lincoln on 16 October 1888: ‘How’s Vincent getting on? I never hear anything from him now, except something about he’s going to Algiers or is there ... Don’t think that even though I don’t write often I’ve forgotten you, because in fact you’re my only brother’ (FR b3706).

facts.said: Perhaps that woman from the Limousin, the Roquette lady, has after all put in a bit of her spiteful gossip to plant this legend.
facts.note: By ‘La Roquette’ Van Gogh meant the wife of the art dealer François Joseph Delarebeyrette, who carried on the trade in Monticellis with her son Gabriel after her husband’s death in 1886. Van Gogh refers to the son as ‘Gabriel de la Roquette’ (see letter 625). This must have been a nickname since the woman’s full name was Evelina Delarebeyrette-Lassarre and her son is always referred to in official documents as Gabriel Delarebeyrette. In letter 686 Vincent talks about ‘Madame de Larebey la Roquette’, so we know that he did know her real name; Theo also calls her ‘La Roquette’ (see letter 830).

facts.said: About the previous letter containing 50 francs, I received it as well, and I also wrote telling you that the day before or two days before I sent the two drawings.
facts.note: This letter from Vincent has not survived; he addressed it wrongly and it was returned to him (see letter 601). The drawings he sent must have been quite large given that in letter 601 Van Gogh writes that he is working on a ‘series of pen drawings of which you’ve had the first two, but in a smaller format’ (ll. 40-42). They must therefore be Orchard with Arles in the background (F 1516 / JH 1376) and The white orchard (F 1414 / JH 1385). Both measure approx. 39.5 x 54 cm.

facts.said: Tell me, isn’t Daumier on show at the Beaux-Arts, and Gavarni?
facts.note: Work by Daumier and Gavarni was on show in the exhibition of caricatures in the Ecole des Beaux-Arts in Paris from 17 April. See exhib. cat. Paris 1888, and La Revue Indépendante, no. 19 (May 1888), vol. 7, p. 382.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 부숑발라동 화랑의 태도에 실망하며 인상파가 아직 충분히 인정받지 못하고 있다고 우려한다. 이에 그림 대신 펜 드로잉 작업으로 전환했고, 하숙집의 부당한 요금 문제로 거처를 옮길 계획을 밝힌다. 마르세유로 이주해 바다 풍경 연작을 그리고 인상파를 위한 전시 공간을 마련하고 싶다는 구상도 전한다.
entries.why: This letter was written after letter 600 of about 20 April 1888, since the question of the letter that had not reached Theo raised in that one has meanwhile been resolved (ll. 1*-6). The remark in the postscript about the expected financial straits at the end of the month tells us that there were certainly still a few more days to go before the end of April.

works.title: Orchard with Arles in the Background
works.said: As for me, I immediately stopped doing paintings and I’ve carried on with a series of pen drawings of which you’ve had the first two, but in a smaller format.

people.name: Boussod, Valadon & Cie
people.note: art dealers in Paris, successors of Goupil & Cie

facts.said: That being so I’m repeating for you what was in the letter — what was new — the visit by Macknight, Russell’s friend, who came back last Sunday by the way.
facts.note: Van Gogh’s first meeting with Macknight in Arles was most probably on Sunday, 15 April (see letter 598), so ‘last Sunday’ must have been 22 April.

facts.said: I don’t now think that I’ll benefit from staying where I am,
facts.note: Van Gogh rented a room from Carrel in rue Amédée-Pichot (see letter 577, n. 4).

facts.said: I had — in a moment of distraction — a classic case — addressed it rue de Laval instead of rue Lepic.
facts.note: Rue Laval was Theo’s previous address in Paris: see letter 218.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 이가 아파 고생하면서도 펜 드로잉 여러 점을 완성했다고 전하며, 훗날 노란 집으로 불릴 건물의 오른쪽 동을 월세 15프랑에 얻었다고 알린다. 외벽은 노랗고 내부는 흰색으로 칠해져 캔버스를 밝은 곳에서 볼 수 있게 됐다며 기뻐하고, 베르나르와 고갱을 초대해 함께 작업할 구상을 내비친다. 건강 문제와 생활비 절약 계획도 함께 이야기한다.
entries.why: Vincent reports that he has rented the Yellow House ‘today’ (l. 21); we can assume that the tenancy started on the first day of the month. He wishes Theo a happy birthday, which was 1 May (ll. 167-168 and 231), and he thanks him for sending his allowance, so we have dated the letter Tuesday, 1 May 1888.

works.said: 30 canvas that I hope will be better than the others.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: It will seem funny to you that the water closet is at the neighbour’s, in quite a large house that belongs to the same owner.
facts.note: The Service du cadastre (land register) in Arles lists one Aimé Verdier, ‘propriétaire à Milhaud (Gard)’ as the owner of lot numbers 398 and 399 from 1858 to 1910. The ‘Maison Verdier’ was all of 2, place Lamartine as well as the large building behind. When Van Gogh lived at 2 place Lamartine, it was no longer owned by Aimé Verdier, who had died in 1872. The house had passed on to his daughter, Marie Louise Verdier, and her husband, Raymond Triare-Brun. See Murphy 2016, p. 273 (n. 13).

facts.said: I’ve rented it for 15 francs a month.
facts.note: Van Gogh rented the right-hand side of this house, shown in the small sketch and to become known as the Yellow House, from 1 May. It was at number 2 place Lamartine, on the northern edge of the city (lot 398). Ill. 2180. He set up his studio in it, but did not start living there until September, once the house had been redecorated and furnished. He officially registered himself at this address on 16 October 1888 (FR b2949 and cf. letter 677). There is a floor plan on blue paper, showing the layout in 1922, made by Léon Ramser (FR b3317). Ill. 2181. See for old photographs of the Yellow House: Dorn 1990, ills.

facts.said: In fact, Bernard writes me that he too has a whole house, but he has it for nothing.
facts.note: Bernard stayed in Saint-Briac in Brittany from 25 April until about 10 August. See letter 664, n. 2. He lived in a small house attached to the inn run by Mrs Lemasson. He wrote to his parents on 26 April 1888: ‘I’ve got my old house, where I’ve settled in, I do as I please. The garden, the first and second floors and the attic are entirely at my disposal.’ (J’ai eu mon ancienne maison où je suis installé, je fais ce que je veux. Le jardin, tout le premier, le deuxième, le grenier sont à ma disposition.) See Harscoët-Maire 1997, pp. 163, 181 (n. 6).

facts.said: Perhaps Gauguin will come to the south.
facts.note: This is the first time Vincent raises the possibility of sharing a studio with Gauguin, who at this point was in Pont-Aven in Brittany. The idea, mentioned in passing, was to take more definite form in the coming months and became a recurrent theme in the letters. Eventually Gauguin stayed in the Yellow House from the end of October to the end of December.

facts.said: I’m inclined to believe she’s the psychological reason for his coming back.
facts.note: Theo must have written that Reid was back in Paris. Soon after the end of March 1888 Reid went to Scotland with a painting by Puvis de Chavannes that he had bought at Durand-Ruel’s in March. The work was exhibited at the Glasgow International Exhibition, which opened on 3 May 1888. See Fowle 1993, p. 12.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 침대 마련 문제와 아틀리에에서 지내는 것의 경제적 이점을 이야기하며, 맥나이트를 방문한 일과 초상화 작업에 대한 포부를 전한다. 건강 회복과 정착에 필요한 비용을 계산하며, 파리를 떠난 후의 신경증과 우울, 그리고 몽티첼리처럼 살고 싶지만 그럴 힘이 없다는 자기 성찰을 길게 풀어놓는다. 누이 빌레미나의 사례를 들어 가족의 신경증적 기질에 대해서도 이야기한다.
entries.why: In the previous letter (602), which dates from 1 May, Van Gogh says he wants to go and look for furniture for his house ‘today or tomorrow morning’. In the present letter he wrote that he had been to see furniture dealers ‘yesterday’ (ll. 1*-2). Since Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave the date as 4 May in Brieven 1914, and she may have had a postmark to go on, we have dated the letter Friday, 4 May 1888.

people.name: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez
Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh

facts.said: I had a postcard from Koning to say he’d received a letter to collect the paintings from the Independents.
facts.note: This question is clarified to some extent in letter 605, where we learn that the organizers of the Indépendants exhibition had announced that the paintings that had been submitted had to be collected on 5 and 6 May (the exhibition closed on 3 May); Koning, however, had misunderstood, and thought that it was 5 and 6 April. See for the exhibited works: letter 582, n. 9.

facts.said: Having no need at all now of space at the hotel, since I have the studio elsewhere, I’ll tell the people it’s 3 francs a day, take it or leave it.
facts.note: Van Gogh was staying in Hotel-Restaurant Carrel: see letter 577, n. 4. The hotel owner had complained that Van Gogh’s paintings took up too much room (letter 601).

facts.said: I think Gruby’s
facts.note: David Gruby, who lived at 66 rue Saint-Lazare in Paris, was a well-known homeopathic doctor whom Theo and Vincent consulted. They knew him through Andries Bonger, who had been a patient of his since March 1882 (FR b1697). Gruby was known as a ‘psychological doctor’, who believed that health revolved around equilibrium and regarded illness as the consequence of a disturbance of the balance. See L. le Leu, Le Dr Gruby. Notes et souvenirs. Paris 1908.

facts.said: Take our sister Wil, she has neither drunk nor led a wild life, and yet we know a photograph of her in which she has the look of a madwoman.
facts.note: In the estate there are various photographs of Willemien at about 20 years old; Van Gogh may have had one of these portraits in mind. Ill. 2183 and Ill. 3113. It is difficult to say how old she is in these photographs, but judging by Van Gogh’s remark the second is the most likely. Later Willemien actually did go mad; she died in an asylum in 1941.

facts.said: Now I’ve thought that perhaps — if Koning were to leave after seeing the Salon, as I believe was his original intention, after he left you could send me the bed he’s occupying now.
facts.note: Koning, who was lodging with Theo in Paris, went back to the Netherlands on 30 May. See letter 616, n. 4.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 스튜디오에 매트리스만 놓고 여름을 나겠다는 실용적 계획을 전하며, 아를 여성들의 아름다움과 그 안에서 프라고나르나 르누아르 같은 화가가 그릴 법한 소재를 발견한다고 말한다. 모네가 풍경화에서 이룬 것을 인물화에서 해낼 미래의 화가상을 상상하며, 로댕은 색채가로서는 부족하다고 평한다. 레이드와의 불화 경위를 설명하고, 화상으로서의 야심이 예술가적 기질을 압도한다고 비판하며, 마크나이트와 드흐룩스 등 지인들에 대한 근황도 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh returns to his previous communication about buying a bed: ‘I’m writing you another line’ (ll. 1*-2), and says, as he does in letter 603 which dates from 4 May, that he saw Macknight ‘yesterday’ (l. 110). We have therefore also dated the present letter Friday, 4 May 1888. In Brieven 1914 Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave the date as 5 May, probably on the basis of a postmark – however, this showed the date the letter was posted.

facts.said: But that’s no reason, is it, to try to use that success to run the French down?
facts.note: See for the Théâtre Libre: letter 592, n. 17. Van Gogh must be referring to the production of Tolstoy’s La puissance des ténèbres which ran there from 10 February until mid-March and was a major success. See André Antoine, Mes souvenirs sur le Théâtre Libre. Paris 1921, pp. 85-89. Gustave Kahn had written about this play in La Revue Indépendante no. 17 (March 1888), vol. 6, pp. 433-441, and there had been an enthusiastic review of the performance in Revue des Deux Mondes 58 (15 March 1888), 3rd series, vol. 86, pp. 426-450.

facts.said: It’s quite possible that as far as houses go I’ll find an even better one, either at Martigues, beside the sea,
facts.note: Martigues is about 55 km to the south-east of Arles on the Mediterranean. Mourier-Petersen (referred to later in the letter as ‘the Dane’), who spent a short time in Martigues at the end of March 1888, may have given Van Gogh this idea. See Larsson 1993, p. 17.

entries.summary: 반 고흐는 라마르틴 광장의 집(노란 집)을 연 200프랑에 임대해 살림을 꾸리기 시작했다고 테오에게 알린다. 여관 생활을 청산하고 자기 집을 갖게 된 기쁨을 전하며, 미스트랄 속에서 그린 드로잉들을 소개한다. 이 지역의 자연을 일본 미술에 비유하며, 언젠가 다른 화가들도 이곳에 모여들기를 바란다는 소망을 밝힌다.
entries.why: Van Gogh thanks Theo for the weekly allowance; as a rule we would date this on or about Sunday, but because he writes that the weather had turned fine after a period of the mistral (ll. 48-52) and this improvement in the weather set in on Monday, 7 May 1888, we have dated the letter that day (Météo-France).

people.name: Anthon Gerard Alexander, ridder van Rappard

facts.said: Is the suburb and the countryside beyond the Colonne du Congrès called Schaarbeek?
facts.note: The ‘Colonne de la Constitution’ (or ‘Colonne du Congrès’) erected in 1859 on the place du Congrès on rue Royale, which in turn opens into the said boulevard du Jardin Botanique.

facts.said: But there should be at least 2 letters that I wrote to you in Paris
facts.note: These were letters 602, 603 and 604, the latter two of which may have been sent together.

facts.said: You’ll see beautiful things at Claude Monet’s.
facts.note: Monet, who had worked in Antibes in the spring, had been back in Giverny since 6 May. See Wildenstein and Walter 1974-1991, vol. 3, p. 9. Theo mounted a small exhibition of Monets (see letter 625, n. 5). His visit to Monet must have taken place in May, given that the exhibition opened at the beginning of June. See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 1999, pp. 111, 187.

facts.said: I also have 40 francs to pay at the hotel,
facts.note: Van Gogh was staying at Hotel-Restaurant Carrel; see letter 577, n. 4.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 묵고 있던 호텔과 숙박비 문제로 다투게 되어 곤경에 처했음을 테오에게 전하며 매트리스 구입 자금을 부탁한다. 브르타뉴로 간 베르나르와 고갱보다 생활비가 더 든다며 속상해하지만 건강이 나아지고 있어 낙담하지는 않는다고 밝힌다. 그동안 그린 습작들을 담은 상자를 테오에게 보내며 작업실 생활로 전환할 계획을 알린다.
entries.why: The letter was written immediately after letter 605: the matter of sending work raised in that one is discussed again in the present letter. As is clear from ll. 1-2, the letter must have been written on the same day as the previous one, so we have likewise dated it Monday, 7 May 1888.

works.title: Path Through a Field with Willows
works.said: There’s a small landscape with a tumbledown house in white, red, green and a cypress beside it — you have the drawing of it and I painted it entirely at home.

works.title: Landscape with Snow
works.said: I’m sending you now in the crate all the studies I have, apart from a few I destroyed, but I’m not signing them all, and there are a dozen that I’ve taken off their stretching frames and there are 14 on stretching frames.
