facts.said: And that means I daren’t buy my mattress and I’ll also have to sleep at another hotel.
facts.note: Van Gogh stayed at Café de la Gare, 30 place Lamartine, until 17 September, when he took up residence in the Yellow House. The proprietors of the café were Joseph Ginoux and his wife Marie. We learn from letters 656 and 691 that Van Gogh was staying in this café.

facts.said: There’s a small landscape with a tumbledown house in white, red, green and a cypress beside it — you have the drawing of it and I painted it entirely at home.
facts.note: The painting is Landscape with a path and pollard willows (F 407 / JH 1402); the drawing that served as the example for the painting, Landscape with a path and pollard willows (F 1499 / JH 1372), dated March 1888 by Van Gogh, was probably in the first batch of drawings sent to Theo at the end of April. See letter 602.

facts.said: I had explained all this business to you in the letters that are still in Paris.
facts.note: These were letters 602, 603 and 604, of which the latter two may have been sent together.

facts.said: I’m sending you now in the crate all the studies I have, apart from a few I destroyed, but I’m not signing them all, and there are a dozen that I’ve taken off their stretching frames and there are 14 on stretching frames.
facts.note: This first consignment of at least 26 paintings from Arles must in any event have included the twelve studies referred to in letter 585, with the exception of Landscape with snow (F 290 / JH 1360), which Van Gogh kept for the moment (see letter 611, n. 4). Those studies were: [1] The Langlois bridge with washerwomen (F 397 / JH 1368), [2] The Gleize bridge with washerwomen (F 396 / JH 1367), [3] Avenue of plane trees (F 398 / JH 1366), [4] An old woman of Arles (F 390 / JH 1357), [5] View of a butcher’s shop (F 389 / JH 1359), [6] Landscape with snow (F 391 / JH 1358), [7] Sprig of almond blossom in a glass (F…

entries.summary: 빈센트는 숙소 문제로 밀린 청구서를 갚느라 수중에 15프랑밖에 남지 않았다며 테오에게 급히 송금을 요청하는 다급한 편지를 쓴다. 외국인이라는 이유로 바가지를 쓴 상황에 분개하면서도, 자신만의 오래 쓸 화실을 마련해 동료 화가와 함께 쓰겠다는 계획을 밝힌다. 분홍빛 과수원과 랑글루아 다리 그림 등을 자신의 빚을 갚는 방식으로 여겨달라며, 언젠가 이 그림들의 가치가 크게 오를 것이라는 확신을 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes that the crate with the first consignment of paintings will go off ‘today’ (l. 36); in his previous letter, of 7 May, he said he had wanted to send it, but had not yet got that far (letter 606). In his letter of 12 May he reports that the consignment has actually been sent (letter 609), and the weather reports confirm what he says in the present letter: ‘the weather’s beautiful’ (ll. 21-22) – from 7 to 10 May it was hot and there was little wind (Météo-France).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여관 숙박비 분쟁으로 힘든 상황 속에서 짐을 되찾기 위해 청구서를 완납했다고 전하며, 이 일을 계기로 독립된 작업실을 마련하기로 결심했다고 알린다. 옛 모브 부인과 테르스티흐에게 바친 그림, 과수원 연작 등을 담은 상자를 보냈다고 설명하며 액자 색상에 대한 세세한 지시도 덧붙인다.
entries.why: The crate with the first consignment of paintings is going off ‘this evening’ (l. 67); since Van Gogh said in the previous letter (607) that he would send the consignment that day, we have dated the present letter the same day, that is Thursday, 10 May 1888.

works.said: Then the series of orchards — I think the white orchard of which I sent you pen drawing

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: Then the series of orchards — I think the white orchard of which I sent you pen drawing
facts.note: The painting he is referring to is The white orchard (F 403 / JH 1378). Vincent had sent Theo the drawing The white orchard (F 1414 / JH 1385) in mid-April. See letter 600, n. 3.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 숙박비 분쟁으로 치안판사를 찾아가 트렁크를 돌려받은 일을 전하며, 하루 1프랑에 식사할 수 있는 더 나은 식당을 찾았다고 알린다. 건강이 나아졌다고 하며, 밀밭 옆 농가와 노란 미나리아재비 들판, 붓꽃이 있는 도랑 등 새로 그린 두 점의 습작을 묘사하고 이를 일본의 꿈 같다고 표현한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he has been to see the justice of the peace, a visit that must have taken place on Saturday (see n. 1). Since he said in letter 607 of 10 May that this is what he was intending to do, he must have gone on 12 May. The weather reports also tell us that the mistral was blowing on 11 and 12 May, and Van Gogh mentions it in ll. 56-57 (Météo-France). We have therefore dated the letter the day of the visit to the justice of the peace, Saturday, 12 May 1888.

works.title: Farmhouse in a wheat field
works.said: Now I have two new studies like this: You already have a drawing of it, a farmhouse beside the wide road in the wheatfields.

works.title: View of Arles with Irises in the Foreground
works.said: A meadow full of very yellow buttercups, a ditch with iris plants with green leaves, with purple flowers, the town in the background, some grey willow trees — a strip of blue sky.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: I’ve found a better restaurant where I eat for 1 franc.
facts.note: This was Restaurant Vénissac on place Lamartine, where Van Gogh ate every day (at least in August and September). It was next door to the Café de la Gare, where he was staying. The owner was the widow Marguerite Vénissac-Canin. See letter 658, n. 10, and letter 691.

facts.said: I hope my consignment arrives before Tersteeg comes to Paris.
facts.note: Tersteeg’s visit to Paris took place in the first half of June; see letter 625.

facts.said: My dear Theo, I’m writing you another few lines to tell you that I’ve been to see the gentleman whom the Arab Jew in Tartarin calls ‘the shustish of the beace’.
facts.note: In 1888 there were two justices of the peace in Arles, one for the western canton and one for the eastern canton. Since Hotel Carrel was on the east side of the town, Van Gogh and the hotel-keeper would have taken their dispute to the justice for the eastern canton. This was Eugène Giraud, who was open for business from 10.00 a.m. on Saturday mornings (L’indicateur marseillais 1888). Van Gogh is referring to Alphonse Daudet’s Aventures prodigieuses de Tartarin de Tarascon , in which an Arab Jew with a strong accent cries out: ‘Au zouge de paix! Au zouge de paix!’ See Daudet 1986-1994, vol. 2, p.

facts.said: Now I have two new studies like this: You already have a drawing of it, a farmhouse beside the wide road in the wheatfields.
facts.note: The study is Farmhouse in a wheatfield (F 408 / JH 1417), reproduced in the letter sketch of the same title F - / JH 1418. Van Gogh had sent Theo the drawing Farmhouse in a wheatfield (F 1415 / JH 1408) not long before; see letter 605.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 숙소를 옮긴 뒤 건강이 좋아졌다고 전하며, 캔버스 재료와 바탕칠에 관한 실용적인 문제들을 다룬다. 아를을 떠나는 덴마크 화가 무리에-페테르센에 대한 아쉬움을 표하고, 르누아르와 세잔의 그림을 떠올리며 프로방스의 색채가 네덜란드와 다름을 이야기한다. 곧 파리로 보낼 그림 꾸러미에 대한 기대와 함께 계속 새로운 소재를 찾아 나서겠다는 의지를 밝힌다.
entries.why: Theo is back in Paris (ll. 28-29). On 12 May Vincent had still not received a response to his request that Theo send him some money as soon as he got back (see letters 608 and 609), so Theo cannot have returned until the 12th at the earliest. Now Vincent thanks him for the 100 francs he has sent (ll. 1*-2) and the rapid reply (ll. 103-105), which means that this reply cannot have been written earlier than 13 May.

works.title: A Lane near Arles
works.said: I have two new studies, a bridge and the verge of a wide road.

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles
works.said: I have two new studies, a bridge and the verge of a wide road.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: He regained his health here and is now very well — he’s good for two years — but after that it would do him good to come back for this same reason of health.
facts.note: Mourier-Petersen was said to have gone to the south of France in part for his health, having spent the winter of 1886 in Paris. We do not know what his health problems were. Van Gogh surmised in letter 613 that Mourier was suffering from a nervous condition brought on by the examinations he had to take in his study of medicine. However, he had abandoned his medical studies as early as 1880 to become an artist; see letter 611, n. 8.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오의 심장 질환 소식에 놀라면서도 리베 박사와 그루비 박사의 치료를 신뢰하라고 조언하며, 자신도 지난겨울 극도로 무기력했던 경험을 들어 위로한다. 정물화 두 점(커피포트와 병 등이 있는 그림, 야생화 마졸리카 병 그림)의 색채 구성을 상세히 묘사하고, 파리의 드 라 부아시에르 백작부인에게 전할 그림을 부탁한다. 화가로서 예술을 위해 건강·젊음·자유를 대가로 치르는 삯마차 말 같은 존재라는 성찰과 함께, 코로가 죽기 전 꿈에서 본 분홍 하늘이 인상주의로 실현되었다는 희망적인 이야기로 마무리한다.
entries.why: The letter dates from after 15 May 1888: it was on that date that Jan Veth wrote to Theo asking him whether he would let him have some works for the exhibition he was organizing (FR b3573). Vincent moreover expects that Theo will be receiving the crate of paintings any day now; it was sent on about 10 May and would take about ten days to get to Paris (see letters 607 and 610). Since Vincent also thanks Theo for 50 francs he had sent him (ll. 120-121), we have dated the letter on or about Sunday, 20 May 1888.

works.title: Still life with coffee pot, dishes and fruit
works.said: … on the left), a pale blue and white chequered milk jug, a cup — on the right — white, with blue and orange designs, on a yellow grey earthenware plate, a blue barbotine or majolica jug with red, green, brown designs, and lastly 2 oranges and 3 lemons; the table is covered with a blue cloth, the background is yellow green, making 6 different blues and 4 or 5 yellows and oranges.

works.title: Still Life: Majolica with Wildflowers
works.said: The other still life is the majolica jug with wild flowers.

works.title: The Seine with the Pont de Clichy
works.said: Père Perruchot’s restaurant is on the ground floor.

works.title: Landscape with Snow
works.said: And it makes sense for you to go, since I can’t be sure that the family’s staying in the same place this year (however, they’ve been coming there for several years, and Perruchot must know their address in town).

people.name: Countess Clara Levaillant de la Boissière
people.note: (c. 1857-?) wife of Eugène Levaillant de la Boissière

people.name: Eugénie Jeanne Boissière
people.note: (c. 1874-?) daughter of Eugène Levaillant de la Boissière

people.name: Marcellin Perruchot
people.note: (1836-?) restaurant owner and wine merchant in Asnières

facts.said: … on the left), a pale blue and white chequered milk jug, a cup — on the right — white, with blue and orange designs, on a yellow grey earthenware plate, a blue barbotine or majolica jug with red, green, brown designs, and lastly 2 oranges and 3 lemons; the table is covered with a blue cloth, the background is yellow green, making 6 different blues and 4 or 5 yellows and oranges.
facts.note: Still life with coffee pot (F 410 / JH 1426). In the margin next to the letter sketch of the same name after the work (F - / JH 1427) Van Gogh noted that it was a no. 30 canvas, whereas it is actually a no. 25 ‘figure’ canvas, 81 x 65 cm. Cf. exhib. cat. New York 1984, p. 46. He omitted the painted border in the letter sketch and in the sketch he sent to Bernard with letter 622. It seems obvious that Van Gogh painted this still life and the one referred to below on 16 and 17 May, because it rained on those days and he could not work outdoors (Météo-France).

facts.said: Père Perruchot’s restaurant is on the ground floor.
facts.note: In 1886 Eugène Levaillant de la Boissière (age 45, of independent means), his wife Clara Levaillant de la Boissière (age 29) and their 12-year-old daughter Eugénie Jeanne were registered as the occupants of an apartment on the first floor of 1 boulevard de Clichy. Nothing more is known about the family. Marcelin Perruchot’s restaurant was on the ground floor; he was also a wine merchant in Asnières. See exhib. cat. Martigny 2000, pp. 142-146.

facts.said: Listen — I’ll do all I can to send you some new drawings for Dordrecht.
facts.note: Evidently Theo had asked Vincent to send drawings for the second exhibition of the Nederlandsche Etsclub, which was to be held at Arti et Amicitiae in Amsterdam. Vincent mentions Dordrecht because the artist and critic Jan Veth of Dordrecht was organizing the exhibition – in a letter of 15 May, Veth had asked Theo to loan etchings, lithographs and drawings (FR b3573). See also letter 620, n. 5.

facts.said: That Hope of Puvis de Chavannes
facts.note: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, Hope, c. 1872 (Paris, Musée d’Orsay). Ill. 315. Van Gogh saw this work at the Puvis de Chavannes retrospective which ran from 20 November to 20 December 1887 at Durand-Ruel’s, where it was exhibited as cat. no. 30. We know from letter 829 that he had been to this exhibition.

facts.said: And it makes sense for you to go, since I can’t be sure that the family’s staying in the same place this year (however, they’ve been coming there for several years, and Perruchot must know their address in town).
facts.note: From what Van Gogh says, it would appear that the family lived in Paris (‘in town’) and only stayed in Asnières during the summer. He says that the countess is ‘far from young’, but he has either seriously overestimated her age or is referring to an older woman, possibly the count’s mother, so that the ‘daughter’ – who is also ‘a lady’ – is the count’s 29-year-old wife, not the 12-year-old girl. No further details have been found in the records in Asnières.

entries.summary: 베르나르에게 보낸 편지에서 마르키즈 제도 원주민 학살을 다룬 책을 읽고 백인 문명의 위선과 잔혹함을 격렬히 비판하며, 고갱의 타히티 여인 그림들을 고귀한 시로 극찬한다. 노란 집을 세내어 새로운 정착을 시작했다는 소식과 함께, 커피포트와 오렌지·레몬이 어우러진 정물화, 붓꽃과 미나리아재비가 가득한 아를 풍경화를 상세히 묘사한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh describes the same works as those in letters 610 and 611 to Theo, and mentions a new still life, so this letter must have been written not long after letter 611 of about Sunday, 20 May. He had evidently not started on the drawings that he sent to Theo around 26 May (letter 613), since he does not mention them to Bernard. For these reasons we have dated the present letter on or about Tuesday, 22 May 1888.

works.title: Still life with coffee pot, dishes and fruit
works.said: With these pieces of crockery, 2 oranges and three lemons.

works.title: Still Life: Bottle, Lemons and Oranges
works.said: Then I have another still life, some lemons in a basket against a yellow background.

works.title: View of Arles with Irises in the Foreground
works.said: These meadows are intersected in the foreground by a ditch full of purple irises.

works.title: Farmhouse in a wheat field
works.said: Then two studies of roadsides — afterwards — done out in the mistral.

works.title: A Lane near Arles
works.said: Then two studies of roadsides — afterwards — done out in the mistral.

facts.said: Then two studies of roadsides — afterwards — done out in the mistral.
facts.note: Farmhouse in a wheatfield (F 408 / JH 1417) and Landscape with the edge of a road (F 567 / JH 1419). The mistral blew on 11 and 12 May (Météo-France).

facts.said: People don’t understand him yet, and he suffers greatly from not selling, like other true poets.
facts.note: Theo had paid Gauguin 400 francs for Among the mangoes : see Gauguin lettres 1983, p. 33.

facts.said: Then ‘Hunting among the clan of old and young Those whom she’ll take to bed late at night’.
facts.note: This is a reference to and quotation from the poem ‘La Prostitution’ by Emile Bernard, who wrote in his 1911 publication: ‘It will perhaps not be without interest that I publish here the sonnet criticized by Vincent, not for the sake of my lines, which are bad, but because of his opinion itself: PROSTITUTION To Vincent Prostitution sallies forth, her face all paint and rouge; Along the brightly lit boulevard she prowls Hunting among the clan of old and young, Those whom she’ll take to bed, tonight, very late.

facts.said: Something like that — it’s not characteristic, because the women of our boulevard — le petit
facts.note: See for the painters of the ‘Petit Boulevard’: letter 584, n. 6.

facts.said: With these pieces of crockery, 2 oranges and three lemons.
facts.note: Still life with coffee pot (F 410 / JH 1426). Van Gogh sent Bernard a sketch of this painting with his next letter (622).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 뒤랑-뤼엘의 인상파 전시 소식에 관심을 보이고, 아를 주변 바위 언덕과 크로 평야를 그린 새 드로잉들을 보낸다. 무리에-페테르센이라는 덴마크 화가에 대해 호의적으로 평하며 테오와 함께 지낼 것을 제안하고, 도미에 화집 구입을 반겼다. 편지 말미에는 세상이 신의 실패한 습작일지도 모른다는 독특한 종교적 사색을 펼치며 더 나은 삶에 대한 희망을 이야기한다.
entries.why: The letter was written on a Saturday according to the postscript: ‘tomorrow, Sunday’ (l. 135). Since Van Gogh says he has read an article in L’Intransigeant of Friday, 25 May (see n. 1), it cannot be Saturday, 19 May. Given these indications, we have dated the letter Saturday, 26 May 1888.

works.title: The Bridge of Langlois at Arles
works.said: Have you met the Dane Mourier-Petersen — he’ll have brought you another two drawings as well.

works.title: Vue de Montmajour / The Plain of La Crau
works.said: They’re views taken from a rocky hill from which you can see in the direction of the Crau (an area from which a very good wine comes), the town of Arles and in the direction of Fontvieille.

people.name: Carel Eliza van der Sande Lacoste

facts.said: My dear Theo, I read an announcement in L’Intransigeant that there’s going to be an exhibition of the Impressionists at Durand-Ruel — there’ll be some works by Caillebotte —I’ve never seen anything of his, and wanted to ask you to write and tell me what they’re like
facts.note: Van Gogh must have read the announcement about it in L’Intransigeant of Friday, 25 May 1888 (p. 3, in the ‘Beaux-Arts’ column under the heading ‘Nouvelles Artistiques’): ‘An exhibition of paintings by Messrs Caillebotte, Eugène Boudoin, J.L. Brown, Lepine, Pissaro [sic], Renoir, Sisley and Whistler opens tomorrow, Thursday, [should read Saturday] at the Durand-Ruel Gallery, 11 rue Le Peletier, and continues until 25 June’ (‘Une exposition de tableaux de MM. Caillebotte, Eugène Boudoin, J.L.

facts.said: As far as intelligence goes, I think he’d be far more preferable to that Lacoste,
facts.note: Van Gogh is most probably referring to Carel Eliza van der Sande Lacoste, who signed out of the register in Dordrecht to go to Amsterdam on 29 October 1880 and returned to Dordrecht from Paris on 31 July 1885. Theo may therefore have known Lacoste from the time he was living in Paris or met him when he was visiting the city.

facts.said: The Swede  is from a good family, he has order and regularity in his means of support, and as a man he makes me think of those characters Pierre Loti creates
facts.note: Given the reference to Mourier-Petersen’s phlegm immediately afterwards, Van Gogh must be referring to the calm, unassuming character of the Japanese and Tahitians as Pierre Loti describes them in Madame Chrysanthème and Le mariage de Loti respectively. Van Gogh had read the latter book about two months previously.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 타세에게 보낼 캔버스 견본을 챙기지 못해 뒤늦게 동봉하며, 화실(노란 집)의 외관과 창문, 문을 새로 칠하기로 한 소식을 기쁘게 전한다. 일본 판화처럼 평평한 색면으로 채색한 펜화를 그리고 싶어 수채 물감을 요청했다고 설명한다. 돈이 완전히 떨어졌다며 코닝과의 그림 교환이 어떻게 되었는지 궁금해하는 짧고 실무적인 편지다.
entries.why: The letter was written on a Sunday (ll. 28-29). It must follow letter 613 of Saturday, 26 May with the paint order that Van Gogh refers to here (ll. 3-4). In letter 613 he says he only has enough money left for tomorrow, Sunday; in the present letter the money has all gone. Since he comments on the sunny weather (ll. 30-31) and the weather reports record sunshine on Sunday, 27 May 1888, we have dated the letter that day (Météo-France).

works.title: The Yellow House (Vincent's House)
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

works.title: The Night Cafe in Arles
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

works.title: Harvest Landscape
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

works.title: The Blue Cart / Harvest at La Crau
works.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: My dear Theo I see that I didn’t add the sample of canvas to the order for Tasset.
facts.note: Van Gogh had enclosed this paint order for Tasset in letter 613. He probably sent a sample of Tasset’s canvas that he had used before so that Theo could order the same thing again (this is the case in letter 621). It is also possible that he sent a sample of the unprepared canvas he had bought in Arles, for which he had requested primer in letter 610.

facts.said: The reason I asked for some watercolour paints is because I’d like to do some pen drawings, but coloured in flat tints like Japanese prints.
facts.note: Van Gogh used these watercolours to paint the following works in June: Fishing boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries (F 1429 / JH 1459), Wheat stacks (F 1425 / JH 1441), The old mill (F 1464 / JH 1497), The harvest (F 1483 / JH 1439) and in July Zouave (F 1482 / JH 1487). See cat. Amsterdam 2007, p. 134, n. 33. In The harvest (F 1484 / JH 1438) watercolour is a minor element.

facts.said: He asked me for two of my drawings for one of his studies; I accepted, saying that he should give you the study — but I’ve had no reply to that.
facts.note: Van Gogh had suggested exchanging two of his drawings for a study by Koning; see letter 600. After he left Paris Koning returned to this question in a letter to Theo of 4 June 1888: ‘I shall send you something soon, then you can pick something out of it to exchange with Vincent. I’d rather have one painted study than the 2 drawings, if he doesn’t mind’ (FR b1077). As far as we know the exchange did not go ahead, although Koning did send work to Theo (see letter 666, n. 9).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 모브 추모 그림과 테르스티흐에게 줄 그림에 대해 논의하며, 테오의 건강을 크게 염려해 그뤼비 박사의 치료를 받으며 충분한 휴양을 취할 것을 간곡히 권한다. 사업상 무리한 해외 출장보다 인상파와 자연 속에서 지내는 삶이 낫다고 설득하며, 자신은 언제든 그림을 포기할 수 있다고까지 말한다. 생트마리로의 여행 계획과 고갱·베르나르를 위한 드로잉 화첩 구상도 함께 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent told Theo on 27 May that the weather was fine (letter 614). In the present letter he says: ‘Thunderstorm and rain today’ (l. 220). The weather reports tell us that there was sudden heavy rain on Monday, 28 May (Météo-France). He also received the allowance that he had expected on Sunday (letters 613 and 614). We have therefore dated the letter Monday, 28 May. 29 May – the date Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave in Brieven 1914, which was probably based on a postmark – must therefore have been the date it was posted.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: If you think the Souvenir de Mauve is among those that are passable — then you should add it to the next Hague consignment, with a simple all-white frame.

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing, The
works.said: If you found another study among them that seemed to you more suitable for Tersteeg, you should put it in without a dedication, and you should keep the one with the dedication to him, which you could then scratch out.

works.said: Ever yours, Vincent I think that for the white orchard we need a cold and raw white frame.

people.name: Andries (André or Dries) Bonger
people.note: (1861-1936) friend of Theo in Paris, brother of Jo van Gogh-Bonger

people.name: Elisabeth (Lies) Huberta Du Quesne-Van Gogh
people.note: (1859-1936) sister of Vincent, second wife of Jean Philippe Theodore du Quesne van Bruchem

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

facts.said: Because the drawings will become better than that.
facts.note: In his letter sketch of the Leporello album – which was to be made after a Japanese example – Van Gogh included four of his Arles drawings: Farmhouse in a wheatfield (F 1415 / JH 1408), which he had probably sent to Theo at the end of April (see letter 602), Landscape with a tree in the foreground (F 1418 / JH 1431) and Montmajour (F 1423 / JH 1433), which he said in letter 613 that he had sent, and The Langlois bridge (F 1470 / JH 1377).

facts.said: Our two sisters will doubtless be quite happy to come to Paris and it won’t do them any harm, that’s quite certain.
facts.note: Theo wanted his sisters Lies and Willemien to come to Paris. In the end Willemien came alone and stayed with Theo for several weeks in the summer of 1888.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱을 아를로 불러 함께 살며 매달 250프랑으로 생활비를 나누자는 구체적인 제안을 테오에게 하고, 이를 위한 고갱에게 보낼 편지 초안까지 작성해 동봉한다. 화가들이 고립되어 사는 것은 손해라며 공동생활과 화가 조합 결성의 필요성을 강조하고, 베르나르도 합류할 것이라 기대한다.
entries.why: Theo has written about Gauguin, prompted by a letter he had received from him. He got Gauguin’s letter, written on 22 May, on 23 May at the earliest (GAC 2). Theo’s last letter to Vincent dated from before 20 May (see letter 611), so Theo could not have written about Gauguin until his next letter, of 27 May (for which Vincent thanked him in letter 615). In response to this, Vincent now encloses an unsigned letter addressed to Gauguin, on which Theo comments soon afterwards (see letter 621).

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: But later on, as Gauguin’s a sailor,
facts.note: On 6 December 1865 Gauguin signed on as a junior officer in the merchant navy aboard the Luzitano, in which he served for two three-month trips to Brazil; he then spent thirteen months, from 27 October 1866, sailing around the world as a second lieutenant on the Chili. On 22 January 1868 he joined the French navy; he left the service on 23 April 1873. See exhib. cat. Washington 1988, pp. 3-4.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent Has Tersteeg come to Paris yet?
facts.note: Tersteeg’s visit to Paris took place in the first half of June; see letter 625.

facts.said: Handshake and best wishes to Koning, after all, it’s a source of satisfaction for you to deliver him in good condition, which might not have been the case if you hadn’t taken him with you.
facts.note: We know, because Theo recommended his doctor to him, that Koning initially had problems with his health. See letter 578, n. 9. As we can deduce from a letter from Koning to Theo, they took their leave of each other at the Gare du Nord on 28 May 1888. Koning was then ‘in an anything but cheerful mood’; he travelled back to Winschoten via Bruges, Ghent, Dordrecht and Rotterdam, arriving home on 2 June (FR b1077).

facts.said: My dear Theo, I thought of Gauguin
facts.note: Gauguin, who had already been living on credit for three months, had asked Theo for help in a letter of 22 May (FR b841 and GAC 2). Theo had evidently written to Vincent about it.

facts.said: In order to prepare things, and to expand on this letter, I’m writing to Gauguin, but without saying anything about all this, just to talk about work.
facts.note: Vincent sent these proposals to Theo (ll. 112 ff.), who did not altogether approve of them, so a new version of the letter had to be written (see letter 621). Vincent had moreover already written to Gauguin (see letter 617). Neither letter is known.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 생트마리로 떠나기 전 편지를 쓰며, 테오의 여행 계획이 건강에 무리가 될까 걱정하고 의사 그루비의 조언을 구하라고 권한다. 고갱에게 편지를 보내 함께 작업하지 못하는 아쉬움을 전했으며, 고갱과의 협업이 성사되길 바라는 마음과 화가들이 고립되지 않고 함께 지내야 한다는 생각을 나눈다. 필요하다면 테오와 함께 미국에 갈 수도 있다고 말한다.
entries.why: Several suggestions have been made for the sequence and dating of the letters Van Gogh wrote in late May and early June 1888. Crucial to this discussion is the answer to the question as to when he went to the seaside town of Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer; in the present letter he says he will go there ‘tomorrow’.There is a summary of the views of Hulsker, Pickvance, Merlhès, the editors of De brieven 1990 and Dorn in: Dorn 1998, p. 25.

people.name: Lucien Pissarro
people.note: (1863-1944) French artist, son of Camille Pissarro

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: I leave early tomorrow morning for Saintes-Maries, on the Mediterranean; I’ll stay there till Saturday evening.
facts.note: Van Gogh went to Saintes-Maries on 30 or 31 May (according to Pickvance and Hulsker on 30 May; according to Dorn on 10 June). He returned to Arles on 4 or 5 June (according to Pickvance and Hulsker on 3 June; according to Dorn on 16 June). See Date.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 네덜란드로 돌아가는 친구 아르놀트 코닝에게 작별 인사를 전하며, 뒤랑뤼엘 화랑에서 본 인상주의 작품들에 대해 이야기할 거리가 많을 것이라 말한다. 다음날 생트마리드라메르로 바다와 하늘을 보러 떠날 계획과 인물화에 본격적으로 도전하고 싶다는 포부를 밝힌다. 갈대펜으로 그린 소나무 언덕 데생을 소개하고, 아를의 투우 경기에서 소가 관중석으로 뛰어들거나 절벽에서 떨어져 죽은 일화를 전한다.
entries.why: The letter was enclosed with letter 617, so we have dated it the same day: Tuesday, 29 or Wednesday, 30 May 1888. See further letter 617, Date.

works.title: Orchard with Arles in the Background
works.said: I’ve just made a drawing even larger than the first two.

facts.said: My dear friend Koning, Learning from Theo that you’re going back to Holland, I wanted to drop you a line to say farewell.
facts.note: Koning left Paris on 28 May. He wrote to Theo from his home in Winschoten on 4 June: ‘I had a nice letter from Vincent. I shall write to him tomorrow and let him have my address’ (FR b1077).

facts.said: You’ll have a great deal to tell the fellows in Holland about what you saw in Paris.
facts.note: Koning wrote to Theo on 15 September 1888 about his stay in Paris: ‘As for me, all I can say is that the trip to Paris did me a great deal of good. Never before have I seen nature as beautiful as I did this summer; most people who weren’t used to my studies thought they were ugly at first, but when they looked at them for a long time they found something in them after all. Obviously I don’t give a damn, I specifically stick to a set programme which I arrived at chiefly through Vincent and Breitner and try by this means to achieve an original concept’ (FR b1080).

facts.said: I’ve just made a drawing even larger than the first two.
facts.note: Vincent means the two reed pen drawings he had previously sent Theo, which he initially wanted to exchange with Koning: Orchard with Arles in the background (F 1516 / JH 1376) and The white orchard (F 1414 / JH 1385). See letter 600.

entries.summary: 생트마리 해변을 다녀온 후 바다를 보며 남프랑스에 머무는 것의 중요성을 재확인하고, 일본 회화에 대한 애정과 유사하게 남프랑스가 인상파의 미래라는 확신을 밝힌다. 고갱을 이곳으로 불러 함께 지내고 싶다는 바람과, 여럿이 협력해야 생활비를 아낄 수 있다는 계산을 전한다. 배 그림과 오두막 드로잉을 보냈으며, 쇠라와 피사로의 색채 이론에 대해서도 언급한다.
entries.why: This is the first letter Van Gogh wrote after returning from Saintes-Maries to Arles on or about Tuesday, 5 June 1888 in the morning; see letter 617, Date. We assume that Van Gogh wrote the same day, both to let Theo know that he was back and to thank him for the weekly allowance, which would normally have reached Arles on or about Monday the 4th, or else must have arrived the same day.

works.title: Seascape at Saintes-Maries
works.said: I’ll make you a consignment of rolled-up paintings as soon as the seascapes are dry.

works.title: Seascape near Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer

works.said: I have another 3 drawings of huts that I still need and which will follow; these ones of the huts are a bit harsh, but I have some more carefully drawn ones.

works.title: Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing, The
works.said: Tell them I have a painting of boats, that and the Langlois bridge

facts.said: I’ll make you a consignment of rolled-up paintings as soon as the seascapes are dry.
facts.note: Fishing boats at sea (F 415 / JH 1452) and Fishing boats at sea (F 417 / JH 1453). We learn from letter 619 that Van Gogh wanted to leave the seascapes behind in Saintes-Maries to dry, but as far as we know he did not go back to the coast. It is not entirely clear whether he took the paintings back to Arles with him after all or had them sent on later; the wording in the present letter would seem to point to the former. In letter 636 he reports that the studies are not dry yet. Theo did not receive the seascapes until mid-August, when they were sent with some thirty other studies (see letter 660).

facts.said: You only have to go down rue de la Paix
facts.note: The rue de la Paix in Paris runs from the Opéra to place Vendôme. This chic shopping street housed art dealers (including Durand-Ruel), fashion houses and jewellers.

facts.said: 30 canvas with more sea and sky on the right.
facts.note: The drawing he sent is Fishing boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries (F 1428 / JH 1458); the painting of the same subject is Fishing boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries (F 413 / JH 1460), but this measures 65 x 81.5 cm and is therefore a no. 25 ‘figure’ canvas. Van Gogh made a watercolour after the drawing first: Fishing boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries (F 1429 / JH 1459). See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 2005, p. 186.

facts.said: I’d like us to earn a lot of money to bring good artists here who too often get despondent in the mud on the Petit Boulevard.
facts.note: See for the artists of the ‘Petit Boulevard’: letter 584, n. 6.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 아를에 합류하는 계획을 서두르지 말고 신중히 진행하자고 테오에게 조언하며, 여동생들을 파리로 데려오는 계획이 우선임을 강조한다. 바그너에 관한 책을 읽으며 회화에도 그런 위대한 예술가가 필요하다고 생각하고, 파리의 레가메 형제 전시 소식도 전한다. 고갱이 작업을 하지 않고 낙담해 있는 상황을 걱정하는 마음도 드러난다.
entries.why: The letter follows letter 620 of about 5 June, in which Van Gogh said he planned to write to Gauguin: in the present letter he says he has done so. It must in any event date from before 7 June, because Vincent informs his brother about the Régamey exhibition in Paris on 7 and 8 June – he also gives the opening times, from which we may deduce that this information would still have been of use to Theo (ll. 36-39).

works.title: Fishing Boats on the Beach at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
works.said: So I’ve written, although I hardly had the time, having two canvases on the easel.

works.title: Three White Cottages in Saintes-Maries
works.said: So I’ve written, although I hardly had the time, having two canvases on the easel.

works.title: Street in Saintes-Maries
works.said: So I’ve written, although I hardly had the time, having two canvases on the easel.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: If you think the letter’s clear enough, send it,
facts.note: Theo was sent the letter to read and forwarded it to Gauguin, who in turn sent it on to Emile Schuffenecker in the second week of June (see Merlhès 1989, p. 68).

facts.said: While waiting, Gauguin could peg out like Meryon, discouraged.
facts.note: Charles Meryon suffered from delusions and bouts of severe depression during which he did not work and refused to eat. While he was in the asylum at Charenton for the second time he had starved himself to death. Jules and Edmond de Goncourt discussed Meryon’s folie in their Journal on several occasions, among them 19 October 1856 and 12 January 1869 (see Goncourt 1887-1906, vol. 1, p. 148; vol. 3, pp. 258-259). Burty’s Maîtres et petits maîtres , which Van Gogh had read in 1885, also contained details of Meryon’s ‘painful years’ (a nnées douloureuses) (Burty 1877, pp. 110-119).

facts.said: Do you know that at 6 rue Coëtlogon, rue de Rennes, on 7 and 8 June from 1 to 7 o’clock there’s an exhibition of paintings and drawings by Régamey that could be very interesting; now there’s two who’ve travelled all over the place, he and his brother.
facts.note: Van Gogh must have got this information from L’Intransigeant of 5 June 1888. The ‘Beaux-Arts’ column reported that it was a private exhibition in Félix Régamey’s studio (his brother Guillaume was not mentioned). As well as some paintings destined for the Musée Guimet, due to open shortly, there were ‘a great many’ drawings and watercolours of scenes from the Far East on show, as well as a number of portraits in pastel.

entries.summary: 베르나르에게 보낸 이 편지에서 빈센트는 오늘날 회화가 그리스 조각이나 독일 음악에 견줄 경지에 이르려면 화가들의 협업과 공동체가 필요하다는 예술론을 펼친다. 검은색과 흰색도 엄연한 색채로 다룰 수 있다는 일본 판화식 색채 단순화 이론을 예시와 함께 상세히 설명한다. 생트마리드라메르 마을에서 바다를 처음 보고 지중해와 어부들, 소박한 배들에 감동받았으며, 고갱의 건강이 여전히 좋지 않다는 소식도 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh wrote this letter after his return from Saintes-Maries around 4 June (letter 620). Since he says that he is working up the drawings that he had made there, it must have been written not long afterwards. It also has to be dated a few days before Tuesday, 12 June (letter 623) because by then he was working on his harvest landscapes, which he does not mention here (he does refer to them in the next letter to Bernard (628)). We have consequently dated the present letter on or about Thursday, 7 June 1888.

works.title: Three White Cottages in Saintes-Maries
works.said: … uated in an orange field, of course, because the sky in the south and the blue Mediterranean produce an orange that is all the more intense the higher in tint the range of blues — The black note of the door, of the window panes, of the little cross on the rooftop, creates a simultaneous contrast of white and black just as pleasing to the eye as that of the blue with the orange.

works.title: Street in Saintes-Maries
works.said: … uated in an orange field, of course, because the sky in the south and the blue Mediterranean produce an orange that is all the more intense the higher in tint the range of blues — The black note of the door, of the window panes, of the little cross on the rooftop, creates a simultaneous contrast of white and black just as pleasing to the eye as that of the blue with the orange.

works.said: I’m quite curious to know what you’ve done lately; I’m still doing landscapes, croquis enclosed.

works.said: I’m quite curious to know what you’ve done lately; I’m still doing landscapes, croquis enclosed.

facts.said: In fact, in Arles they often do wear white and black checks.
facts.note: No obvious examples of the fabrics Van Gogh describes have been found. He may have been referring to the summer clothing worn on feast days – a dress of black cotton or satin worn beneath a skirt of violet lace. The underlying dark colour could be seen through the delicate open weave of the lace, creating the optical effect of a checked dress. With thanks to Dominique Séréna of the Museon Arlaten in Arles.

facts.said: One has a superb orchestration of colours
facts.note: Van Gogh had previously written of ‘symphonies of colour’, possibly deriving the notion from Charles Blanc. See letter 537, n. 7. His reading about Wagner may well also have influenced his choice of words: ‘what an artist – one like that in painting, now that would be something’ (quel artiste – un comme ca dans la peinture/ voila ce qui serait chic) (letter 621).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 라발과 함께 지내며 공동생활의 이점을 경험했다는 편지를 받았다고 전하며, 고갱이 빚 문제로 곤란을 겪고 있어 아를로 오도록 돕는 것이 최선이라 판단한다. 몽티첼리 그림 소식과 카마르그 풍경이 라위스달을 연상시킨다는 소감도 전하며, 계속되는 지출에도 남프랑스에서의 가능성을 낙관한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he sent – the second instalment for June – and writes that it is ‘only Tuesday morning’ (l. 57). He has meanwhile abandoned his plan of going to Saintes-Maries on 10 June (see letter 621). This means that it must have been Tuesday, 12 June 1888.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: I have two or three new drawings and also 2 or three new painted studies.

works.title: Farmhouse in Provence

works.title: Farmhouse in Provence
works.said: I have two or three new drawings and also 2 or three new painted studies.

facts.said: I was pleased to learn that Mourier has come to lodge with you.
facts.note: Mourier-Petersen arrived at Theo’s apartment in rue Lepic on 6 June 1888, and stayed with him until about 15 August 1888. See Larsson 1993, pp. 26-27 (n. 95), 29.

facts.said: But he says that he has the experience that when he was in Martinique with his friend Laval, the two of them together managed better than either one of them alone, and that he therefore fully agreed on the advantages a life in common would have.
facts.note: Gauguin and Laval sailed together from Saint-Nazaire to Panama on 10 April 1887, and then on to Martinique in about the middle of May. Weakened by malaria and dysentery, Gauguin returned to France, arriving about 13 November. See exhib. cat. Washington 1988, pp. 44-45. Laval came back to Pont-Aven later, but before about 25 July 1888; see letter 646.

facts.said: If Gauguin would prefer to take the risk of throwing himself back into business at this point — if he really has hopes of doing something in Paris — for Heaven’s sake let him go there, but I think he’d be wiser to come here for a year at least; I’ve seen someone here who had been to Tonkin and was ill when he came back from that delightful region — he recovered here.
facts.note: This was Paul Eugène Milliet, second lieutenant in the 3rd Zouave Regiment, which was garrisoned in the Caserne Calvin, the barracks in boulevard des Lices in Arles (see letter 628). He had been in Tonkin from 12 January 1885 to 20 August 1887 (Paris, Archives Nationales, Fonds de la Légion d’honneur). Tonkin is the area that now makes up the greater part of northern Vietnam; it had been a French protectorate since 1883 and became part of French Indochina in 1887.

facts.said: I went to Tarascon one day, unfortunately there was so much sun and dust that day that I came home empty-handed.
facts.note: This expedition to Tarascon, around 20 km to the north of Arles, probably took place on 10 or 11 June: the weather was hot and sunny then, and the mistral was blowing – most probably the cause of the dust he mentions (Météo-France).

facts.said: I’ve received a letter from Gauguin, who said he’d received a letter from you containing 50 francs, by which he was very touched, and in which you said a few words about the plan.
facts.note: Gauguin’s letter to Vincent and Theo’s to Gauguin are not known. The latter must have been the reply to Gauguin’s letter to Theo of 22 May 1888. Gauguin thanked Theo for sending him 50 francs somewhere around 5-8 June. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, pp. 176, 184.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 집세와 캔버스 구입으로 돈이 바닥났다며 조기 송금을 부탁하고, 밀밭 풍경화 작업에 대해 이야기한다. 세잔의 그림처럼 프로방스의 강렬한 색채를 자신도 포착하고 있다고 느끼며, 붉은 벽돌 바닥 위에서도 색이 죽지 않는 그림을 완성했다고 자평한다. 고갱이 합류하기를 여전히 고대하고 있다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written soon after letter 623, which dates from Tuesday, 12 June – possibly even the same day, for Van Gogh says ‘I’m writing you another line because I haven’t yet received your letter’ (ll. 1*-3; our italics). In 623 Van Gogh remarked that he hadn’t had a letter that morning. Furthermore, in the present letter he asks if he can have his allowance ‘a few days’ earlier than usual (ll. 11-12).

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: And I have another subject, a farmhouse and wheat stacks, which will probably be its pendant.

works.title: Haystacks in Provence
works.said: And I have another subject, a farmhouse and wheat stacks, which will probably be its pendant.

works.title: The white orchard
works.said: I’m working on a landscape with wheatfields which I believe is no worse than the white orchard, for example.

works.title: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
works.said: I’m working on a landscape with wheatfields which I believe is no worse than the white orchard, for example.

works.title: Montmartre: behind the Moulin de la Galette
works.said: It’s of the same kind as the two Butte Montmartre landscapes that were in the Independents,

works.title: Kitchen Gardens on Montmartre
works.said: It’s of the same kind as the two Butte Montmartre landscapes that were in the Independents,

works.title: Still life with coffee pot, dishes and fruit
works.said: The last canvas absolutely kills all the rest; there’s only a still life with coffee-pots and cups and plates in blue and yellow that can stand beside it.

works.title: Summer evening in Arles
works.said: And that’s precisely why I think I’m going to enlarge the format of my canvases and boldly adopt the square 30 canvas.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱의 협동조합 제안에 신중한 태도를 보이며, 화상이 아닌 화가들 스스로가 운영하는 예술가 협회의 이상을 설명한다. 테르스티흐의 태도 변화, 모네 전시회, 모파상의 소설 등 다양한 화제를 다루며, 밀밭 수확 그림을 30호 캔버스에 작업 중이라고 전한다. 스웨덴 화가 무리에-페테르센이 파리에서 겪는 어려움과 고갱의 가족 상황을 고려한 신중한 협상 태도도 드러난다.
entries.why: Vincent had asked Theo if he could have his allowance a few days earlier (letter 624), and in the present letter he thanks him for the 100 francs he sent (l. 7). The wording ‘that’s the subject I’ve been working on this week’ (l. 105) suggests that the letter was written towards the end of the week. We have therefore dated this part on or about Friday, 15 June 1888.

works.title: Farmhouse in Provence
works.said: I’ve sent you 3 drawings by post today.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: The one with the wheat stacks in a farmyard will seem too bizarre to you, but it was done in great haste as a project for a painting, and it’s to show you what it’s like.

works.title: Haystacks in Provence
works.said: The one with the wheat stacks in a farmyard will seem too bizarre to you, but it was done in great haste as a project for a painting, and it’s to show you what it’s like.

works.title: Still life with coffee pot, dishes and fruit
works.said: 30 canvas — it’s hardly done at all — but it kills the rest of what I have, apart from a still life, worked on with patience.

works.title: Harvest Landscape
works.said: 30 canvas

works.title: The Blue Cart / Harvest at La Crau
works.said: 30 canvas

works.title: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
works.said: 30 canvas

facts.said: It will certainly do Tersteeg no harm to have seen this exhibition;
facts.note: Tersteeg was originally going to go to Paris in May (letter 589); from the present letter, however, it emerges that his visit actually took place in the first half of June.

facts.said: And it’s true I didn’t know he had so large a family; he’ll more likely wish to stay in the north for that reason.
facts.note: Gauguin married a Danish woman, Mette Gad, in Paris on 22 November 1873; they had five children. In November 1884 the family went to live in Copenhagen, but Gauguin could not settle there and went back to Paris in June 1885.

facts.said: 30 canvas
facts.note: Vincent must have sent Theo the drawing The harvest (F 1483 / JH 1439). Shortly afterwards he sent the other drawing of the same subject, The harvest (F 1484 / JH 1438), to his sister Willemien (see letter 626). The no. 30 canvas is The harvest (F 412 / JH 1440).

facts.said: Macknight and one of his friends who’s been in Africa too
facts.note: This friend was the Belgian painter Eugène Boch, whom Macknight invited to join him in Fontvieille in a letter of 19 April 1888. We do not know exactly when he arrived. He went back to Belgium via Paris on 4 September 1888 (see letters 674 and 693). Boch first went to Algeria in 1886 and subsequently went back several times. See exhib. cat. Saarbrücken 1971, p. 48. Macknight left Paris in the spring of 1886. He headed first for the south of France and later that year for the Algerian oasis of Ghardaia. See Bailey 2007, p. 30.

facts.said: I congratulate you on having the Monet exhibition at your premises, and I much regret not seeing it.
facts.note: In June-July 1888 Theo staged an exhibition of ten landscapes which Monet had painted in Antibes (on the Mediterranean coast near Cannes). Theo bought them for 11,900 francs and contracted to pay Monet 50 percent of the resale profit. See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 1999, p. 111; the invitation has survived (FR b1497). La Revue Indépendante, vol. 8 (juillet 1888), no. 21, p. 154 reviewed it, but Theo was not really happy with the article. See Wildenstein 1996, vol. 1, pp. 241-244, and cat. nos. 1158?, 1167, 1171, 1175, 1179, 1181, 1187, 1191, 1192?, 1193, and Correspondance Pissarro 1980-1991, vol. 2, p. 239.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 우울함을 다스리는 법과 프랑스 회화계의 냉담한 현실을 길게 이야기하며, 인상주의 화가들이 가난 속에서도 미래를 위한 씨앗이 되고 있다고 옹호한다. 보색 대비(파랑-주황, 보라-노랑, 빨강-초록)를 활용하는 자신의 색채 이론을 설명하고, 빠르게 그리는 인상주의 기법이 미래에는 대중에게 사랑받을 것이라 예견한다. 파리에서의 경험, 자화상 묘사, 노란 집의 모습, 그리고 초상화 쪽으로 다시 방향을 바꿀 수도 있다는 생각을 자세히 전한다.
entries.why: In letter 625, dated around 15 and 16 June, Vincent told Theo that a letter from home had just been delivered. In the present letter he thanks his sister Willemien (and indirectly his mother) for that letter. The fact that Van Gogh goes at length into his motives for painting, says he has painted landscapes although he really sees himself as more of a portrait painter, but does not say anything about making the portrait of the Zouave, places the letter before 21 June, when he embarked on the portrait sittings…

works.title: The Blue Cart / Harvest at La Crau
works.said: Yesterday I sent you by post a drawing that’s the first scratch for quite a large painting.

works.title: The Seine with the Pont de Clichy
works.said: You talk about ‘whether I had submitted something to Arti’ — certainly not – only Theo sent Mr Tersteeg a consignment of paintings by Impressionists and there was one of mine in it.

works.title: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
works.said: Yesterday I sent you by post a drawing that’s the first scratch for quite a large painting.

works.title: Blossoming Almond Branch in a Glass with a Book
works.said: A long time ago I meant you to have a painted study, and you shall get it.

works.title: Flowering orchard, surrounded by cypress
works.said: A long time ago I meant you to have a painted study, and you shall get it.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: Also L’abbé Constantin by Ohnet, terribly sweet and heavenly, so that even his Mâitre de forges, already tending that way, becomes even more suspect.
facts.note: Van Gogh’s attribution of L’abbé Constantin (1882) to Georges Ohnet is based on a misconception; the novel was by Ludovic Halévy. (The same erroneous attribution occurs in letter 687.) The negative tone of Van Gogh’s opinion would appear to be more in line with the general criticism of Ohnet than with the views about Halévy (cf. letter 557). It is not surprising that he describes the romantic love story as ‘terribly sweet and heavenly’, because it is obvious from the outset that the two lovers, Jean and Bettina, will overcome their problems and eventually be together.

facts.said: I’m afraid that by post, even if I pay the postage, they’ll make you pay excess postage, like the flowers from Menton,
facts.note: It appears from the family correspondence that Uncle Vincent and Aunt Cornelie sometimes sent fresh flowers from Menton in the south of France, where they were staying (FR b2235 and b2250).

facts.said: You talk about ‘whether I had submitted something to Arti’
facts.note: The second exhibition of the Nederlandsche Etsclub, which opened in Arti et Amicitiae in Amsterdam on 1 June 1888. Cf. letter 611, n. 5.

facts.said: Enough, this junk doesn’t leave me completely indifferent; for instance, there’s a copy of Gavarni’s Mascarade humaine, a book Anatomy for artists,
facts.note: John Marshall, Anatomy for artists (1878), which Van Gogh bought in 1884 (see letter 465, n. 6).

facts.said: I really don’t like Mr Vosmaer at all, and am callous enough not to care much about the man’s exchange of the temporary for the eternal.
facts.note: Evidently Willemien had mentioned the death of Carel Vosmaer; the writer had died on 12 June 1888. Van Gogh had previously registered his disapproval of Vosmaer: see letter 452, n. 5.

entries.summary: 러셀에게 보낸 편지에서 수확철의 아를 풍경에 몰두해 있다고 전하며, 그림을 그리다 문득 지저분한 소녀의 얼굴을 스케치한 일화를 소개한다. 브르타뉴에 있는 베르나르와 고갱의 근황(고갱의 간 질환 재발)을 전하고, 모네의 새 작품 전시 소식과 씨 뿌리는 사람을 그리는 작업에 대해 이야기한다.
entries.why: The letter is the outcome of the intention expressed in letter 625, dated around 15 and 16 June: ‘I’ll write a word to Russell’ (l. 156). Vincent has meanwhile embarked on a new subject – the sower – which he did not mention in the letter to Theo; this indicates that some time has passed. The letter must have been written before the heavy showers that started on 20 June, because Van Gogh says he worked on The Trinquetaille bridge (F 426 / JH 1468) that same afternoon (l. 17).

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: The great field all violet, the sky and sun very yellow.

works.title: The Bridge of Trinquetaille
works.said: Well, instead of continuing the letter I began to draw on the very paper the head of a dirty little girl I saw this afternoon whilst I was painting a view of the river with a greenish yellow sky.

works.title: Head of a girl
works.said: Well, instead of continuing the letter I began to draw on the very paper the head of a dirty little girl I saw this afternoon whilst I was painting a view of the river with a greenish yellow sky.

facts.said: It is one of those he did at Martinique.
facts.note: Paul Gauguin, Negresses talking or Conversation (Tropics), 1887 (W251/W227) (Sale, Christie’s New York, 15 May 1985, lot 20). Ill. 108. The painting had been on consignment with Boussod, Valadon & Cie since April 1888; in La Revue Indépendante of May 1888 Félix Fénéon mentioned it in a summary of new work being exhibited by Theo van Gogh, adding: ‘A general exhibition of his work will show what a powerful and unique artist he is’ (Une exposition générale de son oeuvre montrera quel artiste puissant et isolé il est) (Fénéon 1970, vol. 1, p. 111).

facts.said: Please remember me very kindly to Mrs Russell
facts.note: Russell married an Italian model, Anna-Maria (Marianna) Antoinetta Mattiocco, in February 1888.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱, 베르나르와 따로 떨어져 지내게 된 것을 아쉬워하며, 아를의 뜨거운 태양 아래 밭에서 일하는 자신의 건강 호전을 기쁘게 전한다. 씨 뿌리는 사람과 노란 밀밭, 보라색 대지를 그린 그림들을 상세히 묘사하며 색채 대비 이론을 설명하고, 별이 빛나는 밤을 언젠가 그리고 싶다는 소망을 밝힌다. 아프리카로 떠날 밀리에 중위와의 우정, 렘브란트·들라크루아 등에 대한 예술론도 함께 담겨 있다.
entries.why: Vincent told Theo on 21 June that he had received a letter from Bernard (see letter 629). Because he says in the present letter that he is replying to Bernard’s letter immediately (l. 2), it must precede letter 629. He has also progressed further with The sower than he could report in letter 627, which was written around 17 June, and he mentions a new wheatfield. This suggests that a couple of days must have passed since he wrote that letter, so we have dated the present one on or about Tuesday, 19 June 1888.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: Here’s croquis of a sower.

works.title: Summer evening in Arles
works.said: Here’s another landscape.

works.title: Arles: View from the Wheat Fields
works.said: The way Anquetin got his Harvest so well.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: These last few days I read Pierre Loti’s Madame Chrysanthème; it provides interesting remarks about Japan.

facts.said: But how I’d like to see the study you did at the brothel.
facts.note: Bernard sent him a drawing of a brothel soon afterwards, which Vincent sent on to Theo, saying: ‘it’s probable that he has a more finished painted study of it’ (letter 630). Bernard’s drawing Brothel scene (see letter 630, n. 4) was thus probably based on that study of a brothel. However, no such painted version is known today.

facts.said: I was always dreaming about Millet, and then I had acquaintances in Holland in the category of painters like Mauve, Israëls.
facts.note: Van Gogh regarded Israëls’s work as the counterpart of Millet’s. Nothing is known about any contacts between Van Gogh and Israëls, although they very probably met when Vincent was working in the Goupil gallery in The Hague (in July 1883 he quoted something Israëls said; see letter 361). Israëls sold much of his work through Goupil.

facts.said: He’s leaving for Africa in October.
facts.note: Paul Eugène Milliet was due to leave for Guelma in Algeria on 1 November 1888. Cf. letters 714 and 716.

facts.said: These last few days I read Pierre Loti’s Madame Chrysanthème; it provides interesting remarks about Japan.
facts.note: Pierre Loti’s novel Madame Chrysanthème (1888) is set in Nagasaki. A French officer marries the Japanese Kikou-san, or Madame Chrysanthème. In reality the marriage is a paid, temporary concubinage. The Frenchman has no real feelings of love for her; it is more a question of his amazement at how doll-like she is. Loti describes the setting and the customs. The underlying message is that it is difficult for Europeans to penetrate the mysterious closed nature and morals of the Japanese, or the artificial refinement of objects. Van Gogh probably read an illustrated version that he borrowed from Milliet.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 모네 전시에 대한 제프루아의 평론을 언급하며 수확철을 맞아 밀밭 작업에 몰두하고 있음을 전한다. 밀레와 레르미트를 잇는 대작으로 '씨 뿌리는 사람'을 색채와 대형 화폭으로 그려보고 싶다는 오랜 열망과 그에 대한 두려움을 토로한다. 사나운 눈빛의 주아브 병사를 모델로 초상화를 그린 경험과 캉프에서 야생마와 홍학을 볼 계획도 함께 언급하며, 고갱과 베르나르의 근황을 궁금해한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes ‘The past two days we’ve had torrential rain that lasts all day’ (ll. 95-97). Since the rain started on Wednesday, 20 June, we – like Pickvance – think that this observation must have been made on the second rainy day, in other words on Thursday, 21 June 1888. Dorn suggests that Van Gogh is looking back on the third day at the two previous days, but because the rain continued we believe that Van Gogh would then have written of three days of rain. See exhib. cat. New York 1984, p.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: Above all that a yellow sky with a yellow sun.

works.title: The Seated Zouave
works.said: And now the second portrait will be seated; full length, against a white wall.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: 30 canvas.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: The bust-length I painted of him was terribly hard.

works.title: Wheatfield
works.said: I’ve had a week of concentrated hard work in the wheatfields right out in the sun, the result was some studies of wheatfields, landscapes

works.title: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
works.said: I’ve had a week of concentrated hard work in the wheatfields right out in the sun, the result was some studies of wheatfields, landscapes

works.title: Haystacks in Provence
works.said: I’ve had a week of concentrated hard work in the wheatfields right out in the sun, the result was some studies of wheatfields, landscapes

works.title: Summer evening in Arles
works.said: I’ve had a week of concentrated hard work in the wheatfields right out in the sun, the result was some studies of wheatfields, landscapes

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: Only a third or half is urgent.
facts.note: Van Gogh had enclosed a paint order for Tasset with letter 613. He had split it in two, and in letter 617 he reported that he had received part of it. The consignment Van Gogh says here he received two weeks ago – in other words on or about 8 June – was probably the second part of that order. It can be inferred from the end of the paragraph and the reference to ‘the canvas’ in l. 108 that he had sent another order with this letter.

facts.said: I’m hoping to do a tour in the Camargue next Friday, with a vet,
facts.note: There were three vets in Arles in 1888: Arnaud, 14 rampe du Pont; Autheman, Casimir, 5 place du Forum; and Raynaud, 8 rue de la Cavalerie (L’indicateur marseillais 1888). This was probably Antoine Raynaud, who was a military vet working in the stud farm attached to the barracks. Van Gogh would most likely have made his acquaintance through Second Lieutenant Milliet or the Zouave who was sitting for him at this time. The plan to visit the Camargue did not go ahead (see letter 636); cf. however also letter 657, where he writes of a trip around various farms.

facts.said: My dear Theo, I’ve just read Geffroy’s article on Claude Monet.
facts.note: Gustave Geffroy, ‘Dix tableaux de Claude Monet’, La Justice 9 (17 June 1888), no. 3077, pp. 1-2. It emerges from a letter the art critic Gustave Geffroy wrote to Theo on 29 May 1888 that he was planning an article on Van Gogh, for which he evidently wanted to use quotations from the letters to Bernard: ‘In few days’ time, I should be grateful if you would come to Tanguy’s with me, so that I can finish looking at your brother-in-law’s [read: brother’s] work and making my notes.

facts.said: the sower, with colour and in a large format.
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring here to Millet’s painting The sower, which he had repeatedly copied from prints in his early years as an artist, and to Léon Augustin Lhermitte’s drawing of the same title, Le semeur (The sower), which he knew from an engraving in Le Monde Illustré. See letters 156, n. 3 and 545, n. 8.

facts.said: 30 canvas.
facts.note: Vincent had sent the drawing Wheat stacks (F 1425 / JH 1441) to Theo (letter 625). This was ‘the first idea’ for the painting Wheat stacks (F 425 / JH 1442).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 최근 작업에 불만을 느끼면서도 인물화가 풍경화보다 자신을 더 끌어당긴다고 고백하며, 베르나르가 보낸 사창가 스케치를 언급한다. 데생 교본을 구하지 못해 답답해하며 마르세유행을 다시 고려하고, 모네의 빠른 작업 속도를 높이 평가하는 한편 아를의 남프랑스 특유의 쾌활함은 느끼지 못한다고 토로한다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written after 17 June because Van Gogh refers to an article in La Justice of that date (n. 1). He writes: ‘It’s still raining a lot here’ (l. 36). According to the weather records it rained heavily until Saturday, 23 June, and considerably less on 24 and 25 June. Since Saturday, 23 June was the last very rainy day and Van Gogh thanks Theo for sending his allowance, we have dated the letter Saturday, 23 June 1888.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: I wouldn’t be surprised if he wanted to make an exchange with me for the head of a Zouave, although that one’s very ugly.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: I wouldn’t be surprised if he wanted to make an exchange with me for the head of a Zouave, although that one’s very ugly.

facts.said: I wouldn’t be surprised if he wanted to make an exchange with me for the head of a Zouave, although that one’s very ugly.
facts.note: It emerges from letter 633 that Van Gogh wanted to exchange the painting Zouave (F 423 / JH 1486) with Bernard. Eventually he sent the watercolour Zouave (F 1482 / JH 1487) with the dedication ‘A mon cher copain Bernard. Vincent’. A letter from Bernard to his parents tells us that Van Gogh sent this drawing in mid-July: see letter 641.

facts.said: I didn’t know that the article on Claude Monet was by the same hand as the one on Bismarck.
facts.note: Gustave Geffroy, ‘Bismarck’ appeared in Le Figaro, Supplément Littéraire (18 February 1888), pp. 25-26. Geffroy writes about Prince Otto von Bismarck-Schönhausen as a political figure and recounts some anecdotes from his biography. See for Geffroy’s article ‘Dix tableaux de Claude Monet’ in La Justice 9 (17 June 1888): letter 629, n. 1.

facts.said: Besides, they have these books at Latouche’s, and in rue de la Chaussée d’Antin, at the place of that man who always has works by Allongé.
facts.note: See letter 158, n. 3, for Cassagne’s Guide de l’alphabet du dessin and letter 168, n. 21 for his Traité d’aquarelle , Eléments de perspective , Traité pratique de perspective and La perspective du paysagiste . Madame Latouche had a ‘magasin de couleurs fines et tableaux modernes’. Madame Latouche had a ‘magasin de couleurs fines et tableaux modernes’ (shop selling fine colours and modern paintings) at 34 rue Lafayette. She had run the business alone since the death of her husband, the painter Louis Latouche, in 1884. She did framing and lining and exhibited the work of the Impressionists in her shop window.

facts.said: On the back of the drawing there’s a poem with very much the same tone as the drawing, it’s likely that he has a more finished painted study of it.
facts.note: There is no known painted version of Bernard’s Brothel scene .

facts.said: Cassagne .
facts.note: See for Cassagne’s Guide de l’alphabet du dessin : letter 214, n. 2. It was published by Ch. Fouraut et fils, éditeurs, at 47 rue Saint-André des Arts in Paris. Van Gogh needed the book for the drawing lessons he was giving the Zouave Lieutenant Milliet (see letter 628).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 캔버스 가격 비교와 대량 구매를 통한 절약 방안을 테오에게 상세히 설명하며, 자신이 그림을 너무 빨리 그린다는 세간의 평가에 대해 자연에 대한 감정의 진실함에서 나온 것이라 반박한다. 연말까지 50점의 캔버스를 완성해 피사로 등에게 보여줄 계획을 세우고, 고갱이 오지 않더라도 홀로 작업에 매진하겠다는 의지를 밝힌다.
entries.why: The letter must date from after letter 630 of 23 June in which Van Gogh is still complaining about the rain, and before letter 634 of about 28 June in which he writes that he worked on the sower yesterday and today. This sower – an important subject to him – is not mentioned in the present letter. The remark ‘The wheatfields – that has been an opportunity to work’ (l. 116), and the fact that he told Bernard on 27 June (letter 633, l.

works.title: Canal with Women Washing
works.said: I’ve just painted that subject in large format.

works.title: Orchard in Blossom, Bordered by Cypresses
works.said: I’m almost reconciled with the orchard, which wasn’t on a stretching frame, and its pendant with the stippling.

works.title: Orchard with Peach Trees in Blossom
works.said: I’m almost reconciled with the orchard, which wasn’t on a stretching frame, and its pendant with the stippling.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: The wheatfields — that has been an opportunity to work, like the orchards in blossom.
facts.note: See for Van Gogh’s paintings of orchards in blossom in March-April 1888: letter 600, n. 7; for his paintings of wheatfields: letter 629, n. 3.

facts.said: Do you remember among the small drawings a wooden bridge with a washing-place — a view of a town in the background?
facts.note: Canal with bridge and washerwomen (F 1473 / JH 1405). Theo had received the drawing in May; see letter 602, n. 1.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 성경과 그리스도에 대한 깊은 사색을 전하며, 오직 들라크루아와 렘브란트만이 그리스도를 제대로 그렸다고 말한다. 그리스도를 '가장 위대한 예술가'로 보는 독창적 해석과 함께, 화가라는 존재로서 별들 사이에서 사후에도 창작을 계속할 수 있으리라는 상상을 펼친다. 최근 그린 주아브 병사의 초상화와 렘브란트, 포터 등 네덜란드 화가들에 대한 애정도 언급한다.
entries.why: This letter was written one day before 633, as is clear from the opening of that letter. Since the latter dates from Wednesday, 27 June, we have dated the present one Tuesday, 26 June 1888.

works.title: The Seated Zouave
works.said: What I’ve done is very ugly: a drawing of the Zouave, seated, a painted sketch of the Zouave against an all-white wall

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: What I’ve done is very ugly: a drawing of the Zouave, seated, a painted sketch of the Zouave against an all-white wall and lastly his portrait against a green door and some orange bricks of a wall.

people.name: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez

facts.said: Because Cranach, Dürer, Holbein belong to him — it’s he — his personality — that’s the lofty light of the Middle Ages.
facts.note: Lucas Cranach, Albrecht Dürer and Hans Holbein were Protestant artists in the circle around Martin Luther. Bernard wrote to Andries Bonger about this passage on 31 December 1892: ‘What do you think of this idea, for example: Luther is the great light of the Middle Ages. Luther in the Middle Ages and an assertion of that kind, that could damage Vincent... Should such things be included? Tell me frankly what you think.’ (Que pensez vous par exemple de cette idée: Luther c’est la grande lumière du moyen-age. Luther au moyen age et une telle assertion cela pourrait nuire a Vincent... faut il mettre ces choses?

facts.said: Christ’s doctrine.
facts.note: Van Gogh is thinking here in the first place of Delacroix’s painting Christ asleep during the tempest , which he mentions later in the letter. The works by Rembrandt he must have had in mind would have been the print Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane (see letter 148) and the painting The pilgrims at Emmaus (see letter 34). In saying that Millet painted the doctrine of Christ, he means that Millet’s work expresses the values that Christ preached, such as love of one’s fellow man, humility and simplicity.

facts.said: Ah — the brilliant sketch.
facts.note: Eugène Delacroix, Christ asleep during the tempest, c. 1853 (New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art). Ill. 61. It is clear that this is the version of the painting he is referring to (Delacroix painted several) from the fact that elsewhere Vincent writes that he and Theo had seen it at the commercial exhibition of John Saulnier’s collection (letter 676, n. 15).

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent The sonnets are going well
facts.note: Here he is referring to the poems on the back of the drawing Brothel scene , see letter 630, n. 6. He discussed them at greater length in the postscript to letter 633, which was actually intended for the present letter.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 극도의 피로 속에서도 편지를 쓴다며, 세잔의 서툴러 보이는 붓터치가 사실 미스트랄 바람 속에서 그린 결과일 것이라 짐작한다. 자신도 여름 저녁 풍경을 단 한 번의 작업으로 완성했다며 빠른 작업이 결함이 아니라고 주장하고, 형제 테오를 통한 그림 교환과 여러 화가의 공동 작업 가능성을 언급한다. 베르나르의 사창가 소네트에 대해 도덕적 훈계보다 있는 그대로의 관찰이 더 강력하다는 비평을 상세히 덧붙인다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he is tired again after working out in the sun (l. 60), which means that there must have been at least two days of good weather after the rainy period, which ended on 25 June (Météo France). Since he would immediately have seized the chance to work outdoors again, we have dated this letter Wednesday, 27 June 1888.

works.said: 30 canvas — the summer evening

works.said: If you wished, I would earmark for an exchange with you the head of a Zouave that I’ve painted.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent I add about these sonnets
facts.note: These were the poems on the back of the drawing Brothel scene : see letter 630, n. 6. Although Van Gogh calls them ‘sonnets’, strictly speaking they are not.

entries.summary: 탕기 영감이 보낸 물감 품질에 대한 불만을 전하며, 씨 뿌리는 사람 그림을 다시 작업했다고 알린다. 밀레의 무채색 씨 뿌리는 사람과 달리 색채로 노랑과 보라의 동시대비를 표현하려는 자신의 시도를 델라크루아의 아폴로 천장화에 견주어 설명한다. 트랭크타유 다리를 그린 압생트빛 풍경화도 소개하며, 고갱에게서는 여전히 소식이 없다고 전한다.
entries.why: The letter was written a few days after letter 630, which we dated to 23 June 1888: that letter had been returned to Van Gogh because it had been incorrectly addressed (ll. 6-7). He writes in the present letter that he will send the one that had been returned back again straightaway (ll. 12-13), which means that this one must have been written on or about Thursday, 28 June 1888.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: The sky is yellow and green, the earth purple and orange.

works.title: The Bridge of Trinquetaille
works.said: I have a View of the Rhône — the Trinquetaille iron bridge, where the sky and the river are the colour of absinthe — the quays a lilac tone, the people leaning on the parapet almost black, the iron bridge an intense blue — with a bright orange note in the blue background and an intense Veronese green note.

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: So when they returned the letter to me opened, the people at the Post Office had the pleasure of being able to edify themselves by contemplating Bernard’s brothel.
facts.note: Van Gogh had sent Theo Bernard’s Brothel scene ; see letter 630.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Probably in order to convince myself that, as I myself am one of the most absent-minded of mortals, I have no right to criticize the people of the south for their carelessness — I once again made the mistake of addressing my letter to 54 rue de Laval instead of 54 rue Lepic.
facts.note: Rue de Laval was Theo’s old address. Van Gogh had made this mistake before (see letter 601).

facts.said: — yes — that’s what père Martin
facts.note: Pierre Firmin Martin (‘père Martin’) was an art dealer at 29 rue Saint-Georges in Paris. He sold work by the Barbizon School and the Impressionists. We learn from letter 718 that several of Van Gogh’s paintings were exhibited in his gallery.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 남프랑스행 제안을 수락했다는 소식에 기뻐하며, 함께 생활하면 비용을 아낄 수 있다는 실용적 계산을 편다. 수확기의 밀밭과 밀단을 빠르게 그려낸 작업을 언급하며, 몽티셀리·들라크루아·바그너처럼 정교한 색채 계산이 정신을 소진시킨다는 점에서 자신을 그들과 견준다. 고갱과 그림을 공유하고 손익을 나누자는 구체적 협업안도 제시한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he sent. This must have been the first instalment of the allowance for July, since in his letter of 5 July Vincent refers to the recent consignment of paint from Tasset which he says in the present letter he has ‘just’ received. For this reason we date the letter on or about Sunday, 1 July 1888.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: It’s like that with the one of which I sent you the drawing, the harvest and the wheat stacks too

works.title: Harvest Landscape
works.said: It’s like that with the one of which I sent you the drawing, the harvest and the wheat stacks too

works.title: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background

people.name: G. Edouard
people.note: (?-?) seller of artists’ materials in Paris

facts.said: It’s like that with the one of which I sent you the drawing, the harvest and the wheat stacks too
facts.note: These landscapes are The harvest (F 412 / JH 1440) and Wheat stacks (F 425 / JH 1442); the drawings that were sent were The harvest (F 1483 / JH 1439) and Wheat stacks (F 1425 / JH 1441). Vincent had sent them to Theo in mid-June (see letter 625).

facts.said: He’d enclosed his invoice, which comes to 50.85 francs, which enabled me to check his prices and compare them with Edouard’s.
facts.note: Van Gogh must mean G. Edouard’s paint shop at 8 rue Pigalle in Paris, which was taken over by Victor Mulard. The shop is listed under both names in the address books (Almanach du commerce de Paris 1886-1888).

facts.said: Now your letter brings me a big piece of news — that Gauguin accepts the proposal.
facts.note: On 8 July 1888 Gauguin wrote to Emile Schuffenecker: ‘I told Van Gogh that I accepted his proposal and that I counted on Mrs Pouzin to get me out of here and down to the south. I have had no news from Van Gogh which surprises me and bad news from Mrs Pouzin which means it’s bad on all counts, a sign that something good will happen – as you can see I am still optimistic’ (J’ai répondu à Van Gog que j’acceptais sa proposition et que je comptais sur Made Pouzin pour me liberer d’ici et filer dans le midi.

facts.said: So if it’s safer to go to Brittany where one can board for so little
facts.note: The cost of board and lodging at the Gloanec inn was apparently less than 150 francs a year for two people – half what Van Gogh was paying in Provence. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 488 (n. 7).

facts.said: And Jules and Edmond de Goncourt say this, word for word — ‘we took very strong tobacco to stupefy ourselves’ in the furnace of creation.
facts.note: Van Gogh may be referring to the following words of Jules and Edmond de Goncourt: ‘Tobacco, salvation in times of activity, feverishness and prodigious output; is the laudanum of the nervous system’ (Le tabac, une providence dans un siècle d’activité, de fébrilité, de prodigieuse production; c’est le laudanum du système nerveux), included in the collection Idées et sensations . Paris 1866, p. 213.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 일몰 무렵 뒤틀린 떡갈나무와 폐허가 있는 황야에서 몽티첼리풍의 낭만적인 풍경을 목격한 감흥을 전하며, 실제 완성작이 기대에 못 미쳤다고 아쉬워한다. 아연백 물감이 부족해 생트마리에서 그린 습작들이 아직 마르지 않았고, 캉프 여행 계획도 무산되었다고 전한다. 발자크의 '세자르 비로토'를 읽고 있으며, 아를에서 예술 애호가를 찾지 못했지만 강렬한 남프랑스 햇빛 덕분에 외로움을 크게 느끼지 않는다고 고백한다.
entries.why: The letter must date from early July: Van Gogh refers to the consignment of painting supplies from Tasset (ll. 26-27) which he had received at the end of June (see letter 635). The fact that he had recently paid the rent indicates that it was towards the beginning of the month (ll. 40-41). In letter 637 of Sunday, 8 or Monday, 9 July he says – referring to the present letter – that he wrote ‘last Thursday’, which means that it must have been written on Thursday, 5 July 1888.

works.title: Sunny Lawn in a Public Park
works.said: A little corner of blue green sky at the top.

works.title: Seascape near Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
works.said: I get on very well using it, but it has the disadvantage of drying very slowly, so, for example, the studies done at Saintes-Maries aren’t dry yet.

works.title: View to Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer

people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

entries.summary: 빈센트는 물감상 탕기 부부와의 금전 분쟁에 대해 테오에게 단호히 대응할 것을 요청하며, 자신은 빚진 것이 없다고 강하게 주장한다. 게쓰마니 동산의 그리스도를 그린 대작을 모델 없이 그린 것이 잘못이라 여겨 긁어냈다고 전하며, 고갱의 아를행과 러셀의 소식을 궁금해하고 로티의 책과 로트레크의 그림에 대한 감상도 나눈다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he sent, and for the illustrations by Toulouse-Lautrec (ll. 151-152), which had appeared in the Paris Illustré of 7 July. We generally date letters in which the receipt of money is confirmed to around a Sunday, but Van Gogh could not have received the illustrations in Saturday’s Paris Illustré on the same day. We have therefore dated the letter Sunday, 8 or Monday, 9 July 1888.

works.title: Rock-hill with trees: Montmajour
works.said: I have two large new ones.

works.title: Haystacks near a Farm
works.said: They quibbled with me at the post office, saying that the drawings I was sending you were too big to be sent that way.
