people.note: (1814-1898) seller of artists' materials in Paris

people.name: Siegfried Bing
people.note: (1838-1905) dealer in oriental art in Paris

facts.said: I read that Bing’s holding a Japanese exhibition and publishing a magazine on Japanese art.
facts.note: The Exposition historique de l’art et de la gravure au Japon, which ran from 28 May 1888 in Bing’s gallery at 22 rue de Provence. See exhib. cat. Richmond 1986, pp. 21 (fig. 7) and 28. In May 1888 Bing started publishing the magazine Le Japon Artistique. Documents d’Art et d’Industrie, which appeared monthly until 1891. Each issue contained a lead article, detailed illustrations, some in colour, and descriptions of works of art, many of them from Bing’s collection. Van Gogh may have read about the magazine and the exhibition in the July issue of La Revue Indépendante.

facts.said: The only thing I actually owe is to Bing.
facts.note: The art dealer Siegfried Bing had run a gallery for Chinese and Japanese art at 19 rue Chauchat, Paris, since 1878. In the 1880s he opened branches that traded for varying lengths of time at 22 rue de Provence (adjoining rue Chauchat), 13 rue Bleue (opened in 1881) and 19 rue de la Paix (closed in 1886). In the summer of 1884 he established the firm of S. Bing et Cie, with himself as the major shareholder. See exhib. cat. Richmond 1986 and exhib. cat. Amsterdam 2004-1.

facts.said: I have two large new ones.
facts.note: These were probably The rock of Montmajour with pine trees (F 1447 / JH 1503) at 49 x 60 cm and Olive trees, Montmajour (F - / JH add. 3) at 48 x 60 cm. Van Gogh did three more and sent all five drawings to Theo by post soon afterwards (see letter 639).

facts.said: I’d like to send you the 30 studies
facts.note: In mid-August Van Gogh gave Milliet 36 studies to take to Paris; see letter 660, n. 1.

facts.said: If you happened to see their manager
facts.note: In letter 676 Van Gogh mentions a man called Lévy, who was one of Bing’s branch managers. This is probably who he means here. This branch manager is mentioned again in letters 640, 642 and 686. Lévy stood in for Bing in his absence. The collector Raymond Koechlin wrote about his first visit to the gallery in 1890: ‘Bing was unwell when I called at rue de Provence, and I was received by Mr Lévy or ‘Father Lévy’, as he was affectionately known’. See Max Put, Plunder and Pleasure. Japanese Art in the West, 1863-1930. Leiden 2000, p. 79.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 몽마주르 정원 나들이와 탕기 영감과의 금전 갈등, 러셀과의 그림 교환 계획을 전한다. 매미와 남프랑스의 이국적 풍경을 일본 화첩에 비유하고, 화가는 죽어서도 작품을 통해 후대와 소통한다는 사유와 함께 별을 향해 떠나는 죽음의 은유를 인상 깊게 서술한다.
entries.why: In letter 637 of Sunday, 8 or Monday, 9 July, Van Gogh says that he is going to see Boch in Fontvieille ‘this afternoon’. Since he writes in the present letter that he was there ‘yesterday’, we may safely assume that it was written a day later. We have therefore dated it Monday, 9 or Tuesday, 10 July 1888.

works.said: That makes 3 drawings;

works.said: I had the further thought that if you care to recall that I painted portraits of père Tanguy (which he still has),

works.said: I had the further thought that if you care to recall that I painted portraits of père Tanguy (which he still has), of mère Tanguy (which they sold), of their friend (it’s true that I was paid 20 francs by him for the latter portrait),

people.name: Philips van Marnix of St. Aldegonde

facts.said: What you were saying about that conversation at the Nouvelle Athènes
facts.note: Café in the place Pigalle in Paris, where the group of artists and writers around Manet, Degas and Desboutin met regularly.

facts.said: At the moment I have a charwoman, who sweeps and scrubs the house twice a week for 1 franc;
facts.note: The cleaning woman was Thérèse Balmoissière. See Murphy 2016, p. 94. Van Gogh paid her 20 francs a month (see letter 736). See also letter 747, n. 1.

facts.said: According to the excellent master Ziem, a man becomes ambitious the moment he can’t get a hard-on.
facts.note: What Van Gogh writes here is confirmed by a letter from Ziem to Arsène Houssaye of 26 September 1885: ‘Just imagine that right here I am producing some of my finest pictures: the autumnal fruits of the waking hours, the worries and the scourgings which clot the sperm to solidify brain matter. Matter is pretty. Your Zanzibar Ziem.’ (Figurez-vous que je fais ici même, mes plus beaux tableaux: le fruit automnal des veilles, des préoccupations, des macérations qui figent le sperme pour solidifier la matière cérébrale. Matière est jolie. Votre Zanzibar Ziem.) Taken from Pierre Miquel, Félix Ziem 1821-1911. 2 vols.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 몽마주르 시리즈의 펜 드로잉 5점을 보내며, 고갱과의 동업 준비로 돈을 벌 수 없는 상황에서 작업으로 성의를 다하고 있다고 전한다. 크로 평원과 론강 유역을 그린 드로잉이 자신의 최고작이라 자평하며, 미스트랄과 모기에 시달리면서도 이 풍경에서 옛 네덜란드 화가 라위스달을 떠올린다. 캔버스 가격 비교와 일본풍 감상법에 대한 생각도 함께 나눈다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written not too long after letter 638, which dates from 9 or 10 July: in that one Van Gogh wrote that he had three finished drawings, now he has five. He also says that ‘after the 14 July holiday’ (l. 47) Theo will probably be glad to refresh his eye on the drawings he has just sent. The letter in any event dates from before letter 640, which was written on Sunday, 15 July – in that one Van Gogh reiterates that he has sent the drawings.

people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: All the same, they took them, which pleased me, because after the 14 July holiday
facts.note: 14 July is the French national holiday commemorating the storming of the Bastille (14 July 1789), the start of the French Revolution.

facts.said: My dear Theo I’ve just sent you by post a roll containing 5 large pen drawings.
facts.note: The rock of Montmajour with pine trees (F 1447 / JH 1503) and Olive trees, Montmajour (F - / JH add. 3), see letter 637; Hill with the ruins of Montmajour Abbey (F 1446 / JH 1504), see letter 638; La Crau seen from Montmajour (F 1420 / JH 1501) and Landscape near Montmajour with a train (F 1424 / JH 1502).

facts.said: Handshake, and thank you for the 12 tubes of zinc white that Tasset has just sent.
facts.note: In letter 636 Van Gogh commented that Tasset had not sent enough zinc white in the previous batch.

facts.said: As I see it, the two views of the Crau and the countryside along the banks of the Rhône are the best I’ve done with my pen.
facts.note: La Crau seen from Montmajour (F 1420 / JH 1501) and Landscape near Montmajour with a train (F 1424 / JH 1502). Ill. 2147- 2148.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오에게 일본 판화상 빙과의 거래를 계속 유지할 것을 권하며, 저렴하게 대량의 우키요에를 확보해 많은 화가들에게 기쁨을 줄 수 있다고 강조한다. 앙케탱과 베르나르에게 큰 영향을 준 탕부랭에서의 일본 판화 전시 경험을 회상하고, 고갱과의 교환도 그 연장선에 있다고 설명한다. 자신의 모든 작업이 일본 미술에 기반하고 있으며 프랑스 인상주의 안에서 새롭게 뿌리내리고 있다는 생각을 밝힌다.
entries.why: The letter was written during the morning of the day Van Gogh wrote letter 642. Since that one dates from Sunday, 15 July 1888, so does this.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: Bernard having sold his first painting there, Anquetin having sold a study there, and I having made the exchange with Gauguin,

works.title: Two Cut Sunflowers
works.said: Bernard having sold his first painting there, Anquetin having sold a study there, and I having made the exchange with Gauguin,

works.title: Portrait of a Lady with Red Hair Band
works.said: Then a month later, before I left, I no longer had the money and I’d also given a good many Japanese prints to Bernard, when I made the exchanges with him.

works.title: Self-Portrait with Straw Hat
works.said: Then a month later, before I left, I no longer had the money and I’d also given a good many Japanese prints to Bernard, when I made the exchanges with him.

works.title: Portrait of Julien Tanguy
works.said: 50 Total 200 francs Payment of this bill isn’t urgent, but an advance would nevertheless be agreeable to me.

works.title: Portrait of a man with a mustache
works.said: 50 Total 200 francs Payment of this bill isn’t urgent, but an advance would nevertheless be agreeable to me.

works.title: Portrait of Père Tanguy
works.said: 50 Total 200 francs Payment of this bill isn’t urgent, but an advance would nevertheless be agreeable to me.

works.title: The plain La Crau" near Arles, seen from Montmajour"
works.said: I’ve sent you a roll of drawings.

people.name: Siegfried Bing
people.note: (1838-1905) dealer in oriental art in Paris

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: The exhibition of Japanese prints that I had at the Tambourin had quite an influence on Anquetin and Bernard, but it was such a disaster.
facts.note: For Café Le Tambourin, where Van Gogh exhibited his work, see letter 571, nn. 2-3. It is assumed that Van Gogh’s exhibition of Japanese prints took place in February-March 1887 because the portrait of Agostina Segatori (with a Japanese print in the background) is dated to this period. In any event it must have been before the end of April 1887, because that was when Bernard left for Brittany and it is apparent from the present letter that he went to see the exhibition. Japanese graphic art was a major influence on the new style – Cloisonnism – that Anquetin and Bernard developed. Cf. letter 575, n. 7.

facts.said: For 100 francs, if we pay the 90 francs, besides all of what we have left, we’ll have a new stock of 660 Japanese prints.
facts.note: 3 sous = 0.15 francs, so one could buy 666 prints for 100 francs.

facts.said: I’m working on some drawings for Bernard so that he’ll send me some of his.
facts.note: See letter 641 for the drawings Van Gogh sent Bernard. Bernard sent Van Gogh several sketches soon afterwards, see letter 649.

facts.said: There’s an attic at Bing’s, and in it there’s a heap of 10 thousand Japanese prints, landscapes, figures, old Japanese prints too.
facts.note: This may have been the attic at the back of Bing’s branch at 22 rue de Provence; in 1899 it was converted for use as a workshop for Bing’s craftsmen. See exhib. cat. Amsterdam 2004-1.

facts.said: de Clichy, I have fewer regrets about the time and effort.
facts.note: Read: ‘Avenue’ de Clichy. Van Gogh staged an exhibition of paintings in the Grand Bouillon-Restaurant du Chalet in avenue de Clichy in November-December 1887; see letter 575, n. 9. On the basis of this passage Kōdera assumed that Van Gogh also exhibited Japanese prints there, but there is nothing here that bears this out. Cf. cat. Amsterdam 1991, p. 12.

entries.summary: 베르나르에게 보낸 편지로, 라 크로 평야를 새의 눈으로 내려다본 두 점의 대형 펜화가 가장 일본적인 작품이라 자평한다. 한 병사와의 대화를 통해 사람이 사는 평범한 풍경이 바다보다 더 아름답다는 통찰을 전한다. 병을 앓았던 고갱이 겨울을 함께 보내러 올 가능성을 언급하며 여비 마련의 어려움과, 서로 크로키를 교환하자는 제안을 한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes that he has drawings ready to send to Bernard (l. 56). In his letter to Theo of Sunday, 15 July, he says that he had sent them ‘today’ and that he had also written to Bernard that Sunday (letter 642, ll. 139 and 177). The present letter is accordingly dated Sunday, 15 July 1888.

works.title: The plain La Crau" near Arles, seen from Montmajour"
works.said: Have made large pen drawings — 2 — an immense flat expanse of country — seen in bird’s-eye view from the top of a hill — vineyards, harvested fields of wheat, all of it multiplied endlessly, streaming away like the surface of a sea towards the horizon bounded by the hillocks of La Crau.

works.title: The plain La Crau" at Arles with a small train"
works.said: Have made large pen drawings — 2 — an immense flat expanse of country — seen in bird’s-eye view from the top of a hill — vineyards, harvested fields of wheat, all of it multiplied endlessly, streaming away like the surface of a sea towards the horizon bounded by the hillocks of La Crau.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: Perhaps you’ll be inclined to forgive me for not having replied to your letter straightaway, seeing that I’m attaching a small batch of croquis to this one.

facts.said: Perhaps you’ll be inclined to forgive me for not having replied to your letter straightaway, seeing that I’m attaching a small batch of croquis to this one.
facts.note: Vincent sent six drawings, going by what he wrote to Theo later that day (letter 642) and what Bernard wrote to his parents in July. He told them he had received a packet containing ‘six truly remarkable pen drawings. There’s a head of a Zouave that amazes me. Vincent’s becoming very good. At the same time that he’s an excellent artist, he’s a thinker, because every one of his works contains an idea that flashes on the eye of the man who looks for it. And his literature keeps me excited, too, it’s so vivid’ (six dessins à la plume vraiment remarquables. Il y a une tête de zouave qui m’a étonné.

facts.said: In the croquis, The garden, there’s perhaps something like ‘the shaggy carpets of flowers and woven greenery’
facts.note: This is derived from the first two verses of the 30th rondeau, ‘Les fourriers d’Esté sont venus’ van Charles d’Orléans: The harbingers of Summer have arrived To dress his dwelling-place, And have had his carpets spread, Of flowers and verdure wove. Spreading shaggy carpets out Of green grass o’er the land, The harbingers [of Summer have arrived.] Hearts weary and dejected once Thanks be to God, are healthy now and blithe, Away with you, be gone, Winter, you’ll stay no more; The harbingers [of Summer have arrived!] (Les fourriers d’Esté sont venusPour appareiller son logis,Et ont fait tendre ses tappis,De fleurs…

facts.said: In the croquis, The garden, there’s perhaps something like ‘the shaggy carpets of flowers and woven greenery’ of Crivelli or Virelli,
facts.note: Since Bernard often mentions Crivelli in his correspondence, it is likely that Van Gogh is responding here to something Bernard had written. Bernard may also have cited the preceding quotation. Carlo Crivelli mainly painted biblical scenes, often with detailed flower still lifes in the foreground. However, this might also be a reference to Vittore Crivelli, a maker of religious paintings and very probably Carlo’s brother. Cf. Anna Bovero, Tutta la pittura del Crivelli. Milano 1961, and Sandra di Provvido, La pittura di Vittore Crivelli. L’Aquila 1972.

facts.said: Have made large pen drawings — 2 — an immense flat expanse of country — seen in bird’s-eye view from the top of a hill — vineyards, harvested fields of wheat, all of it multiplied endlessly, streaming away like the surface of a sea towards the horizon bounded by the hillocks of La Crau.
facts.note: La Crau seen from Montmajour (F 1420 / JH 1501) and Landscape near Montmajour with a train (F 1424 / JH 1502). The drawings measure roughly 48.5 x 60.5 cm.

facts.said: I have a consignment that’s about to go off,
facts.note: These must be the paintings that Milliet was to take to Paris in mid-August; see letter 660.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 방 씨의 일본 판화 컬렉션(재고)을 계속 유지하고 활용할 것을 테오에게 강하게 권한다. 진정한 일본 미술은 호쿠사이 같은 초기 작품에 있으며, 렘브란트·베르메르 등 네덜란드 거장들과 마찬가지로 오랜 안목이 필요하다고 설명한다. 베르나르에게 판화를 보낸 일, 불랑제 장군 사건, 빅토르 위고의 시집 등 파리 소식에도 관심을 보인다.
entries.why: Van Gogh observes that he has got through ‘another Sunday’ (l. 176). In view of the mention of the purchase of Japanese prints from Bing about which he had written to Theo the same morning (letter 640), this must have been Sunday, 15 July 1888.

facts.said: And you, if you don’t want to lose on it, I would urge you to make some exchanges with painters whom you know — as Besnard still owes you a study, to tell the truth.
facts.note: In an undated letter to Theo (who handled work for him from time to time) Besnard asked for 200 francs as a matter of urgency: ‘I really must have 200 francs by tomorrow afternoon. You’re the only one I can confide in. In return, you can choose whichever watercolour you like from those I have left in the house’ (J’ai absolument besoin de deux cents francs pour demain après midi. Il n’y a que vous à qui je puisse me confier. Vous choisirez en échange l’aquarelle qui vous plaira parmi celles qui me restent à la maison) (FR b1168). Vincent may be referring to this arrangement. Besnard’s oil study The parting, n.d.

facts.said: Today I sent Bernard 6 drawings after painted studies; I promised him 6 more and asked for an exchange of croquis after his painted studies.
facts.note: See letter 641, n. 1, for the batch of six drawings sent to Bernard. Soon afterwards Van Gogh sent him another nine sketches after painted studies (see letter 643). For his part, Bernard sent a series of ten sketches, for which Van Gogh thanked him in letter 649.

facts.said: It seems to me that both of them were right to fight, being unable to get along.
facts.note: On 13 July Boulanger had fought a duel with Président du Conseil Charles Floquet, an opponent of the Boulangist movement. Boulanger had been seriously injured and had lost the duel. Van Gogh may heave heard Boulanger speak in Paris; as minister of war he had often spoken in public in 1886-1887. However he might also have based his opinion on the lengthy reports of Boulanger’s appearances in the daily and weekly press. See Garrigues 1991, for the duel: pp. 183-184. His speeches were published in Les discours du Général Boulanger depuis le 4 août 1881 jusqu’au 4 septembre 1887. Paris 1888.

facts.said: I didn’t conceal that there were some at Bing’s, only I said they were 5 sous,
facts.note: Vincent and Theo only paid 3 sous per sheet; evidently they had persuaded Bing to give them a discount. See letter 640.

facts.said: that hope’s in the stars.
facts.note: In Hugo’s anthology L’année terrible (1872), which deals with the Franco-Prussian War of 1870-1871, he discusses the role of the stars in the present and the hereafter several times.

entries.summary: 베르나르에게 보낸 편지에서 빈센트는 세잔이 사랑한 프로방스 풍경(라 크로, 카마르그)을 담은 크로키 9점을 보냈다고 전하며, 자신이 말한 '협업'이 한 그림을 함께 그리는 것이 아니라 서로 다르지만 어우러지는 작품군을 이루는 것이라 설명한다. 렘브란트와 파울루스 포터, 반 라위스달의 관계를 예로 들어 화가들이 서로 영향을 주고받으며 형성하는 '유파'의 의미를 설파한다. 화가들이 서로 반목하기보다 협력해야 물질적 어려움을 극복하고 더 행복해질 수 있다는 예술 공동체에 대한 신념을 담담히 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh has just sent Bernard the drawings he had promised in letter 641 of 15 July. The form of words he used in that letter to announce the new ‘half a dozen’ shows that he was planning to start on them almost right away (ll. 58-65), carrying on from the first set of six sent with letter 645/B10.

works.title: Street in Saintes-Maries
works.said: My dear old Bernard, Today I’ve just sent you another 9 croquis after painted studies.

works.title: Sower with Setting Sun
works.said: My dear old Bernard, Today I’ve just sent you another 9 croquis after painted studies.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: My dear old Bernard, Today I’ve just sent you another 9 croquis after painted studies.

facts.said: My dear old Bernard, Today I’ve just sent you another 9 croquis after painted studies.
facts.note: Van Gogh had sent six drawings shortly before; see letter 641, n. 1. Most of the drawings in the two batches have been identified. In addition to the two listed in letter 641, Zouave (F 1482 / JH 1487) and Newly mown lawn with a weeping tree (F 1450 / JH 1509), Roskill has identified a further 11 drawings, but it is impossible to say which was in which batch.

facts.said: And then there’s the fact that the material difficulties of the painter’s life make collaboration, union among painters, desirable — (just as much as in the days of the guilds of St Luke).
facts.note: Luke the evangelist was the patron saint of painters. The guilds of St Luke, which began springing up in the fifteenth century, drew up statutes in consultation with the local authority that closely regulated the training and defined the rights and duties of painters. The guilds had to guarantee that apprentices received a proper training, and were obliged to look after the welfare of their members. See G.J. Hoogewerff, De geschiedenis van de St. Lucasgilden in Nederland. Amsterdam 1947.

facts.said: My dear old Bernard — by collaboration
facts.note: Bernard must have responded to what Van Gogh had written two letters previously: ‘Ah, if several painters agreed to collaborate on great things’ (letter 633 of 27 June).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 큰 캔버스에 몰두하느라 지쳤다면서도 정원 꽃밭을 그린 새 습작들을 소개한다. 프린센하허의 노쇠한 지인 소식에 인생의 무상함을 느끼며 네덜란드에 대한 향수를 고백하고, 세잔의 그림에서도 미스트랄 바람의 거친 영향이 보인다고 관찰한다. 일본 화가들처럼 그림을 부르주아 가정의 장식으로 널리 받아들여지게 하고 싶다는 바람을 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for a letter, not for sending his allowance – he does that in letter 645 of about Sunday, 22 July. This letter precedes that one, as we can tell from the remarks about Gauguin (ll. 22-24) and Macknight (ll. 25-28). It is not possible to pinpoint an exact date, though Vincent has meanwhile started some new studies, which means that a few days must have elapsed since his last letter to Theo of Sunday, 15 July (642).

works.title: Flowering Garden with Path
works.said: I have a new drawing of a garden full of flowers; I also have two painted studies of it.

works.title: Flowering Garden
works.said: I have a new drawing of a garden full of flowers; I also have two painted studies of it.

people.name: Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

people.name: Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: What, if anything, would be urgent would rather be the canvas, seeing that I have a whole lot of stretching frames from which I’ve removed the studies, and on which in the meantime I must put other canvases.
facts.note: This order eventually arrived in Arles on 9 August: see letter 658. For this order see also letter 652.

facts.said: What you say about Princenhage, it’s true that it’s the same story all over again — but when at long last the fellow isn’t there any more, then for his little circle it will be one more emptiness and desolation.
facts.note: Uncle Vincent van Gogh of Princenhage was seriously ill – he had a lung condition (letter 615). He died soon after this, on 28 July 1888.

facts.said: What you write about Reid isn’t very cheerful either — at times he used to speak so often of making himself a painter, and of retiring to live with an aunt in the country, that it’s just possible that he’s carrying out this plan now.
facts.note: According to his son Alexander, Reid was a skilled amateur artist and he often went ‘on sketching expeditions’ with Van Gogh on Sundays. He did not, though, have an aunt in the country. See Alexander McNeill Reid, notes for a biography of Alex Reid (unpublished manuscript, Acc. 6425, National Library of Scotland; photocopy).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 부소 화랑이 테오를 런던으로 보낼 가능성을 언급하며, 자신은 몸이 망가졌지만 그림 그리는 권리와 이유만은 확실하다고 토로한다. 고갱이 여전히 빚과 병 때문에 오지 못하고 있는 상황을 걱정하며, 붓을 놓지 않고 일에 몰두하는 것만이 자신을 지탱한다고 고백하는 다소 절박한 편지다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he sent (l. 191) and tells him that Macknight has finally expressed an opinion of his work (l. 176). There was no mention of this in letter 644, which was written between 17 and 20 July. Since Vincent did not tell Theo that Russell had written to him until about 24 July (see letter 650) and Russell’s letter (letter 647) is dated 22 July, the present letter must have been written before letter 650. Russell’s letter could not have reached Arles until 23 July at the earliest.

works.title: Flowering Garden with Path
works.said: Yesterday Macknight broke his silence a little by saying he very much liked my last two studies (the flower-garden),

works.title: Flowering Garden
works.said: Yesterday Macknight broke his silence a little by saying he very much liked my last two studies (the flower-garden),

people.name: Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

facts.said: Jules Dupré had found some art lover who was paying him.
facts.note: The third volume of the diaries of Edmond and Jules de Goncourt, covering the years 1866-1870, was published in April 1888. On 10 July 1866 they remarked on Jules Dupré’s fervour in their Journal : ‘There is at the same time something of an apostle, a workman and a loony in the great landscape painter.’ (Il y a à la fois de l’apôtre, de l’ouvrier et du toqué, chez le grand paysagiste.) In the same diary entry, they said of Dupré’s patron: ‘Went to Isle-Adam to see the beautiful and curious collection of modern landscapes belonging to the coach-builder Charles Binder ...

facts.said: Now, there’s the pro of this con, and — — we’ll have to turn it to account.
facts.note: The sheet is not full. Van Gogh apparently meant to end his letter here (in his next letter to Theo he seemed to think that he had actually done so – see the opening sentences of letter 650), but in fact he continued on another sheet. The fact that the second sheet does belong to the present letter is confirmed in l. 98, where Van Gogh refers back to ll. 60-66 on the first sheet.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 건강을 회복하고 있다는 소식에 안도하며, 그가 아를에 온다면 자신에게 큰 도움이 될 것이라 기대한다. 혼자 지내는 시간이 길어지며 무뎌질까 걱정하는 심경을 전하고, 모델을 구해 인물 습작을 하고 싶다는 바람을 밝힌다. 최근 완성한 습작들을 벽에 못 박아 걸어두고 마치 전시회처럼 살펴보고 있다고 전한다.
entries.why: The letter in any event dates from after letter 645 of about Sunday 22 July, for here Van Gogh asks if he can have his allowance on ‘Sunday’. If this request was to have any effect, he must have written the letter no later than the middle of the week. Russell wrote to Van Gogh on 22 July, and his letter must have arrived on 24 or 25 July (647).

facts.said: I’d very much like it if Russell were to do something — however, he has a wife, children, a studio, a house under construction, and I can very well imagine that even a rich man may not always be able to spend 100 francs — were it only that — on paintings.
facts.note: Russell and his wife Marianna had a daughter, Jeanne, in July 1888. Their first child, John-Paolo, died in the spring of 1887. For Russell’s house see letter 623, n. 16.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르가 보낸 데생들에 큰 만족을 표하며, 렘브란트와 보들레르에 대한 견해차를 상세히 논한다. 페르메이르의 절제된 팔레트와 벨라스케스를 예로 들며 완성도 높은 결작이 주는 무한함의 감각을 이야기하고, 렘브란트가 상상력이 없다고 알려졌음에도 자화상 속 천사를 통해 초월적 이미지를 창조했다는 역설을 설명한다. 편지 말미에는 최근 완성한 12세 소녀의 초상화를 짧게 소개한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh thanks Bernard for the drawings he has sent, which shows that this letter follows the last one he wrote to him, letter 643 of between 17 and 20 July, in which Van Gogh was still waiting for news from Bernard. The letter must have been written at the end of the week, because he has just finished the painting Mousmé (l. 119). He mentions its completion in similar terms in letter 650 of 29 July. We have therefore dated this letter, too, to Sunday, 29 July 1888.

works.title: La Mousmé
works.said: Have just finished portrait of young girl of 12, brown eyes, black hair and eyebrows, flesh yellow grey, the background white, strongly tinged with veronese, jacket blood-red with violet stripes, skirt blue with large orange spots, an oleander flower in her sweet little hand.

people.name: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez

facts.said: A ray of light from above skims his down-turned face and the bushy red hair.
facts.note: There is a good chance that Van Gogh bought Eugène Gaujean’s etching Christ at the column. This print after an oil sketch attributed to Rembrandt (now in Cologne, Wallraf-Richartz Museum; Bredius 1969, no. 591), was included in Catalogue des tableaux anciens de toutes les écoles composant la très importante collection de M. Le Baron de Beurnonville. Paris 1881, lot 435, facing p. 264. Ill. 2203. The print was in the Van Gogh estate (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Van Gogh may have known that Christ has red hair in the painting.

facts.said: It’s charming.
facts.note: The batch included five drawings of nude women. Van Gogh says in letter 651 that he did not like Lubricity as much as the others, so that could not be the one he is talking about here. The four drawings he is referring to are Women bathing and the brothel scenes Female nude seated on a bed, Female nude reclining on a bed and A woman washing herself, the latter being the one Van Gogh calls ‘the one washing herself’. Ill. 2199, 2200, 2201, 2202.

entries.summary: 테오가 화상으로서 하는 일도 예술가의 작업만큼 가치 있다는 긴 사유를 전하며, 서로의 희생과 예술 부흥에 대한 신념을 나눈다. 무스메(프로방스 소녀) 초상화 완성 소식과 러셀·기요맹에게 고갱 그림 구매를 권유한 일을 알리고, 베르나르가 보낸 크로키와 마크나이트·보흐 등 동료 화가들에 대한 평가를 상세히 전한다. 수염을 깎은 자신의 모습을 반 데르 후스의 광인 화가 그림에 빗대며 자조한다.
entries.why: In Brieven 1914 Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave the date as ‘29 Juillet’ – she may have had a postmark to go on. This date is borne out by Van Gogh’s remark that it took him all week to make Mousmé (‘my whole week’, l. 67); this is a form of words that looks back over the week. He does not thank Theo for his allowance in this letter, which also helps to confirm the date since the money did not arrive until Monday (see letter 652). For these reasons we have dated the letter Sunday, 29 July 1888.

works.title: La Mousmé
works.said: Now, if you know what a ‘mousmé’ is (you’ll know when you’ve read Loti’s Madame Chrysanthème), I’ve just painted one.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: That makes 2 figures, the Zouave,

works.title: The Seated Zouave
works.said: That makes 2 figures, the Zouave,

facts.said: At least, when you go there that scoundrel and his worthy spouse shake your hand — it’s in a café, of course
facts.note: Macknight and Boch were staying at Café de l’Alcazar on the Cours in Fontvieille. The café was run by Jean Peyrol and his wife Emilie Peyrol-Girard (Mairie de Fontvieille; Brussels, Musées Royaux des Beaux-Arts, letters from Macknight to Boch 1888-1889).

facts.said: I’ve received from Bernard 10 croquis like his brothel;
facts.note: Bernard’s drawing Brothel scene, 1888 (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 2322, which Vincent had sent on to Theo with letter 630.

facts.said: And the same for Guillaumin, I’d like him to buy a figure by G.
facts.note: Van Gogh must mean that Russell, who had previously bought work from Guillaumin (see letter 602), should buy a figure painting by him.

facts.said: I’m sending him Geffroy’s article.
facts.note: Gustave Geffroy, ‘Dix tableaux de Claude Monet’, La Justice 9 (17 June 1888), no. 3077, pp. 1-2.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 렘브란트와 프란스 할스를 진지하게 연구하라고 강하게 촉구하며, 두 화가 모두 무엇보다 '인물화가'였다는 핵심을 놓치지 말라고 강조한다. 벨라스케스, 고야, 들라크루아, 졸라, 발자크 등을 아우르며 위대한 예술가들의 광기와 천재성에 대한 사색을 펼친다. 보들레르의 렘브란트론은 피상적이라 비판하며 회화를 논할 때는 잠자코 있으라는 신랄한 평도 남긴다.
entries.why: Assuming that Van Gogh honoured his promise to write again soon, the present letter dates from shortly after the previous one to Bernard (letter 649, of 29 July). The opening words accordingly appear to be an immediate continuation of their discussion about painting, while the drawings that Bernard had sent are examined at the end. Van Gogh’s new model, Joseph Roulin, who posed for him on 31 July, is not mentioned, despite the fact that the importance of painting portraits is stressed in this letter.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 숙부의 별세 소식을 전하며 삶이 연기처럼 덧없다는 상념과 함께 그림보다 사람에게 애착을 가져야 한다는 생각을 밝힌다. 러셀에게 판화 연작을 보내 고갱의 그림 구매를 설득하려는 계획과, 우체부 룰랭을 새 모델로 삼아 초상화를 그리는 근황을 전한다. 저녁 무렵 론강의 석탄 배를 보고 호쿠사이 판화 같다고 감탄하며, 앞으로 인물화 연작에 집중하겠다는 예술적 방향 전환의 의지를 드러낸다.
entries.why: This letter was written on the same day as letter 653 (see l. 79). The date of that letter is certain: it reports the birth of Marcelle Roulin ‘today’. The present letter can therefore also be dated Tuesday, 31 July 1888. This is confirmed by Van Gogh’s comment that that evening he had seen a coal barge which was wet after a shower; it rained on 31 July (Météo-France).

works.title: Flowering Garden with Path
works.said: Macknight came to look again yesterday, and also found the portrait of a young girl good, and again said that he finds my garden

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: Now I’m working with another model, a postman in a blue uniform with gold trimmings, a big, bearded face, very Socratic.

works.title: Railway Carriages
works.said: It’s in a railway yard that I saw this effect; it’s a place that I’ve just found and where there will be plenty of other things to do.

works.title: Coal Barges
works.said: It was too late to do it, but one day, when this coal-boat comes back, it’ll have to be tackled.

people.name: Siegfried Bing
people.note: (1838-1905) dealer in oriental art in Paris

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

people.name: Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: He has offered to take charge of my consignment that I have to make to you, and I believe I’ll accept that; that way you’ll have them, and without costs, on the 18th.
facts.note: Milliet went on leave to Northern France (letter 659). On the way there he delivered Van Gogh’s second batch – 36 paintings – to Theo in Paris. He arrived on Friday, 17 August 1888 (letter 662).

facts.said: Now I’m working with another model, a postman in a blue uniform with gold trimmings, a big, bearded face, very Socratic.
facts.note: In a letter to Willemien van Gogh, Roulin described himself as ‘Entreposeur des Postes’ and gave his address as ‘Rue de la Montagne des Cordes 10’ (FR b710; Verzamelde brieven 1973, vol. 4, p. 164). According to Priou he was brigadier-chargeur at Arles station, responsible for loading and unloading sacks of mail. See Priou 1955, p. 27. The rue de la Montagne de Corde was to the north of place Lamartine. Van Gogh said that Roulin resembled the philosopher Socrates on more than one occasion, undoubtedly because of his shaggy beard and Republican convictions. Cf. Head of Socrates (Paris, Musée du Louvre). Ill.

facts.said: You did well to send the colours and canvases, my supplies being exhausted across the board.
facts.note: This is the ‘rather large’ paint and canvas order that Vincent had sent with letter 644. Theo must have sent a sample of canvas for Vincent’s opinion, as we learn from letter 654.

facts.said: I thought I’d do a series of drawings after my painted studies for him;
facts.note: Van Gogh sent twelve drawings to Russell before about 3 August: see letter 654, n. 1. The batch was meant to dispose him favourably towards buying a work by Gauguin and consequently does not seem to be connected to the exchange proposed previously (letter 589).

facts.said: It seems that they’re more or less expecting you for the funeral, and perhaps you’ll be there now, in fact.
facts.note: Uncle Vincent van Gogh died on 28 July 1888. Theo attended the funeral in Princenhage; see letter 656.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 여름 정원의 화려한 색채와 우체부 룰랭의 초상화, 열두 살 소녀의 초상 등 최근 작업을 상세히 묘사한다. 고갱과 함께 살 가능성을 언급하며 서로의 경제적 부담을 줄이고 동료애를 나눌 수 있으리라 기대하고, 큰아버지의 죽음 소식에 대한 소회도 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes that Madame Roulin had given birth that day (l. 38). Marcelle Roulin was born on Tuesday, 31 July 1888. This fixes the date of the present letter. Vincent said in letter 652 that he would write to ‘our sister’ the same day.

works.title: Flowering Garden with Path
works.said: At the end, black cypresses against little low white houses with orange roofs — and a delicate green-blue strip of sky.

works.title: Sunny Lawn in a Public Park
works.said: The blue cast shadows of the bushes on the grass.

works.title: La Mousmé
works.said: The background light green, almost white.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: The background in this one is a harsh green door, and some orange bricks of the wall and the white plaster.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: A negro boy with a red and white cow, a negress in blue, and some green forest.

works.title: Two Cut Sunflowers
works.said: A negro boy with a red and white cow, a negress in blue, and some green forest.

Cornelis (Cor) Marinus van Gogh (Uncle Cor or C.M.)
people.note: (1824-1908) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer and bookseller in Amsterdam

people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

people.name: Cornelia (Cornelie) van Gogh-Carbentus (Aunt Cornelie)
people.note: (1829-1913) wife of Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Cent), sister of Anna van Gogh-Carbentus

facts.said: His wife gave birth today and so he’s in really fine feather and glowing with satisfaction.
facts.note: Marcelle, Joseph and Augustine Roulin’s daughter, was born on Tuesday, 31 July 1888.

facts.said: However, I imagine it would disappoint you and appear ugly were you to see it.
facts.note: Van Gogh added the sentence ‘Echter ... zaagt’ (However ... see it) later.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱에게서 아직 돈이 없어 오지 못한다는 편지를 받았다고 전하며, 노란 집을 반년 더 계약할지 고갱이 보고 결정하겠다고 말한다. 모델을 구해 초상화 두 점을 작업 중이며, 소크라테스 같은 얼굴을 한 우체부를 그리는 중이라 소개하고 인물화가 자신의 실력 향상에 가장 중요하다고 강조한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he had not been able to pay his rent on the first of the month and that his landlord would be coming back on the following Monday (that must have been 6 August). The letter was therefore written between these two dates. Accordingly we have dated it on or about Friday, 3 August 1888.

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: I couldn’t pay my rent on the 1st, having a model for the whole week — I have two portraits of the same model on the go, which are more important to me than the rest.

works.title: Portrait of Josepf Roulin
works.said: I sent Russell 12 drawings after painted studies,

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: We’ll soon be at Michaelmas, and I’ve only rented the house until then;
facts.note: Michaelmas, 29 September, was traditionally the day on which leases expired (and commenced) in France. Van Gogh had rented the Yellow House from 1 May, see letter 602, n. 3.

facts.said: In my last letter I forgot to reply to you on the subject of Tasset’s new canvas at 5.50 francs.
facts.note: This relates to the new canvas – Vincent must have received a sample of it. The order eventually arrived in Arles on 9 August (see letter 658).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 네덜란드 화가들의 건강하고 소박한 삶을 예찬하며, 예술적 창조력을 위해 절제된 생활(과도한 성적 방탕을 피하는 것)이 필요하다는 지론을 강하게 펼친다. 베르나르의 할머니 초상과 정물화를 렘브란트에 견주어 높이 평가하고, 렘브란트·베르메르·들라크루아 등을 예로 든다. 최근 완성한 우편배달부 룰랭의 두 초상화에 대해서도 자세히 설명한다.
entries.why: In letter 654 to Theo, which dates from about 3 August, Van Gogh reported that he was working on two portraits of Roulin, the postman. In the present one he says that they are now finished, so it must have been written a few days later. In letter 657 of 8 August he writes that he has started on new work, so we have dated the present letter on or about Sunday, 5 August 1888.

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: I’ve just made a portrait of a postman — or rather, two portraits even — Socratic type, no less Socratic for being something of an alcoholic, and with a high colour as a result.

facts.said: But — I’ve seen those virile things, the portrait of your grandmother and the still lifes — judging from your drawings I have vague doubts whether these new studies would have the same vigour, just from the virile point of view.
facts.note: Van Gogh must be referring to the drawings Bernard had sent, which are mentioned in letters 649 and 651.

facts.said: Have you ever done better, have you ever been more yourself, and someone?
facts.note: Van Gogh may have taken this expression – that one must try to become ‘someone’ – from Edmond de Goncourt’s foreword to his novel Chérie (1884): see letter 550, n. 12.

facts.said: Rubens , ah, there you have it, he was a handsome man and a good fucker,
facts.note: Van Gogh may have deduced that Rubens was virile and sexually active from the fact that in 1630, at the age of 53, he married the 16-year-old Hélène Fourment, by whom he had five children in seven years. He made several paintings of his young wife in seductive poses. See De Dijn 2002, p. 208.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 삼촌의 장례식과 동생 코르의 근황을 전하며, 미스트랄 바람 속에서 그린 데생들과 우편배달부 룰랭의 초상화 두 점, 곧 태어난 아기도 그릴 계획을 이야기한다. '밤의 카페' 작업을 시작했다고 알리며, 죽음과 영원한 삶에 대한 깊은 사색—삼촌의 평온한 죽은 얼굴, 요람 속 아기의 눈에 담긴 무한함—을 길게 풀어놓는다. 렘브란트와 들라크루아 같은 화가들의 예술적 불멸성에 대한 성찰로 마무리한다.
entries.why: Since Theo has already returned from attending Uncle Vincent’s funeral and has reported on it (ll. 1*-2) the letter must date from early August (Uncle Vincent died on Saturday, 28 July). The letter was written on a Monday (l. 28) and Vincent was going to pay the rent for August that day (ll. 26-27) as he had promised to do (see letter 654 of about 3 August). The letter must therefore have been written on Monday, 6 August 1888.

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: Last week I did not only one but even two portraits of my postman, one half-length, with hands, and a life-size head.

people.name: Cornelis (Cor) Marinus van Gogh (Uncle Cor or C.M.)
people.note: (1824-1908) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer and bookseller in Amsterdam

people.name: Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

people.name: Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: I must now tell you something disagreeable again about money; it’s that I won’t manage this week, because this very day I pay 25 francs;
facts.note: Van Gogh had had to ask the landlord for more time to pay (see letter 654). The rent for the Yellow House was 15 francs a month (see letter 664).

facts.said: it’s absolutely Raoul — you know that perpetual old bohemian student type whom I knew last year.
facts.note: Nothing is known about this Raoul, whom Van Gogh met in Paris.

facts.said: The chap, not accepting money, was more expensive, eating, drinking with me, and in addition I gave him Rochefort’s La Lanterne.
facts.note: Exactly what Van Gogh gave Roulin is not clear. It may have been one or more copies of the popular political satire weekly La Lanterne, founded by Henri Rochefort, which appeared in 1868 and 1869, or of the radical socialist anticlerical daily of the same title, which had been published since 1877 and with which Rochefort was associated for some time. See Henri Rochefort, Nouméa to Newcastle. The story of an escape. Translated from the French by Kenneth R. Dutton. Newcastle 2002. Introduction, p. 1.

entries.summary: 대형 드로잉 세 점과 리토그래프를 보냈다고 전하며, 남프랑스 정원의 화려한 색채를 묘사하고 자신을 이곳에 올 미래 화가들의 선구자로 여긴다고 말한다. 아버지를 닮은 늙은 농부를 그리려다 무산된 일화와 함께, 밀레·들라크루아 등 앞세대 거장들의 유산이 사라지고 있음을 안타까워한다. 고갱과의 공동 작업 계획, 돈이 5프랑밖에 남지 않은 궁핍한 처지도 함께 전한다.
entries.why: The content of this letter follows on from letter 656 of 6 August: Van Gogh now sends the drawings and lithographs he promised, and still expects to receive his money on Saturday. Since the present letter was written on a Wednesday (l. 128), it must have been the first Wednesday after 6 August, in other words Wednesday, 8 August 1888.

works.title: Garden with flowers
works.said: The vertical small farmhouse garden is, it seems to me, the best of the three large ones.

works.title: Wheat field with View of Arles
works.said: Now the harvest,

works.title: Flowering Garden with Path
works.said: The third, horizontal, garden is the one of which I’ve also done some painted studies.

works.title: Flowering Garden
works.said: The third, horizontal, garden is the one of which I’ve also done some painted studies.

works.title: Seascape near Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
works.said: Now the harvest, the garden, the sower and the two seascapes are croquis after painted studies.

works.title: Seascape at Saintes-Maries
works.said: Now the harvest, the garden, the sower and the two seascapes are croquis after painted studies.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: Now the harvest, the garden, the sower and the two seascapes are croquis after painted studies.

works.title: Sunny Lawn in a Public Park
works.said: Now the harvest, the garden, the sower and the two seascapes are croquis after painted studies.

facts.said: Really glorious sunshine, in which Voltaire dried himself off while drinking his coffee.
facts.note: Voltaire’s coffee-drinking must have been legendary: in an early-nineteenth-century illustrated advertisement, ‘Le Roi du Café’ has Voltaire’s head. The story that he drank fifty cups of coffee a day was quoted by the King of Prussia in 1778 in his Eloge funèbre for the writer. Voltaire himself once said ‘coffee revives me’ (le café me ranime), and his love of it assumed impressive proportions in his correspondence. See Inventaire Voltaire. Sous la direction de Jean Goulemot et al. Révision générale par André Magnan. Paris 1995, p. 185. Nothing is known about Voltaire’s staying in the south of France.

facts.said: The one with the sunflowers is the little garden of a bathhouse.
facts.note: Garden of a bathhouse (F 1457 / JH 1539). The bathhouse has not been identified. There are two listed in the Arles address books – at 18 rue du Grand-Prieuré and 38 rue de Vers (L’indicateur marseillais 1888). The latter was closer to Van Gogh’s house in place Lamartine – moreover, the architecture in rue du Grand-Prieuré does not resemble that in Van Gogh’s drawing. See cat. Amsterdam 2007, pp. 153-157, cat. no. 345.

facts.said: I can easily see him coming back sometime.
facts.note: In a letter to Theo of 5 August 1888 Koning wrote: ‘how’s Vincent doing? I wrote him a long letter a while back and would like to hear from him’ (FR b1079). Contrary to what Vincent thought, Koning never went back to France. See exhib. cat. Barneveld 1981.

facts.said: My dear Theo, I’ve just sent off 3 large drawings, as well as some other, smaller ones
facts.note: Van Gogh sent three drawings of approx. 49 x 61 cm and five of approx. 24 x 32 cm; see nn. 3 -10.

facts.said: Must also tell you that I made a very interesting tour round the farms with someone who knows the area.
facts.note: We do not know who accompanied Van Gogh on this excursion around the farms; it may have been the vet who had to break a previous engagement; see letter 629, n. 14, and letter 636.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 타셋에게서 온 캔버스와 물감 배송비를 계산하며, 고갱과 함께 살면 생활비를 절약할 수 있다는 구체적 계획을 다시 설명한다. 자신이 다니는 식당의 벨라스케스풍 회색 톤 실내와 부엌 정경을 세밀하게 묘사하고, 우유빛 피부의 시골 처녀와 그 어머니에게서 본 베르메르 같은 인상도 전한다. 건강이 회복되고 있으며 여자관계를 절제하는 것이 창작에 도움이 된다는 생각도 밝힌다.
entries.why: Letter 657 was sent on the same day Van Gogh also sent Theo some drawings. All this happened ‘yesterday’ (ll. 32-33). Since we dated letter 657 8 August, we have dated the present letter Thursday, 9 August 1888.

works.title: Garden with flowers
works.said: In that case, it’s excellent that I have colours and canvases in stock, because I can already spot half a dozen subjects, especially this little farmhouse garden of which I sent you the drawing yesterday.

people.name: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez
Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: Isn’t it true that in this business with Gauguin, with him spending 2.75 a day (at least, I think I recall that he mentioned that amount, he or Bernard),
facts.note: In 1888 the average prices for rent and food in Pont-Aven were 20 and 62.50 francs respectively, so the average of 2.75 francs a day is correct. See also Dorn 1990, p. 222 (n. 73).

facts.said: Also, I paid 5.60 francs for the last consignment but one, and so if carriage charges are shown on the last invoice but one, it would be too much.
facts.note: This last consignment but one from Tasset was probably the consignment at the end of June mentioned in letter 635. Van Gogh had received the bill for this along with the order.

facts.said: In the kitchen, an old woman and a short, fat, serving-woman,
facts.note: The old woman in the kitchen was probably the owner of the restaurant, the widow Vénissac-Canin. She was 70 in 1888. We do not know who the serving-women were; no live-in staff were registered at her address in 1886, but her 27-year-old daughter Louise was still living at home (ACA).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오가 보낸 물감과 캐사뉴의 책, 소설 '루시 펠르랭의 종말'을 잘 받았다며 감사를 전하고, 성적 주제를 다룬 문학에 대한 자신의 견해를 솔직하게 풀어놓는다. 뜨겁고 바람 없는 남프랑스 여름 햇살과 노란빛의 아름다움에 감탄하며 엉겅퀴와 유랑민의 마차, 기차 화물칸을 그린 근작들을 소개한다. 밀리에 소위가 곧 테오에게 그림을 전달할 예정이라 알리고, 숙부의 유산 문제로 테오가 겪었을 부당함에 대한 위로와 형제애를 표현한다.
entries.why: In the present letter Vincent thanks Theo for the 50 francs he sent (l. 2). This must have been the second of the August allowances: Van Gogh mentions the hot weather, which set in on 11 August (Météo-France). We have therefore dated the letter on or about Sunday, 12 August 1888.

works.title: Thistles
works.said: As far as studies go, I have two studies of thistles on a piece of waste ground, thistles white with the fine dust from the road.

works.title: Encampment of Gypsies with Caravans
works.said: And a little study of a halting-place of fairground people, red and green caravans,

works.title: Railway Carriages
works.said: And a little study of a halting-place of fairground people, red and green caravans, and also a little study of carriages of the Paris-Lyon-Mediterranée,

people.name: Cornelis (Cor) Marinus van Gogh (Uncle Cor or C.M.)
people.note: (1824-1908) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer and bookseller in Amsterdam

people.name: Vincent van Gogh (Uncle Vincent or Uncle Cent)
people.note: (1820-1888) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer

facts.said: My dear Theo, I have to thank you for quite a few things, first of all your letter and the 50-franc note it contained, but then also for the consignment of colours and canvas that I’ve been to collect at the station (the geranium lake arrived too), and lastly for the Cassagne book and for La fin de Lucie Pellegrin.
facts.note: The novella La fin de Lucie Pellegrin by Paul Alexis was published in 1880; the author adapted it as a one-act play, which premiered on 15 June 1888 in the Théâtre Libre in Paris. This was probably why Theo sent it to Vincent. It is not possible to tell whether he sent the dramatized version or the novella. In the stage version of La fin de Lucie Pellegrin , the terminally ill coquette Lucie is visited by her Parisian ‘friends’. The women find her asleep and sit gossiping in her room about Lucie’s past in the beau monde, the wealth she accumulated but then frittered away, and the affairs she had.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 36점의 습작을 테오에게 보내면서 모델을 구하기 어려운 현실을 토로하고, 고갱과 함께 살 경우의 생활비 문제를 신중히 계산한다. 부그로처럼 매끄럽게 그리지 않아 모델들이 초상화를 부끄러워한다고 아쉬워하며, 졸라의 소설 속 인물과 칼라일의 말을 인용해 성공에 대한 초연한 태도와 화가들의 공동체적 삶에 대한 신념을 피력한다.
entries.why: The letter was written before Wednesday, 15 August, the day Van Gogh sent a telegram to Theo to tell him that Milliet would be arriving on Friday (letter 661) – in the present letter he still thinks it will be Sunday. It is also likely that it follows letter 659 of about Sunday, 12 August: in that one he acknowledges receipt of his painting supplies, and this would have enabled him to start the new study of barges with men unloading sand that he mentions here.

Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: The roll that he’ll bring you contains 36 studies;
facts.note: This second consignment from Arles can be reconstructed to a significant extent. As well as the five works mentioned by Van Gogh (see nn. 2 -6 below), the batch certainly included the following seven paintings, which we know that Theo had from later letters: Joseph Roulin (F 433 / JH 1524), Mousmé (F 431 / JH 1519), The harvest (F 412 / JH 1440), Fishing boats at sea (F 417 / JH 1453), Newly mown lawn with a weeping tree (F 428 / JH 1499), Cottages in Saintes-Maries (F 419 / JH 1465) and Rocks with a tree (F 466 / JH 1489). See letters 662, 673, 678 and 680.

facts.said: Now our sister will come soon to spend some time with you; I have no doubt that she’ll enjoy herself.
facts.note: Willemien stayed with Theo for a couple of weeks; she went to Paris on 15 August (FR b2421) and stayed until early September (letter 672). Originally Elisabeth was to have gone with her; cf. letter 615, n. 7.

entries.summary: 밀리에가 금요일 아침 7시 정각 파리의 세르클 밀리테르에서 그림을 전달할 것이라는 내용을 담은 매우 짧은 전보 형식의 편지다. 간결한 실무 연락으로, 밀리에를 통한 파리로의 작품 운송 일정을 알리는 것이 목적이다.
entries.why: Date of postmark: Wednesday, 15 August 1888.

facts.said: Paris Arles 664 18 15 2h30 s milliet will deliver paintings friday morning 7 o’clock sharp cercle militaire
facts.note: The Cercle national des armées de terre et de mer in avenue de l’Opéra was set up in 1887 and was a club for army and naval officers; they could eat there and stay overnight. Milliet probably stayed there while he was in Paris.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 밀리에 중위가 파리에 도착하는 일정을 알리고, 누이 빌레미나가 자신의 습작들을 볼 수 있도록 배려해달라고 부탁한다. 우편배달부 룰랭의 초상화를 한 번의 세션으로 완성한 것을 자신의 강점으로 이야기하며, 도미에처럼 즉흥적으로 인물을 그리는 것에 대한 유혹과 자기 회의를 드러낸다. 모네와 졸라, 모파상 등을 언급하며 다음 세대 화가들에 대한 희망을 이야기한다.
entries.why: Given the statement ‘You’ll have received my telegram’ (l. 1), the letter cannot be dated earlier than Wednesday, 15 August (the date the telegram was sent, letter 661). Since Vincent assumes that Theo will receive the letter before Friday morning (‘It will be easiest ... if you go to see him there at 7 sharp in the morning’, ll. 6-8), he cannot have written it on Thursday. We have therefore dated it – as did Jo van Gogh-Bonger in Brieven 1914, and she may have had a postmark to go on – Wednesday, 15 August 1888.

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: Now, I’ve kept the large portrait of the postman, and his head enclosed herewith is — a single sitting.

works.title: Quay with men unloading sand barges
works.said: I’ve added to this consignment a drawing of the painting that I’m working on now; the boats with man unloading sand.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: No reply from our friend Russell, and Gauguin fully deserved one, for sure.
facts.note: Van Gogh expected a response from Russell to the batch of drawings he had sent him and to his request that Russell buy a work from Gauguin. See letter 652, n. 3.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 곧 소개할 카마르그 목동 파티앙스 에스칼리에의 초상과 우편배달부 룰랭의 초상 데생을 언급하며, 파리 취향의 화상 포르티에가 자신의 거친 화풍을 여전히 거부할 것이라 예상한다. 정확한 재현보다 강렬한 표현을 위해 색을 자의적으로 사용하는 자신의 방법을 예술가 친구의 초상(별처럼 빛나는 파란 배경에 금발)과 농부의 초상(타오르는 오렌지빛 배경) 두 예시로 설명한다. 생활비 문제로 힘들지만 좋은 화가가 되는 것을 선택하겠다는 의지와, 태양 아래서 되찾은 건강에 대한 감사도 전한다.
entries.why: This letter was previously dated Saturday, 11 August 1888 (in exhib. cat. New York 1984, in De brieven 1990 and in Hulsker 1993-1, p. 32). It is clear from the subjects discussed (the portraits of Patience Escalier and the postman Joseph Roulin) that it was written in August, and Van Gogh says that it is Saturday (l. 122). Were this actually to have been 11 August it is strange that he writes about Eugène Boch with so much affection here (ll. 36 ff. and n.

works.title: Portrait of a Peasant (Patience Escalier)
works.said: Today without fail I’ll send you the drawing I made after this painting,

works.title: Peasant of the Camargue / Portrait of Patience Escalier
works.said: Today without fail I’ll send you the drawing I made after this painting,

works.title: The Potato Eaters
works.said: The colour of this portrait of a peasant isn’t as dark as the Nuenen potato eaters — but the very civilized Parisian, Portier , probably so-called because he kicks paintings out of the door — will find himself up against the same question again.

works.title: Portrait of Eugène Boch
works.said: I’d like to do the portrait of an artist friend who dreams great dreams, who works as the nightingale sings, because that’s his nature.

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: I don’t believe that my peasant will do any harm, for example, to the Lautrec that you have,
facts.note: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Young woman at a table, ‘Poudre de riz’, 1887 (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 432. Theo had bought this painting from the artist for 150 francs on 12 January 1888 (FR b1156).

entries.summary: 고갱에게서 거의 한 달째 소식이 없어 그가 브르타뉴에 남을 가능성을 우려하면서도, 테오에게 침대와 가구를 마련할 300프랑을 빌려 노란 집에 정착할 뜻을 강하게 밝힌다. 여인숙 생활을 청산하고 고갱을 맞이할 준비된 집을 갖는 것이 계획의 핵심이며, 고갱이 오지 않더라도 계획을 포기하지 않겠다고 단언한다. 늙은 농부(에스칼리에)의 초상화가 씨 뿌리는 사람보다 낫다고 평가한다.
entries.why: As a rule we would date the letter on or about Sunday, 19 August, given the receipt of the allowance of 100 francs. It emerges from letter 663, however, that the money had not arrived by Saturday; so we have dated the letter Sunday, 19 or Monday, 20 August 1888. This is consistent with Van Gogh’s comment that it has been almost a month since he heard from Gauguin (ll. 15-16): that was letter 646 of about 22 July.

works.title: Portrait of a Peasant (Patience Escalier)
works.said: I believe that the painting of the head of the old peasant

works.title: Peasant of the Camargue / Portrait of Patience Escalier
works.said: Vincent Have you received the drawings of the gardens and the two figure drawings?

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: I believe that the painting of the head of the old peasant  is as strange in colour as the sower,

works.title: Garden with flowers
works.said: Vincent Have you received the drawings of the gardens

facts.said: I’ve just received a letter from Bernard, who joined Gauguin, Laval and someone else at Pont-Aven several days ago.
facts.note: In letter 655 of about 5 August Van Gogh had answered Bernard’s question as to whether Gauguin was still in Pont-Aven in the affirmative. However, Bernard had already decided to go to Pont-Aven before he received it, as we learn from a letter he wrote to his sister Madeleine on 29 July. His plan was to arrive on 8 or 10 August, and Gauguin wrote to Schuffenecker on 14 August 1888: ‘Young Bernard is here and has brought some interesting things back from St-Briac’ (Le petit Bernard est ici et a rapporté de St-Briac des choses intéressantes) (see Harscoët-Maire 1997, p. 180 and Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 210).

facts.said: Now that’s said, I’m not going to Pont-Aven if it means I have to stay at the guest-house there, with those Englishmen and those people from L’Ecole des Beaux-Arts, with whom one debates every evening.
facts.note: This remark about debates with Englishmen and academic artists must have been prompted by Bernard’s letter. In Pont-Aven there was something of a hierarchy among the three hotels where artists stayed: the Americans and British stayed at the Hôtel des Voyageurs, the French and a few less well-off foreigners at the Hôtel du Lion d’Or, and the penniless painters at the Auberge Gloanec. See exhib. cat. Paris 2003, p. 24. Gauguin had written to Van Gogh about his relations with the academic artists in letter 646; he wrote to Schuffenecker on 14 August 1888: ‘All the Americans here are violently against Impressionism.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 인물화에 대한 강렬한 열망을 토로하며 감자 먹는 사람들 시절 습작의 연장선에 있는 새로운 인물 습작을 언급한다. 모래를 하역하는 남자, 엉겅퀴와 나비 떼 그림 구상도 전하며, 작업실을 해바라기 연작으로 장식하려는 계획을 처음으로 밝힌다. 렘브란트의 노년 자화상에서 느끼는 웃음과 기쁨을 이야기하며 고갱과 함께하고 싶은 그리움을 드러낸다.
entries.why: This letter was written in reply to one from Bernard that Van Gogh mentions in letter 664 to Theo of 19 or 20 August. Both these letters must have been written at about the same time, but because the one to Theo says nothing about the plan for a sunflower series outlined here (ll. 58-60), we assume that the letter to Bernard is the later of the two, and we have therefore dated it on or about Tuesday, 21 August 1888.

works.title: Portrait of a Peasant (Patience Escalier)
works.said: Ah, I do have a new figure all the same,

works.title: Quay with men unloading sand barges
works.said: It’s just a sketch, or rather, a rough sketch done out in the mistral.

works.title: The Potato Eaters
works.said: Ah, I do have a new figure all the same, which is absolutely a continuation of certain studies of heads done in Holland; I showed you them once, with a painting from that time, potato eaters.

works.title: Peasant of the Camargue / Portrait of Patience Escalier
works.said: Well — it turned into something entirely different, while still being correct.

works.title: Portrait of Patience Escalier
works.said: Well — it turned into something entirely different, while still being correct.

works.title: Thistles
works.said: Next, I’m attempting to do dusty thistles with a great swarm of butterflies swirling above them.

works.title: Grass and Butterflies
works.said: Next, I’m attempting to do dusty thistles with a great swarm of butterflies swirling above them.

facts.said: I’m thinking of decorating my studio with half a dozen paintings of Sunflowers.
facts.note: In his idea for a decorative scheme Van Gogh may have been influenced in part by Bernard, who had done something similar for his studio. See letter 596, n. 1. Van Gogh worked on his decoration for the studio and other rooms in the Yellow House from mid-August until the end of December 1888, starting with a series of paintings of sunflowers. He bore in mind the possibility that this integrated series (he spoke of an ‘ensemble’ and ‘a whole’) could be shown outside the Yellow House, and considered exhibiting it in the offices of the Revue Indépendante.

facts.said: Well — it turned into something entirely different, while still being correct.
facts.note: If Van Gogh did send a drawing, it has not survived. The only known drawing after the portrait, Patience Escalier (‘The peasant’) (F 1460 / JH 1549), was sent to Theo with letter 663. Bernard probably did, though, get the drawing Patience Escalier (‘The peasant’) (F 1461 / JH 1564), since its provenance goes back to Ambroise Vollard, who bought many works by Van Gogh from Bernard between 1894 and 1905. However, that drawing was made after the second portrait of Escalier (F 444 / JH 1563) which dates from later in August (see letter 671) and so cannot be the one referred to here.

facts.said: But since Giotto, a sickly character, that’s the way things are.
facts.note: The sense of this sentence is not entirely clear. It is possible that Van Gogh intended to write ‘ainsi’ (so) instead of ‘ici’ (here), and it is also conceivable that he didn’t finish the sentence.

entries.summary: 고갱이 아직 남프랑스로 올 뜻이 있다는 소식을 전하며, 반 고흐는 함께 쓸 화실을 꾸미겠다는 기대감에 부풀어 해바라기 연작 3점을 한 번에 그려나가고 있다고 전한다. 노란 꽃병에 담긴 열두 송이 해바라기를 포함해 파랑과 노랑의 교향곡 같은 장식화를 구상하며, 아침 일찍부터 시들기 전에 서둘러 완성하려 애쓴다. 화구상 타셋의 캔버스와 물감에 대한 실용적 언급, 그리고 인상주의를 넘어 누구나 이해할 수 있는 단순한 화법을 찾고 싶다는 바람도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: See letter 665, Date, for the sequence of letters 665-671 and our dating of them.

people.name: François Alexandre Joseph Léon Bourgeois
people.note: (1830-1892) seller of artists’ materials and owner of a paint factory in Paris

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: Koning has written that he’s going to stay in The Hague; he intends to send you some studies.
facts.note: Around 15 September 1888 Koning, who had returned to Winschoten after he left Paris, moved to 163 Van Diemenstraat in The Hague (FR b1080-b1081). He wrote to Theo about his studies: ‘I can well imagine that at the moment I’m nowhere near where I want to be, but I firmly believe it will come. Anyway, judge for yourself. This morning I packed up the best of my studies or paintings, call them what you will, and I shall send them to you today’ (FR 1080). On 18 September 1888 Koning sent seven studies to Paris: ‘There are 4 no. 10 ... 2 no. 8 and 1 no. 6’ (FR b1081).

facts.said: Next door to your shop, in the restaurant, as you know, there’s such a beautiful decoration of flowers there; I still remember the big sunflower in the window.
facts.note: Next door to Boussod, Valadon & Cie, at 21 boulevard Montmartre, there was a restaurant belonging to the Duval chain (Almanach du commerce de Paris 1886). See letter 502, n. 8. Around 1900 the restaurant was called Le Soleil, as can be seen on a contemporary postcard. See exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, pp. 50-51.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent Gauguin said that Bernard had made an album of croquis of mine, and that he’d shown it to him.
facts.note: Nothing is known about this album. Van Gogh had sent two batches of drawings to Bernard in mid-July; see letter 641, n. 1.

facts.said: I have another study on the go, of dusty thistles with an innumerable swarm of white and yellow butterflies.
facts.note: This study is not known, but the subject may have been similar to that of the drawing Thistles by the roadside (F 1466 / JH 1552). For an earlier attribution see letter 665, n. 8.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 파리 체류를 즐기라 전하며, 노란 해바라기 열두 송이로 작업실 전체를 장식하려는 계획을 밝힌다. 밀레, 코로, 들라크루아 등 거장들의 작품을 감상하라 권하고, 룰랭 가족이 아이 이름을 마르셀로 지은 혁명적인 세례식 일화를 유쾌하게 전하며 고갱이 오면 프로방스를 함께 도보 여행하고 싶다는 바람을 밝힌다.
entries.why: This letter was written on the same day as letter 666 and is accordingly dated Tuesday, 21 or Wednesday, 22 August 1888. See also letter 665, Date.

facts.said: If I can get the mother and father to agree to let me paint it, then I’ll do a child in a cradle one of these days.
facts.note: It was some time before Van Gogh put this plan into effect: he painted the whole Roulin family, including the baby, in December 1888 (cf. letter 723).

facts.said: Then he sang the Marseillaise hideously and named the child Marcelle, like the daughter of the good General Boulanger,
facts.note: General Boulanger had called his daughter, born on 12 December 1868, Marcelle.

facts.said: Then he sang the Marseillaise hideously and named the child Marcelle, like the daughter of the good General Boulanger, to the great vexation of this innocent child’s grandmother
facts.note: This grandmother was Rosalie Pelicot-Décès, Augustine Roulin’s mother. She lived in Lambesc, a small village some 55 km to the east of Arles (see letter 748, n. 1). Joseph Roulin’s mother, Marguerite Cathérine Roulin-Aubran, had died in 1865 (Mairie de Lambesc).

facts.said: Do you remember that one day at the Hôtel Drouot we saw a quite extraordinary Manet, some large pink peonies and their green leaves on a light background?
facts.note: Edouard Manet, Vase of peonies on a pedestal, 1864 (Paris, Musée d’Orsay). Ill. 227. Vincent and Theo saw this work on 5 June 1886 during the sale of John Saulnier’s collection in the Hôtel Drouot in Paris, where it was listed as cat. no. 62, Vase of flowers by Paul [sic] Manet. See auct. cat. Paris 1886.

facts.said: Another reason why Seurat’s La Grande Jatte, Signac’s landscapes with coarse stippling,
facts.note: Van Gogh could have seen Signac’s work in Paris at the VIIIe Exposition de peinture (15 May - 15 June 1886), the second and third exhibitions of the Indépendants (21 August - 21 September 1886 and 26 March - 3 May 1887 respectively) and at La Revue Indépendante in the winter of 1887-1888. There is nothing to indicate that he had been to Signac’s studio.

facts.said: Another reason why Seurat’s La Grande Jatte,
facts.note: Georges Seurat, La Grande Jatte (Sunday afternoon on the island of La Grande Jatte), 1884-1886. (The Art Institute of Chicago. Helen Birch Bartlett Memorial Collection). Ill. 425. Van Gogh probably saw the work at the VIIIe Exposition de peinture (15 May - 15 June 1886), and in February 1888 in Seurat’s studio; see letter 589, n. 19.

facts.said: But I consulted this postman whom I painted,
facts.note: Van Gogh had painted two portraits of Roulin the postman in late July and early August: Joseph Roulin (F 432 / JH 1522) and Joseph Roulin (F 433 / JH 1524).

facts.said: However, let’s not forget Bouvard et Pécuchet, let’s not forget À vau l’eau,
facts.note: Joris-Karl Huysmans’ novel A vau-l’eau (1882) examines petit-bourgeois life in the suburbs of Paris. The central character, Folantin, dreams of the high life, but he is poor, eats in cheap cafés and seeks relief in brothels to satisfy his yearning for love. He is so bored that he is constantly looking for new challenges, yet all he finds is the misery of the everyday, ennui.

facts.said: Ah — Macknight has cleared off at last
facts.note: Macknight left Fontvieille in late August 1888 for Moret-sur-Loing. He headed to Brittany in November. See Bailey 2007, pp. 33-34.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌레미나에게 프랑스어로 편지 쓰는 것이 더 편하다고 말하며, 조각과 회화에 대한 그녀의 감수성을 칭찬한다. 몽티셀리를 정신적 아버지처럼 여기며 그의 강렬한 노랑과 오렌지색 화풍을 자신이 이어가고 있다고 이야기하고, 고갱이 오면 몽티셀리처럼 차려입고 마르세유를 걷겠다는 계획을 유쾌하게 전한다. 노란 배경의 해바라기 연작(14송이)을 준비 중이며 언젠가 마르세유에서 전시하고 싶다는 바람도 밝힌다.
entries.why: This letter to Willemien, who was staying with Theo in Paris, was probably enclosed with letter 669, so we have dated it on or about Sunday, 26 August 1888. See also the notes to letter 665, Date.

facts.said: Theo should have them, and I really urge you to read them, first because they’re really beautiful, and also, English people are talking about them a lot at the moment.
facts.note: The American poet Walt Whitman’s reputation had been established in England since the 1870s; in France his work did not really start to be appreciated until the 1880s and 1890s. Whitman’s poems were published in a French translation in the magazines La Vogue and La Revue Indépendante in 1886 and 1887. Willemien took Vincent’s advice. As early as October 1888 she wrote to Theo: ‘Your Whitman’s doing the rounds, too. I thought it was so wonderfully good that for the moment it has spoiled my taste for lighter poetry altogether, or rather taken it away.

facts.said: When friend Gauguin’s here, and we go to Marseille, I firmly intend to walk there on the Canebière, dressed exactly like him, as I’ve seen his portrait, with an enormous yellow hat, a black velvet jacket, white trousers, yellow gloves and a reed cane and with a great southern air.
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring to Jules Monge’s Adolphe Monticelli, 1883 (Paris, Musée d’Orsay), or the similar drawing on the cover of the weekly La Provence Artistique et Pittoresque 1 (21 August 1881), no. 12. Ill. 2235. In the accompanying article A. Meyer described Monticelli as follows: ‘I can still see him striding up and down the Avenues, dressed in a baggy black velvet jacket, over immaculate white trousers, dazzling long cuffs showing above his yellow gloves, dispensing good humour all along this fashionable walk of the time.’ (Je le vois encore arpentant les Allées; vêtu d’un grand sac en velours noir, sur un…

facts.said: When friend Gauguin’s here, and we go to Marseille, I firmly intend to walk there on the Canebière,
facts.note: ‘La Canebière’ is Marseille’s main boulevard, which leads to the old docks.

entries.summary: 집세 지불을 위해 돈을 빨리 보내달라는 요청과 함께, 아를 여인과 늙은 농부 에스칼리에를 모델로 한 그림 작업을 전한다. 모델을 섰던 아를 여인이 선불을 받고는 나타나지 않아 곤란을 겪은 일화를 전하며, 정물화와 낡은 신발 그림도 작업 중이라고 알린다. 인물화에 대한 야심과 함께 미스트랄로 인한 고단함을 토로한다.
entries.why: Since Vincent mentions paying the rent on the house (ll. 1*-2), the letter must date from the last week of August. He suggests that Theo might send a money order (so that the allowance would arrive on Saturday). The letter with the money did indeed come on Saturday, 1 September (see letter 672). Assuming this means that Theo complied with Vincent’s request, he must have received the present letter on Friday at the latest. We have consequently dated the letter Wednesday, 29 or Thursday, 30 August 1888.

facts.said: I have a bouquet on the go as well, and also a still life of a pair of old shoes.
facts.note: Since Van Gogh had expressed a desire to paint a study of oleanders shortly before (see letter 660), it seems likely that he carried out his plan here. There are two still lifes of oleanders: Oleander branches in a majolica jug (F 593 / JH 1566) and Oleander branches in a majolica jug (F 594 / JH 1567). Zinnias in a majolica jug (F 592 / JH 1568) also dates from late August, early September, given the flowering times of the species pictured (zinnias, asters and marigolds). The still life of shoes is Shoes (F 461 / JH 1569).

facts.said: He probably doesn’t have a sou at the moment.
facts.note: Van Gogh expected a response from Russell to the batch of drawings he sent him and to his request that he buy a work from Gauguin. See letter 652, n. 3.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 집세 갱신 문제로 고갱이 올 경우를 대비해 3개월 단위 임대로 결정했다고 알린다. 모델 구하기의 어려움과 고립감에서 오는 낙담을 토로하면서도 고갱과 다른 화가들도 같은 처지임을 스스로 위안 삼는다. 발자크 소설과 도데의 소설을 읽으며 문명사회의 공허함을 느낀다는 소회도 함께 전한다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written on 1 September. We know this because the landlord came to collect the rent that day and Van Gogh had to let him know whether or not he wanted to go on renting the Yellow House (l. 6). It emerges from letter 654 that the landlord usually came for his money on the first of the month. Jo van Gogh-Bonger also gave it this date in Brieven 1914 and she may have had a postmark to go on. Accordingly, we date it Saturday, 1 September 1888.

facts.said: I believe that I’ll have to read a book about elephant hunting, or a totally mendacious book of categorically impossible adventures, by Gustave Aimard
facts.note: Gustave Aimard, who travelled widely, wrote more than a hundred novels of adventure and travel that were very popular in their day, including Les trappeurs de l’Arkansas (1858) and La loi de lynch (1859). Van Gogh may have come up with the name by way of Tartarin, the self-styled lion hunter in Daudet’s eponymous novels, who is a great fan of Aimard’s tales.

facts.said: I’m sending you 3 volumes of Balzac today;
facts.note: The three volumes of Balzac that Van Gogh sent probably included the novel César Birotteau (1837), which he had promised to send Theo; see letter 636, n. 8.

entries.summary: 벨기에 화가 외젠 보흐와 함께 시간을 보내며 그의 초상화(별이 빛나는 하늘을 배경으로 한 '시인')를 그린 이야기를 전한다. 도데의 소설 '랭모르텔'과 '타르타랭'을 비교하며 문학적 감상을 나누고, 초상화를 통해 영원한 것을 표현하고 싶다는 예술관—델라크루아적 색채로 인물의 정신을 담아내려는 포부—를 진지하게 피력한다. 고갱과 함께 지낼 경우의 생활비 계산, 여동생 빌레미나에 대한 걱정도 함께 언급된다.
entries.why: In letter 672 of Saturday, 1 September, Van Gogh says he is reading Daudet’s L’immortel; in the present one he writes that he has meanwhile finished it. The letter probably precedes letter 676, which dates from 8 September, because in that he says he hopes to achieve a good result with the portrait of Boch; in the present letter he has only just made the first sketch for the painting. facts.said: What a difference, then, living together — myself I have to pay 45 a month for my lodging alone.
facts.note: Van Gogh says that he pays 45 francs ‘for my lodging alone’; in other words his meals were not included in that sum. He paid 1 franc a night for his room in the Café de la Gare, and 15 francs a month for the Yellow House. See letters 602 and 611.

facts.said: You can see clearly from the drawing of the small seascape
facts.note: The drawing after the above seascape is Fishing boats at sea (F 1430b / JH 1541). Vincent had sent it to Theo on 8 August (see letter 657).

facts.said: The Belgian was saying that with Macknight he paid 80 francs for board and lodging.
facts.note: Macknight and Boch stayed at the Café de l’Alcazar in Fontvieille; see letter 650, n. 20.

facts.said: I believe you’ll enjoy meeting him, he’s still young.
facts.note: Boch turned 33 on 1 September, so he was only two years younger than Van Gogh. By the time he wrote letter 674 Van Gogh had found out his age.

facts.said: I’ve finished Daudet’s L’immortel — I rather like the remark by the sculptor Védrine, who says that achieving fame is something like when smoking, sticking your cigar in your mouth by the lighted end.
facts.note: A reference to Alphonse Daudet, L’immortel (1888): ‘Fame... I have tasted it two or three times, I know what it is... look, when you’re smoking you sometimes happen to pick up your cigar by the wrong end. Well, then, that’s fame. A good cigar with the lit end and the ash in your mouth...’ (La gloire... j’en ai goûté deux ou trois fois, je sais ce que c’est... tiens, il t’arrive en fumant de prendre ton cigare à rebours, eh bien! c’est ça gloire. Un bon cigare dans la bouche par le côté du feu et de la cendre...). See Daudet 1986-1994, vol. 3, p. 712 (chapter 3).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 벨기에 화가 보흐와의 만남, 그의 화가 여동생 안나와 자신의 여동생 빌레미나의 만남을 주선하려는 구상을 전한다. 물감이 거의 떨어져 대량 주문이 필요하다고 알리며, 고갱과 베르나르의 답신이 없어 고갱의 아를행에 대해 점점 회의적으로 변하는 심정을 토로하고, 남프랑스에 예술가들을 위한 영구적인 스튜디오를 마련하고 싶다는 꿈을 다시 이야기한다.
entries.why: Since Van Gogh says in letter 673 of Monday, 3 September that he will be seeing Boch again ‘tomorrow’, and he writes in the present letter that he expects him ‘this morning’, we have dated this letter Tuesday, 4 September 1888.

facts.said: Waiting until you’re very rich is a sorry system, and that’s what I don’t like about the De Goncourts, although it’s the truth — they end up paying a hundred thousand francs for their home and their peace of mind.
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring here to what Jules and Edmond de Goncourt noted in their Journal on 12 September 1868: ‘After buying this house for almost a hundred thousand francs, which bourgeois logic would view as totally unreasonable given our limited funds, we offer two thousand francs, which is more than the Emperor or de Rothschild would pay for a passing fancy, for a Japanese monstrosity, a fascinating bronze, which something told us we just had to have’.

facts.said: Which you’ll find attached.
facts.note: Van Gogh had enclosed this paint order and letter for Tasset with letter 668, sent on 23 or 24 August, in other words rather more than ‘a week ago’. On 8 September (letter 676) he confirmed that Tasset’s consignment had arrived. In view of the short intervening period, this cannot possibly have been the new order sent with the present letter, so it must be the order that went with letter 668. See also Arrangement above.

facts.said: His sister is even older than he is.
facts.note: Boch turned 33 on 1 September 1888. His sister Anna was seven years older. Boch had lived in Paris since 1879 and travelled widely: In 1881 he went to Italy, and between 1885 and 1910 he visited, among other places, Corsica, Spain, the south of France, the Balearics and Algeria. See exhib. cat. Saarbrücken 1971, pp. 44, 47-48.

entries.summary: 테오가 보낸 300프랑에 감사하며, 숙소 주인에게 화가 나 사흘 밤을 새워 '밤의 카페' 그림을 그렸다는 사연을 전한다. 붉은색과 초록색으로 인간의 끔찍한 정념을 표현하려 했다고 설명하며, 방의 색채 구성을 상세히 묘사한다. 고갱과 베르나르에게도 편지를 썼고, 고갱이 온다면 가구를 마련해 정착할 곳을 만들고 싶다는 바람도 덧붙인다.
entries.why: The day he wrote this letter Van Gogh had read the report of Lévy-Bing’s suicide in L’Intransigeant (ll. 53-54). This was published on Saturday, 8 September 1888 (see n. 9). Jo van Gogh-Bonger also gave this date in Brieven 1914 – she may have had a postmark.
