people.note: (?-?) manager at Siegfried Bing's gallery in Paris

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: When Paul Mantz saw Delacroix’s violent and exalted sketch, Christ’s boat, at the exhibition that we saw in the Champs-Elysées, he turned away from it and cried out in his article, ‘I did not know that one could be so terrifying with blue and green’.
facts.note: At the beginning of June 1886 Vincent and Theo had been to see the sale exhibition of John Saulnier’s collection at the Drouot auction house; among the works on show was Delacroix’s Christ asleep during the tempest . The sale was on 5 June, the viewing days were 2 and 4 June (Lugt 1938-1987, no. 48531) See auct. cat. Paris 1886, and Johnson 1981-1989, vol. 3, pp. 232-238. See also letter 632, n. 12.

facts.said: It gives me great pleasure that Pissarro found something in the young girl.
facts.note: Camille Pissarro had been to see Theo in the afternoon of Thursday, 6 September 1888, as we can make out from a letter he wrote to his son Lucien. See Correspondance Pissarro 1980-1991, vol. 2, pp. 250-252 (letter 505). Theo had shown Pissarro the painting Mousmé (F 431 / JH 1519).

facts.said: My dear Theo, Thank you a thousand times for your kind letter and the 300 francs it contained
facts.note: In letter 664 Vincent had asked Theo for a loan of 300 francs to buy furniture for the Yellow House.

facts.said: I’d given a piece of my mind to the said lodging-house keeper,
facts.note: This must be Joseph Ginoux, from whom Van Gogh rented a room in the Café de la Gare; see letter 606.

facts.said: Well, to the great delight of the lodging-house keeper, the postman whom I’ve already painted,
facts.note: Van Gogh had painted two portraits of Roulin in late July and early August: Joseph Roulin (F 432 / JH 1522) and Joseph Roulin (F 433 / JH 1524).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 노란 집을 손수 꾸민 이야기를 자세히 전하며, 고갱을 맞이할 방을 해바라기 그림으로 장식하겠다는 계획을 설명한다. 도미에풍의 개성 있는 아틀리에를 만들고 싶다는 포부와 함께, 밤의 카페 그림에서 표현하려 한 광기와 파멸의 분위기(핑크·붉은색·녹색의 강렬한 대비)를 상세히 서술한다. 아버지를 닮은 노인 손님을 우연히 목격한 일화도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: In his previous letter of Saturday, 8 September (676), Vincent thanked Theo for sending him 300 francs and promised to write again ‘tomorrow’ (l. 87). It is probable that he went out and bought furniture as soon as he got the money – a Sunday would seem to be less likely. The present letter, in which he says he made a start on furnishing the house yesterday (l. 5), must therefore have been written on Sunday, 9 September 1888.

works.title: The Yellow House
works.said: One of these days you’ll see a painting of the little house itself, in full sunshine or else with the window lit and the starry sky.

works.title: Still Life with French novels and glass with a rose
works.said: Not that I insist, but it’s so that the studies shouldn’t be confused with compositions, and to say beforehand that the first exhibition would be one of studies.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: Because there’s still hardly more than the sower

works.title: The Night Cafe in Arles
works.said: My dear Theo, I’ve just put the croquis of the new painting, the ‘Night café’, in the post — as well as another one that I did some time ago.

works.title: The Night Café

works.title: Three Sunflowers in a Vase
works.said: The room where you’ll stay then, or which will be Gauguin’s if Gauguin comes, will have a decoration of large yellow sunflowers on its white walls.

people.name: Theodorus van Gogh
people.note: (1822-1885) husband of Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus, father of Vincent, clergyman

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: My dear Theo, I’ve just put the croquis of the new painting, the ‘Night café’, in the post — as well as another one that I did some time ago.
facts.note: Vincent sent Theo the drawing The night café (F 1463 / JH 1576) after the painting The night café (F 463 / JH 1575). Assuming that the remark about the Japanese prints also refers to the other drawing he sent, this could have been Fishing boats on the beach at Saintes-Maries (F 1429 / JH 1459). Like F 1463, this drawing, which dates from June 1888, was done in the Japanese style (‘coloured in flat tints’ as Van Gogh himself put it in letter 614).

facts.said: Now yesterday I worked at furnishing the house.
facts.note: At Vincent’s request Theo had sent him 300 francs to furnish the Yellow House; see letter 676.

facts.said: He who, looking at a Sisley — Sisley, the most tactful and sensitive of the Impressionists — had already said: ‘I can’t stop myself thinking that the artist who painted that was a little tipsy’.
facts.note: Tersteeg’s comment probably related to one of the three landscapes Theo had bought from Sisley in 1887, which were still in Boussod, Valadon & Cie’s stock: The first days of autumn (D648), The abandoned house (D652) and Plateau at Roches-Courtaut . See Rewald 1986-1, pp. 16, 32, 97. Tersteeg had called in at the Paris branch in June 1888. The last of these works was also part of the batch of modern paintings that Theo had sent to the Hague branch of Goupil’s in March 1888. See letter 589, n. 4.

facts.said: One of these days you’ll see a painting of the little house itself, in full sunshine or else with the window lit and the starry sky.
facts.note: Van Gogh painted The Yellow House (‘The street’) (F 464 / JH 1589) at the end of September.

facts.said: The room where you’ll stay then, or which will be Gauguin’s if Gauguin comes, will have a decoration of large yellow sunflowers on its white walls.
facts.note: Van Gogh had done four paintings of sunflowers in the last week of August: F 453 / JH 1559, F 459 / JH 1560, F 456 / JH 1561 and F 454 / JH 1562. As we learn from the rest of the letter, he intended the last two no. 30 canvases for Gauguin’s room.

entries.summary: 고갱이 보낸 곤궁을 호소하는 편지에 대해 테오가 여비까지 부담하는 것은 부당하다는 의견을 밝히며, 만약 고갱이 자신의 그림 전부를 공유하는 형태의 동업이라면 모두에게 이득이 될 것이라고 제안한다. 렘브란트와 프란스 할스의 초상화 속 평온함을 언급하며 함께할 미래에 대한 기대와 우려를 동시에 드러내고, 고갱이 결혼한 몸임을 상기시키며 조건을 명확히 할 필요성을 강조한다.
entries.why: The remark ‘[you] have just sent the money ... for furnishing the house’ (l. 31) would indicate that this letter was written soon after 8 September, the day Vincent had received 300 francs (letter 676). At this point he has not yet replied to Gauguin’s letter; he did so on or about 11 September (letter 680, l. 71). We, like Merlhès and Dorn, have consequently dated the present letter on or about Monday, 10 September 1888.

facts.said: I find it absolutely unfair that you, who’ve just sent the money that you yourself have had to borrow for furnishing the house,
facts.note: Theo had sent Vincent 300 francs to furnish the Yellow House; see letter 676. Whether Theo had actually had to borrow money is questionable; he may have suggested something of the kind in order to curb Vincent’s spending.

facts.said: Russell replied, by the way — negatively as far as buying a Gauguin is concerned,
facts.note: Van Gogh had sent twelve drawings to Russell at the beginning of August 1888 in the hope of making him favourably disposed towards buying a work from Gauguin. See letter 652, n. 3.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Enclosed herewith letter from Gauguin, which arrived at the same time as a letter from Bernard.
facts.note: The letter to Gauguin is letter 675; the letter from Bernard has not survived (it was not sent on to Theo).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 라발과 자신 사이에서 망설이는 상황에 대해 테오에게 솔직한 판단을 전하며, 고갱이 오든 안 오든 자신은 꾸준히 작업하겠다고 다짐한다. 낡은 물레방아와 공장이 있는 풍경, 도스토옙스키에 관한 글에서 받은 영감 등 여러 습작을 소개하며 노란 집이 정착된 화실로 자리잡아가는 데 안도감을 느낀다. 별이 빛나는 밤 그림에 대한 열망도 다시 언급한다.
entries.why: The letter was in any event written after 8 September, since it contains a reference to an article on Dostoevsky that had appeared on the eighth in Le Figaro, and again on the tenth in L’Intransigeant (see n. 5). It probably dates from the first half of the week because Van Gogh has done two new paintings since The night café (which was finished on Saturday, 8 September; see letter 676). Later in the week he must have been working on three paintings, as he reports in letter 681 of Sunday, 16 September.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: My letter to Gauguin has gone off; I asked them for an exchange if they wish; I would so much like to have here Gauguin’s portrait of Bernard and Bernard’s of Gauguin.

works.title: The Old Mill
works.said: I have a study of an old mill, painted in broken tones

works.title: Quay with men unloading sand barges
works.said: My letter to Gauguin has gone off; I asked them for an exchange if they wish; I would so much like to have here Gauguin’s portrait of Bernard and Bernard’s of Gauguin.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: I have a study of an old mill, painted in broken tones like the Oak on the rock; that study which you said you had framed with the sower.

works.title: Rocks
works.said: I have a study of an old mill, painted in broken tones like the Oak on the rock; that study which you said you had framed with the sower.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: Exaggerated studies like the sower, like the night café

works.title: Summer evening in Arles
works.said: I have a third study now, of a landscape with factory, and an enormous sun in a red sky, above red roofs, in which nature seems to be in a rage, on a day of nasty mistral.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: Included herewith an article that will interest you; you’d be well advised to go to see that.
facts.note: Later in the letter it transpires that this is about a short report on Dostoevsky. It must have been Jules Prével’s article, ‘Courrier des théâtres’, which discussed the Russian writer and his play Crime and Punishment . This piece was in Le Figaro on Saturday, 8 September 1888, p. 4, and in L’Intransigeant on 10 September 1888, in the ‘Theatres’ column by Dom Blasius.

facts.said: But Gauguin will have to be loyal, but seeing that the arrival of his friend Laval has opened up another resource for him for the time being, I believe he’s hesitating between Laval and us.
facts.note: Charles Laval had been in Pont-Aven since July; see letter 646.

facts.said: My letter to Gauguin has gone off; I asked them for an exchange if they wish; I would so much like to have here Gauguin’s portrait of Bernard and Bernard’s of Gauguin.
facts.note: In this letter to Gauguin and Bernard, which has not survived, Van Gogh had suggested that the two should paint each other’s portraits in Pont-Aven in exchange for work by him. The exchange is mentioned several times in subsequent letters. Gauguin and Bernard complied with Van Gogh’s request in early October, but instead of painting each other’s portrait they opted to paint a self-portrait with the other’s portrait in the background (see letter 692). In exchange Gauguin got Self-portrait (F 476 / JH 1581) and Bernard Quay with sand barges (F 449 / JH 1558); see letters 697 and 698.

facts.said: And Durand-Ruel didn’t earn from it either; at one point he had quantities of those paintings without being able to dispose of them.
facts.note: After noticing Monet’s work at the 1870 Salon, Durand-Ruel exhibited a painting by the artist in his London branch that same year. In 1872 he bought 29 paintings directly from Monet, and a further 34 the following year. He was taking a significant risk, for many of them remained in his stock for years. See Wildenstein 1996, vol. 1, pp. 86, 99-100.

facts.said: Exaggerated studies like the sower, like the night café now, usually seem to me atrociously ugly and bad, but when I’m moved by something, as here by this little article on Dostoevsky,
facts.note: Van Gogh would have been moved above all by the description of Dostoevsky’s hard life; he was epileptic and lived in great poverty for years. He was condemned to death for treason, but was granted a last-minute reprieve. He was then sent to a forced labour camp in Siberia, where he wrote The house of the dead (see letter 812, n. 16).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생에게 노란 집의 방 두 개를 꾸미는 계획—손님방에는 벨기에 화가 보흐의 초상화를, 자기 방에는 대형 해바라기 연작을—을 설명하며 일본식 배치 미학을 언급한다. 밤의 카페 실내화와 별이 빛나는 밤하늘을 검은색 없이 표현하는 새로운 시도를 자세히 묘사하며, 아를이 이미 '일본'과 같다고 느낀다고 말한다. 모파상과 발자크 등 문학 이야기를 곁들이며, 병들고 초라해질수록 더 밝고 빛나는 색으로 복수하고 싶다는 예술적 다짐을 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent tells Willemien that he sent Theo the drawing of the night café ‘today’ (l. 48); he wrote the same thing in letter 677, so that the first part of the present letter – written the same day – must be dated Sunday, 9 September 1888. In ll. 97*-99, however, he says that he had put the letter aside for ‘several days’ and that he was now carrying on with it.

works.title: The Night Cafe in Arles
works.said: Today I sent Theo a drawing of it, which is like a Japanese print.

works.title: Café Terrace at Night
works.said: With nothing but beautiful blue, violet and green, and in these surroundings the lighted square is coloured pale sulphur, lemon green.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: I’ve also done a new portrait of myself, as a study, in which I look like a Japanese.

works.title: Portrait of Eugène Boch
works.said: I have one to start with, the portrait of a young Belgian Impressionist; I’ve painted him as something of a poet, his refined and nervous head standing out against a deep ultramarine background of the night sky, with the twinkling of the stars.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: I want to stuff at least 6 very large canvases into this tiny little room, the way the Japanese do, especially the huge bouquets of sunflowers.

works.title: Sunflowers (Munich version)
works.said: I want to stuff at least 6 very large canvases into this tiny little room, the way the Japanese do, especially the huge bouquets of sunflowers.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: In this canvas there are 6 or 7 different reds, from blood-red to delicate pink, contrasting with the same number of pale or dark greens.

works.title: Three White Cottages in Saintes-Maries
works.said: I myself thought you would have taken the white huts under the blue sky among the greenery, which I did at Saintes-Maries, on the Mediterranean.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: With nothing but beautiful blue, violet and green, and in these surroundings the lighted square is coloured pale sulphur, lemon green.
facts.note: Café terrace at night (F 467 / JH 1580). The pavement café is the Grand Café du Forum in the place du Forum in Arles.

facts.said: My dear sister, Your letter gave me great pleasure, and today I have the leisure to reply to you in peace and quiet.
facts.note: Vincent had received this letter from Willemien on Sunday, 2 September; see letter 673.

facts.said: Today I sent Theo a drawing of it, which is like a Japanese print.
facts.note: Vincent had sent Theo the drawing of The night café (F 1463 / JH 1576); see letter 677.

facts.said: Theo wrote telling me that he has given you some Japanese prints.
facts.note: On 19 October 1888 Willemien wrote to Theo and told him that she got great pleasure from the Japanese prints. There must have been a considerable number, since she said that she had given fifteen or so to a friend (FR b2275).

facts.said: I say this because the beginning of Bel-ami is precisely the description of a starry night in Paris, with the lighted cafés of the boulevard,
facts.note: For Maupassant’s Bel-ami see letter 568, n. 11. Van Gogh is referring to the description of the boulevards of Paris on a summer evening at the beginning of the book. There is no mention of a starry sky, but Maupassant does describe the brightly-lit café’s Duroy, the central character, walks past: ‘The big cafés, full of people, overflowed out on to the pavements, displaying their clientele of drinkers in the harsh, bright lights of their illuminated facades’.

entries.summary: 노란 집으로 이사할 준비를 하며 침대와 생활용품 구입 비용을 테오에게 요청하는 실무적인 내용이 중심이다. 정원의 늘어진 나무와 삼나무를 그린 큰 캔버스, 가스등이 켜진 카페 테라스의 밤 풍경, 거울을 보고 그린 자화상까지 이번 주에 완성한 세 점을 소개한다. 피가로지에서 읽은 인상주의풍 유리집 묘사에 영감을 받아 노란 집도 예술가의 집으로 꾸미고 싶다는 바람을 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh discusses an article that had appeared in Le Figaro on Saturday, 15 September (see n. 6). Since he also says that he will be moving into the Yellow House the next day and it is likely that he paid his hotel by the week and would therefore leave on a Monday, we have dated the letter Sunday, 16 September 1888. Monday, 17 September 1888, the date Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave in Brieven 1914, may have been the date of the postmark (the letter was written in the evening (l. 2).

works.title: The Poet's Garden
works.said: 30 square canvas of a corner of a garden with a weeping tree, grass, round-trimmed cedar bushes, an oleander bush.

works.title: Café Terrace at Night
works.said: The second shows the outside of a café, lit on the terrace outside by a large gas-lamp in the blue night, with a patch of starry blue sky.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: The third painting this week is a portrait of myself, almost colourless, in ashy tones against a pale Veronese background.

works.title: Sunny Lawn in a Public Park
works.said: Therefore the same corner of a garden of which you already have a study in the last consignment.

facts.said: This house, if I remember well, must be in Auteuil.
facts.note: Van Gogh got his information from Maurice de Fleury’s article ‘La maison d’un moderniste, L’Architecture de demain’, in Le Figaro, Supplément Littéraire 14 (15 September 1888), no. 37, pp. 2-3. The term ‘Impressionist house’ does not occur in the article. Fleury wrote: ‘Just like the house of an artist (the delightful home of this prince: Edmond de Goncourt), it is in Auteuil that you could find the house of a modernist.’ (Tout comme la maison d’un artiste (le délectant logis de ce prince: Edmond de Goncourt), c’est à Auteuil que vous pourriez trouver la maison d’un moderniste.) He described the house built for…

entries.summary: 빈센트는 마침내 노란 집에서 첫날 밤을 보냈다며 큰 기쁨을 표현하고, 가구 마련을 위해 추가 송금을 요청한다. 이 집을 화가들의 피난처이자 후대에 이어질 스튜디오로 만들겠다는 원대한 포부를 밝히며, 고갱과 베르나르의 합류 문제를 신중하게 다루어야 한다고 조언한다. 들라크루아가 색채를 위해 아프리카까지 갔던 것처럼 남프랑스의 빛과 색이 갖는 예술적 가치를 강조한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for his allowance of 50 francs and for the 16 September issue of Le Courrier Français that he had sent (see n. 1). From the strap-line of this newspaper – ‘published every Saturday’ (paraissant tous les samedis) – it would appear that this issue had actually come out on Saturday, 15 September. The letter was written early in the morning, as we learn from the opening words of letter 683, which was written later the same day. Van Gogh repeats what he wrote in ‘yesterday’s’ letter (ll. 21 and 38).

works.title: The Poet's Garden
works.said: 30 square canvas on the go, a garden again, or rather a walk under plane trees, with green turf and black clumps of pines.

works.title: A Lane in the Public Garden at Arles
works.said: 30 square canvas on the go, a garden again, or rather a walk under plane trees, with green turf and black clumps of pines.

people.name: Agostina Segatori
people.note: (1841-1910) manageress of restaurant Le Tambourin in Paris

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: Now the surroundings, with the public garden, the night cafés, the grocer’s shop,
facts.note: There were three public gardens ‘jardins publics’ abutting the place Lamartine (see letter 604, n. 2). The night café that Van Gogh painted (see letter 676) was the Café de la Gare at 30 place Lamartine. The Café du Prado (no. 13) and the Café de l’Alcazar (no. 17) were also in the square. See L’indicateur arlésien 1887 and 1888. Next door to Van Gogh’s house, in the left-hand side of the premises at no. 2 place Lamartine, was the grocer’s shop run by François Damase and Marguerite Crévoulin.

facts.said: Thank you in advance for the Japanese prints.
facts.note: Milliet had been on leave in Northern France and had visited Theo on his way there; see letter 652, n. 9. See letter 685 for the Japanese prints he brought back with him. Vincent had asked for them in letter 677.

facts.said: I’ve also received Maurin’s drawing, which is superb.
facts.note: The print Before the accident after the drawing by Charles Maurin was printed as a ‘Supplément’ in Le Courrier Français of 16 September 1888. The engraver was ‘SGap’. There are three copies in the estate, one with drawing pin holes (inv. nos. t*1419-1 with drawing pin holes, t*1419-2 and t*1419-3). Ill. 2245. Cf. also letter 685.

facts.said: You’re doing that in your business; it’s undeniable that it will increase in future, even though you have many vexations at present.
facts.note: Evidently Theo’s dissatisfaction with the situation at work, which was already a subject of discussion in April 1888, was unchanged. Cf. letter 600, n. 5.

entries.summary: 아를의 자연과 빛에 완전히 매료되어 정원, 카페, 해바라기, 초상화 등 여러 점을 연달아 그려냈다는 벅찬 소식을 전한다. 페트라르카와 지오토 등 문학과 미술사 이야기를 곁들이며 색채가 감정을 암시해야 한다는 자신의 예술관을 펼친다. 물감과 캔버스, 돈이 바닥났다며 재정 지원을 부탁하고, 베르나르와 고갱의 우정, 쇠라·시냐크의 점묘법에 대한 생각도 함께 나눈다.
entries.why: The letter was written the same day as the previous one to Theo (l. 1*), so we have dated it Tuesday, 18 September 1888. See further the notes to letter 682, Date.

works.title: The Poet's Garden
works.said: That gives me 3 paintings of the gardens facing the house.

works.title: Café Terrace at Night
works.said: Then the two cafés.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: Then Boch’s portrait, and mine.

works.title: The Old Mill
works.said: The old mill.

works.title: A Lane in the Public Garden at Arles
works.said: My dear Theo, I already wrote to you early this morning, then I went to continue working on a painting of a sunny garden.

works.title: Park at Arles with the Entrance Seen through the Trees, The
works.said: Then I brought it back — and went out again with a blank canvas and that’s done, too.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: Then the two cafés.

works.title: Portrait of Eugène Boch
works.said: Then Boch’s portrait, and mine.

people.name: Jean Joseph Thomas
people.note: (1814-1898) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: It’s a public garden where I am, just near the street of the good little ladies, and Mourier, for example, never went there, whereas we used to walk in these gardens almost every day, but on the other side (there are 3 of them).
facts.note: Rue du Bout d’Arles ran from the Roubine du Roi Canal to rue des Récollets; the ‘maisons de tolérance’ (brothels) were in these two streets. Van Gogh meant the public garden to the south-east of place Lamartine. See letter 604, n. 2, for the other parks.

facts.said: Now Petrarch was just near here, in Avignon,
facts.note: Petrarch spent much of his youth in Avignon, the residence of the popes. After studying in Montpellier and Bologna he returned there and remained for some considerable time. Avignon was important above all as the place where the poet met his muse Laura, on 6 April 1327 in the Church of St Claire.

facts.said: Then the two cafés.
facts.note: The night café (F 463 / JH 1575) and Café terrace at night (F 467 / JH 1580).

facts.said: 10 canvas, portrait, also costs me 5 francs.
facts.note: By ‘the square no. 30 canvas’ and ‘the no. 10 canvas, portrait’ Van Gogh is referring in general to the canvas sizes for which he was seeking frames, although he did already have specific works in mind: The public garden (‘The poet’s garden’) (F 468 / JH 1578), which he sent to Theo in a walnut frame in May 1889 (see letter 777), and Eugène Boch (‘The poet’) (F 462 / JH 1574), which he planned to hang in his bedroom (see letter 693).

facts.said: My dear Theo, when you’ve seen the cypresses, the oleanders, the sun down here — and that day will come, don’t worry — you’ll think even more often of beautiful works by Puvis de Chavannes: Pleasant land
facts.note: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, Pleasant land, c. 1882 (New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, Mary Gertrude Abbey Fund) had been on show at the Puvis de Chavannes retrospective at Durand-Ruel’s in Paris from 20 November-20 December 1887 (cat. no. 83). Ill. 314.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르가 고갱의 초상화를 그리지 않는 것에 놀라움을 표하며 언젠가 자신이 둘의 초상을 그리고 싶다는 뜻을 전한다. 베르나르가 아를에서 겨울을 보내고 싶어 하는 것에 대해 생활비와 매춘업소를 그리려는 계획을 현실적으로 조언하며, 군 복무 후 아프리카에서 그런 소재를 자유롭게 그릴 수 있을 것이라 말한다. 남프랑스의 강한 태양이 들라크루아와 몽티첼리적 색채의 원천임을 강조한다.
entries.why: On 18 September Vincent told Theo about receiving a letter from Bernard (see letters 682 and 683). Those letters, however, give no indication that he had already replied, which increases the likelihood that this one had not yet been written. He did tell Theo about his reply in letter 687 of 25 September. There are no further clues to help us pinpoint the date more accurately, so we have dated the present letter between Wednesday, 19 and Tuesday 25 September 1888.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: I, for example — it’s true that I’ve just done that study of a night café

facts.said: I, for example — it’s true that I’ve just done that study of a night café
facts.note: This study, which Van Gogh painted at the beginning of September, and which, judging by his choice of words, he must have mentioned in the lost letter, was The night café (F 463 / JH 1575).

facts.said: The south will delight you and make you a great artist; Gauguin himself owes his superiority to the south.
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring to Gauguin’s stay in tropical Martinique between May and October 1887.

facts.said: If Gauguin comes, however.
facts.note: It would appear that Van Gogh did not finish this sentence. After ‘pourtant’ he originally wrote: ‘ou si un autre viendrait a sa place’ (‘or if someone else were to come in his place’), but then crossed it out.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 노란 집을 실용적인 '화가의 집'으로 꾸미는 진행 상황(화장대, 스토브, 찬장 구입)을 전하며, 러셀처럼 수천 프랑을 쓰기보다 검소하고 견고하게 꾸미는 방식을 선호한다고 말한다. 어머니 초상화를 언급하며 색채 없이는 진정한 닮음을 담을 수 없다는 생각을 밝히고, '올리브 동산의 그리스도' 습작을 모델 없이는 그릴 수 없어 긁어냈다고 전한다. 인상주의가 오래갈 것이라는 믿음과 자신이 언젠가 타뉘 영감 같은 존재가 되고 싶다는 소망으로 마무리한다.
entries.why: We learn from the last page of letter 687 that Theo’s letter containing 100 francs, for which Vincent thanks him in the present letter, had arrived on ‘Friday’ (l. 215). This must have been Friday, 21 September 1888, since Vincent again refers to the Maurin illustration Theo had sent, which he had thanked him for around 18 September (letter 682).

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: Only I don’t like it at all as a real likeness; I’ve just painted my own portrait, and I have the same ashy coloration,

works.title: Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear
works.said: Among them I love the café-concert on two sheets, with a line of purple female musicians against the yellow-lit wall;

people.name: Siegfried Bing
people.note: (1838-1905) dealer in oriental art in Paris

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: I hope you’ll give me details of your visit to Maurin.
facts.note: Theo must have visited Charles Maurin in his studio at 18 rue de Chabrol – this address is given in the catalogue of the Indépendants’ fourth exhibition (1888). On 17 September, Maurin wrote to Félix Vallotton about this visit from Theo: ‘Boussod et Valadon called on me today – he wants to exhibit my work, I told him that it’s unsaleable, they’re not fancy goods, but all the same, he insists.’ (Venu aujourd’hui chez moi Boussod et Valadon – il veut m’exposer, je lui dis que ça n’est pas vendable, pas article de Paris; mais quoique, et il insiste.) See G. Guisan, D.

entries.summary: 비 오는 날씨 속에서 겨울 동안 인물을 기억만으로 빠르게 그리는 연습을 하겠다는 계획을 전하며, 스튜디오에 정리한 일본 판화와 들라크루아·도미에 작품들에 대한 애정을 밝힌다. 톨스토이의 종교론 기사를 읽고 새로운 시대의 위안이 될 신앙에 대해 사색하며, 몬티첼리의 색채와 아를 여인들의 아름다움을 일본 미술의 단순함과 연결지어 논한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes: ‘The fine weather of these past few days has disappeared and has been replaced by mud and rain’ (ll. 1-2). Friday, 21 September was the last fine day, after that the temperature dropped and it started to rain. The weather records report precipitation on 22 and 25 September, and prolonged rain on 23 and 24 September. The weather turned dry on 26 September (Météo-France).

people.name: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez

facts.said: I’ve arranged all the Japanese prints in the studio, and the Daumiers
facts.note: These Daumiers probably included the lithograph Emotions de chasse (Emotions of the hunt) from Le Charivari of 17 September 1858. It emerges from a letter Gauguin wrote to Schuffenecker on 22 December 1888 that there was an impression of this lithograph in the Yellow House. See Merlhès 1989, pp. 241-243 (ill. on p. 242).

facts.said: If you come across the Delacroix Pietà,
facts.note: The lithograph by Célestin François Nanteuil-Leboeuf after Delacroix’s Pietà is in the Van Goghs’ estate. Ill. 75. (t*622) It bears the stamp: ‘Les artistes anciens et modernes’. This series of lithographs – Van Gogh writes that they could be bought for 1 franc each – is also mentioned in letters 726, 732 and 798. One of the other Delacroix prints may have been the lithograph The Good Samaritan , see letter 768, n. 22.

facts.said: And we wouldn’t be able to study Japanese art, it seems to me, without becoming much happier and more cheerful, and it makes us return to nature, despite our education and our work in a world of convention.
facts.note: In his introduction in Le Japon Artistique, Bing wrote about the Japanese artist: ‘he believes that nature contains the primordial elements of all things and, according to him, there exists nothing in creation, be it a lowly blade of grass, that is not worthy of finding its place in the lofty concepts of art’ (il est persuadé que la nature renferme les éléments primordiaux de toutes choses et, suivant lui, il n’existe rien dans la création, fût-ce un infime brin d’herbe, qui ne soit digne de trouver sa place dans les conceptions élevées de l’art). Siegfried Bing, ‘Programme’, Le Japon Artistique 1 (May 1888), p.

facts.said: I’m reading an article on Tolstoy in the Revue des Deux Mondes — it appears that Tolstoy takes an enormous interest in his people’s religion.
facts.note: This long article by Anatole Leroy-Beaulieu appeared on 15 September 1888 in the Revue des Deux Mondes. It is the fifth part of the series ‘La Religion en Russie’, and is subtitled ‘Les Réformateurs. Le comte Léon Tolstoï, ses précurseurs et ses émules.’ See Revue des Deux Mondes 58-3. Paris 1888, vol. 89, pp. 414-443.

facts.said: Like George Eliot in England.
facts.note: George Eliot, whose books Van Gogh had read in his youth, believed that orthodox Christianity must be replaced by an ethical religion that would instill in us ‘a more deeply awing sense of responsibility to man, springing from sympathy with the difficulty of the human lot’. See Alan Jacobs, ‘George Eliot: Good without God’, First Things 102 (April 2000), pp. 50-53.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 갈아엎은 밭 그림 등 가을 작업이 순조롭게 진행 중이라 전하며 밀리에 중위의 초상화 작업의 어려움도 토로한다. 캔버스와 물감을 대량으로 주문하고, 낙엽이 지는 가을철 집중 작업을 위한 준비를 갖춘다. 톨스토이의 '나의 신앙'을 읽으며 부활보다 인류의 지속과 성실한 노동을 믿는 그의 사상에 깊이 공감하는 대목이 인상적이다.
entries.why: Van Gogh refers to his previous letter, 686 of Sunday, 23 or Monday, 24 September, in which he wrote about the bad weather. In the present letter he reports that he has painted a landscape in the intervals between the showers – a day later he writes, ‘the day has been so beautiful again’ (letter 689). Given that the weather turned fine again on 26 September (Météo-France), we have dated the present letter Tuesday, 25 September 1888.

works.title: The Lover: Portrait of Lieutenant Paul-Eugène Milliet
works.said: I’m also working on the portrait of Milliet,

works.title: Ploughed fields
works.said: An immense field of an ashy lilac, furrows, innumerable clods of earth, the horizon of blue hills and green bushes and small farmsteads with orange-coloured roofs.

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: 1 tube of Prussian blue goes as far as 6 ultramarine or cobalt and costs 3 times less.
facts.note: This is confirmed by one of Tanguy’s price lists – undated – on which ‘Bleu de Berlin (ou Prusse)’ and ‘bleu minéral’ cost 0.25 francs, and ‘Bleu de Cobalt’ costs 1 franc (FR b1445).

facts.said: I’ll send you five drawings by Bernard, of the same kind as the others.
facts.note: Bernard had sent six sketches altogether; see letter 696. They were probably Meadow with figures and animals, Idyll at Asnières, Figures by the riverside and the sheet Brothel scene with Two sketches of prostitutes on the back (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 2257, 2258, 2259, 2260, 2287. See Roskill 1970-2, pp. 223-224. In letter 690 Van Gogh thanks Bernard for sending them. The fact that two of the sketches are together on a single sheet (with another one on the back) explains why Van Gogh refers to five sketches here and six in letter 696.

facts.said: It seems to me that it would definitely suit Bernard’s book here, but his father would have to be a touch more magnanimous towards him.
facts.note: Evidently Bernard had complained to Van Gogh that his father did not support him enough. However the published letters he wrote to his family in 1888 do not give this impression. Cf. Harscoët-Maire 1997, pp. 160-183.

entries.summary: 정원의 협죽도와 삼나무를 그린 연작을 세 번째로 다시 그리며 사물의 본질을 포착하려는 집념을 전하고, 물감과 캔버스의 긴급한 추가 주문을 요청한다. 쇠라, 시냐크, 고갱, 기요맹 등 동료 화가들에 견줄 만한 '장식' 연작을 89년까지 완성하겠다는 포부를 밝히며, 몽티첼리풍의 두터운 임파스토 기법을 언급한다. 고갱이 라발과 다른 동업을 계획할 수도 있다는 소식에도 담담히 반응하며 계속 작업에 몰두하겠다는 의지를 보인다.
entries.why: The letter was written one day after 687, on a day when the weather had been fine: ‘I’m well aware that I wrote to you only yesterday, but the day has been so beautiful again’ (ll. 1-2). Van Gogh wrote it in the evening after working outdoors all day. On 25 September there was still some rain; from 26 September the weather was dry, with temperatures around 25ºC and scattered cloud (Météo-France). On these grounds we have dated the letter Wednesday, 26 September 1888.

works.title: Busch in the Park at Arles - The garden of the poet II
works.said: 30 again.

works.title: The Poet's Garden
works.said: 30 canvas of the same place, only from a quite different viewpoint, in which the whole garden is coloured in very different greens under a pale lemon yellow sky.

works.title: The Lover: Portrait of Lieutenant Paul-Eugène Milliet
works.said: Tomorrow I hope to work with Milliet again.

works.title: Sunny Lawn in a Public Park
works.said: You know this round bush already, since you already have a study of the garden.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: So I’d like, myself, to have by that time — whether we were to exhibit it or not — the series of studies: Decoration.

works.title: Sunflowers (Munich version)
works.said: So I’d like, myself, to have by that time — whether we were to exhibit it or not — the series of studies: Decoration.

works.title: Ploughed fields
works.said: Milliet was pleased today that I’d done the ploughed field;

facts.said: 30 again.
facts.note: The enclosed sketch is The public garden (‘The poet’s garden’) (F 1465 / JH 1583). There is a similar letter sketch in letter 693 to Eugène Boch. The painting after which the drawing and the letter sketch of this ‘round cedar or cypress bush’ were done is not known. Soon after this Van Gogh described the work as ‘the garden with the round bush and the oleanders’ (694). We do not know whether there is anything written on the back of the enclosed sketch. It was sold at Sotheby’s New York on 13 November 1997 (present whereabouts unknown).

facts.said: Because if he joins up with Laval, that’s only fair, since Laval’s his pupil and they’ve already kept house together.
facts.note: Laval had been with Gauguin in Pont-Aven since July 1888. They had been together on Martinique: letter 623, n. 3.

facts.said: So I’d like, myself, to have by that time — whether we were to exhibit it or not — the series of studies: Decoration.
facts.note: At this point Van Gogh in any event counted the two no. 30 canvases of sunflowers, Sunflowers in a vase (F 456 / JH 1561) and Sunflowers in a vase (F 454 / JH 1562), as part of this series, which he intended for the decoration of the Yellow House; see letter 677. He probably also regarded the paintings for which he was having frames made as part of the decoration. For this see letter 673, n. 16.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르에게 군 복무를 앞두고 체력을 보충할 것을 신신당부하며, 아버지가 경제적으로 지원해주기를 바란다고 전한다. 남프랑스와 아프리카의 강렬한 자연이 화가로서의 재능을 발전시킬 좋은 기회가 될 것이라 격려하면서도 건강 관리의 중요성을 거듭 강조하며, 고갱과 함께 지내게 되면 베르나르의 비용 부담을 덜어주겠다고 약속한다.
entries.why: In letter 689 of Wednesday, 26 September, Vincent told Theo that he was expecting a letter from Bernard at any moment, following up on the sketches that the latter had sent (ll. 140-142). He had not yet had the letter that he was expecting when he wrote this one. One can assume that he would have replied not long after receiving Bernard’s sketches, and he had told Theo on Tuesday, 25 September that he had got them (in letter 687). Because, moreover, he now writes: ‘the weather’s really beautiful’ (ll.

facts.said: My dear old Bernard, I’m writing a line to thank you kindly for your drawings; I find them done in a bit too much of a rush, and I like the two drawings of whores the most;
facts.note: See letter 687, n. 14, for the drawings Bernard sent. Van Gogh discusses the two sketches Prostitute, which are both on one side of a sheet. Brothel scene is on the back.

entries.summary: 테오의 다리 통증을 걱정하며 남프랑스의 햇빛이 최고의 치료제라고 위로한다. '별이 빛나는 밤'과 노란 집을 그린 두 점의 습작을 스케치와 함께 설명하며 그림의 색채를 자세히 묘사한다. 고갱이 아직 결심을 못 하고 있다는 편지 소식을 전하며, 좋은 그림은 진주나 다이아몬드와 같다는 비유로 화상으로서의 자신감을 이야기한다.
entries.why: In letter 687 Vincent asked Theo if he could have his next allowance on Friday again. Assuming that his brother acceded to this request and that Vincent – as usual – thanked him for the money soon after receiving it (ll. 1*-2), we have dated this letter on or about Saturday, 29 September 1888.

works.title: The yellow house (Vincent's House)
works.said: I’ll send you another, better drawing of it than this croquis from memory;

works.title: The Lover: Portrait of Lieutenant Paul-Eugène Milliet
works.said: Milliet greets you warmly, I have his portrait now, with the red képi against an emerald background, and in this background the emblem of his regiment, the crescent and a 5-pointed star.

works.title: The Yellow House
works.said: I’ll send you another, better drawing of it than this croquis from memory;

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: The night café that I painted isn’t in the painting; it’s to the left of the restaurant.

works.title: Ploughed fields
works.said: I wouldn’t be surprised if you liked the starry night and the ploughed fields

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: My friend the postman lives at the bottom of the street on the left, between the two railway bridges.
facts.note: Since Roulin lived in rue de la Montagne des Cordes (on the right after the two bridges), Van Gogh must be referring to Roulin’s place of work: the station’s mail room was in the cul-de-sac Impasse Lamartine, on the left beside the Yellow House in the sketch. Cf. the map in exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, p. 109.

facts.said: Milliet finds it horrible, but I don’t need to tell you that when he says he can’t understand that someone can enjoy doing such an ordinary grocer’s shop, and such stiff, square houses with no charm at all, I reflect that Zola did a certain boulevard at the beginning of L’assommoir
facts.note: The description in chapter 1 of boulevard de la Chapelle and boulevard de Rochechouart in Paris, where the hôtel de la Villette was located in Zola’s L’assommoir . See Zola 1960-1967, vol. 2, pp. 376ff, 1547.

facts.said: I’ll send you another, better drawing of it than this croquis from memory;
facts.note: The letter sketch The Yellow House (‘The street’) (F 1453 / JH 1590) is after the painting of the same name F 464 / JH 1589. See letter 700 for the drawing Van Gogh sent to Theo later.

facts.said: The night café that I painted isn’t in the painting; it’s to the left of the restaurant.
facts.note: This was the Café de la Gare, where Van Gogh had painted The night café (F 463 / JH 1575). See letter 676.

facts.said: Milliet finds it horrible, but I don’t need to tell you that when he says he can’t understand that someone can enjoy doing such an ordinary grocer’s shop,
facts.note: Next door to Van Gogh’s house, in the left-hand side of the premises at 2 place Lamartine, was the grocer’s shop run by François Damase and Marguerite Crévoulin.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 보리나주에서 활동하는 화가 친구 외젠 보흐에게 그곳 광부들의 삶이 평생의 화폭이 될 것이라 격려한다. 노란 집을 가구로 채워 고갱을 맞을 준비를 마쳤다고 전하며, 최근 완성한 7점의 30호 캔버스(밤의 카페, 공원 풍경, 별이 빛나는 밤의 론강 등)를 상세히 묘사한다. 보흐의 초상화가 이미 자신의 침실에 걸려 있다고도 전한다.
entries.why: Date of postmark: 2 October 1888.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: First of all the night café where I stayed, with lamp effects — painted at night.

works.title: The Poet's Garden
works.said: A blue sky in raw cobalt.

works.title: A Lane in the Public Garden at Arles
works.said: A blue sky in raw cobalt.

works.title: Ploughed fields
works.said: And ploughed fields, a landscape with nothing but clods of earth, the furrows the colour of an old clog under the forget-me-not sky with white flecks.

works.title: The Yellow House
works.said: And a view of my house and its surroundings under a sulphur sun, the sky hard, bright cobalt.

works.title: Café Terrace at Night
works.said: And a view of the café on place du Forum, where we used to go, painted at night.

works.title: Portrait of Eugène Boch
works.said: Your portrait is in my bedroom, with the one of Milliet the Zouave that I’ve just done.

works.title: The Lover: Portrait of Lieutenant Paul-Eugène Milliet
works.said: Your portrait is in my bedroom, with the one of Milliet the Zouave that I’ve just done.

facts.said: I congratulate you on not having hesitated this time — and on having tackled the Borinage.
facts.note: See letter 669, n. 16, for Boch’s stay in the Borinage. Van Gogh addressed the letter care of ‘M. Moriau / Rue de la Station’ (see Additional details). This ‘Moriau’ was François Eugène Morriaux. He lived at 42 rue de la Station in Frameries, and had a tavern (AEM).

facts.said: If you ever go to Petit-Wasmes, would you find out if Jean Baptiste Denis (farmer) and Joseph Quinez (miner)
facts.note: When he died in 1895 the miner Joseph Quinez, born in Wasmes, was living in rue Royale in Wasmes; he was married to Amélie Thiébaut, with whom he had previously lived at number 39 rue de Louise (AEM).

facts.said: I’d very much like to ask you to do an exchange with me of one of your studies of the coal-mines.

facts.note: As a result of the efforts of Camille Corot, Honoré Daumier was in a position to buy a house in Valmondois, near Auvers-sur-Oise, in February 1874. Through his friend Bardon, Corot had raised more than half of the 13,000 francs needed. This generous act was common knowledge thanks to reports in the press – for instance it was mentioned in Daumier’s obituary in La Révolution Française in 1879 – and by way of Causeries sur les artistes de mon temps by Jean Gigoux, which Van Gogh had read. Gigoux wrote: ‘Good old Daumier! He was unable to hide how he was living.

facts.said: How happy I am for Gauguin; I won’t search for expressions to tell you so — let’s be of bold good heart!
facts.note: Theo had sent Gauguin 300 francs as the proceeds of the sale of several ceramic pieces, as we learn from letters from Gauguin to Theo and to Schuffenecker. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, pp. 247-249. This money enabled Gauguin to settle his debts in Pont-Aven so he could go to Arles.

facts.said: What Gauguin’s portrait says to me, first and foremost, is that he mustn’t go on that way, he must console himself, he must become the richer Gauguin of the negresses again.
facts.note: Van Gogh means paintings of negresses that Gauguin did during his stay on Martinique between May and October 1887. Theo and Vincent had two of these works in their collection: On the shore of the lake, Martinique and Among the mangoes . See letter 576, n. 2 and letter 612, n. 1.

facts.said: I feel that he’s more Millet than I am, but I’m more Diaz than he is, and like Diaz, I’ll try to please the public so that some sous may come into the community.
facts.note: Van Gogh must be referring to the fact that Diaz’s paintings, unlike those of Rousseau and Millet, were always accepted at the Salon. Diaz painted fast and sold well, which put him in a position to give his friends financial help. Sensier relates how Diaz, who was a great admirer of Millet, came to his friend’s aid: ‘Diaz was waiting to see if some Castilian would appear with a gold ingot, and, in the meantime, he struggled with his public sales at the auctioneers’ to which he sent his paintings each year. The wait was long and hard. In the end, Diaz arrives one memorable day like the victorious El Cid.

facts.said: As for what Gauguin says about ‘Persian’, it’s true, I don’t believe it would be shocking, placed in the Dieulafoy Museum; it could be placed there with no problem.
facts.note: From 1884 to 1886 the French archaeologist Auguste Marcel Dieulafoy and his wife Jeanne undertook archaeological studies in Susa, some 300 km to the west of Isfahan, in the palaces of Darius i the Great and Artaxerxes ii. Fragments from their excavations were taken to Paris, where the Dieulafoy Gallery opened on the first floor of the Louvre on 6 June 1888. Van Gogh must have read the article ‘Au Louvre: La salle Dieulafoy’ about the collection in L’Intransigeant of 8 June 1888, p. 2. See exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, p. 383 (n. 258).

facts.said: I mercilessly destroyed an important canvas — a Christ with the angel in Gethsemane — as well as another one depicting the poet with a starry sky — because the form hadn’t been studied from the model beforehand, necessary in such cases
facts.note: Vincent told Theo about his second, abortive attempt to paint a Christ without a model on 21 September (letter 685). At the beginning of September he had painted ‘a poet’ with a starry sky from a model: Eugène Boch (‘The poet’) (F 462 / JH 1574).

This study is not known. On the basis of the size it could be Brothel scene (F 478 / JH 1599), which is a no. 6 canvas (33 x 41 cm). However, Van Gogh says that he had set the study in the night café, where he had painted F 463, and the interior in F 478 does not resemble it. What’s more, the scene does not match the description Van Gogh gives here. It is therefore more likely that F 478 is the rough sketch that Van Gogh painted in November 1888 and mentioned in letter 718. Cf. also Dorn 1990, p. 249 (n. 52) and exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, pp. 195, 387 (n. 114).

In an act of homage to Van Gogh, Bernard portrayed himself in front of the painting in his Self-portrait of 1892 (private collection).

entries.why: Van Gogh writes that he sent a telegram ‘yesterday’ asking for 20 francs (ll. 1*-2). Since he urgently requested 20 francs in letter 699 of Monday, 8 October (he had already spent the money he had received that day), it seems likely that he would have sent the telegram that same day, Monday, or certainly on Tuesday. This date tallies with his asking Theo in the present letter – not once, but twice – to be sure to see to it that the allowance got to Arles by Sunday (ll. 6 and 85-86).

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: Did you see that my drawing, which I added to the Bernard drawings,
facts.note: See letter 697, n. 10, for Bernard’s set of drawings titled At the brothel. The drawing of the house is The Yellow House (‘The street’) (F 1413 / JH 1591).

facts.said: My dear Theo, Yesterday I sent you a telegram to ask you for another twenty francs.
facts.note: Van Gogh had also urgently requested this extra 20 francs (a ‘louis’) in letter 699.

facts.said: 30 canvas of that drawing.
facts.note: The painting is The Yellow House (‘The street’) (F 464 / JH 1589).

facts.said: I’m doing a study of a brothel for Bernard, from memory.
facts.note: This painting of a brothel is not known. See letter 698, n. 6.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 몸이 아프다는 이유로 도착을 연기한 것에 답답함을 토로하며, 정말 아프면 오히려 아를에 와서 회복해야 하는 것 아니냐고 반문한다. 테오에게 추가 생활비를 요청하며 가구 구입 내역을 보고하고, 고갱에게 보낸 답장 사본을 첨부해 석판화 공동 출판 제안에는 신중한 입장을 밝힌다. 그럼에도 '가능한 한 빨리 오라'는 재촉의 말로 고갱에 대한 간절한 기다림을 드러낸다.
entries.why: On Tuesday, 9 or Wednesday, 10 October Van Gogh said that the previous day – in other words Monday, 8 or Tuesday, 9 October – he had sent Theo a telegram asking for 20 francs (letter 700). Theo had evidently not replied on the day he received it, but he would not have delayed long in sending the money order, so we assume he did so on 9 or 10 October. In the present letter Vincent thanks Theo for the money order for 20 francs. He has meanwhile used it to buy a dressing table.

works.title: Couple in the Park at Arles - The garden of the poet III
works.said: The one I’ve just done is another garden.

works.title: Entrance to the Public Park in Arles
works.said: The one I’ve just done is another garden.

facts.said: In my list of necessary purchases I said 35 francs for the chest of drawers-dressing table
facts.note: In letter 694 Van Gogh had made a list of things he still wanted to buy for the Yellow House. He had estimated 40 francs for the dressing table with chest of drawers.

facts.said: That he dreads the journey....
facts.note: The letter from Gauguin to Vincent has not survived; he had also written to tell Theo that he would travel to Arles at the end of the month. He informed Schuffenecker on 8 October that he had had another attack of dysentery. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, pp. 247-249.

entries.summary: 테오가 그림 비용으로 인한 부담을 짊어지는 것에 대해 깊은 죄책감과 걱정을 표하며, 화상의 일도 예술가의 창작만큼 가치 있는 일이라고 위로한다. 고갱이 쓸 서랍장을 구입한 일과 몬티첼리의 죽음에 대한 소문을 반박하며, 자신이 몬티첼리의 화풍을 계승하는 스튜디오를 아를에 세우고 있다는 자부심을 드러낸다. 우편배달부 룰랭에 대한 애정 어린 묘사도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: In letter 701 Van Gogh says he has ‘just’ bought a piece of furniture. The present letter appears to have been written later on the same day, since Van Gogh meanwhile appears to be regretting his purchase (ll. 103-104). We have therefore dated this letter, like 701, Wednesday, 10 or Thursday, 11 October 1888.

people.name: Cornelis (Cor) Marinus van Gogh (Uncle Cor or C.M.)
people.note: (1824-1908) brother of Theodorus van Gogh, art dealer and bookseller in Amsterdam

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: Thus C.M., even without helping us in any other way, could buy another study from us.
facts.note: Vincent had sent drawings and studies to his uncle, the art dealer Cornelis Marinus van Gogh, several times in 1882-1883: cf. letter 388, n. 1.

facts.said: So I almost have a feeling of remorse at having today bought this piece of furniture, although it’s good, because I had to ask you to send me money sooner than if it hadn’t been for that.
facts.note: Van Gogh had bought a dressing table and asked whether Theo could send the sum he had spent by money order (letter 701).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 타라스콩의 승합마차를 그린 그림과 정원의 연인들, 트랭크타유 다리 등 완성한 여러 30호 캔버스를 상세히 묘사하며 집 장식 연작이 진전되고 있음을 알린다. 고갱이 이곳에 오면 더 빨리 회복할 것이라 확신하며, 화가들도 목수나 대장장이처럼 성실하게 일해야 한다는 생각을 밝힌다. 극도로 지친 상태에서도 15점에 이르는 연작 목록을 자세히 정리해 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for a 50-franc money order and is delighted to have received his allowance earlier than he expected: he had asked Theo to make sure he got his money by Sunday at the latest (letter 700). (He received a money order for 20 francs as early as Tuesday or Wednesday; see letter 701.) He now looks back over the work he had done that week: ‘5 canvases that I’ve started on this week’ (ll. 115-116); he mentioned the first canvas on Wednesday, 10 October (letter 701) and he has just painted the last one.

works.title: Railway Bridge over Avenue Montmajour, Arles, The
works.said: That canvas is a little like a Bosboom in coloration.

works.title: Couple in the Park at Arles - The garden of the poet III

works.title: The Trinquetaille Bridge
works.said: 30 canvases, the Trinquetaille bridge and another bridge; the railway goes over the road.

works.said: 2 canvases of sunflowers

facts.said: 30 canvas once again.
facts.note: The letter sketch The Tarascon diligence (F - / JH 1606) is after the painting of the same title, F 478a / JH 1605. At that time the coaches for Tarascon left from the Auberge de la Poste (according to Le Forum Républicain of 28 October 1888 (front page)). This inn was at 7 rue Marché-Neuf (L’indicateur arlésien 1887, p. 26).

facts.said: I wrote to Gauguin again the day before yesterday, to say once again that he would probably recover much more quickly here.
facts.note: Vincent had sent Theo a ‘copy’ of his letter to Gauguin on 10 October (see letter 701).

facts.said: That canvas is a little like a Bosboom in coloration.
facts.note: The letter sketch The viaduct (F - / JH 1607) after the painting of the same title, F 480 / JH 1603. The ‘other bridge’ was the railway bridge that carried the Paris-Lyon-Méditerranée line over avenue de Montmajour, the street that led into place Lamartine.

entries.summary: 고갱과 베르나르 무리가 자신이 보낸 캔버스 7점을 모두 보관하기로 했다는 반가운 소식과 함께, 강한 미스트랄 바람 속에서도 한 주에 캔버스 5점을 완성한 강행군 후 16시간을 내리 잤다고 전한다. 쇠라에게 안부를 전하며 자신이 진행 중인 '장식' 연작이 이미 15점에 이르렀음을 알리고, 프로방스 지역 문인 모임 펠리브르주와 미스트랄 등을 언급하며 이 지역에 대한 애정을 표현한다. 몽티첼리의 뒤를 이어 마르세유에서 작업하고 싶다는 바람도 덧붙인다.
entries.why: Van Gogh enclosed an article that appeared in the newspaper on 14 October (see n. 13). He had slept for 16 hours (l. 33); the five paintings he had done the week before made up for the fact that his fatigue had caught up with him this week (ll. 39-41). He also writes that he cannot work because of the ‘very violent mistral’ (ll. 27-28). The weather records show the mistral blowing on 14 October, becoming worse on 15 October (Météo-France). We have consequently dated the letter Monday, 15 October 1888.

works.title: Quay with men unloading sand barges
works.said: Bernard will make another study for me in exchange,

works.title: Garden Behind a House
works.said: Bernard will make another study for me in exchange,

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: Gauguin has my portrait,

works.title: Self-Portrait with Straw Hat
works.said: Gauguin has my portrait, and Bernard says that he’d like to have one like it, although he already has one of me, which I exchanged with him at the time for the portrait of his Grandmother.

works.title: The Zouave
works.said: And it pleased me that they weren’t averse to what I had done in figure painting.

works.title: Couple in the Park at Arles - The garden of the poet III
works.said: But I made a good week of it, eh, with 5 canvases;

works.title: Railway Bridge over Avenue Montmajour, Arles, The
works.said: But I made a good week of it, eh, with 5 canvases;

works.title: The Trinquetaille Bridge
works.said: But I made a good week of it, eh, with 5 canvases;

facts.said: My dear Theo, Letter from Gauguin, who tells me that he’s sent you a consignment of paintings and studies.
facts.note: Gauguin had told Theo on 7 or 8 October that he would give Bernard’s mother, who was going from Pont-Aven to Paris, several canvases to take with her. Bernard was to bring the rest of the paintings, among them The vision after the sermon (see letter 688); he left for Paris about 10 November. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, pp. 247, 266, 275. We know from a letter Theo wrote to his sister Willemien (6 December 1888) that he had received twenty paintings from Gauguin altogether; they included winter and spring landscapes and views of the village.

facts.said: And it pleased me that they weren’t averse to what I had done in figure painting.
facts.note: In terms of the batch of paintings sent to Bernard and Gauguin, by ‘what I had done in figure painting’ Van Gogh can only mean Self-portrait (F 476 / JH 1581). He could, however, also be alluding here to his figure paintings from Arles; Bernard had been sent the drawing Zouave (F 1482 / JH 1487) in July, and had probably meanwhile also received Mousmé (F 1504 / JH 1520) and possibly Joseph Roulin (F 1723 / JH 1523). See letter 641, n. 1.

facts.said: 30 canvases,
facts.note: Van Gogh had listed these fifteen paintings in his last letter (letter 703). Besides the five new canvases (n. 8) they were Sunflowers in a vase (F 456 / JH 1561), Sunflowers in a vase (F 454 / JH 1562), The public garden (‘The poet’s garden’) (F 468 / JH 1578), a now lost painting of the park (cf.

facts.said: I’m sending you article on Provence which seemed well-written to me.
facts.note: The article Van Gogh sent was probably Paul Mariéton, ‘En Provence. Sensations d’un félibre’, from L’Homme de Bronze of 14 October 1888. The second part appeared in the same paper a week later. Mariéton describes his impressions of a trip through Provence, starting in Avignon; he visited Frédéric Mistral and travelled with him to Salon-de-Provence. There they visited Antoine Crousillat, nicknamed ‘the nestor of the Félibres’ (le doyen des Félibres). Arles, Montmajour and Fontvieille are among the places mentioned in the section Van Gogh is referring to.

facts.said: I still can’t do anything, but in any case there’s a very violent mistral, which raises clouds of dust that turns the trees on boulevard des Lices
facts.note: The trees along boulevard des Lices in Arles (also known as ‘la Lice’).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 자신의 침실을 그린 새 캔버스를 상세히 묘사하며, 보라색 벽과 붉은 타일 바닥 등 색채 배치를 통해 휴식과 수면의 느낌을 표현하고자 했다고 설명한다. 그림자를 배제하고 일본 판화처럼 평평한 색조로 단순화한 것이 강제로 취해야 했던 휴식에 대한 자신만의 반격이라고 말하며 테오의 건강도 물어본다.
entries.why: In his last letter of Monday, 15 October Van Gogh was still recovering from the exhaustion brought on by the work of the previous week (704); in the present letter he reports that he has started work again. He wrote to Gauguin that he had had two and a half days of rest (letter 706). He had done his last painting on Saturday, 13 October (letter 703), so he must in any event have rested on Sunday, 14 and Monday, 15 October. On these grounds we have dated the present letter Tuesday, 16 October 1888.

works.title: Bedroom in Arles
works.said: In short, looking at the painting should rest the mind, or rather, the imagination.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: It will contrast, for example, with the Tarascon diligence and the night café.

entries.summary: 고갱에게 20일경 도착 예정을 확인하며 반가움을 전하는 편지로, 시야가 피로해 이틀 반을 쉰 뒤 다시 작업에 나섰다고 알린다. 자신의 침실을 그린 그림을 쇠라풍의 단순한 색면으로 완성했다며 색채 배합을 세세히 설명한다. 스튜디오에 가스등을 설치해 겨울에도 작업할 수 있게 되었고, 미스트랄이 불어도 아를의 시가 서서히 스며들 것이라며 고갱을 기다린다.
entries.why: The letter was written after Van Gogh had heard from Gauguin that he was coming to Arles on 20 October. We have assumed that Van Gogh replied immediately otherwise there would not have been time for the letter to reach Gauguin before he set out. Since it is unlikely that Vincent had received Gauguin’s letter on 16 October – if he had, he would have told Theo about it when he wrote to him that evening (letter 705) – we have dated this letter Wednesday, 17 October 1888.

works.title: Bedroom in Arles
works.said: 30 canvas of my bedroom

facts.said: I still have in my memory the feelings that the journey from Paris to Arles gave me this past winter.
facts.note: Van Gogh had made the journey from Paris to Arles on Sunday, 19 and Monday, 20 February 1888 (letter 577).

facts.said: My dear Gauguin, Thanks for your letter, and thanks most of all for your promise to come as early as the twentieth.
facts.note: Gauguin was to arrive in Arles on Tuesday, 23 October 1888; see letter 712, n. 2. This must be a reference to a new letter from Gauguin, and not the one Van Gogh said that he had received in letter 704, otherwise he would undoubtedly have told Theo then that Gauguin wanted to come on 20 October.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오가 언급한 새 네덜란드 화가 친구들의 그림 내용을 궁금해하며, 남프랑스가 새로운 색채파의 근거지가 될 것이라는 확신을 전한다. 고갱이 곧 도착할 예정임을 알리고, 그날 오후 완성한 '침실' 그림에 대해 소박하고 힘 있는 표현 기법을 설명한다. 리슈팽, 모파상, 발자크의 소설에 대한 감상과 형제가 함께 이룬 예술적 성취에 대한 애틋한 마음도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: Vincent tells Theo about Gauguin’s letter, which he must have received on Wednesday, 17 October (see letter 706). He adds a postscript to the letter and says he finished The bedroom ‘this afternoon’ (l. 99); in letter 705 of 16 October he said he intended to get going on it ‘very early tomorrow with the fresh morning light’. Since, moreover, Theo’s letter of 19 October was a reply to the present letter, we have dated it Wednesday, 17 October 1888.

works.title: Bedroom in Arles
works.said: Good handshake Ever yours, Vincent I’m adding another line to tell you that this afternoon I finished the canvas of the bedroom.

works.title: Still Life with French novels and glass with a rose
works.said: This bedroom is something like that still life of French novels with yellow, pink, green covers,

people.name: Anthon Gerard Alexander, ridder van Rappard
Siegfried Bing
people.note: (1838-1905) dealer in oriental art in Paris

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

facts.said: My dear Theo, What you say about two new friends
facts.note: The two new friends are the Dutch artist Meijer Isaac de Haan and his apprentice Joseph Jacob Isaäcson, who had been in Paris since 1 August 1888.

facts.said: The simplicity, the bleaching-out, the solemnity of great effects of sunlight.
facts.note: Gauguin may have written this in the (now lost) letter that Van Gogh had just received, but Van Gogh could also be referring to letter 688, in which Gauguin had described the colouration and the ‘great rustic simplicity’ of The vision after the sermon .

facts.said: Look at Monsieur Parent,
facts.note: In Maupassant’s novella Monsieur Parent (1885), Henri Parent, a forty-year-old man of independent means, leads a miserable existence thanks to the whims and moods of his younger wife Henriëtte; his only comfort is their small son Georges. When he confronts her with her adultery with a friend of the family, Henriëtte walks out on him, taking the boy with her – he, it turns out, is really the lover’s son. From then on Henri leads an unstable and lonely existence and spends most of his time in cafés.

facts.said: (Have you read Madame Chrysanthème yet?)
facts.note: See letter 628, n. 20, for Loti’s Madame Chrysanthème . Van Gogh wrote this sentence in brackets at the top of the first page of the second sheet p. [2r:5].

entries.summary: 빈센트는 스튜디오에 가스를 설치한 비용과 추가 생활비를 요청하며, 최근 극도로 지쳐 반 데르 후스의 광기에 가까운 상태를 느꼈다고 고백한다. 인상주의가 단순한 광학 실험이 아니라 위대한 것을 향한 경향이라는 믿음을 밝히고, 사이프러스와 초승달이 있는 풍경화('시인의 정원' 연작 네 번째 작품)를 고갱의 침실 장식용으로 그렸다고 설명한다. 고갱이 도착하기 전 자신만의 독창성을 보여주고 싶다는 마음을 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for his letter and the money; it emerges from various passages in which he responds to what his brother had written (among them ll. 3-4 and ll. 39-41) that this was letter 708. Letter 708 is dated 19 October so it cannot possibly have reached Arles before 20 October. Since Theo in turn replied to the present letter on 23 October (see letter 711) – and Vincent probably wrote again on Monday, (see letter 710) – we have dated it Sunday, 21 October 1888.

works.title: The Lovers: The Poet's Garden IV
works.said: Two lovers, the man pale blue with a yellow hat, the woman has a pink bodice and a black skirt.

works.title: The Yellow House
works.said: I’ve had gas put in, in the studio and the kitchen, which is costing me 25 francs for installation.

works.title: Busch in the Park at Arles - The garden of the poet II
