facts.said: I’ve had gas put in, in the studio and the kitchen, which is costing me 25 francs for installation.
facts.note: The piles of sand in Van Gogh’s painting The Yellow House (‘The street’) (F 464 / JH 1589) have been linked to the laying on of gas to the houses in place Lamartine. See Light! The industrial age 1750-1900: art & science, technology & society. Andreas Blühm and Louise Lippincott. Exhib. cat. Amsterdam (Van Gogh Museum) and Pittsburgh (The Carnegie Museum of Art) 2000, p. 202. It emerges from Van Gogh’s correspondence that Arles had street lighting and the cafés had gaslight (see e.g. letters 656 and 691).

facts.said: may come any day now, I’ll absolutely absolutely need at least another 50 francs.
facts.note: Gauguin had said that he would be setting out for Arles on 20 October (letter 706).

entries.summary: 가을 정원을 그린 대작을 완성했다고 전하며, 그림 그리기를 그만두겠다는 다짐을 매번 어길 수밖에 없다고 고백한다. 고갱과 함께 쇠라까지 합류하는 화가 조합을 상상하며 각자 만 프랑 상당의 기여를 하는 공상을 펼치고, 물감과 캔버스 추가 주문을 요청한다. 돈을 너무 많이 요구하는 데 대한 두려움도 함께 토로한다.
entries.why: The letter was written shortly after letter 709 of 21 October. In that one Van Gogh said that he would take three days off; in the present letter he reports that he has done a painting after all, so it is very unlikely to have been written the same day. He asks, as he did in letter 709, for another 50 francs (l. 101), and says he expects Gauguin ‘any day now’ (l. 72). Since Gauguin arrived at just after five in the morning of 23 October, the letter must have been written before this.

works.title: Public Park at Arles, The
works.said: A little sand, a little lawn, a little blue sky.

facts.said: Once again that falls right in line with what I was telling you, that I wished absolutely absolutely to do 10 thousand francs worth of painting for the house.
facts.note: Van Gogh wrote in letter 700 that his decoration would have to be worth 10,000 francs to get back the money he had spent. He mentioned the same sum in letter 607 as the amount he wanted to earn, apparently as compensation for the money he had cost Theo.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 마침내 고갱이 아를에 도착했다는 기쁜 소식을 전하며 그가 건강해 보이고 함께라면 많은 것을 이룰 수 있으리라 기대한다. 그림이 팔리지 않아 테오에게 진 빚에 대한 부담감과 평생 그림값을 갚아야 하는 화가의 숙명을 무겁게 토로한다. 고갱이 베르나르와 교환한 브르타뉴 여인들 그림을 가져온 것도 반갑게 언급한다.
entries.why: Vincent writes that Gauguin has arrived – that was the morning of Tuesday, 23 October (see n. 2) – and that he has already sent Theo a telegram to tell him (l. 3). Since he also reacts to news – among other things the sale of Gauguin’s painting – in Theo’s letter of 23 October (711) and Theo in his turn replies to the present letter on 27 October (713), this one must date from about Thursday, 25 October 1888.

works.title: Trunk of an Old Yew Tree
works.said: thirty canvas.

works.title: The Sower II
works.said: thirty canvas.

facts.said: As you learned from my telegram, Gauguin arrived in good health.
facts.note: Gauguin arrived at four in the morning on Tuesday, 23 October. It had taken him from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday morning to get from Pont-Aven to Arles, as he told Schuffenecker on 25 October 1888. See Merlhès 1989, pp. 124-127. For the route he took see Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 510 (n. 294), exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, p. 54 (fig. 5), and Murphy 2016, p. 281 (n. 1).

entries.summary: 고갱이 실제로 노련한 선원이었다는 사실에 깊은 존경을 표하며, 그가 들려준 브르타뉴와 열대 지방 이야기에 큰 흥미를 느낀다고 전한다. 밭 가는 사람과 씨 뿌리는 사람을 그린 새 습작을 언급하며, 자바에 화가들의 식민지를 세우자는 상상, 가스등 아래 인물을 그리고 싶다는 구상 등 색채와 이국적 풍경에 대한 열망을 드러낸다. 노란 집이 아프리카와 북유럽 사이의 중간 기착지 같은 존재가 될 것이라는 비유도 인상적이다.
entries.why: Vincent writes that he has just received a money order for 50 francs (ll. 1*-2); Theo had said on 27 October that he would send it. It was not until letter 715 that Vincent replied to Theo’s letter of 27 October (letter 713), which he had consequently not received when he wrote the present letter. It is not possible to say for certain whether the money order arrived the same day – the 27th. We have therefore dated the present letter Saturday, 27 or Sunday, 28 October 1888.

works.title: Trunk of an Old Yew Tree
works.said: Like this.

works.title: The Sower II
works.said: This week I did a new study of a sower; the landscape utterly flat, the figure small and blurred.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Thank you for your money order for 50 francs, which I’ve just received.
facts.note: Theo said on 27 October that he would send this; see letter 713.

facts.said: He has — if he’s to be compared with something — links with those Icelandic fishermen of Loti’s.
facts.note: Pierre Loti’s Pêcheur d’Islande (1886) is a novel about the hard, dangerous life of Breton fishermen, who fished in Icelandic waters. The story centres on the love between the fisherman Yann and the middle-class girl Gaud. At first Yann rejects her, but she remains faithful to him in her thoughts. When it is discovered on her father’s death that he had frittered away his fortune, the gulf between them narrows and they find each other again. They marry six days before Yann goes back to sea for months. It is to be his last voyage, from which he would not return.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 마침내 아를에 도착해 함께 생활하게 되었다며 큰 안도와 기쁨을 전한다. 둘이 지출을 합치면 오히려 생활비가 절감될 것이라 낙관하고, 화가들의 스튜디오를 반영구적인 거점으로 발전시키고 싶다는 포부를 다시 밝힌다. 씨 뿌리는 사람과 해바라기 등 고갱이 마음에 들어한 작품들을 언급하며 함께 사창가를 연구 삼아 방문할 계획도 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent is replying to Theo’s letter of 27 October (713), and the opening words – about Theo’s concern for Vincent’s health – appear to indicate that he did so soon after he received it. We have consequently dated the present letter on or about Monday, 29 October 1888.

works.title: Bedroom in Arles
works.said: Ever yours, Vincent I don’t yet know what Gauguin thinks about my decoration in general; I only know that there are some studies that he really does like, namely, the Sower, the Sunflowers, the Bedroom.

works.title: The Sower II
works.said: Ever yours, Vincent I don’t yet know what Gauguin thinks about my decoration in general; I only know that there are some studies that he really does like, namely, the Sower,

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: Ever yours, Vincent I don’t yet know what Gauguin thinks about my decoration in general; I only know that there are some studies that he really does like, namely, the Sower, the Sunflowers,

works.title: Sunflowers (Munich version)
works.said: Ever yours, Vincent I don’t yet know what Gauguin thinks about my decoration in general; I only know that there are some studies that he really does like, namely, the Sower, the Sunflowers,

facts.said: Gauguin has already just about found his Arlésienne,
facts.note: On 27 October Gauguin had told Theo that he wanted to use the first few days ‘to acquaint myself with the character of the country’ (pour m’initier au caractère du pays). See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 266. Van Gogh must mean that Gauguin had succeeded in capturing his idea of the Arlésienne in a sketch – possibly the drawing of an Arlésienne in his sketchbook (Jerusalem, The Israel Museum), published as Le carnet de Paul Gauguin (1952). Gauguin’s drawing and painting of Madame Ginoux were done a week later, so they cannot be what is meant here.

entries.summary: 고갱과 함께 쓴 편지로, 고갱을 야수의 본능을 지닌 순수한 인간이라 평하며 화가들의 조합 결성 가능성을 논의했다고 전한다. 새로운 예술의 부흥이 열대 지방에서 시작될 것이라는 믿음을 밝히고, 두 사람이 함께 사창가를 취재하며 그림을 구상 중이라는 근황을 알린다. 고갱도 뒷부분에 직접 글을 덧붙여 밀리에에게 안부를 전하고 열대에 대한 구상에 공감을 표한다.
entries.why: The letter must have preceded letter 717 to Theo, written about 3 November, in which Van Gogh reported that he had begun the painting of the red vineyard. In the present letter he gives quite a detailed description of his current projects, but does not mention this painting, so it may be assumed that he had not yet started on it. On the other hand, this letter could not have been written before 1 November, because that was the day Milliet left for Africa (see ll. 73-74 and letter 714).

works.title: Garden Behind a House
works.said: I was a little surprised not yet to have received the studies that you promised in exchange for mine.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: At the moment Gauguin has a canvas in progress of the same night café that I also painted, but with figures seen in the brothels.

works.title: Portrait of Eugène Boch
works.said: I declare I don’t understand why I don’t do figure studies,

works.title: The Lover: Portrait of Lieutenant Paul-Eugène Milliet
works.said: I declare I don’t understand why I don’t do figure studies,

works.title: Les Alyscamps: Falling Autumn Leaves
works.said: I’ve made two studies of falling leaves in an avenue of poplars, and a third study of the whole of this avenue, entirely yellow.

works.title: Les Alyscamps
works.said: I’ve made two studies of falling leaves in an avenue of poplars, and a third study of the whole of this avenue, entirely yellow.

works.title: Les Alyscamps
works.said: I’ve made two studies of falling leaves in an avenue of poplars, and a third study of the whole of this avenue, entirely yellow.

works.title: Les Alyscamps
works.said: I’ve made two studies of falling leaves in an avenue of poplars, and a third study of the whole of this avenue, entirely yellow.

facts.said: At the moment Gauguin has a canvas in progress of the same night café that I also painted, but with figures seen in the brothels.
facts.note: Paul Gauguin, Night café, Arles, 1888 (W318/W305) (Moscow, Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts). Ill. 2240. Van Gogh’s painting of the Café de la Gare is The night café (F 463 / JH 1575).

facts.said: His idea about the future of a new generation in the tropics seems absolutely right to me as a painter, and I still intend going back there when I find the funds.
facts.note: Gauguin had lived with Laval on Martinique from May to November 1887; in Arles he was making plans to return to the tropics. He finally left for Tahiti on 1 April 1891. See exhib. cat. Washington 1988, pp. 45, 50, 205.

facts.said: My dear old Bernard, We’ve done a great deal of work these past few days, and in the meantime I’ve read Zola’s Le rêve,
facts.note: Le rêve (The dream) (1888), Emile Zola’s most recent novel in the Rougon-Macquart series, was published on 11 October 1888. It is the story of the orphan Angélique Marie, who spends her time embroidering the lives of saints and dreaming of a knight in shining armour. He appears in the person of Félicien. At the height of her happiness, however, after the nuptial mass, she dies in her husband’s arms. Losing touch with reality and coping with disillusion, including disappointments with catastrophic outcomes, are recurring themes in Zola’s work.

facts.said: I declare I don’t understand why I don’t do figure studies,
facts.note: The last figure pieces that Van Gogh had made – apart from his Self-portrait, which he traded with Gauguin – dated from September: the portraits of Eugène Boch and Lieutenant Milliet (F 462 / JH 1574 and F 473 / JH 1588, respectively).

facts.said: On very coarse, but very good sacking.
facts.note: Soon after arriving in Arles, Gauguin bought 20 metres of ‘very strong canvas’, as Vincent informed Theo in letter 717. It was coarse jute, which Van Gogh and Gauguin divided equally and worked on almost exclusively until they ran out of it in December. For the paintings made on this jute, see exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, pp. 354-369.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱과 함께 지내는 생활이 순조롭게 진행되고 있음을 전하며, 고갱이 그린 포도밭 그림과 자신이 완성한 아를 여인의 초상, 낙엽 그림 두 점을 소개한다. 고갱이 생활용품을 구입한 비용 정산 문제를 다루고, 드 한과 이사악손의 그림에 대한 관심과 열대 지방에서의 색채 작업 가능성을 논한다. 붉은 포도밭을 함께 본 인상적인 풍경도 묘사한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for sending 100 francs, which must have been the first part of his allowance for November: by the beginning of November the two artists had most likely used up the last allowance of 50 francs, received on 27 or 28 October. Cf. also n. 9.

works.title: Les Alyscamps: Falling Autumn Leaves
works.said: I’ve done two canvases of a leaf-fall, which Gauguin liked I think,

works.title: Les Alyscamps
works.said: I’ve done two canvases of a leaf-fall, which Gauguin liked I think,

works.title: L'Arlésienne
works.said: She’s leaning on a green table and is sitting in a wooden armchair — coloured orange.

works.title: The Night Café
works.said: Also a painting of the same night café that I too have painted.

works.title: The Red Vineyard
works.said: I’ve done two canvases of a leaf-fall, which Gauguin liked I think, and am now working on a vineyard, all purple and yellow.

people.name: Marie Ginoux-Julien
people.note: (1848-1911) manageress of Café de la Gare in Arles, wife of Joseph Ginoux

facts.said: Your arrangement for the money is absolutely fine.
facts.note: It had been agreed that Theo would send 300 francs a month (150 francs for each), in three 100-franc instalments. It is most likely that Theo reverted to the system that he and Vincent had used earlier for three monthly payments (starting in June 1882; see letter 234). This meant that Vincent usually received his allowance in instalments arriving around the 1st, 11th and 21st of every month, though sometimes a payment was deferred. Theo thus sent money three times a month in November and December 1888. See also Dorn 1990, p. 479.

facts.said: Also a painting of the same night café that I too have painted.
facts.note: For Gauguin’s Night café, Arles, see letter 716, n. 4. Van Gogh’s painting of the Café de la Gare is The night café (F 463 / JH 1575).

facts.said: De Haan’s drawings are very fine, I like them a lot.
facts.note: Theo had sent two photographs of drawings by De Haan; see letter 708.

facts.said: Gauguin is very happy that you like his consignment from Brittany,
facts.note: Regarding the batch of paintings Gauguin sent to Theo from Pont-Aven, see letter 704, n. 1.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 뒤자르댕의 전시 제안을 거절하기로 하고, 앞으로 어떤 전시에도 크게 연연하지 않겠다는 입장을 밝힌다. 고갱이 '포도 따는 여인들' 그림을 완성했다는 소식과 함께, 둘이 함께 지내며 나쁜 날씨에는 기억에 의존해 그리는 작업 방식, 액자를 직접 저렴하게 만드는 방법 등 공동생활의 실용적 디테일을 전한다. 자신이 그린 보라와 노랑의 포도밭 그림을 몽티셀리 옆에 걸어도 좋을 것이라는 자부심도 드러낸다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes: ‘The weather’s windy and rainy here’ (l. 87). The weather reports record rain from 9 to 14 November, with the most falling on the 10th, but there was little wind during these days, apart from a moderate mistral on 10 November (Météo-France), which makes that date the most likely. This agrees with what Van Gogh says about his work: in the previous letter of about 3 November, he and Gauguin were working on their paintings of the vineyard (717), which have meanwhile been finished.

works.title: The Brothel
works.said: I’ve done a rough sketch of a brothel,

works.title: The Red Vineyard
works.said: I myself have also finished a canvas of a vineyard, all purple and yellow with little blue and violet figures and a yellow sun.

people.name: Julien François Tanguy (père Tanguy)
people.note: (1825-1894) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: In any case he doesn’t at all urge me to do it.
facts.note: Gauguin also refused the invitation to exhibit at the Revue Indépendante. He explained his decision to Theo at the beginning of December: ‘I consider this hole of a place to exhibit could do us harm from every point of view. First: after Signac, Dubois-Pillet, it would mean arriving on the scene like a very young newcomer. What’s more, those gentlemen tend to be ill-disposed towards me, and yet their clientele is insignificant, and of a different kind from mine.’ (Je juge ce trou d’exposition comme pouvant nous nuire sous tous les points de vue.

facts.said: He has a study of mine for troubling to take the canvases to Paris
facts.note: Milliet had left for Africa on 1 November; see letter 714. It is not known which of Van Gogh’s studies he received as a token of gratitude for delivering the paintings to Theo in August (see letter 652).

facts.said: There were a few canvases at Tanguy’s place first of all, at Thomas’s and then at Martin’s.
facts.note: During his stay in Paris, canvases by Van Gogh were on display at Tanguy’s (see letter 572). In 1888 Tanguy still had paintings of his in the shop, as evidenced by a letter from Geffroy to Theo (see letter 629, n. 1). In July 1888, however, Vincent had asked Theo to remove his new paintings (from Arles) from Tanguy’s; see letter 637. Later on in this letter it appears that there were still a few of his canvases at Tanguy’s and Thomas’s; it is not known when his work was to be seen at Martin’s, but his choice of words (‘first of all ... then’) seems to indicate that it was recently too.

facts.said: Gauguin came here on 20 Oct.,
facts.note: Van Gogh is mistaken: Gauguin did say that he would come around the 20th (see letter 706), but he finally arrived on 23 October. See letter 712, n. 2.

facts.said: What will please you is that Gauguin has finished his canvas of the women picking grapes, it’s as fine as the negresses and if, say, you paid the same price for it as for the negresses (400 I think)
facts.note: For Gauguin’s Among the mangoes , which Theo had indeed purchased for 400 francs, see letter 612, n. 1.

entries.summary: 안톤 마우버의 부인이 감사 편지를 보내온 소식과 라발의 뛰어난 자화상, 베르나르의 바다 그림을 교환으로 얻은 소식을 전한다. 고갱이 돼지와 함께 있는 누드 여인을 그리는 매우 독창적인 작품을 작업 중이라며 그를 훌륭한 예술가이자 좋은 친구로 칭송한다. 에텐 정원을 회상한 그림과 초록빛 여인이 책 읽는 그림 등 상상력에 기반한 새로운 작업도 소개한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for sending 100 francs, which must have been the second part of his November allowance. Normally this fact would prompt a dating to about 11 November, but because Vincent’s letter of 10 November does not mention the money (letter 718), we have dated the present letter to Sunday, 11 or Monday, 12 November 1888.

works.title: Memory of the Garden at Etten
works.said: A reminiscence of our garden at Etten with cabbages, cypresses, dahlias and figures.

works.title: The Novel Reader
works.said: A completely green woman.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: You’ll be pleased to hear that I’ve had a letter from Jet Mauve thanking us for the painting.

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.said: Laval’s self-portrait, extremely good.

works.title: Garden Behind a House
works.said: Laval’s self-portrait, extremely good.

works.title: Quay with men unloading sand barges
works.said: Also a seascape by Bernard in exchange for canvases of mine.

people.name: Guillaume Charles Tasset
people.note: (1843-1925) seller of artists' materials in Paris

facts.said: You’ll be pleased to hear that I’ve had a letter from Jet Mauve thanking us for the painting.
facts.note: Van Gogh had sent Theo Pink peach trees (‘Souvenir de Mauve’) (F 394/ JH 1379) to give to Mauve’s widow in memory of her late husband; see letter 590, n. 5. Willemien van Gogh wrote on 23 December 1888 to Theo and Jo Bonger about Pink peach trees: ‘Israëls had seen Vincent’s painting at Jet’s and had said, he is a clever lad!’ (FR b2387).

facts.said: Laval’s self-portrait, extremely good.
facts.note: Charles Laval, Self-portrait, 1888 (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 2247. Laval sent this self-portrait, reproduced in the letter sketch, in exchange for a study from the batch Van Gogh sent to Pont-Aven. It is not known which work Laval chose, but it must have been one of the following: ‘Red sunset’, Garden with flowers (F 578 / JH 1538) and an unidentified work (see letter 698, n. 1). Later Van Gogh reserved his Self-portrait (F 501 / JH 1634) for him (see letter 736), possibly because he found his study of too little value to exchange for Laval’s self-portrait, which he admired greatly; see also letter 800.

facts.said: I think it excellent that you’re taking a Luce.
facts.note: It is not known whether Theo actually bought a work by Maximilien Luce. The two paintings by Luce that are now in the Van Gogh Museum were both painted after Theo’s death and so could not have belonged to his collection. Neither the account book nor the insurance policies issued to Jo van Gogh-Bonger in 1892 and 1893 mention any work by Luce. See Account book 2002, FR b4553 and b4557.

facts.said: The consignment from Tasset arrived the day before yesterday, and we were very pleased with it.
facts.note: In letter 710 of 22 October, Van Gogh had ordered new canvas and paint; in letter 713 Theo wrote that Tasset would send what Vincent had requested as soon as possible.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 여동생 빌에게 모베 부인의 답장을 받은 기쁨을 전하며, 에텐 정원을 회상하며 그린 그림을 상세히 설명한다. 그림 속 두 여인은 실제로는 어머니와 빌을 상징하며, 색채 배치만으로도 시적인 감정을 표현할 수 있다는 예술관을 들려준다. 고갱과 함께 살게 되어 상상력만으로 그림을 그리도록 격려받고 있다는 근황도 전한다.
entries.why: Because Vincent describes the same paintings he mentioned to Theo in letter 719, written on Sunday, 11 or Monday, 12 November 1888, this letter must have been written at about the same time. We have therefore dated it to about Monday, 12 November 1888.

works.title: Memory of the Garden at Etten
works.said: It’s quite a big canvas.

works.title: The Novel Reader
works.said: She’s holding a yellow book in her hand.

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: My dear sister, One thing that has given me great pleasure is that I’ve finally received a reply from Mrs Mauve.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: It’s good that you’ve at last begun to read Au bonheur des dames &c.
facts.note: In October 1888 Willemien had stayed for a while with the Korteweg family in Middelharnis. On 19 October she wrote to Theo: ‘Here I’ve finished reading “Au bonheur des dames”. Oh, how superb it is! ... I’ll certainly read more by Zola, but not for the time being. I still have a cupboard full of your books and would like to give them to you if you come home. Do you remember Denise and Mouret meeting in the Jardin des Tuileries? That’s a beautiful ending’ (FR b2275). For Zola’s Au bonheur des dames , see letter 464, n. 2.

facts.said: Her letter was dated from The Hague, but she doesn’t say if she’ll stay there; personally I thought she was still living in Laren.
facts.note: From 1885 Jet and Anton Mauve lived with their three children at Villa Johanna in Laren. After Mauve’s death on 5 February 1888, Jet and her children moved to The Hague. On 30 June 1888 they were registered as living at Riouwstraat 70, where Jet would die on 28 March 1894 (GAH).

entries.summary: 고갱이 보낸 '브르타뉴 아이들'을 칭찬하면서도 곧 도착할 포도 따는 여인과 돼지 치는 여인 그림이 훨씬 낫다고 전한다. 테오가 자신의 그림을 구필 화랑에 걸려는 데 대해 강하게 반대하며, 예전 근무 경험 때문에 구필과 다시 얽히고 싶지 않다는 자존심 섞인 입장을 분명히 밝힌다. 노란 안락의자와 고갱의 붉고 초록빛 안락의자를 그린 두 점의 밤 정경 작품, 그리고 함께 지내며 생활비를 절감하는 이야기도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: The letter was written between the second and third payment of the November allowance – meaning between letter 719 of Sunday, 11 or Monday, 12 November and letter 722, written on or about 21 November. Van Gogh reports that he and Gauguin are managing well with 150 francs each per month (ll. 113-114); Gauguin had been in Arles since 23 October. Furthermore, Gauguin has retouched the painting that Theo sent on 13 November; the retouching did not take long (see n. 1).

works.title: L'Arlésienne
works.said: In reply I’ve produced work these last few days even more hurriedly.

works.title: Small pear tree in blossom
works.said: Now I’m writing to you in reply to what you were telling me, that you would frame a small canvas of a pink peach tree I think, to place it with those gentlemen.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.said: But — he likes mine better.

works.title: Sunflowers (Munich version)
works.said: But — he likes mine better.

works.title: Van Gogh's Chair
works.said: 30 canvases, a wooden and straw chair all yellow on red tiles against a wall (daytime).

works.title: Paul Gauguin's Armchair
works.said: Then Gauguin’s armchair, red and green, night effect, on the seat two novels and a candle.

people.name: Hermanus Gijsbertus Tersteeg (H.G.T., T. or Mr T.)
people.note: (1845-1927) art dealer at the Goupil gallery in The Hague

people.name: Boussod, Valadon & Cie
people.note: art dealers in Paris, successors of Goupil & Cie

facts.said: They all think that what I’ve sent was done too hastily.
facts.note: It is not clear who the critics of Van Gogh’s working method are in this passage, which must be connected with ll. 172-182 below. ‘What I’ve sent’ (l. 131) must refer to the two batches of paintings sent from Arles, which were at Theo’s (see letters 606 and 660). Druick and Zegers assume that this ‘can only be Gauguin, possibly along with anyone else who may have seen the pictures that Vincent sent to Paris in May and August’ (see exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, p. 207).

facts.said: It does me enormous good to have company as intelligent as Gauguin and to see him work.
facts.note: Gauguin, by contrast, wrote to Bernard in the second half of November 1888 about his relations with Van Gogh: ‘In general, Vincent and I see eye to eye on very little, especially on painting. He admires Daudet, Daubigny, Ziem and the great Rousseau, all of them people I can’t stand. And on the other hand, he detests Ingres, Raphael, Degas, all of them people whom I admire; I reply, you’re right, soldier, for the sake of a quiet life. He likes my paintings very much, but when I’m doing them he always finds that I’m wrong in this and that. He’s a romantic, and I’m more drawn towards a primitive condition.

facts.said: He has a child now,
facts.note: On or about 13 November 1888, Gauguin wrote the following to Schuffenecker about Guillaumin’s letter: ‘Guillaumin has written me a distressing letter; he tells me about his wish to exhibit with the Indépendants this year’ (Guillaumin m’a écrit une lettre désolante; il me parle de son désir d’exposer cette année aux Indépendants). See Merlhès 1989, p. 139. A daughter, called Madeleine, had been born to Guillaumin on 14 October.

facts.said: He’s enjoying working up there.
facts.note: Boch had written to Van Gogh at the beginning of October from the Borinage; see letter 693. Boch’s sister Anna was a member of the artists’ society Les Vingt from 1886 to 1894. Regarding this group, see letter 580, n. 6.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱의 그림 판매 성공을 기뻐하며 장차 마르티니크에 정착하려는 고갱의 계획을 논의한다. 네덜란드 화가 드 한과 이사악손에게 렘브란트와 들라크루아 연구를 권하고, 태양이 강렬한 새 씨 뿌리는 사람 그림을 소개하며 서른 점이 모일 때까지 전시를 미루자고 제안한다. 고갱과의 공동생활에 대한 만족감도 드러낸다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the 100 francs he sent, which must have been the third instalment of his November allowance. For this reason we have dated the letter to about Wednesday, 21 November 1888.

works.title: The Sower III (version 1)
works.said: 30 canvas.

works.title: The Sower III (version 2)
works.said: 30 canvas.

works.title: Portrait of Gauguin
works.said: Gauguin’s working on a very beautiful painting of washerwomen, and also a big still life of an orange pumpkin and some apples and white linen on a yellow background and foreground.

facts.said: Am very happy that Gauguin’s success as regards selling continues.
facts.note: On 13 November Theo informed Gauguin that he had sold two of his canvases. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 280. These were Dogs running in a meadow (W282/W265), sold on 10 November 1888 to Cheret for 300 francs, and Inlet opposite the fishing port of Pont-Aven (W276/W266), sold on 12 November 1888 to Dupuis for 500 francs. In his letter (for which Vincent thanks him here), Theo undoubtedly wrote about the sale on 13 November of a third painting by Gauguin: the ledgers of Boussod, Valadon & Cie record that on that day View of Pont-Aven was sold to Dupuis for 500 francs.

facts.said: May De Haan never lose touch with the serious study of Rembrandt, to which the two drawings of his that I’m currently looking at testify!
facts.note: Theo had sent two unspecified photographs of drawings by De Haan (see letter 708). On 6 December 1888 he wrote to Willemien about De Haan: ‘His earlier work somewhat resembles Vincent’s work from Nuenen, although it does not have Vincent’s fury but instead something resigned and Rembrandtesque that is indeed worthwhile’ (FR b916).

entries.summary: 테오가 보낸 100프랑에 감사하며 겨울철 상상화 작업과 함께 룰랭 가족 전체의 초상화를 완성했다는 기쁜 소식을 전한다. 고갱이 정물화와 풍경화, 세탁부 그림, 그리고 자신의 초상화를 활발히 그리고 있다고 알리며, 브뤼셀의 뱅티스트전 초대 소식과 고갱 부인 문제에 대한 우려도 함께 언급한다. 좋은 습작을 많이 쌓되 무리하게 팔지 말고 진지한 작품만 선별해 팔자는 원칙을 재확인한다.
entries.why: Vincent confirms the receipt of the allowance (l. 4), which must have been the first instalment for December (Vincent responds to Theo’s reaction to the sower, which was mentioned in letter 722 of about 21 November). According to the system of allowance payments (see letter 719, Date and n. 9), we have therefore dated the present letter to about Saturday, 1 December 1888.

works.title: Memory of the Garden at Etten
works.said: Only I’ve spoiled that thing I did of the garden at Nuenen

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: Portrait of Joseph Roulin
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: Madame Augustine Roulin with Baby
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: Portrait of Armand Roulin
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: Portrait of Augustine Roulin
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: The Schoolboy
works.said: 15 canvases.

works.title: The Sower (Sower at Sunset)
works.said: From time to time a canvas that makes a painting, such as that sower, which I too think is better than the first one.

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: 15 canvases.
facts.note: Joseph Roulin and his wife Augustine had two sons and one daughter: Armand (17), Camille (11) and Marcelle (4 months). The head of Roulin previously painted by Van Gogh is Joseph Roulin (F 433 / JH 1524), dating from the end of July or beginning of August 1888. Van Gogh says that the new portraits are no.

facts.said: From time to time a canvas that makes a painting, such as that sower, which I too think is better than the first one.
facts.note: Van Gogh’s ‘sower in question’ refers to Sower with setting sun (F 450 / JH 1627), of which he had made a sketch in his last letter to Theo (722). Assuming that ‘I too’ is a reaction to what Theo had written to him in response to this sketch, ‘the first one’ must refer to the first painting he made of a sower in Arles, Sower with setting sun (F 422 / JH 1470), made around mid-June, which Theo had had since mid-August. It is not likely that he is referring here to Sower (F 494 / JH 1617).

facts.said: His imagination is already leading him to think of settling in Brussels, which would indeed be a means of finding himself in a position to see his Danish wife again.
facts.note: Gauguin wanted to travel to Copenhagen to visit his wife, Mette, and their five children, as emerges from a letter he wrote to Mette at the end of June 1889: ‘For me it was a question of going to see them [= the children] over 6 months ago; (all of a sudden) you people in Copenhagen, you thought it wasn’t responsible to go to that sort of expense’ (Il était question pour moi d’aller les voir il y a plus de 6 mois (tout d’un coup) vous avez trouvé vous autres de Copenhague que ce n’était pas sérieux de faire pareille dépense). See Gauguin lettres 1946, pp. 158-159.

facts.said: Vincent Gauguin will write to you tomorrow, he’s waiting for a reply to his letter
facts.note: Around 22 November Gauguin had sent five of his new paintings to Theo, asking him to confirm their receipt at once. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 288. That Theo did as requested is apparent from Gauguin’s letter (mentioned in n. 12 above).

facts.said: But old mother Bernard simply appropriated them.
facts.note: At the beginning of June, Theo had sent 50 francs to Gauguin, who had promised him work in return (see letter 623, n. 1). Bernard’s mother, Héloïse Bernard-Bodin, had brought a consignment of paintings by Gauguin from Pont-Aven to Paris (letter 704, n. 1), and Gauguin had heard from Bernard that she had kept the drawings intended for Theo. In a letter from the second half of November, Gauguin had therefore asked Bernard to put things to rights. See Correspondance Gauguin 1984, p. 284. It cannot be said with certainty which of Gauguin’s drawings Theo received.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱이 아를과 노란 집, 그리고 자신에게 실망하여 낙담한 상태임을 전하며, 그가 떠나든 남든 스스로 결정하도록 차분히 기다리겠다고 말한다. 두 사람 사이의 어려움이 외부 요인이 아니라 서로의 내면에 있다고 통찰하며, 고갱에게는 평온이 필요하다는 짧지만 무거운 심경을 전한다.
entries.why: Letter 726 used to be placed before 724, but we think – as do Pickvance, Merlhès and Dorn – that the order of these letters should be reversed. See exhib. cat. New York 1984, p. 262; Merlhès 1989, pp. 226-227; and Dorn 1990, pp. 525-527. In the present letter Vincent thanks Theo for the money he sent (ll. 2-4). Previous editions have assumed that this was the third instalment of the December allowance, namely the payment due on the 23rd (on this subject, see letter 736).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 고갱과 함께 몽펠리에 미술관의 브뤼야스 컬렉션을 관람한 경험을 전하며, 들라크루아가 그린 브뤼야스의 초상이 테오나 자신과 닮았다고 느낀 강렬한 인상을 묘사한다. 렘브란트와 들라크루아에 대해 고갱과 나눈 격렬한 토론(마치 방전된 전지처럼 지쳤다고 표현)을 전하며, 렘브란트를 '마술사', 들라크루아를 '신의 사람'으로 비유한 프로망탱의 말을 인용한다. 드 한과 이사악손 등 네덜란드 화가 친구들에게도 이 경험을 전해달라고 부탁한다.

facts.said: My dear Theo, Yesterday Gauguin and I went to Montpellier to see the museum there, and especially the Bruyas room
facts.note: The Musée Fabre in Montpellier, a city about 70 km to the west of Arles, housed the collection of Alfred Bruyas. This wealthy collector had become known mainly as the Maecenas of Gustave Courbet. In 1868 Bruyas donated part of his collection to the Musée Fabre, and his bequest followed in 1876. The Bruyas Collection contains 142, principally French, contemporary paintings (including 17 portraits of Bruyas), 48 drawings and 17 bronzes.

facts.said: Say so to Degas,
facts.note: Since late 1886 Theo had been dealing in the work of Degas. It emerges from a number of undated letters written by Degas to Theo (FR b1145-1152) that they kept in touch and that Theo visited Degas in his studio. See also Thomson in exhib. cat. Amsterdam 1999, p. 107, and Kendall 1999, p. 38. Theo had probably written something about Degas to Vincent that was similar to what he wrote to his sister Willemien on 6 December 1888: ‘Degas is terribly pleased with Gauguin’s work. So much so that he even wants to go to Arles to visit him.

entries.summary: 귀를 자른 사건 이후 병원에 입원한 반 고흐가 테오를 안심시키기 위해 직접 쓴 짧은 편지로, 곧 집으로 돌아갈 수 있기를 바란다고 전한다. 고갱이 왜 소식이 없는지 궁금해하며 그가 파리로 떠난 것을 이해한다는 뜻을 전한다. 담당 의사 펠릭스 레이가 이어 쓴 글에서는 환자의 흥분 상태가 일시적이며 곧 회복될 것이라는 낙관적인 소견을 덧붙인다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘Arles, le 2 Janvier 1889’.

people.name: Andries (André or Dries) Bonger
people.note: (1861-1936) friend of Theo in Paris, brother of Jo van Gogh-Bonger

people.name: Johanna (Jo or Net) Gezina van Gogh-Bonger
Félix Rey
people.note: (1865-1932) assistant physician in the hospital in Arles

facts.said: I’ll stay here at the hospital for another few days — then I dare plan to return home very calmly.
facts.note: On the evening of 23 December 1888, Van Gogh suffered an acute mental breakdown. As a result he cut off his left ear and took it to a prostitute in a local brothel. The police found him at home the next morning and had him admitted to hospital. On 24 December Gauguin sent a telegram to Theo, who immediately took the night train to Arles. Despite Van Gogh’s repeated pleas, Gauguin did not come to visit him in hospital (see letter 736).

facts.said: Good handshake, I’ve read and re-read your letter about the meeting with the Bongers.
facts.note: After a long period of silence, Theo was again in touch with Andries Bonger and his sister Jo, who had refused his proposal of marriage in 1887 (see letter 572, n. 1). The renewed acquaintance led to Theo and Jo’s engagement. On 21 December 1888 Theo told his mother of their plans and asked for her consent (FR b917). The engagement party took place on 9 January in Amsterdam (see letter 731), and the marriage was solemnized there on 18 April 1889 (see letter 759). At that time Theo was staying with his cousin Jan Stricker (FR b2891).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 자신의 사고(귀 절단 사건) 소식에 놀라 병문안 온 테오에게 걱정 끼친 것을 미안해하며 곧 병원에서 퇴원해 작업을 재개하겠다고 알린다. 봉허르 가족과 화해한 테오의 소식을 기뻐하고, 노란 집을 관리해 준 룰랭에게 고마움을 전한다. 고갱에게는 그의 그림들을 돌려주고 가구비를 갚아야 한다는 책임감도 밝힌다.
entries.why: The letter was written when Van Gogh was allowed to leave the hospital for a few hours and went to the Yellow House (ll. 7-11, 40-42). This was on Friday, 4 January 1889, as evidenced by a letter Joseph Roulin sent on this day to Theo (FR b1068).

people.name: Andries (André or Dries) Bonger
people.note: (1861-1936) friend of Theo in Paris, brother of Jo van Gogh-Bonger

people.name: Anne (Annie) Marie Louise Bonger-Van der Linden
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: We owe him the money he spent on the furniture.
facts.note: Gauguin had bought ‘a chest of drawers’ and ‘various household utensils’ for the Yellow House; see letter 717.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent Also write a line to Mother on my behalf, so that no one will be worried.
facts.note: Theo must have informed their mother straightaway of Vincent’s condition, because she already answered his letter on 29 December from Leiden (FR b2425). This remarkable letter from Mrs van Gogh was published in its entirety, along with an English translation, in Jansen et al. 2003-2. Vincent also wrote to his mother; see letter 733.

facts.said: When I come out I’ll be able to continue on my way here again, and soon the fine days will come and I’ll start on the orchards in blossom again.
facts.note: In March-April 1888 Van Gogh had made a series of paintings of orchards in blossom; see letter 600, n. 7.

facts.said: The charwoman and my friend Roulin had taken care of the house, put everything in good order.
facts.note: Van Gogh was home again for the first time in two weeks, in the company of Roulin, who informed Theo that he and Vincent had spent four hours in the Yellow House. Roulin went on to write: ‘he is as meek as a lamb’ (il est doux comme un agneau) (FR b1068). The charwoman was Thérèse Balmoissière.

facts.said: Say so on my behalf to André, and give him a very cordial handshake from me.
facts.note: In the second half of 1887, Theo and Andries Bonger had drifted apart, since the latter wanted nothing to do with the bohemian artists with whom Theo associated since Vincent’s arrival in Paris. See Brief happiness 1999, pp. 20-21. Andries’s wife, Annie, may also have played a role in their estrangement.

entries.summary: 귀 절단 사건 이후 병원에서 처음 외출한 순간 고갱에게 보낸 진심 어린 우정의 편지로, 병중에도 그를 많이 생각했다고 전한다. 테오가 걱정하지 않도록 안심시켜 달라 부탁하며, 노란 집에 대해 성급히 나쁘게 말하지 말아 달라고 조심스럽게 청한다. 자신을 병원에서 빼내준 룰랭에게 고마움을 표하며 짧지만 절실한 화해와 우정의 몸짓을 보인다.
entries.why: Like letter 729 to Theo, this letter was written on Friday, 4 January 1889. This was, after all, the day of Vincent’s ‘first trip out of the hospital’ (ll. 2-3). See letter 729, Date.

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: With a good handshake Ever yours, Vincent Roulin has been really kind to me, it was he who had the presence of mind to get me out of there before the others were convinced.
facts.note: Van Gogh means that Roulin had arranged for him to leave the hospital for a short while on 4 January. On that day Roulin wrote to Theo: ‘Monsieur the house doctor felt slightly anxious about letting him go out; I told him that I would be in charge of accompanying him and seeing that he returns to the hospital’ (FR b1068).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 귀 절단 사건 이후 병원에서 퇴원해 집으로 돌아왔음을 알리며 테오를 걱정시킨 것에 대해 사과한다. 레이 박사의 초상화를 그릴 계획과 몽펠리에 미술관에서 본 들라크루아의 브뤼야스 초상에 대한 감동을 전하며, 부모님께는 가벼운 병으로 둘러대 달라고 부탁한다. 병원에서의 며칠이 오히려 흥미로운 경험이었다고 담담히 서술한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he has returned home ‘today’ (l. 5). We know from a letter dated 7 January 1889 which Joseph Roulin wrote to Theo (FR b1069), as well as from Roulin’s letter of 8 January 1889 to Willemien (FR b710), that Vincent was released from hospital on 7 January 1889. For this last letter, see Documentation, 8 January 1889.

works.title: Portrait of Doctor Felix Rey
works.said: Now I’m planning to do Mr Rey’s portrait and possibly other portraits as soon as I’ve accustomed myself a little to painting once again.

works.title: Irises
works.said: In any case, as regards the Independents,

works.title: Flowering peach tree
works.said: I’ll write to Mother and Wil one of these days, I must also write to Jet Mauve.

people.name: Johanna (Jo or Net) Gezina van Gogh-Bonger

facts.said: We dined together today.
facts.note: Roulin had accompanied Van Gogh the first time he was allowed to leave the hospital, on 4 January, and had arranged some practical matters for him, such as paying the rent and cleaning out the house. See letter 730. When Van Gogh was released from hospital, Roulin stayed with him the whole day. See Joseph Roulin to Willemien van Gogh, Documentation, 8 January 1889.

facts.said: I told him that we’d get an engraving of it for his study.
facts.note: A bit further on in the letter Van Gogh mentions the publisher François Buffa. An undated publisher’s catalogue of Buffa lists the etching that C.L. Dake made after Rembrandt’s Anatomy lesson. The large print (64 x 84 cm) was available on various kinds of paper, the most expensive costing 60 guilders (c. 120 francs). See Catalogue des éditions de François Buffa & fils. Fournisseurs de la cour, éditeurs, marchands de Beaux-arts, tableaux, aquarelles, gravures, eau-fortes, encadrements, ouvrages illustrés, restauration et vernissage de tableaux, etc. etc. Exposition permanente. Amsterdam, Kalverstraat 39.

facts.said: I dare hope to get to know him better.
facts.note: In letter 735 Van Gogh reports that this doctor came from Paris, but it is not known to whom he is referring. In any case, it is certain that Albert Delon had worked as a house physician in Paris (below his contributions to L’Homme de Bronze is written ‘former house physician of the hospital in Paris’ (ancien interne des hospices de Paris)). He treated Van Gogh in February 1889. See letter 747, n. 1. Dr Auriol, who had also been trained in Paris, also worked at the hospital as a surgeon (ACA).

facts.said: In any case, as regards the Independents,
facts.note: Evidently Theo had been asked to submit works by Vincent to the fifth exhibition of the Société des Artistes Indépendants, to be held in Paris from 3 September to 4 October 1889. At their 1888 exhibition Van Gogh had exhibited three works; see letter 582, nn. 8 and 9. It is possible that the exhibition, which was usually held in the spring, was postponed to coincide with the World Exhibition (5 May - 5 November).

facts.said: As his family are in the north, and as he’s been invited to exhibit in Belgium and has some success in Paris at the moment,
facts.note: Gauguin had been invited to display his work at the sixth exhibition of the artists’ society Les Vingt in Brussels; see letter 723, n. 12. By Gauguin’s success in Paris Vincent is referring to the fact that between 10 November and 4 December Theo had sold works by Gauguin for a total of 1,700 francs. See letter 722, n. 1.

entries.to_en: Anna van Gogh and Willemien van Gogh
entries.summary: 어머니와 여동생 빌레미나에게 새해 인사를 전하며 12월에 몸이 좋지 않았지만 완전히 회복했다고 안심시키는 편지이다. 테오가 자신의 병에 대해 이야기했을까 봐 걱정해 직접 소식을 전하며, 겨울철 홍수에도 네덜란드보다 온화한 날씨라고 알린다. 테오의 방문이 예년보다 일찍 있을 수도 있다는 소식과 함께 가족에 대한 그리움을 표현한다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘Arles 7 Januari 89’.

people.name: Willemina (Wil or Willemien) Jacoba van Gogh
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

facts.said: It wouldn’t really surprise me if he came rather earlier than usual this year, that’s to say before the exhibition instead of after it.
facts.note: Theo usually had two weeks of holiday, during which he went to the Netherlands. Vincent’s mention of ‘the exhibition’ no doubt refers to the annual Salon in Paris, which was held from 1 May until mid-July. In 1889 the World Exhibition would also be starting in May, on the 5th. He assumed that Theo would be going to the Netherlands earlier this year, because of his intended marriage to Jo Bonger; evidently Theo had told him that he wanted to marry before the exhibition opened (the marriage took place on 18 April).

entries.summary: 귀 절단 사건 이후 빈센트는 테오의 약혼 소식에 축하를 전하며, 병원에서 회복 중인 자신의 상태(불면증, 상처 치유 등)를 자세히 알린다. 고갱이 열대지방행 계획을 포기하지 않았다는 소식에 기뻐하고, 자신을 치료한 레이 의사와 화상들 간의 사업 관계 조율에 대해서도 이야기한다. 집주인이 자신을 내쫓으려 한다는 걱정과 드가에 대한 인상적인 회고도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written a couple of days after 7 January, the day Van Gogh was released from hospital: he not only had his wound dressed again that day, but he also received the announcement of Theo and Jo’s engagement. Like Jo van Gogh-Bonger in Brieven 1914, who had sent the announcement (l. 3), we have dated the letter to Wednesday, 9 January 1889.

works.title: Still life with a plate of onions
works.said: I’m fighting this insomnia with a very, very strong dose of camphor in my pillow and my mattress, and I recommend it to you if you ever have trouble sleeping.

works.title: Self-portrait, dedicated to Paul Gauguin
works.said: Have you seen the portrait of me that Gauguin has,

facts.said: My dear Theo, Even before receiving (this very moment) your kind letter, I received a letter from your fiancée this morning announcing the engagement.
facts.note: For this engagement announcement, see letter 731. Theo stayed from 5 to 13 January in the Netherlands; the engagement party took place on 9 January. Vincent sent the present letter to Amsterdam (cf. l. 206).

facts.said: I’ve just been told that in my absence the owner of my house here apparently made a contract with a fellow who has a tobacco shop, to turn me out and give him, the tobacconist, the house.
facts.note: Even though Van Gogh speaks of ‘the owner of my house’ (this was Marie Louise Verdier), it is more likely that he is referring to his agent Bernard Soulè. See letter 602, n. 19. The tobacconist was probably Charles Viany, who signed the petition against Van Gogh at the end of February: ‘Viany, retail tobacconist’ (Viany, receveur buraliste). His wife, Marie Ourtoule, was the ‘retail tobacconist of place Lamartine’ (débitante de tabac demeurant Place de Lamartine) in the summons drawn up in response to the petition. See letter 750, nn. 2 and 3 and Documentation (shortly before 27 February 1889).

facts.said: continue to menace the area around Marseille.
facts.note: In 1884-1885 there had been a cholera epidemic in Marseille. The last plague epidemic in Western Europe was ‘the great plague’ of 1720-1722, which began in Marseille and spread over all of Provence. The passage was no doubt prompted by Dr Rey’s involvement in fighting the smallpox epidemic raging in Arles from October 1888 until the end of April 1889. In his report on this epidemic, Rey recorded 41 cases of infection and 6 deaths. The governors of the hospital praised his efforts in a ‘congratulatory note for his devotion [to duty]’ (note de félicitation pour son dévouement) (ACA).

facts.said: himself does his full duty as regards listening to you and putting you and his son together.
facts.note: Van Gogh later added ‘et à mettre ensemble son fils et toi’ (and putting you and his son together). In May 1891 Cornelis Marinus van Gogh (Uncle Cor) transferred ownership of his bookshop and art dealership to his son Vincent, who carried on the business under the name C.M. van Gogh.

facts.said: Have you seen the portrait of me that Gauguin has, and have you seen the portrait that Gauguin did of himself during those final days?
facts.note: Paul Gauguin, Self-portrait dedicated to Charles Laval (later to Eugène Carrière), 1888 (W384) (Washington, National Gallery of Art, Collection of Mr and Mrs Paul Mellon). Ill. 2144. In Wildenstein 1963 this portrait was dated to 1889, but recent research has shown that Gauguin painted it in December 1888, on the canvas of coarse jute he had bought in Arles (see letters 717, n. 7 and 716, n. 8, and exhib. cat. Chicago 2001, pp. 247, 362-363.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 병원에서 퇴원한 후 극심한 생활고를 상세한 지출 내역과 함께 토로하며, 며칠간 굶다시피 했음을 전한다. 고갱이 급전보를 보내 초래한 불필요한 비용을 비판하면서도 그를 무책임이 아닌 상상력과 자존심에 이끌린 인물로 이해하려 하고, 자신의 해바라기 그림은 절대 내줄 수 없다는 단호한 입장을 밝힌다. 룰랭 가족과의 우정, 드 한의 그림에 대한 감상, 그리고 자신의 빈 의자와 고갱의 빈 의자를 그린 두 점의 습작을 언급하며 편지를 맺는다.
entries.why: On the basis of ll. 48-49: ‘today, 17 January’ (‘aujourd’hui 17 janvier’), the letter has been dated to Thursday, 17 January 1889.

facts.said: Nevertheless, I’ve started work again and I already have 3 studies done in the studio
facts.note: These three studies were probably Still life with onions and Annuaire de la santé (F 604 / JH 1656), Self-portrait with bandaged ear (F 527 / JH 1657) and Self-portrait with bandaged ear and pipe (F 529 / JH 1658). F 604 probably contains a depiction of the envelope in which Theo’s letter had arrived on 23 December (l. 23). His handwriting is recognizable, and the number ‘67’ in the postmark refers to place des Abbesses (office 67), the address of the post office where the letter was franked. There are also two postage stamps, one yellowish green, the other blue.

facts.said: Next there must be added the fact that you sent 30 francs to Roulin, out of which he paid the 21.50 for the rent for December.
facts.note: Theo had sent Roulin a postal order for 30 francs to pay the rent for December (21.50 francs). Roulin confirmed receipt of the payment in his letter to Theo of 7 January 1889 (FR b1069).

facts.said: The increase in salary is minimal, and he’ll have to leave his wife and his children for a while, who won’t be able to follow him until much later because the expenses of a whole family would be heavier in Marseille.
facts.note: In Marseille Roulin took up the post of ‘courrier-convoyeur’ (an official in the postal carriage in the train, in charge of loading and unloading the postbags at each station and sorting the post during the journey). Van Gogh made a note of Roulin’s duties and his address in Marseille (see letter 742, Additional details). Roulin’s wife was staying with their children at her mother’s in Lambesc until they could move to Marseille in October 1889 (see letter 814).

facts.said: I didn’t think I was doing anything compromising by saying to Mr Rey myself that if he went to Paris it would give me great pleasure if he wanted to take a painting from me to Mr Rivet as a keepsake.
facts.note: This question also arose in letter 735. On 30 December 1888 Félix Rey had written to Theo: In a few months, when I submit my doctoral thesis in Paris, I too should be happy if somebody were able to take an interest in me at a difficult moment. (Dans quelques mois, lorsque j’irai passer ma thèse de doctorat à Paris; je serais heureux moi aussi, que quelqu’un pût s’interesser à moi dans le malheur) (FR b1056; see Documentation, 30 December 1888). The letter Theo wrote to Rey, to which Vincent refers, was no doubt a reaction to this. It is not known if Van Gogh gave Rivet a painting.

facts.said: But for the moment I’m keeping my canvases here, and I’m categorically keeping those sunflowers of mine.
facts.note: This reveals that Gauguin had asked in the missing part of letter 734 for the painting Sunflowers in a vase (F 454 / JH 1562), the ‘sunflowers on a yellow background’ which is also mentioned in letter 739. It had been hanging – together with its pendant, Sunflowers in a vase (F 456 / JH 1561) – in Gauguin’s room in Arles (letter 743). Van Gogh did not want to trade F 454 for the studies Gauguin had left behind, and suggested making a repetition as a compromise (letter 739). He had intended the first two versions of the sunflowers for Theo (letter 741).

entries.summary: 가스 요금까지 지불하고 나니 생활비가 거의 남지 않았다며 추가 송금을 요청하고, 몸이 여전히 쇠약해 회복이 더디다고 전한다. 테오의 약혼 소식에 대한 축하와 함께 어머니의 오랜 바람이 이루어졌다며 기뻐한다. 우편배달부 룰랭이 박봉으로 세 자녀를 키우면서도 소크라테스 같은 인품을 지녔다고 애정 어린 평을 남기며, 고갱과는 여전히 서로를 아끼는 사이라고 전한다.
entries.why: Because Jo van Gogh-Bonger dated the letter to Saturday, 19 January 1889 in Brieven 1914 – it is possible she had a postmark to rely on – we have retained this dating. In any case it must have been written after letter 736 of Thursday, 17 January, in which Vincent had given a summary of his expenses, as appears from the remark about the gas bill (ll. 2-5), a subject not yet mentioned on the 17th. Here he says he received it ‘yesterday’. The phrase ‘I must write you another line today’ (ll.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 아를을 떠난 고갱에게 보내는 편지에서 노란 집에 홀로 남겨진 상실감과 룰랭 가족과의 이별 장면을 애틋하게 묘사한다. 고갱이 원했던 해바라기 그림을 둘러싼 소유권 문제를 다루면서도 두 점을 다시 그려 화해하자고 제안하며, 룰랭 부인의 초상(라 베르쇠즈) 작업에 대한 색채 구상을 상세히 전한다. 정신적 위기 속에서도 베를리오즈와 바그너의 음악처럼 위로가 되는 회화를 만들고 싶다는 예술적 신념을 재확인한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh writes that Roulin has just left for Marseille (l. 8). Since his departure took place on Monday, 21 January 1889 (see letter 738, l. 232), we have dated the letter to the same day.

facts.said: And I believe that if one placed this canvas just as it is in a boat, even one of Icelandic fishermen, there would be some who would feel the lullaby in it.
facts.note: Van Gogh’s idea of hanging his painting of the Berceuse in a fishing boat was prompted by what Pierre Loti writes in Pêcheur d’Islande (1886) about the custom of fishermen to hang the image of a saint in the saloon: ‘Against a panel at the far end, a Blessed Virgin in ceramic was set on a little shelf, in a place of honour. She was a little antique, these sailors’ patron saint, and painted in a naïve style. But ceramic figures last much longer than real men; and her red and blue robe still had the effect of a very fresh little thing in the midst of all the dark greys of this poor wooden house.

facts.said: And that then it was perhaps up to me to show that I still had the right to be kept frankly au courant.
facts.note: Gauguin was considering returning to Paris around mid-December 1888, but changed his mind and decided to stay. See letter 724, n. 1.

facts.said: Today I made a fresh start on the canvas I had painted of Mrs Roulin, the one which had remained in a vague state as regards the hands because of my accident.
facts.note: Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 508 / JH 1671). See Hoermann Lister 2001, p. 72. A short while later Van Gogh made repetitions of both Sunflowers in a vase (F 456 / JH 1561) and Sunflowers in a vase (F 454 / JH 1562), which had been hanging in Gauguin's room, in order to make an exchange (see letters 743 and 745).

facts.said: a consolatory art for distressed hearts!
facts.note: The fact that Van Gogh mentions Berlioz and Wagner in the same sentence could be connected with the book he had read about Wagner (see letter 621, n. 7), which included an article by Wagner on Berlioz. The article ‘L’Amour dans la musique’ (Love in music), which Van Gogh talks about in letter 686, also mentions Berlioz a number of times.

entries.summary: 아를 병원에서 겪은 발작에 대해 담담하고 다소 자조적인 어조로 설명하며, 자신의 광기에 대한 판단은 후세에 맡기겠다는 태도를 보인다. '자장가(라 베르쇠즈)'라 이름 붙인 룰랭 부인의 초상화를 색채별로 상세히 설명하며 반 에이든의 문학과 자신의 회화적 시도를 연결짓는다. 퇴원 후 자신을 치료한 레이 박사의 초상화도 그렸으며, 테오의 약혼 소식과 여름에 그린 해바라기 연작도 함께 전한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he is working on his painting of the Berceuse (ll. 43-45). Because he also reports this to Gauguin and Theo in the letters of Monday, 21 and Tuesday, 22 January (letters 739 and 741), we have dated the present letter to about Tuesday, 22 January 1889.

facts.said: My dear friend Koning, Thank you for sending me New Year’s greetings from the far north of our old native country.
facts.note: Koning had sent a postcard from Winschoten on 31 December 1888 (letter 727).

facts.said: Theo went to see Breitner recently,
facts.note: Theo met Breitner while staying in Amsterdam from 6 to 11 January 1889. Breitner was then working in a studio at Eerste Parkstraat 438. They had already known each other for a long time. See Jessica Voeten, Het Witsenhuis. Amsterdam and Antwerp 2003, p. 29.

facts.said: If you see Breitner, you may let him read this epistle or tell him about it just as I write it, without bringing too much of your own imagination into play.
facts.note: Van Gogh later pencilled in the sentence ‘als ... brengen’ (If you ... into play’).

facts.said: And if not, whether I already was before that time;
facts.note: In 1880 Mr van Gogh was planning to have his son committed to the Belgian lunatic asylum of Geel. See letter 155, n. 1 and 185, n. 3.

facts.said: I’ve seen absolutely nothing of your studies sent to Theo (I believe), despite urging you to make an exchange.
facts.note: For the studies that Koning sent to Theo, see letter 666, n. 9. The proposal to exchange work with Koning came up in letters 600 and 614.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 룰랭 가족과의 이별 장면을 감동적으로 묘사하며, 자신의 그림이 화가 수업 비용을 회수할 자격이 있다는 소신을 밝힌다. 고갱의 갑작스러운 떠남에 대한 안타까움과 자책, 테오의 결혼 소식에 대한 진심 어린 축복, 해바라기 그림에 대한 고갱의 찬사와 몽티첼리 부케에 견줄 만한 가치 등을 이야기하며 가족에 대한 어린 시절 추억도 회상한다.
entries.why: Vincent reports that Roulin left ‘yesterday’. The letter can therefore be dated to Tuesday, 22 January 1889 (See letter 743, Date). This agrees with the fact that Theo forwarded this letter on Wednesday, 23 January to his fiancée, Jo Bonger (see Brief happiness 1999, p. 106).

facts.said: And although today everyone will be afraid of me, that may disappear with time.
facts.note: The fear that others were afraid of him is confirmed by Theo, who wrote to Jo Bonger a short time later, on 14 February 1889: ‘If I had time, I should go and see him and go hiking with him, for instance. That’s the only thing I can think of that would really give him peace of mind. If one of the painters might like to do that I shall send him there. But those he gets on with are slightly afraid of him, which Gauguin’s visit to him did nothing to change, on the contrary’ (see FR b2035; Brief happiness 1999, p. 160).

facts.said: And all in all it will give me pleasure to continue the exchanges with Gauguin,
facts.note: Van Gogh and Gauguin had exchanged paintings in November 1887 (see letter 576, n. 2) and in October 1888 (see letter 697).

facts.said: To telegraph, as you rightly say, I couldn’t do by the same sheer chance, for I didn’t know if you were still in Amsterdam or back in Paris.
facts.note: In letters 736 and 738 Vincent had urgently requested money from Theo, because the money that he expected to receive around 10 January did not arrive until the 17th.

facts.said: I’ve just finished a new canvas which has an almost chic little look to it, a willow basket with lemons and oranges — a cypress branch and a pair of blue gloves, you’ve already seen some of these fruit-baskets of mine.
facts.note: Blue gloves and a basket of oranges and lemons (F 502 / JH 1664). In Paris Van Gogh had painted two still lifes of baskets of fruit: Basket of apples (F 378 / JH 1340) and Basket of apples (F 379 / JH 1341). In Arles he made Basket of oranges (F 395 / JH 1363), which he compared in letter 592 with the Paris still lifes and included in the first batch of paintings he sent to Theo (see letter 606).

facts.said: If, for example, our Monticelli bouquet is worth 500 francs to an art lover, and it’s worth that, then I dare assure you that my sunflowers
facts.note: Van Gogh no doubt means ‘the two canvases of sunflowers’ mentioned later in the letter: Sunflowers in a vase (F 456 / JH 1561) and Sunflowers in a vase (F 454 / JH 1562). They were hanging in Gauguin’s room in the Yellow House, and Vincent assumed that Theo had seen them during his visit to Arles (see letter 743).

entries.summary: 발작 이후 회복 상태를 전하며 해바라기와 자장가 그림을 반복 제작해 7~9점의 연작으로 구성하려는 계획을 설명한다. 몬티첼리와 브뤼야스의 전통을 잇고 있다는 확신과 함께 2월, 3월 동안 250프랑씩 추가 지원이 필요하다고 요청한다. 고갱과의 관계, 미쳐도 좋으니 계속 작업하게 해달라는 절박함, 열대 예술론에 대한 신념을 함께 토로한다.
entries.why: Van Gogh says that he has just put the finishing touches on the repetitions of the sunflower paintings (ll. 19-20). We know that Roulin visited Van Gogh shortly afterwards. From letter 744, which we have dated to Wednesday, 30 January, it emerges that Roulin had visited Vincent the previous Monday (letter 744, ll. 3-4).

facts.said: I tell you, the so-called ‘Félibres’ had anyway spared themselves neither trouble nor expense.
facts.note: In Provence, pastoral plays were especially popular, having developed from the liturgy. In the nineteenth century they combined Christmas traditions, hymns and stereotypes patterned after life (the ‘santons’). The plot followed the story of the Nativity and was garnished with local intrigues. For the Provençal poets’ society ‘Les Félibres’, see letter 704, n. 14. The ‘Folies arlésiennes’, where Van Gogh had seen the play, was a café-concert with a ‘salle des fêtes’ in Arles. It was located at 4 avenue Victor Hugo.

facts.said: And once again, either lock me up in a madhouse straightaway,
facts.note: During his first stay in hospital, Van Gogh had been in isolation (in a ‘cabanon’, or padded cell) for two or three days, as emerges from Dr Félix Rey’s letter of 17 March 1922 to Gustave Coquiot (FR b3282). Rey described the cell to Theo as ‘un appartement isolé’ (separate quarters) (FR b1055; Documentation, 29 December 1888).

facts.said: I think I’ve already told you that in addition I have a canvas of a Berceuse, the very same one I was working on when my illness came and interrupted me.
facts.note: Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 508 / JH 1671); Van Gogh wrote about this canvas in letter 741.

facts.said: Beware of 93, you may perhaps tell me.
facts.note: The French Revolution began with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 and led in 1793 to the Jacobin Reign of Terror, during which tens of thousands of people died under the guillotine.

facts.said: Today I also have 2 versions of this one.
facts.note: The second version is Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 506 / JH 1670). See Hoermann Lister 2001, p. 72.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 우편배달부 룰랭과의 재회와 프랑스 총선 결과에 대한 마르세유 군중의 감동적인 반응을 전한다. 해바라기 연작을 반복해서 그렸고 자장가를 부르는 여인(베르소즈) 그림 두 점을 완성했다고 알리며, 주변 사람들의 따뜻한 배려에 감사한다. 정신적으로 여전히 격정이 남아 있음을 인정하면서도 이곳 프랑스인들과 함께한 시간에 대한 애정을 표현한다.
entries.why: The letter dates from after the elections of Sunday, 27 January (see n. 1) and from before 1 February 1889 (l. 104). Jo van Gogh-Bonger gave the date as 30 January 1889 in Brieven 1914 – presumably she relied on a postmark. Because this date agrees with Van Gogh’s observation ‘The weather today has been magnificent with no wind’ (ll. 92-93) – after the mistral it was in fact almost completely calm from 28-31 January (Météo-France) – we have likewise dated the letter to Wednesday, 30 January 1889.

facts.said: There was good reason for it too — the whole of France having shivered.
facts.note: On 27 January 1889 the controversial general Georges Boulanger was elected to a Paris seat in the Chamber of Deputies by a large majority. Great numbers of his supporters took to the street, demanding that Boulanger should occupy the Palais de l’Elysée and depose President Carnot. Boulanger refused, however, to stage a coup. Roulin was a Boulangist (cf. letter 667).

facts.said: When Roulin came I had just finished the repetition of my sunflowers, and I showed him the two examples of the Berceuse between these four bouquets.
facts.note: These two versions of Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) are F 508 / JH 1671 and F 506 / JH 1670.

facts.said: Everyone here is good towards me, the neighbours &c., good and attentive as in one’s native country.
facts.note: The Roulins, the Ginouxs of the Café de la Gare and the charwoman, Thérèse Balmoissière, were all supportive of Van Gogh. He was on less good terms with his immediate neighbours, Mr and Mrs Crévoulin, whom he mockingly compares in letter 657 with the Buteaux in Zola’s La terre . A short while later they signed the petition to have Van Gogh committed (see letter 750).

facts.said: Today I started work on a third Berceuse.
facts.note: The third version of the Berceuse is Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 505 / JH 1669). See Hoermann Lister 2001, p. 72.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 룰랭 부인을 모델로 세 번 그린 '자장가(베르세즈)' 연작을 소개하며, 미스트랄의 언어가 음악적으로 들린다는 인상을 전한다. 자신의 병을 담담히 받아들이며 야망은 화가라는 직업과 어울리지 않는다는 성찰을 밝히고, 재발 시에는 다시 병원이나 정신과 의사를 찾겠다고 다짐한다. 이웃들이 자신에게 친절하며 병자들끼리 한 가족처럼 지낸다고 전하고, 고갱이 해바라기 그림을 원한다면 그 대가로 좋은 작품을 달라고 요청한다.
entries.why: Jo van Gogh-Bonger, who presumably had the postmark at her disposal, dated the letter to Sunday, 3 February 1889 (Brieven 1914). We have retained this dating, which agrees with the receipt of Theo’s letter containing 100 francs – Vincent hoped to receive it ‘as early as possible after 1 February’ (letter 744, ll. 103-104), to which he would have liked to reply immediately (ll. 1*-6).

facts.said: Yesterday I went back to see the girl I went to when I went out of my mind.
facts.note: The ‘Chronique locale’ in Le Forum Républicain of Sunday, 30 December 1888 reported that in the night of 23 December Van Gogh had offered his severed ear to ‘a certain Rachel’ (la nommée Rachel) at ‘brothel No. 1’ (maison de tolérance No. 1) in rue du Bout d’Arles. The brothel was on the corner of rue des Glacières and rue du Bout d'Arles. Police officer Alphonse Robert later recalled that the girl worked under the name of Gaby (Doiteau and Leroy 1939, p. 6). The identity of the prostitute Rachel/Gaby remains a mystery. For an interpretation see Murphy 2016, pp. 66-69, 217-227.

facts.said: But I’ve already told Rey that at the slightest serious symptom I’d come back and then subject myself to the alienist doctors of Aix
facts.note: From Van Gogh’s first stay in hospital, there had been tentative plans to have him taken to an asylum in Aix-en-Provence. On 29 December 1888 the mayor of Arles was asked to take measures to this end; see letter 728, n. 1. Roulin wrote about it to Theo on 28 December, and Mrs van Gogh was informed as well, as is apparent from her letter to Theo, written a day later (FR b1066 and FR b2425). At the end of February 1889 there was again talk of transferring Van Gogh to Aix; see letter 750, n. 3.

facts.said: Now as regards your move from rue Lepic to rue Rodier
facts.note: This move did not take place; on 4 February Theo rented an apartment at 8 cité Pigalle. He moved into the apartment with Jo on 20 April 1889. See Brief happiness 1999, pp. 27, 137. In January Theo had drawn a floor plan for Jo of the layout of the apartment (FR b1900; see Brief happiness 1999, p. 128 (with illustration opposite p. 144). He also gave his parents-in-law detailed information about the new apartment, including a floor plan.

facts.said: I’ve done the Berceuse three times,
facts.note: The three versions of Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) are F 508 / JH 1671, F 506 / JH 1670 and F 505 / JH 1669.

facts.said: I’ve done the Berceuse three times, now since Mrs Roulin was the model and I was only the painter, I let her choose between the three, her and her husband, only on condition that I’d do a repetition for myself of the one she took, which I’m working on at present.
facts.note: The Roulins chose Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 505 / JH 1669); the repetition of it (the fourth version) is F 507 / JH 1672. See Hoermann Lister 2001, p. 73.

entries.summary: 정신 발작에서 회복해 다시 귀가한 뒤, 자신의 병이 이 지역 특유의 것이라면 이곳에서 조용히 견디는 편이 낫다고 판단한다는 뜻을 밝힌다. 엑스로의 이송 문제에 대해 자신의 의견도 존중받아야 한다고 주장하며, 아를 사람들의 편견에도 불구하고 이웃과 레이 박사에게서 받은 우정에 감사한다고 전한다. 코닝, 드 한, 이사악손 등 화가들에게는 더 이상 아를행을 권하지 않겠다고 말한다.
entries.why: This letter, which arrived in Paris on the evening of Tuesday, 19 February, was forwarded by Theo to Jo Bonger on 20 February. See Brief happiness 1999, p. 172. We have therefore dated it to Monday, 18 February 1889.

facts.said: Today I’ve just returned home for the time being, I hope for good.
facts.note: Around 4 February 1889 Van Gogh suffered a second mental breakdown. Rev. Frédéric Salles informed Theo on 7 February that Vincent had been readmitted to hospital that day, and that the doctors advised him to have himself admitted to an asylum. Salles wrote: ‘For three days he has thought he is being poisoned and just sees poisoners and victims of poison everywhere. The cleaning woman, who is showing considerable devotion in caring for him, faced with his more than abnormal condition, felt it her duty to tell others, and neighbours brought it to the attention of the police ...

facts.said: Our sister wrote to me that your fiancée would come to stay with them for a while.
facts.note: Jo stayed from 21 February to 7 March with Mrs van Gogh and Willemien in Breda. See Brief happiness 1999 pp. 174, 198.

facts.said: That in response to a letter I wrote him a few days ago.
facts.note: This was letter 746 of 15 February; Van Gogh’s letter of ‘a few days ago’ was letter 740, written on or about 22 January.

facts.said: Where can I go that’s worse than where I’ve already been twice – the isolation cell.
facts.note: For Van Gogh’s first confinement in the padded cell, see letter 743, n. 10. On 7 February he had again been placed in ‘a private cell’ (une cellule particulière), as Salles wrote to Theo (FR b1046).

facts.said: If sooner or later it were desirable that I should go to Aix, as has already been suggested
facts.note: Regarding the plans to transfer Van Gogh to an asylum in Aix-en-Provence, see letter 745, n. 6.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 병원에서 지내며 다시 작업을 시작했다고 전하며, 룰랭 부인이 가져간 라 베르쇠즈를 새로 그리고 있음을 알린다. 고갱과 베르나르의 편지에 아직 답하지 못한 어려움과 남부 지방 특유의 불안정한 정서(니스의 지진 공포 등)에 대한 예민한 반응을 토로한다. 병세가 심해질 가능성을 담담히 받아들이면서도 파리로 돌아가는 것은 원치 않는다는 심경을 전한다.
entries.why: On Tuesday, 26 February 1889 the Rev. Salles informed Theo that Vincent had been readmitted to hospital that very day, by order of the chief of police, after being at home for several days. Theo passed this news on to Jo on 27 February (see Brief Happiness 1999, p. 184). The present letter must have been written before Vincent’s hospitalization, because he is still at home, working on a repetition of The Berceuse.

facts.said: Mr Salles remitted me the 50 francs immediately.
facts.note: Salles wrote to Theo that Vincent had received these 50 francs, ‘when he left the hospital’ (au moment où il est sorti de l’hospice) (FR b1047, 26 February 1889). This must have been as early as 18 February, since Vincent wrote at the time: ‘Today I’ve just returned home for the time being’ (letter 747, ll. 4-5).

facts.said: When Mrs Roulin also left, to go and live with her mother in the country for the time being,
facts.note: The mother of Augustine Roulin, Rosalie Pelicot-Décès, lived in rue de la Campane in Lambesc, about 40 km east of Arles (Mairie de Lambesc).

facts.said: Currently all the town is anxious, nobody knows precisely why, and I saw in the newspapers that recently in places not very distant from here there had been more light shakes of earth tremor again.
facts.note: Van Gogh must be referring to the earthquake in the Dauphiné on 18 February 1889, which registered 6-7 on a scale of 12 and was therefore a moderate tremor. The Courrier des Alpes reported it on 21 February. We are indebted to Geneviève Patau, Institut du Physique du Globe de Paris, Département de Sismologie, for this information. A report of this earthquake in the local Arles newspapers has not been traced.

facts.said: She had a good eye and took the best one, only I’m currently redoing it.
facts.note: The sketch Van Gogh refers to is his first version: Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 508 / JH 1671). The two repetitions are F 505 / JH 1669 and F 506 / JH 1670. The Roulins had chosen F 505 / JH 1669; the repetition of it (the fourth version) is F 507 / JH 1672.

facts.said: As regards Koning, really I daren’t encourage him too much to come here, nor even with his gusto to get carried away with the south, with the experience I’m having of it at the moment.
facts.note: Koning had written in letter 746 about his plan to travel with a friend to France.

entries.summary: 80명 넘는 주민들의 탄원으로 다시 감금된 상황을 테오에게 알리며, 억울함 속에서도 흥분하지 않고 침착하게 버티겠다는 의지를 전한다. 테오가 직접 나서서 자신을 풀어주려 하지 말고 결혼과 자기 삶에 집중하라고 신신당부하며, 화실과 가구를 잃을까 걱정하는 현실적인 문제도 언급한다. 예술가로서 겪는 고난을 깨진 항아리에 비유하며 인간으로서 불평 없이 견디는 것이 삶의 유일한 교훈이라고 토로한다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘le 19 mars’. The subjects mentioned indicate that this must be Tuesday, 19 March 1889.

facts.said: The chief of police or the chief inspector then gave the order to have me locked up once again.
facts.note: As a result of this petition, Joseph d’Ornano, chief of police of the city of Arles, drew up a report on 27 February 1889 containing the neighbours’ statements. They reproached Van Gogh for over-indulging in drink, ‘after which he is in a state of over-excitement such that he no longer knows what he is doing or what he is saying’ (se livre à des excès de boissons après lesquels il se trouve dans un état de surexcitation tel qu’il ne sait plus, ni ce qu’il fait, ni ce qu’il dit).

facts.said: Besides, humility suits me after the experience of repeated attacks.
facts.note: After his first attack on 23 December 1888, during which he cut off part of his left ear (see letter 728, n. 1), Van Gogh remained in hospital until 7 January 1889. Less than a month later he suffered a renewed attack, which led to his hospitalization on 7 February (letter 747, n. 1). On the 18th he was allowed to leave the institution during the day, though he continued to eat and sleep at the hospital (see letters 757 and 748). A third attack followed on 26 February. In a later letter to Willemien, Vincent wrote that he had had four serious attacks of his illness (see letter 764).

facts.said: Wait until your journey to Holland at least.
facts.note: Theo travelled on 30 March to the Netherlands for his marriage to Jo on 18 April in Amsterdam. Immediately afterwards, they left for Brussels, where they spent their one-day honeymoon, returning on Saturday, 20 April to Paris. See Brief happiness 1999, pp. 27, 240 (n. 1) and letter 762.

facts.said: Tardieu) designating me as a man not worthy of living at liberty, or something like that.
facts.note: This petition, signed by 30 residents of the neighbourhood around place Lamartine, urgently requested the mayor, Jacques Tardieu, to have Van Gogh committed, because he supposedly presented a danger to the inhabitants of Arles. See Documentation, shortly before 27 February 1889 and Ill. 2278. Thus the number was considerably smaller than that mentioned by Van Gogh.

facts.said: I can’t move without expenses,
facts.note: In the light of the petition, the doctors and the Rev. Salles thought it better for Vincent not to return to the Yellow House, but to take up residence in another part of town. Salles informed Theo of this in his letter of 1 March 1889 (FR b1048).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 자신이 엄밀히 말해 미쳤다고 생각하지 않는다고 밝히며, 살 신부가 새 거처를 찾아주려는 노력에 감사한다. 시냐크의 방문을 반기면서도 자신을 둘러싼 소문과 간섭에 억울함을 토로하고, 반복되는 정신적 충격이 만성 질환으로 이어질까 우려한다. 차라리 정신병원에 남는 것이 낫다는 심경과 함께 테오의 결혼과 안정에 대한 바람을 전한다.
entries.why: Theo has replied to Vincent’s letter of 19 March (750). The present letter is an immediate reaction to Theo’s reply (ll. 1*-2). Signac, who was supposed to visit Vincent on 23 and 24 March, has not yet come (ll. 26-27). On the basis of this information, and considering that Van Gogh did not expect Theo to receive the letter before Sunday (ll. 44-45), we have dated it to Friday, 22 March 1889.

facts.said: Already I’ve seen in a newspaper here a really very good article on decadent or Impressionist literature
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring to the article ‘Les décadents’ by Adrien Frissant, which had been published in instalments in Le Forum Républicain of 3, 10 and 24 February and 3 March 1888. Frissant ridicules the basic principles, use of language and the conduct of the ‘Ecole décadente’, attacking in particular the incomprehensibility of symbolist poetry. In the last instalment he quotes the poet René Ghil, who had written in his foreword to his Légendes d’âmes et de sang not to seek words ‘which narrate’ but rather words ‘which impress’. Frissant therefore speaks of ‘the “Impressionist” language’ to which Van Gogh refers.

facts.said: Rest assured that if nothing happens I would now be able to do the same work in the orchards, and perhaps better, that I did the other year.
facts.note: In March-April 1888 Van Gogh had made a series of paintings of orchards in blossom; see letter 600, n. 7.

facts.said: I also envisage the thing that way.
facts.note: In response to Vincent’s previous letter (750), Theo must have gone into the issue of what should happen when Vincent was released from hospital. He, too, undoubtedly thought that moving to a different part of town was the best option.

facts.said: You’ll see that the canvases I’ve done in the intervals are calm and not inferior to others.
facts.note: Between the various attacks of his illness, Van Gogh painted the following canvases in any case: Still life with onions and Annuaire de la santé (F 604 / JH 1656), Self-portrait with bandaged ear (F 527 / JH 1657), Self-portrait with bandaged ear and pipe (F 529 / JH 1658), Félix Rey (F 500 / JH 1659), Blue gloves and a basket of oranges and lemons (F 502 / JH 1664), Sunflowers in a vase (F 455 / JH 1668), Sunflowers in a vase (F 458 / JH 1667) and three versions of Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’) (F 505 / JH 1669, F 506 / JH 1670 and F 507 / JH 1672).

entries.summary: 화가 시냐크가 방문해 큰 위로가 되었다는 소식을 전하며, 경찰이 부순 자물쇠 문제와 시냐크와 나눈 편안한 대화를 이야기한다. 지역 주민들의 탄원으로 작업과 생활에 어려움을 겪고 있지만 예술가로서의 자유를 지켜야 한다는 결의를 밝힌다. 병과 건강의 문제를 넘어선 근본적인 고통을 토로하며, 화구 몇 가지를 보내달라고 부탁한다.
entries.why: Paul Signac visited Van Gogh on Saturday, 23 and Sunday, 24 March, as emerges from what Signac wrote to Theo that same Sunday (see n. 1). Van Gogh wrote the present letter just after Signac had left. For this reason we have dated it, as did Jo van Gogh-Bonger in Brieven 1914 – she possibly had a postmark to rely on – to Sunday, 24 March 1889.

works.said: As a keepsake I gave him a still life which had exasperated the good gendarmes of the town of Arles because it depicted two smoked herrings, which are called gendarmes, as you know.

works.title: Smoked Herrings
works.said: You know that I did this same still life two or three times before in Paris,
