facts.said: Didn’t Rochefort with Hugo, Quinet and others give an eternal example by suffering exile, and the first even the penal colony.
facts.note: Henri Rochefort was banished three times and, after the 1871 Commune, sentenced to hard labour. Victor Hugo lived in exile for 20 years on Jersey and Guernsey, because he opposed Napoleon iii . After the fall of the empire (1871), he returned to Paris. Under Napoleon iii, Edgar Quinet was forced to flee to Belgium during the coup of 2 December 1851 because of his extremely democratic ideas. He was banished to Switzerland in 1858 and returned to France in 1870.

facts.said: My dear Theo, I’m writing to tell you that I’ve seen Signac, which did me a lot of good.
facts.note: Signac gave the following account of his visit to Vincent in a letter he wrote to Theo on Sunday, 24 March 1889: ‘I found your brother in a perfect state of physical and mental health. We went out together yesterday afternoon and again this morning. He took me to see his paintings, of which many are very good and all of them very intriguing. His kind doctor, the house physician Rey, believes that if he had a very methodical life, eating and drinking normally and at regular times, there would be every chance that his terrible crises would not be repeated.

facts.said: Do you know that expression by a Dutch poet I am tied to the earth With more than earthly bonds.
facts.note: Taken from the last verse of the poem ‘Stem des harten’ (Voice of the heart) by P.A. de Génestet: God grants the fullness of His best blessings; And sometimes gives poor mortal beings Both life’s zest and heavenly rest, Tying their hearts to the earth with more than earthly bonds. [God] schenkt de volheid van zijn beste zegeningen; En somtijds geeft Hij aan zijn arme stervelingen Ook levenslust bij hemelrust, En hecht hun hart aan de aard met meer dan aardsche banden. See De Génestet 1869, vol. 1, p. 138.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 이웃들의 청원 소동에도 불구하고 진짜 이웃들은 자신을 지지했다는 사실에 안도하며, 살레 목사의 도움으로 새 거처를 구할 가능성을 전한다. 베르소즈를 다섯 번째로 다시 그리고 있다고 말하며, 카르팡트라의 고대 묘비명 '누구도 원망하지 않은 여인'에 대한 사색을 나눈다. 테오의 결혼을 축하하며 진정한 평온과 남쪽의 의미에 대한 깊은 성찰로 편지를 맺는다.
entries.why: Vincent writes: ‘A few more words before you leave’ (l. 1*) and ‘If I want this letter to leave today I must end it’ (ll. 97-98). Theo took the night train to the Netherlands on 30 March, which is why we have dated the letter, as did Jo van Gogh-Bonger in Brieven 1914 – she perhaps relied on a postmark – to Friday, 29 March 1889.

facts.said: And here I am, going back to my figure of the Berceuse for the 5th time.
facts.note: Preceding his hospitalization on 26 February, Van Gogh had painted four versions of Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’): F 508 / JH 1671, F 505 / JH 1669, F 506 / JH 1670 and F 507 / JH 1672. See letter 748, n. 2. The fifth and last version, which is the one discussed here, was F 504 / JH 1655. See Hoermann Lister 2001, p. 73.

facts.said: When I went home I was able to learn that the real neighbours, those whom I know, weren’t among those who got up that petition.
facts.note: Van Gogh must be referring to the café proprietor Joseph Ginoux and his wife, Marie, who were friends of his. Ginoux had not signed the petition, but the statement he made to the police confirmed the neighbours’ complaints about Van Gogh’s indecent behaviour. See letter 750, nn. 2 and 3, Documentation, shortly before 27 February 1889, and Ill. 2278-2280.

facts.said: Here is this very, very, very old epitaph, let’s say from the time of Flaubert’s Salammbô:
facts.note: Flaubert’s historical novel Salammbô (1863) takes place in ancient Carthage. It is the story of rebellious mercenaries at the end of the First Punic War (264-241 BC). Their indignation at their paltry pay causes them to launch an attack on Carthage. They threaten the capital with the help of African tribes, but ultimately suffer a crushing defeat at the hands of Hamilkar Barkas.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 테오와 요안나의 결혼을 축하하며, 룰랭이 찾아와 위로가 되었다고 전한다. 살레 신부와 레이 의사의 권유로 노란 집을 떠나야 하는 상황을 담담히 받아들이며, 자신이 설치한 가스 시설 등은 미래의 후계자를 위한 것이었다고 의미를 부여한다. 몸은 회복 중이나 막연한 슬픔이 남아 있다고 고백하며, 룰랭 같은 소박하고 신실한 사람에게서 배우는 인생의 교훈에 깊은 애정을 표한다.
entries.why: Vincent thanks Theo for the money he sent – this must have been the first instalment of his April allowance. Theo must have sent this money shortly before leaving for the Netherlands on the evening of Saturday, 30 March. Because Vincent says that he has ‘waited a few days before replying’ (l. 15), and also expects that his brother will receive the present letter ‘around Sunday’ in the Netherlands (l. 21), we have dated it to about Thursday, 4 April 1889.

works.title: Peach Trees in Blossom
works.said: Just now I have on the easel an orchard of peach trees beside a road with the Alpilles in the background.

Félix Rey

people.name: Joseph Etienne Roulin
people.note: (1841-1903) postal worker in Arles and Marseille

facts.said: I still have to thank you for your last letter, as well as for the consignment of colours from Tasset  and several issues of Le Fifre with drawings by Forain.
facts.note: From 23 February 1889 until 1 June 1889, Jean Louis Forain wrote and illustrated Le Fifre, a magazine he also published, which appeared weekly in an edition of only a few copies. A total of 15 issues were published. A few issues from 1889, the first year of publication, have been preserved in the Van Gogh family estate; these are nos. 3 (9 March), 5 (23 March), 9 (20 April), 10 (27 April), 11 (4 May) and 12 (11 May). Each issue consists of one large folded sheet. One example by way of illustration: the title-page of the third issue, ‘Laissez courir les frais...’ (‘Hang the expense...’), Le Fifre.

facts.said: His visit gave me considerable pleasure, he often has to carry burdens which one would say were too heavy.
facts.note: Roulin had been transferred to Marseille at the end of January; see letter 736, n. 14. ‘Carry burdens’ could be intended literally: as a railway postman, Roulin was responsible for loading and unloading the postbags at each station.

facts.said: I still have to thank you for your last letter, as well as for the consignment of colours from Tasset
facts.note: On 24 March Vincent had asked Theo to send, before leaving for the Netherlands, 11 tubes of paint. See letter 752.

facts.said: It appears that there’s a fine article on Monet in Le Figaro,
facts.note: The article ‘Claude Monet’ by Octave Mirbeau had appeared in Le Figaro (p. 1) on 10 March 1889. In this very positive article Mirbeau praised the originality of Monet, whose only teacher was nature. At first his art was controversial, but now his talent had been recognized: ‘his imposing and learned simplicity ... his implacable harmony’ (sa grandiose et savante simplicité ... son implacable harmonie). Mirbeau praises the way Monet brings nature to life in his paintings, and describes how he works outside – day in, day out, come rain or shine.

entries.summary: 폴 시냐크에게 보낸 편지로, 그의 우호적인 방문이 큰 위안이 되었음을 감사하며 자신은 병원과 그 주변에서 다시 그림을 그리고 있다고 전한다. 일본 풍경을 연상시키는 작은 정원과 오두막이 있는 과수원 그림 두 점을 소개하며, 정신은 정상으로 돌아왔지만 여전히 깊은 불안이 남아 있다고 고백한다. 깊은 우정만이 삶의 가장 좋은 위안이라는 성찰로 편지를 맺는다.
entries.why: Signac’s postcard of 8 April was postmarked on Wednesday, 10 April at Arles (letter 755). We may assume that Van Gogh replied quickly. This is in keeping with Signac’s response to the present letter: he wrote back on ‘Friday’ (see letter 757). We have therefore dated the letter to Wednesday, 10 April 1889.

works.title: Peach Trees in Blossom
works.said: The foreground, enclosures with reed hedges where little peach trees are in blossom – everything there is small, the gardens, the fields, the gardens, the trees, even those mountains, as in certain Japanese landscapes, that’s why this subject attracted me.

works.title: Orchards in blossom, view of Arles
works.said: The other landscape is almost all green with a little lilac and grey – on a rainy day.

facts.said: I’ve rented an apartment consisting of two very small rooms.
facts.note: In letter 758 Van Gogh reports that this small apartment was owned by Dr Rey. As the house physician, Rey lived at the hospital, so it is possible that he had put his apartment, or part of it, at Van Gogh’s disposal. Rey’s address was Rampe du Pont, near the Pont de Trinquetaille (ACA; L’indicateur marseillais 1889).

facts.said: I remain much obliged to you for your most friendly and beneficial visit, which considerably contributed to cheering me up.
facts.note: Signac had visited Van Gogh in Arles on 23 and 24 March; see letter 752.

facts.said: The other landscape is almost all green with a little lilac and grey – on a rainy day.
facts.note: The letter sketch Orchard in blossom with a view of Arles (F - / JH 1684) was made after the painting of the same name (F 515 / JH 1683). It had rained from 5 to 9 April (Météo-France).

facts.said: I’ve also been without news of him for a fortnight.
facts.note: Theo had last written shortly before his departure for the Netherlands on 30 March; Vincent thanks him for his letter in letter 754.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 캔버스와 물감을 다시 주문하며 봄 과수원 습작 6점을 완성했다고 전한다. 레이 박사 소유의 작은 방으로 이사하게 된 사정과 이전 화실을 정리하기 위한 비용 문제를 설명하고, 테오의 결혼을 진심으로 축하한다. 시냐크의 카시스 초대는 경제적 여유가 없어 응할 수 없다는 소식도 덧붙인다.
entries.why: Vincent tells Theo about Signac’s proposal to come and paint in Cassis (ll. 43-44). This means that he must have received Signac’s letter of 12 April (letter 757). Thus the present letter was written on 13 April at the earliest. Furthermore, he hopes that the wedding has gone according to Theo’s liking (ll. 36-37). The marriage was solemnized on 18 April, but its date does not provide a foothold for the dating of this letter, because Vincent did not know exactly which day Theo was to be married (see letter 756, l.

facts.said: But to be able to move home and send you a consignment of canvases I would have to pay the other landlord.
facts.note: The owner of the Yellow House was Marie Louise Verdier; Van Gogh paid his rent to Verdier’s agent, Bernard Soulè, who was in charge of the building. See letter 602, n. 19.

facts.said: However, like the previous time when you went to Holland, it’s above all sheer chance.
facts.note: During Theo’s previous stay in the Netherlands (5–13 January 1889, for the official announcement of the engagement), something had gone wrong with Vincent’s allowance; see letter 741.

facts.said: In the meantime I’ve been obliged to ask Tasset for 10 metres of canvas and a few tubes.
facts.note: Van Gogh had last mentioned receiving paint and canvas from Tasset in November 1888 (letter 719).

facts.said: Also I still need 12 zinc white large tubes 1 Emerald ,, ,, 2 Cobalt ,, ,, 2 Ultramarine ,, ,, 1 Vermilion ,, ,, 4 Veronese Green ,, ,, 3 Chrome I ,, ,, 1 ,, II ,, ,, 2 Geranium lake medium tubes I have 6 spring studies, including two large orchards.
facts.note: Van Gogh named two of these studies in his letter to Signac (letter 756): La Crau with peach trees in blossom (F 514 / JH 1681) and Orchard in blossom with a view of Arles (F 515 / JH 1683). The two large orchards are the no. 30 canvases Orchard in blossom with a view of Arles (F 516 / JH 1685) and Orchard (F 511 / JH 1386). Among these spring studies were also Road with pollard willows (F 520 / JH 1690) and Field with flowers under a stormy sky (F 575 / JH 1422). Cf. also Feilchenfeldt 2005, pp. 294-295 (he adds Orchard (F 552 / JH 1381), but we date that painting to April 1888).

entries.summary: 아를에서의 독립적인 생활을 포기하고 생레미 정신병원에 자발적으로 입원하기로 결심했음을 테오에게 전하며, 혼자 화실을 꾸려나갈 자신이 없다고 솔직히 고백한다. 광기를 하나의 질병으로 받아들이려 노력하고 있으며, 술과 담배가 원인일 수도 있다는 점, 입원 중에도 그림 그릴 기회를 갖고 싶다는 바람을 전한다. 지금까지 자신을 지원해준 테오에게 깊은 감사를 표하며, 이제 그 애정을 새 아내 요한나에게 옮겨달라고 부탁한다.
entries.why: Jo van Gogh-Bonger, who possibly had a postmark to rely on, dated the letter to ‘21 April 1889’ (Brieven 1914). Because this dating agrees with Theo’s remark in letter 762 of 24 April that he received the present letter ‘yesterday’ (l. 5), we have dated it to Sunday, 21 April 1889. That was Easter Sunday, the day Vincent was supposed to leave the Yellow House (see letter 754). Appropriately enough, he writes here that he has meanwhile stored his furniture (ll. 13-14).

Johanna (Jo or Net) Gezina van Gogh-Bonger
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus

facts.said: Out of the 65 francs which I owe him, I’ve paid my landlord  only 25 francs, having had to pay 3 months’ rent in advance on a room where I shan’t live but where I’ve stored my furniture,
facts.note: Van Gogh stayed in hospital until his departure for Saint-Rémy on 8 May. Letter 767 and correspondence with Joseph and Marie Ginoux reveals that he had stored his furniture with them in the Café de la Gare. Salles had informed Theo on 19 April 1889: ‘For the time being the furniture has been sent to the house of a neighbour, to whom your brother has paid three months’ rent for this purpose, 18 francs in all’ (Pour le moment les meubles sont remises chez un voisin auquel votre frère a payé trois mois de location pour cet objet, en tout 18 f.) (FR b1050).

facts.said: Out of the 65 francs which I owe him,
facts.note: The 65 francs was the rent for three months for the Yellow House (February–April). Since December Van Gogh had rented the whole house for 21.50 francs a month (see letter 735).

facts.said: At the end of the month I’d still wish to go to the mental hospital at St-Rémy or another institution of that kind, which Mr Salles has told me about.
facts.note: The institution, a ‘private establishment dedicated to the treatment of insane persons of both sexes’ (établissement privé consacré au traitement des aliénés des deux sexes), was housed in the former monastery of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole, just outside Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, about 25 km north-east of Arles. Salles told Theo about it in the above-mentioned letter of 19 April, and sent him a prospectus (see letter 762, n. 2). Regarding this asylum, see Leroy 1948 and Jean-Marc Boulon, Vincent van Gogh à Saint-Paul-de-Mausole. Marseille 2003.

facts.said: My dear Theo You’ll probably be back in Paris when this letter arrives.
facts.note: Theo and Jo arrived in Paris on Saturday, 20 April; see letter 762.

facts.said: Out of the 65 francs which I owe him, I’ve paid my landlord
facts.note: The owner of the Yellow House was Marie Louise Verdier; Van Gogh paid his rent to Verdier’s agent, Bernard Soulè, who was in charge of the building. See letter 602, n. 19.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 살 신부와 상의한 끝에 생레미 요양원에 스스로 들어가기로 한 결정을 테오에게 설명하며, 반복된 발작이 심각했음을 인정한다. 화가들의 공동생활이라는 이상은 옳았으나 실패했다고 자평하고, 자연이 약보다 자신에게 더 도움이 될 것이라 믿는다. 이사 전 정리할 세금과 밀린 집세 등 실무적인 문제도 언급한다.
entries.why: The letter must have been written before receipt of Theo’s letter of 24 April (letter 762), because Vincent asks here if Theo is already back in Paris, whereas Theo reported in his letter that he had meanwhile arrived in Paris. In that same letter Theo responds to Vincent’s letter of 21 April (letter 760). We may therefore assume that the present letter had not yet arrived and that their letters had crossed. For this reason we have dated this letter to about Wednesday, 24 April 1889.

people.name: Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus
people.note: (1819-1907) wife of Theodorus van Gogh, mother of Vincent

people.name: Félix Rey
people.note: (1865-1932) assistant physician in the hospital in Arles

people.name: Bernard Soulè
people.note: (1826-1903) agent of Van Gogh's landlord in Arles

facts.said: My dear Theo, I saw Mr Salles again and he told me what he’d written to you.
facts.note: Salles had informed Theo on 19 April about Vincent’s decision to have himself admitted to an asylum, and had sent him information about the institution at Saint-Rémy (FR b1050). See letter 756, n. 6 and letter 762, n. 2.

facts.said: I’ll have to pay perhaps another 11.87 francs in movable property tax, I’ve been sent a bill for it at least, in addition to the rest of the rent that I still owe the landlord.
facts.note: The owner of the Yellow House was Marie Louise Verdier; Van Gogh paid his rent to Verdier’s agent, Bernard Soulè, who was in charge of the building. See letter 602, n. 19.

facts.said: Which wasn’t the case, because for me that crisis Anyway, it softens me a great deal in many judgements that, with more or less presumption, I’ve too often made about people who nevertheless wished me well.
facts.note: Here Van Gogh is less harsh in his judgement of the people who had signed the petition complaining about him in February. He had previously accused them of a cowardly and meddlesome attitude towards him (see letters 750 and 751).

facts.said: But no beginning again.
facts.note: This ‘failure’ refers to Van Gogh’s dashed hopes of turning the Yellow House into a true artists’ house. The first attack of his illness had put an abrupt end to his collaboration with Gauguin (see letter 728).

facts.said: Must tell you that I think it possible that you’ll find Mr Salles’ letter still addressed to rue Lepic.
facts.note: Since 20 April Theo had been living with his wife, Jo Bonger, at 8 cité Pigalle. See Brief happiness 1999, p. 27.

entries.summary: 테오의 결혼 소식에 기뻐하며 어머니가 젊어 보인다는 소식에도 안도감을 전한다. 생레미 요양원 입원 절차가 진행 중임을 알리고, 외인부대 입대까지 고려했다는 이야기와 함께 건강이 신체적으로는 나아졌다고 전한다. 올리브나무와 협죽도의 아름다움을 델라크루아에 비유하며 예찬하고, 곧 그림 두 상자를 보내겠다고 약속한다.
entries.why: The letter was written on the day the Rev. Salles was to go to Saint-Rémy (l. 16); we know from a letter written by Dr Peyron to Theo on 29 April that this visit took place the day before (FR b1059). On the basis of this we have dated the present letter to Sunday, 28 April 1889. The fact that Jo van Gogh-Bonger dated it to 29 April (Brieven 1914) could have to do with the postmark, in which case the letter was sent a day later.

Johanna (Jo or Net) Gezina van Gogh-Bonger
Anna Cornelia van Gogh-Carbentus

facts.said: I went to see Mr Salles with your letter for the director of the St-Rémy asylum,
facts.note: Theo had sent a letter of recommendation to Dr Peyron with letter 762. See Documentation, 24 April 1889. Peyron replied on 29 April (FR b1059).

facts.said: Is not Renan’s Christ a thousand times more consoling than so many papier mâché Christs one is served up with in the Duval establishments called Protestant, Catholic or whatever else churches?
facts.note: Van Gogh draws a parallel between the churches and the Duval restaurants, because the latter were popular and fashionable, and catered for the masses. Regarding Duval restaurants, see letter 502, n. 8.

facts.said: By the way, do you know that it’s very curious that during all this strange and inexplicable movement which took place in Arles and in which I was mixed up,
facts.note: In mentioning his own involvement, Van Gogh is referring to his abnormal behaviour, which had caused so much commotion among the residents of his neighbourhood, resulting in the petition for his confinement in hospital (letter 750).

entries.summary: 빈센트는 들라크루아와 코로, 밀레처럼 자신에게도 생활의 안정이 필요하다고 성찰하며, 몽펠리에 미술관에서 본 그림들이 세월에 바래가는 것에 대한 비애를 전한다. 홍수와 습기로 스튜디오와 작품들이 손상된 일을 이야기하며 자신이 세우려던 화가 공동체의 꿈이 좌절되었음을 애통해한다. 생레미 요양원 입원 조건(월 100프랑, 외부 작업 금지)에 대한 실망과 차라리 외인부대에 입대할까 하는 극단적 생각까지 언급하며, 짐 꾸러미에 담을 작품 목록(밤의 카페, 침실, 해바라기, 고갱·라발·베르나르 초상 등)을 상세히 나열한다.
entries.why: Vincent congratulates Theo on the occasion of his birthday (1 May). Because of this, and the fact that Jo van Gogh-Bonger (who possibly had a postmark to rely on) dated the letter to ‘30 April 1889’ (Brieven 1914), we have dated the letter to Tuesday, 30 April 1889.

facts.said: the night café the green vineyard the red vineyard the bedroom the furrows ditto portrait of Boch ,, Laval ,, Gauguin ,, Bernard The Alyscamps (lane of tombs) ditto
facts.note: Van Gogh had made four paintings of the Alyscamps: F 568 / JH 1622, F 569 / JH 1623, F 487 / JH 1621 and F 486 / JH 1620. Only one of them can be traced with certainty to the family estate: The Alyscamps (‘Leaf-fall’) (F 487 / JH 1621). His list contains two canvases of the Alyscamps, and it is plausible that he also sent F 486 / JH 1620, which had been hanging in Gauguin’s room together with F 487 (see letter 716). These two paintings were part of the decoration, as were a number of other works which he here describes as ‘worthy of being put on stretching frames’. Feilchenfeldt and cat.

facts.said: You’ll perhaps read with some interest the article I’m cutting out of a Marseille newspaper, because in it one glimpses Monticelli, and I find the description of the painting of a corner of the cemetery extremely interesting.
facts.note: Van Gogh is referring to the following description: ‘It was difficult to portray this cemetery with a more truthful feeling of desolation. A bleak, arid patch of ground, enclosed by grey walls, on which the torrid July sun casts its consuming light. Not a single flower on the bare graves, not a shrub to shelter them nor a cypress to protect them. Powdery stones giving life, through their fissures, to a few wild plants, through the midst of which run small lizards. Over there, in the corner, a gravedigger, his foot resting on his spade, for he has just dug a grave, wiping his brow.

facts.said: the night café the green vineyard the red vineyard the bedroom the furrows ditto portrait of Boch ,, Laval ,, Gauguin ,, Bernard The Alyscamps (lane of tombs) ditto Garden with large conifer bush and oleanders ditto cedar and geraniums Sunflowers flowers: Scabious &c.
facts.note: The only painting in which ‘scabious’ are possibly depicted is Wild flowers in a majolica jug (F 600 / JH 1424). Taking into account that the blue must originally have been more purple, the flowers in the middle could be scabious (presumably Centaurium scabiosa). However, Van Gogh had already painted F 600 in May 1888, in which case he kept it for a year before sending it. Another possibility is that the painting mentioned here is no longer known.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 누이 빌레미나가 암 환자를 간병하는 것에 대한 존경을 표하며, 고통과 헌신의 관계에 대한 은유적 사색을 전한다. 자신이 생레미 요양원에 최소 3개월간 입원하게 되었으며, 그간 여러 차례의 발작을 겪었음을 담담히 알린다. 요양원 병동과 정원을 그린 두 점의 그림을 상세히 묘사하고, 디킨스와 비처 스토우의 책, 렌 등을 읽으며 마음을 다스리고 있다고 전한다.
entries.why: Vincent replies to a letter from Willemien, which in letter 763 of 28 April he mentions having received. In letter 768 of 3 May to Theo, he writes that he wrote to his sister ‘the other day’. On the basis of this, we have dated the present letter to between Sunday, 28 April and Thursday, 2 May 1889.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent I don’t know if Lies is in Soesterberg at the moment,
facts.note: Elisabeth and Willemien were nursing the sick Mrs du Quesne in Soesterberg, as emerges from Theo’s letter to them both of 24 January 1889. The letter from Theo and Jo of 26 April 1889 is also addressed to both sisters (FR b919, FR b923). On 6 May Jo’s sister Mien received a postcard from Willemien in Soesterberg (FR b2900).

facts.said: Last year I did about ten or a dozen orchards in blossom
facts.note: In March-April 1888 Van Gogh had made a series of paintings of orchards in blossom; see letter 600, n. 7.

facts.said: ‘A rolling stone gathers no moss’
facts.note: The saying ‘A rolling stone gathers no moss’ is used here to mean that someone who does not stay in the same place for long or does not practise the same trade long enough will never progress (WNT).

facts.said: If you have the Drône book
facts.note: It is not known which book Willemien wrote about. Van Gogh writes ‘Drône’, but he certainly misread her handwriting. The writer Gustave Droz is the most likely candidate: in July 1889 Vincent was corresponding with Willemien about his book Monsieur, madame et bébé (see letter 785).

entries.summary: 고갱의 검술 마스크와 스케치를 포함한 그림 상자 두 개를 발송했다고 전하며, 병원 생활이 언제까지고 계속될 수는 없어 결단이 필요한 시점이라고 말한다. 화가로서 돈이 드는 것에 대한 죄책감에서, 차라리 5년간 외인부대에 입대하는 것을 진지하게 고려한다고 밝힌다. 생레미로 가는 것도 마다하지 않겠다며, 밤 카페에 머물 가능성과 함께 결정은 테오와 살 신부에게 맡기겠다고 전한다.
entries.why: In letter 765 of 30 April, Van Gogh wrote that he was busy packing up his paintings; now he mentions having sent two crates (ll. 1*-2). He also says: ‘It has been very hot today’ (l. 121). On Thursday, 2 May it was relatively warm: on 1 May it had been only 16.5 degrees, whereas on 2 May the temperature rose to 19.4 (Météo-France). Vincent has clearly not yet received Theo’s letter of 2 May (letter 766), containing his reaction to Vincent’s plans to join the Foreign Legion.

works.title: Red Chestnuts in the Public Park at Arles
works.said: I have on the go an avenue of chestnut trees with pink flowers with a little cherry tree in flower and a wisteria plant and the path in the park flecked with sunlight and shade.

facts.said: And be well aware, I won’t refuse anything, not even going to St-Rémy, despite these obstacles of the cost of board and lodging being higher than we hoped at first,
facts.note: Van Gogh thought at first that the cost of bed and board in the asylum was 80 francs a month (letter 760); in the meantime he had learned from Salles that the minimum would be 100 francs (letter 765). Peyron had also written to Theo about this on 29 April 1889. See Hulsker 1993-2, p. 177. When Vincent moved into the asylum, Theo began to make monthly notes in his account book of these expenses; see Account book 2002, pp. 44-45.

facts.said: I could perhaps go again to lodge at the night café where I’ve stored my furniture,
facts.note: Van Gogh had stored his furniture in the Café de la Gare owned by Joseph Ginoux; see letter 760, n. 4. He had lodged there from 7 May to 17 September 1888.

facts.said: Having taken the precaution of paying 30 francs to the bursar
facts.note: Read: ‘l’économe’ (bursar). Marius Huard fulfilled this function at the hospital in Arles (L’indicateur marseillais 1889).

facts.said: D58 and 59 – by goods train, and it will take a good week more before you receive them.
facts.note: This consignment can be largely reconstructed. Van Gogh wrote in letter 765 that the following works from the consignment should be put on stretching frames: The night café (F 463 / JH 1575), The green vineyard (F 475 / JH 1595), The red vineyard (F 495 / JH 1626), The bedroom (F 482 / JH 1608), Ploughed fields (‘The furrows’) (F 574 / JH 1586), Ploughed field with a tree-trunk (‘The furrows’) (F 573 / JH 1618), Eugène Boch (‘The poet’) (F 462 / JH 1574), The Alyscamps (‘Leaf-fall’) (F 486 / JH 1620), The Alyscamps (‘Leaf-fall’) (F 487 / JH 1621), ‘the poet’s garden’, The public garden with a couple strolling…

entries.summary: 빈센트는 생레미 요양원행을 받아들이기로 하며 순교자가 아닌 평범한 삶을 원한다는 심경을 밝힌다. 화가로서 자신은 그리 중요하지 않을 것이라 겸손하게 말하면서도 병중에도 다시 창작할 수 있으리라는 희망을 품는다. 밀레, 들라크루아, 모네 등 예술가들에 대한 폭넓은 평가와 함께, 화가들이 쉽게 미쳐버리는 삶의 방식에 대한 성찰, 고갱의 안부에 대한 그리움도 담겨 있다.
entries.why: Vincent writes that Theo’s letter did him good ‘today’. This was letter 766 of 2 May, which is why we have dated the present letter to Friday, 3 May 1889. This is in keeping with the date given it by Jo van Gogh-Bonger in Brieven 1914; it is possible that she had a postmark to rely on.

facts.said: Ever yours, Vincent Ah, when I wrote to you that we mustn’t forget to appreciate what’s good in those who aren’t Impressionists, I didn’t exactly mean to say that I was urging you to admire the Salon beyond measure, but rather a heap of people like, for example, Jourdan, who has just died in Avignon,
facts.note: Adolphe Jourdan had died on 22 February 1889 in Nîmes, a city not far from Avignon.

facts.said: (In my room I have the famous portrait of a man (the wood engraving) that you know, a mandarin woman by Monorou (the large print from the Bing album), the blade of grass (from the same album), the Pietà and the good Samaritan by Delacroix, and Meissonier’s reader, then two large reed pen drawings.)
facts.note: These were most likely The courtyard of the hospital (F 1467 / JH 1688) and the drawing which Van Gogh had made that day, Weeping tree on a lawn (F 1468 / JH 1498). They measure 49 x 61.5 cm and 45.5 x 59 cm, respectively.

facts.said: You’ll clearly see that the two women’s expressions
facts.note: The two women Van Gogh refers to are the portraits of Augustine Roulin and Marie Ginoux. The consignment most likely contained four versions of Augustine Roulin (‘La berceuse’), F 504 / JH 1655, F 506 / JH 1670, F 507 / JH 1672 and F 508 / JH 1671 (see letter 774, n. 2), as well as Marie Ginoux (‘The Arlésienne’) (F 489 / JH 1625). Provenance research undertaken by The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York has revealed that the second version, Marie Ginoux (‘The Arlésienne’) (F 488 / JH 1624), was in the possession of Madame Ginoux. See also Feilchenfeldt 2005, p. 297.

facts.said: (In my room I have the famous portrait of a man (the wood engraving) that you know, a mandarin woman by Monorou (the large print from the Bing album), the blade of grass (from the same album), the Pietà and the good Samaritan by Delacroix,
facts.note: Delacroix made two paintings of The Good Samaritan: one dating from 1849-1851 (private collection) and one from 1852 (London, Victoria and Albert Museum). The lithograph by Jules Joseph Augustin Laurens, which Van Gogh owned, is based on the first version, in which the injured man is lifted off his horse. See Johnson 1981-1989, vol. 3, pp. 224-225, 229, cat. nos. 437, 446. Van Gogh’s copy, to which he applied a grid to aid him in copying it, has been preserved (Amsterdam, Van Gogh Museum). Ill. 2290. (t*139) The painting he made after it is The Good Samaritan (after Delacroix) (F 633 / JH 1974) of May 1890.

entries.summary: 생트 폴 드 모솔(생레미) 요양원 입소를 돕던 신부 프레데릭 살르가 반 고흐에게 보낸 짧은 실무 편지이다. 자신이 화요일에 바빠 다음 날인 수요일에 8시 51분 기차로 동행하겠다고 제안하며, 원장 페이롱 박사를 이미 만나본 만큼 직접 동행하는 것이 적절하다고 설명한다. 반 고흐의 생레미 이송을 위한 실질적 일정 조율을 보여주는 편지이다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘Dimanche soir 5 Mai 89’.

people.name: Théophile Zacharie Auguste Peyron
people.note: (1827-1895) director of the asylum in Saint-Rémy

facts.said: Sunday evening, 5 May 1889 Having to go away tomorrow and being busy on Tuesdays, I place myself at your disposal to accompany you to St-Rémy on Wednesday.
facts.note: Van Gogh and Salles left according to schedule on Wednesday, 8 May 1889 for the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole in Saint-Rémy. Van Gogh’s name was recorded on that date in Le grand registre de l’asile de Saint-Rémy. See Documentation, 8 May 1889.

facts.said: Having already seen Mr Peyron, it is appropriate that I should accompany you myself.
facts.note: On Monday, 29 April Salles had had a talk with Dr Peyron about Vincent’s admission to the asylum. See letter 763, Date.

entries.summary: 아를의 카페 주인 조제프 지누는 생레미의 공기가 빈센트의 건강 회복에 도움이 되고 있다는 소식을 듣고 기쁘다는 안부 편지를 보낸다. 약속했던 호두나무 액자를 완성해 병원 관리인에게 전달했다고 알리며, 지누 부인과 함께 빈센트가 곧 건강해져 다시 만나기를 바란다는 따뜻한 인사를 전한다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘Arles, le 31 Mai 1889’.

facts.said: I have had a fine frame made as we had agreed, in walnut and impeccable.
facts.note: Because Ginoux says that he has delivered the frame to the hospital bursar, it is not likely that this frame was intended for one of the paintings still in Arles, since these were being stored at Ginoux’s (cf. letter 760). It is more reasonable to assume that the frame was made for a work that Van Gogh had given to his doctor, Félix Rey. Rey, at any rate, is the only hospital employee known to have received work from Van Gogh. He owned his portrait, Félix Rey (F 500 / JH 1659); see letter 736.

facts.said: I delivered it to the bursar.
facts.note: The hospital bursar was Marius Huard (L’indicateur marseillais 1889).

entries.summary: 서점 주인 랑블로가 반 고흐에게 보낸 짧은 업무 편지로, 주문한 책이 절판되었다는 소식을 전한다. 다른 책을 원하면 제목을 알려달라고 요청하며, 그렇지 않으면 다음 방문 때 환불해주겠다고 안내한다. 지극히 실용적이고 사무적인 내용의 짧은 서신이다.
entries.why: Letter headed: ‘Arles, le 16 juillet 1889’.

facts.said: Sir, I have made enquiries in Paris about the book you ordered from me
facts.note: On Sunday, 7 July 1889 Van Gogh undertook a supervised journey to Arles (see letters 787 and 789). It is not known which book he ordered.

facts.said: Jauffret.
facts.note: The bookshop owned by Anaïs Jauffret, 12 rue de la Poissonnerie, was taken over in 1889 by Marie Henriette Pauline Lamblot-Gaudin.

entries.summary: 빈센트는 베르나르가 그린 성서적 주제의 그림들(양치기의 경배, 수태고지, 겟세마네의 그리스도 등)을 강하게 비판하며, 현실과 동떨어진 추상적 종교화보다 밀레처럼 진실하고 가능한 소재를 그릴 것을 촉구한다. 자신이 그린 요양원 정원의 벼락 맞은 나무 그림과 밀밭 위 떠오르는 해 그림을 상세히 설명하며 색채로 불안과 평온의 감정을 표현했다고 말한다. 지오토와 코로 등을 예로 들며 성서적 소재도 절제된 방식이어야 한다는 자신의 미학을 펼친다.
entries.why: Van Gogh reports that he has finished five no. 30 canvases of olive groves (l. 160); he writes the same in letter 823 to Theo, which dates from Tuesday, 26 November 1889. We have therefore dated the present letter to on or about Tuesday, 26 November 1889.

works.title: Lullaby: Madame Augustine Roulin Rocking a Cradle (La Berceuse)
works.said: When Gauguin was in Arles, I once or twice allowed myself to be led into abstraction, as you know, in a woman rocking a cradle,

works.title: The Novel Reader
works.said: When Gauguin was in Arles, I once or twice allowed myself to be led into abstraction, as you know, in a woman rocking a cradle, a dark woman reading novels in a yellow library,

works.title: The Starry Night
works.said: However, once again I’m allowing myself to do stars too big, &c., new setback, and I’ve enough of that.

works.title: Garden of the Asylum
works.said: A ray of sun — the last glimmer — exalts the dark ochre to orange — small dark figures prowl here and there between the trunks.

works.title: The garden of St. Paul's Hospital
works.said: A ray of sun — the last glimmer — exalts the dark ochre to orange — small dark figures prowl here and there between the trunks.

works.title: Wheatfield with a Reaper
works.said: A field of yellow wheat and a yellow sun.

works.title: Olive Grove
works.said: So at present am working in the olive trees, seeking the different effects of a grey sky against yellow earth, with dark green note of the foliage; another time the earth and foliage all purplish against yellow sky, then red ochre earth and pink and green sky.

works.title: Olive Trees
works.said: So at present am working in the olive trees, seeking the different effects of a grey sky against yellow earth, with dark green note of the foliage; another time the earth and foliage all purplish against yellow sky, then red ochre earth and pink and green sky.

facts.said: But this is enough for you to understand that I would long to see things of yours again, like the painting of yours that Gauguin has, those Breton women walking in a meadow,
facts.note: For Bernard’s Breton women in the meadow , see letter 712, n. 4. Bernard himself claimed that this work had influenced Gauguin: ‘This is the canvas of which I once spoke in the Mercure de France, ‘Breton women in the meadow’, in my article Histoire de l’Ecole dite de Pont-Aven, and which brought about such a change in technique and assumptions in Gauguin. In 1888 he had exchanged it with me for a painting of his of the same size, and had taken it to Arles, where Vincent saw it and made a copy of it’ (Lettres à Bernard 1911, p. 144).

facts.said: When Gauguin was in Arles, I once or twice allowed myself to be led into abstraction, as you know, in a woman rocking a cradle,
facts.note: While Gauguin was in Arles, Van Gogh had started the first version of La berceuse (F 508 / JH 1671), which he finished in January 1889. See Hoermann Lister 2001.

facts.said: However, once again I’m allowing myself to do stars too big, &c., new setback, and I’ve enough of that.
facts.note: Van Gogh seems to be referring to Starry night (F 612 / JH 1731), which he had made in June of that year. When mentioning the work in earlier letters, however, he was not so negative about it; he even defended it to Theo (see letters 813 and 816).

facts.said: Gauguin and I saw a tiny panel of his in Montpellier, the death of some sainted woman or other.
facts.note: In December 1888 Van Gogh and Gauguin had travelled to Montpellier to visit the Musée Fabre. The ‘tiny panel’ Van Gogh refers to is The death and assumption of the Virgin (now no longer attributed to Giotto). See letter 726, n. 12.

facts.said: A ray of sun — the last glimmer — exalts the dark ochre to orange — small dark figures prowl here and there between the trunks.
facts.note: The canvas Van Gogh describes in such detail is The garden of the asylum. There are two variants, F 660 / JH 1849 and F 659 / JH 1850; the one referred to here is probably the second one. See Hendriks and Van Tilborgh 2001, pp. 154-156.

entries.summary: 지누 부인이 빈센트에게 답장이 늦어진 이유를 설명하며, 남편 조제프 지누가 황소에게 옆구리를 받혀 다쳤다가 회복 중이라고 전한다. 자신도 매우 피곤한 상태이지만 점차 나아지고 있다고 알리며, 부탁받은 물건을 토요일에 보내겠다고 약속한다. 이웃들의 안부와 함께 빈센트를 그리워하며 다시 아를에서 만나지 못한 것을 아쉬워하는 따뜻한 인사로 마무리한다.

facts.said: On Saturday he will send what you ask of us.
facts.note: Van Gogh had asked the Ginouxs to send to Auvers the furniture he had stored with them in Arles. He confirmed receipt of it in letter 898, written on or about 10 July.
